title: DSA and Competitive Programming
description: Master Data Structures and Algorithms from basics to advanced competitive programming levels.

topics.title: What is Data Structures and Algorithms?
topics.description: An absolute beginner's introduction to Data Structures and Algorithms, explaining what it is and why it matters.

subtopics.title: Core concept of Data Structures and Algorithms

topics.title: Why use Data Structures and Algorithms?
topics.description: Understanding the real-world applications and use cases of Data Structures and Algorithms in modern engineering.

topics.title: History and Ecosystem
topics.description: A brief look at how Data Structures and Algorithms evolved and where it fits in the broader ecosystem today.

topics.title: Input/output
topics.description: Reading input fast and printing output correctly is the first thing every judge checks. Learn buffered readers, tokenising lines and formatting numbers.

topics.title: Variables and Data Types
topics.description: Choosing the right type avoids overflow and precision bugs. Know the ranges of int and long, when doubles lose precision, and how chars map to integers.

topics.title: Operators and Conditions
topics.description: Arithmetic, comparison and logical operators plus precedence rules. Integer division, modulo with negatives and short-circuit evaluation cause most beginner bugs.

topics.title: Loops and Nested Loops
topics.description: for, while and do-while loops and how nesting multiplies work. Learn to count iterations, break early and avoid off-by-one errors.

topics.title: Functions and Parameters
topics.description: Breaking code into functions with clear inputs. Pass-by-value semantics, reference types, and recursion basics.

topics.title: Return values
topics.description: Returning results instead of printing inside helpers, multiple return values via arrays or objects, and sentinel values.

topics.title: Arrays and Strings
topics.description: Fixed-size arrays and immutable strings are the workhorses of every problem. Learn creation, indexing, length and conversions between them.

topics.title: Debugging and Dry runs
topics.description: Tracing code by hand on tiny inputs finds most bugs faster than a debugger. Learn to build a trace table and to bisect with prints.

topics.title: Edge cases
topics.description: Empty inputs, single elements, duplicates, negatives, maximum sizes and overflow. Systematically listing them before coding prevents wrong answers.

topics.title: Time Complexity
topics.description: How running time grows with input size. Count dominant operations, drop constants, and match constraints to acceptable complexities.

topics.title: Space Complexity
topics.description: Memory used beyond the input, including recursion stacks. Learn to count auxiliary space and to trade memory for time.

topics.title: Big O, Omega, Theta
topics.description: Upper, lower and tight bounds. Big O is what interviewers mean, but knowing Theta helps you argue an algorithm is optimal.

subtopics.title: Definitions of O, Ω and Θ

topics.title: Best/Average/Worst case
topics.description: The same algorithm can behave differently per input. Quick sort is O(n log n) on average but O(n²) worst; know which case matters.

topics.title: Loop analysis
topics.description: Translating loop structures into sums. Loops that halve or multiply give logarithms; triangular nested loops still give n².

topics.title: Recursion analysis
topics.description: Recurrence relations describe recursive running time. Count calls and work per call, then solve or bound the recurrence.

topics.title: Recurrence relations
topics.description: Solving recurrences with the master theorem, substitution and recursion trees. Recognise the standard shapes that appear in divide and conquer.

topics.title: Amortized analysis
topics.description: Average cost per operation over a sequence, even when single operations are expensive. Dynamic arrays and union-find are the classic examples.

topics.title: Array representation
topics.description: Contiguous memory gives O(1) indexing and cache-friendly scans. Understand 1D versus 2D layout, row-major order and bounds.

topics.title: Indexing and Traversal
topics.description: Forward, backward and strided traversal, plus safe index arithmetic. Most array bugs are off-by-one or wrap-around mistakes.

topics.title: Insertion and Deletion
topics.description: Inserting or deleting in the middle shifts elements, costing O(n). Learn the shifting loops and why swap-with-last helps when order is irrelevant.

topics.title: Searching and Min/Max
topics.description: Linear scans to find an element, the minimum, the maximum, or the second largest in one pass while tracking candidates.

topics.title: Frequency counting
topics.description: Count occurrences with a fixed-size array when values are bounded, or a hash map otherwise. Powers anagram checks, majority elements and mode finding.

topics.title: Reversal and Rotation
topics.description: Reverse in place with two pointers, then rotate using the three-reversal trick in O(n) time and O(1) space.

subtopics.title: Rotation by k with three reversals

topics.title: Merging and Sorted arrays
topics.description: Merge two sorted arrays with two pointers, in place from the back when one array has spare capacity. The core of merge sort and k-way merge.

subtopics.title: Intersection and union of sorted arrays

topics.title: Prefix/Suffix sums
topics.description: Precompute running totals so any range sum is O(1). Extends to prefix XOR, prefix counts and 2D prefix sums.

topics.title: Two pointers
topics.description: Move two indices toward each other or in the same direction to replace nested loops. Works on sorted arrays and for partition-style problems.

topics.title: Sliding window
topics.description: Maintain a window over the array and update an aggregate as it slides, turning O(n·k) into O(n). Fixed and variable-size variants.

topics.title: Kadane's algorithm
topics.description: Maximum subarray sum in one pass by deciding at each element whether to extend or restart. Extends to circular arrays and max product.

topics.title: Matrix and 2D grids
topics.description: Row and column traversal, transposition, rotation and spiral order. Grids also appear in BFS and DP problems.

topics.title: Intervals
topics.description: Merge, insert, intersect and count overlapping intervals after sorting. The pattern behind meeting rooms and calendar problems.

topics.title: Character operations
topics.description: Characters are small integers underneath. Check case, digits and alphabet position with arithmetic and the standard character helpers.

topics.title: Traversal and Reversal
topics.description: Iterating characters, building results with StringBuilder and reversing in place with two pointers or the builder.

topics.title: Palindrome and Anagrams
topics.description: Palindromes compare mirrored positions; anagrams compare character counts. Both appear constantly as sub-steps of harder problems.

topics.title: Frequency maps
topics.description: Count characters with an int[26], int[128] or HashMap<Character,Integer> depending on the alphabet. Powers first-unique, anagram and window problems.

topics.title: Substrings and Subsequences
topics.description: Substrings are contiguous, subsequences are not. Know how many exist and the standard enumeration and DP techniques for each.

topics.title: Pattern matching
topics.description: Find occurrences of a pattern in text. Naive is O(nm); KMP and Z-algorithm reach O(n+m) using prefix information.

topics.title: String hashing
topics.description: Polynomial rolling hashes let you compare substrings in O(1) after O(n) preprocessing. Watch for collisions and use double hashing when needed.

topics.title: Sliding window on strings
topics.description: Windows over strings with character counts: longest substring without repeats, minimum window substring, and permutation-in-string.

topics.title: Two pointers on strings
topics.description: Compare or rearrange characters from both ends or with a reader/writer pair: valid palindrome, reverse vowels, compress string.

topics.title: String building and parsing
topics.description: StringBuilder, splitting, joining and parsing numbers safely. Also tokenising expressions and handling whitespace.

topics.title: Hash functions
topics.description: A hash function maps keys to bucket indices. Good ones are fast and spread keys uniformly; bad ones cause clustering and slow lookups.

topics.title: Hash tables
topics.description: Arrays of buckets indexed by hash, giving average O(1) insert, delete and lookup. Load factor and resizing keep operations fast.

topics.title: Sets and Maps
topics.description: HashSet for membership, HashMap for key-value lookups, plus their ordered cousins. Choosing between them is a daily decision.

topics.title: Collisions
topics.description: Two keys hashing to the same bucket. Chaining stores lists per bucket; open addressing probes for the next free slot.

topics.title: Frequency counting with hash maps
topics.description: Count how often each key appears using a map. It is the first step of many problems: top-k, duplicates, majority, grouping.

topics.title: Duplicate detection
topics.description: Detect repeats with a set in one pass, or in O(1) space when values are bounded by marking visited indices.

topics.title: Lookup optimization
topics.description: Replace inner loops with hash lookups: two-sum, pair difference, checking existence of complements. O(n²) becomes O(n).

topics.title: Prefix-sum hashing
topics.description: Combine prefix sums with a hash map to count subarrays with a given sum, divisible sums, or equal 0/1 counts.

topics.title: Bubble Sort
topics.description: Repeatedly swap adjacent out-of-order elements. O(n²) but simple, stable, and useful for teaching the idea of passes and early exit.

topics.title: Selection Sort
topics.description: Select the minimum of the unsorted part and swap it into place. Always O(n²) comparisons but only O(n) swaps.

topics.title: Insertion Sort
topics.description: Insert each element into the sorted prefix by shifting larger elements right. Great for small or nearly sorted inputs, and used inside hybrid sorts.

topics.title: Merge Sort
topics.description: Divide, sort halves recursively, merge. Guaranteed O(n log n), stable, needs O(n) extra space. Basis for counting inversions.

topics.title: Quick Sort
topics.description: Partition around a pivot and recurse. Average O(n log n) and in place, but O(n²) with bad pivots; randomisation fixes typical inputs.

topics.title: Heap Sort
topics.description: Build a max-heap, then repeatedly move the root to the end. O(n log n) worst case and in place, but not stable and cache-unfriendly.

topics.title: Counting and Radix Sort
topics.description: Non-comparison sorts that beat n log n when keys are small integers or fixed-length digits. Counting sort is the stable building block of radix sort.

topics.title: Stability and In-place
topics.description: Stable sorts keep equal elements in input order; in-place sorts use O(1) extra memory. Know which standard sorts have which property.

topics.title: Linear search
topics.description: Scan every element until a match. O(n), works on unsorted data, and is the right choice for tiny inputs or single queries.

topics.title: Binary search
topics.description: Halve a sorted range each step to find a target in O(log n). Master the loop invariants to avoid infinite loops and off-by-one errors.

topics.title: Lower/Upper bound
topics.description: Find the first element ≥ x (lower bound) or > x (upper bound). These two functions solve most "find position" problems.

topics.title: First/Last occurrence
topics.description: Binary search that keeps going after a match to find the leftmost or rightmost index. Same loop, different direction on equality.

topics.title: Rotated arrays
topics.description: A sorted array rotated at an unknown pivot still allows O(log n) search by deciding which half is sorted each step.

topics.title: Binary search on answers
topics.description: When the answer is a number with a yes/no feasibility that is monotonic, binary search the answer and test feasibility each step.

topics.title: Monotonic predicates
topics.description: Binary search works on any predicate that flips from false to true once. Learn to phrase problems as "find the first true".

topics.title: Singly linked lists
topics.description: Nodes with a value and a next pointer. O(1) insert at head, O(n) access by index, and the dummy-head trick for clean edge cases.

topics.title: Doubly linked lists
topics.description: Each node links forward and backward, enabling O(1) deletion given a node reference. The backbone of LRU caches.

topics.title: Circular linked lists
topics.description: The last node points back to the first. Useful for round-robin scheduling and Josephus-style problems; traversal must stop on returning to the start.

topics.title: Traversal and Insertion
topics.description: Walk the list with a cursor, insert after a node or at a position, and keep the tail pointer updated for O(1) append.

topics.title: Deletion and Reversal
topics.description: Delete by relinking the previous node; reverse iteratively with three pointers or recursively. Reversal in groups of k is the classic follow-up.

topics.title: Cycle detection (Floyd's algorithm)
topics.description: Floyd's tortoise and hare: a slow and fast pointer meet iff there is a cycle. Then find the cycle start and length in O(1) space.

topics.title: Fast/slow pointers
topics.description: Two pointers at different speeds find the middle, the kth from end, and split lists, all in one pass.

topics.title: Merging and Sorting
topics.description: Merge two sorted lists by relinking nodes, sort a list with merge sort in O(n log n) and O(1) extra space, and merge k lists with a heap.

subtopics.title: Merging k lists with a heap

topics.title: Stack operations
topics.description: Last-in, first-out with O(1) push, pop and peek. Implemented on arrays or linked lists; ArrayDeque is the Java choice.

topics.title: Queue operations
topics.description: First-in, first-out with O(1) enqueue and dequeue. The backbone of BFS and task scheduling.

topics.title: Circular queue
topics.description: A fixed array with wrap-around head and tail indices gives O(1) operations without shifting. Track size or leave one slot empty to distinguish full from empty.

topics.title: Deque
topics.description: Double-ended queue with O(1) operations at both ends. Powers sliding-window maximum and 0-1 BFS.

subtopics.title: Push and pop at both ends

topics.title: Monotonic stack
topics.description: A stack kept increasing or decreasing to answer next-greater/smaller queries in O(n). Used in histogram, stock span and rain water problems.

topics.title: Monotonic queue
topics.description: A deque of candidates in monotonic order for windowed minimum or maximum, and for optimising certain DP transitions.

topics.title: Next greater element
topics.description: For every element find the next one to the right that is larger. Solved right-to-left with a stack, including circular variants.

topics.title: Balanced brackets
topics.description: Push openers, pop on closers and check matching types. A model for any nested-structure validation.

topics.title: Expression evaluation
topics.description: Evaluate infix expressions with two stacks or convert to postfix. Handle precedence, parentheses and unary minus.

topics.title: Call stack
topics.description: Each call pushes a frame with parameters and locals. Depth is limited, so deep recursion can overflow; know when to convert to iteration.

topics.title: Base cases
topics.description: The terminating condition of a recursion. Wrong or missing base cases cause infinite recursion or off-by-one answers.

topics.title: Recursion trees
topics.description: Draw the tree of calls to count work and spot repeated subproblems. This is how you discover where memoisation helps.

topics.title: Subsets and Permutations
topics.description: Generate all subsets (2^n) and permutations (n!) by choosing or skipping each element. Handle duplicates by sorting and skipping.

topics.title: Combinations
topics.description: Choose k of n without regard to order by always moving forward through indices. Combination sum variants allow reuse.

topics.title: N-Queens
topics.description: Place n queens so none attack. Row-by-row backtracking with sets for columns and both diagonals runs fast enough for n ≤ 12.

topics.title: Sudoku
topics.description: Fill empty cells with backtracking, checking row, column and 3×3 box. Choosing the most constrained cell first speeds it up dramatically.

topics.title: Constraint pruning
topics.description: Cut branches that cannot lead to a solution as early as possible. Ordering, bounds and feasibility checks turn exponential searches into fast ones.

topics.title: Binary trees
topics.description: Each node has up to two children. Learn node structure, recursion over left and right, and the vocabulary: root, leaf, depth, height.

topics.title: Traversals
topics.description: Preorder, inorder, postorder and level-order. Know both recursive and iterative versions and what each order is used for.

topics.title: Height and Depth
topics.description: Depth counts edges from the root; height counts edges to the deepest leaf. Compute height bottom-up and check balance in the same pass.

topics.title: Diameter and Views
topics.description: Diameter is the longest path between any nodes. Left, right, top and bottom views come from BFS with horizontal distance or DFS with level tracking.

topics.title: Balanced trees
topics.description: Height-balanced trees keep operations O(log n). AVL rotations and red-black rules are the standard ways to maintain balance.

topics.title: Lowest common ancestor
topics.description: The deepest node that is an ancestor of both targets. Recursive postorder for binary trees, value comparison for BSTs, binary lifting for many queries.

topics.title: Tree construction
topics.description: Rebuild a tree from preorder+inorder or postorder+inorder using index maps. Also construct from level order and from sorted arrays.

topics.title: Serialization
topics.description: Encode a tree as a string and decode it back. Preorder with null markers is simplest; level order matches the LeetCode format.

topics.title: Tree DP
topics.description: Compute answers for subtrees and combine at the parent: max path sum, house robber III, subtree sizes, rerooting.

topics.title: BST properties
topics.description: Left subtree values are smaller, right subtree values larger, recursively. Inorder traversal yields sorted order; operations cost O(height).

topics.title: Search and Validation
topics.description: Search by comparing and descending. Validate with min/max bounds passed down, not by checking only direct children.

topics.title: BST insertion and deletion
topics.description: Insert at the leaf position found by search. Deletion has three cases: leaf, one child, two children (replace with inorder successor).

topics.title: Predecessor/Successor
topics.description: The next smaller or larger value. Found by walking the tree with bounds, or via parent pointers, without a full traversal.

topics.title: Kth smallest
topics.description: Inorder traversal visits values in order, so stop at the kth. Augmenting nodes with subtree sizes makes it O(height).

topics.title: Balanced BST concepts
topics.description: Self-balancing trees (AVL, red-black, treaps) guarantee O(log n). Know rotations conceptually and when a sorted structure beats a hash map.

topics.title: Min/max heaps
topics.description: A complete binary tree stored in an array where each parent is ≤ (min) or ≥ (max) its children. O(log n) insert and extract, O(1) peek.

topics.title: Heapify
topics.description: Sift-up after insert and sift-down after removal restore the heap property. Building from an array bottom-up is O(n).

topics.title: Heap sort and heap building
topics.description: Build a max-heap then repeatedly swap the root to the end and sift down. O(n log n), in place, not stable.

topics.title: Top K
topics.description: Keep a heap of size k to find the k largest or smallest or most frequent elements in O(n log k). Quickselect gives O(n) average.

subtopics.title: Min-heap of size k for largest

topics.title: K-way merge
topics.description: Merge k sorted sequences by keeping one element from each in a heap. Used for merging lists, sorted matrices and external sorting.

topics.title: Median of streams
topics.description: Maintain a max-heap of the lower half and a min-heap of the upper half; the median is at their roots. O(log n) per insert.

topics.title: Scheduling problems
topics.description: Greedy plus heap: meeting rooms, task scheduler, CPU scheduling, reorganising strings. The heap always yields the next best choice.

subtopics.title: Meeting rooms with a min-heap of end times

topics.title: Prefix trees
topics.description: A tree where each edge is a character and each path a prefix. Lookups cost O(word length) regardless of dictionary size.

topics.title: Insertion and Search
topics.description: Walk or create nodes per character, then set the end flag. Search follows the same path and checks the flag; startsWith skips the flag.

topics.title: Deletion
topics.description: Remove a word by clearing the flag and pruning nodes with no children, walking back up recursively.

topics.title: Autocomplete
topics.description: Find the node for a prefix, then DFS to collect completions. Store top suggestions per node for constant-time results in production.

topics.title: Prefix matching
topics.description: Trie problems: longest common prefix, replace words with roots, word search II on a grid with trie-guided DFS.

topics.title: Bitwise tries
topics.description: A trie over bits of integers answers maximum XOR queries in O(32) per number.

topics.title: Graph representations
topics.description: Adjacency lists for sparse graphs, matrices for dense ones or fast edge lookup, edge lists for sorting-based algorithms.

topics.title: Directed/undirected graphs
topics.description: Undirected edges are stored twice; directed edges once. Direction changes cycle detection, degrees and reachability.

topics.title: Weighted graphs
topics.description: Edges carry costs. Store (neighbour, weight) pairs and pick algorithms by weight sign and density.

topics.title: BFS and DFS
topics.description: The two fundamental traversals: BFS explores by distance with a queue, DFS goes deep with recursion or a stack. Track visited to avoid loops.

topics.title: Connected components
topics.description: Count or label components with repeated DFS/BFS or union-find. Number of islands is the grid version.

topics.title: Cycle detection in graphs
topics.description: Undirected: DFS with parent tracking or union-find. Directed: DFS colouring (white/grey/black) or a topological sort that fails.

topics.title: Bipartite graphs
topics.description: Vertices split into two sets with edges only across. Check by 2-colouring with BFS/DFS; odd cycles make it impossible.

topics.title: Topological sorting
topics.description: Linear order of a DAG respecting edges. Kahn's algorithm uses in-degrees and a queue; DFS uses reverse postorder.

topics.title: Union-find
topics.description: Disjoint sets with near-constant find and union using path compression and union by rank. Ideal for dynamic connectivity and Kruskal.

topics.title: Shortest paths
topics.description: Dijkstra for non-negative weights, Bellman-Ford for negative edges, Floyd-Warshall for all pairs, BFS for unweighted.

topics.title: Minimum spanning trees
topics.description: Connect all vertices with minimum total weight. Kruskal sorts edges and uses union-find; Prim grows from a vertex with a heap.

topics.title: Bridges and articulation points
topics.description: Edges or vertices whose removal disconnects the graph. Found in one DFS with discovery and low-link times (Tarjan).

topics.title: Greedy choice property
topics.description: A locally optimal choice leads to a global optimum. Greedy works only when this property holds, so learn to argue it or find a counterexample.

topics.title: Interval scheduling
topics.description: Sort intervals and sweep: merge overlaps, count non-overlapping, remove the minimum to make them disjoint.

topics.title: Activity selection
topics.description: Pick the maximum number of compatible activities by always choosing the one that ends earliest.

topics.title: Fractional knapsack
topics.description: Take items by best value-to-weight ratio, allowing fractions. Contrast with 0/1 knapsack where greedy fails.

topics.title: Huffman coding
topics.description: Build an optimal prefix code by repeatedly merging the two least frequent symbols with a min-heap.

topics.title: Jump problems
topics.description: Jump game variants: can you reach the end, minimum jumps. Track the farthest reachable index and expand a window greedily.

topics.title: Proof techniques
topics.description: Exchange arguments and "greedy stays ahead" justify greedy algorithms. Being able to sketch a proof is what interviewers look for.

topics.title: Memoization and Tabulation
topics.description: Top-down caches recursive results; bottom-up fills a table in dependency order. Same states, different control flow.

topics.title: State design and Transitions
topics.description: Define what a state represents, what decisions move between states and the base cases. Most DP mistakes are state definition mistakes.

topics.title: 1D/2D DP
topics.description: Climbing stairs, house robber, unique paths, minimum path sum. Learn to write the table and shrink it to O(1) or O(n) space.

topics.title: Knapsack and Coin change
topics.description: 0/1 knapsack chooses each item once; unbounded allows reuse. Coin change counts ways or minimises coins with the same table shape.

topics.title: LIS and LCS
topics.description: Longest increasing subsequence in O(n log n) with patience sorting; longest common subsequence with a 2D table.

subtopics.title: LIS O(n²) and O(n log n)

topics.title: Edit distance
topics.description: Minimum insert/delete/replace operations to transform one string into another. A 2D table with three transitions.

topics.title: Grid and Interval DP
topics.description: Grid DP moves through cells; interval DP solves ranges by splitting: matrix chain, burst balloons, palindrome partitioning.

topics.title: Tree and Bitmask DP
topics.description: DP over subtrees and DP over subsets encoded as bitmasks (TSP, assignment). Bitmask DP handles n up to about 20.

topics.title: Binary representation
topics.description: Two's complement, sign bits, and how ints wrap. Read and write binary confidently before manipulating bits.

topics.title: Bitwise operators
topics.description: AND, OR, XOR, NOT and shifts with their identities. Shifts multiply or divide by powers of two.

topics.title: Masks
topics.description: A mask isolates or sets specific bits. Build masks with shifts and combine them with AND/OR to read and write flags.

topics.title: Set/clear/toggle bits
topics.description: Set with OR, clear with AND NOT, toggle with XOR. The three basic edits that all bit tricks build on.

topics.title: XOR patterns
topics.description: XOR cancels pairs, so it finds the single non-duplicate, the missing number, and swaps without a temp.

topics.title: Subsets and Bit counting
topics.description: Enumerate subsets with masks and count set bits with Kernighan's trick or built-ins. Power-of-two checks use x & (x - 1).

topics.title: GCD and LCM
topics.description: Euclid's algorithm computes GCD in O(log min(a, b)); LCM = a / gcd × b. Watch for overflow in LCM.

topics.title: Primes and Sieve
topics.description: Trial division up to √n for one number; the sieve of Eratosthenes lists all primes to n in O(n log log n).

topics.title: Modular arithmetic
topics.description: Keep numbers small with mod at every step. Learn the rules for +, -, × and why division needs modular inverses.

topics.title: Fast exponentiation
topics.description: Compute a^b in O(log b) by squaring. Extends to matrix exponentiation for linear recurrences.

topics.title: Combinatorics
topics.description: Count arrangements with nCr, nPr, stars and bars, and inclusion-exclusion. Precompute factorials modulo a prime for many queries.

topics.title: Permutations and Combinations
topics.description: Generating and counting orderings and selections, including next-permutation in lexicographic order.

topics.title: Probability fundamentals
topics.description: Basic probability, expected value and linearity of expectation, which often gives surprisingly simple solutions.

topics.title: Segment trees
topics.description: Range queries and point updates in O(log n) over an array. Each node stores an aggregate (sum, min, max) of its range.

topics.title: Lazy propagation
topics.description: Range updates in O(log n) by storing pending updates on nodes and pushing them down only when needed.

topics.title: Fenwick trees
topics.description: Binary indexed tree: prefix sums and point updates in O(log n) with a tiny array and simple code.

topics.title: Sparse tables
topics.description: O(1) range minimum queries on static arrays after O(n log n) preprocessing, using overlapping power-of-two blocks.

topics.title: Advanced graph algorithms
topics.description: Strongly connected components (Tarjan/Kosaraju), max flow (Edmonds-Karp/Dinic) and bipartite matching.

topics.title: Advanced string matching
topics.description: Suffix arrays, suffix automata and Aho-Corasick for multiple patterns; Manacher for all palindromes in O(n).

topics.title: Sweep line
topics.description: Process events in sorted order while maintaining an active set: skyline, meeting rooms, rectangle union, closest pair.

topics.title: Pattern recognition
topics.description: Map a new problem onto known patterns: two pointers, sliding window, BFS, DP, heap. Recognition is the skill that speeds everything up.

topics.title: Brute-force-to-optimized thinking
topics.description: Start with the obvious solution, state its complexity, then remove redundant work. Interviewers reward this progression.

topics.title: Dry runs
topics.description: Walk through your code on a small example out loud. It catches off-by-one and edge-case bugs before the interviewer does.

topics.title: Complexity explanation
topics.description: State time and space with reasoning, not just the answer. Mention trade-offs and what changes for larger constraints.

topics.title: Timed contests
topics.description: Practice under time pressure to build speed and calm. Read all problems, pick the easiest, and manage attempts and penalties.

topics.title: Mock interviews
topics.description: Simulate the real thing: think aloud, ask clarifying questions, code cleanly, test. Record and review yourself.

title: Core Java, OOP and Collections
description: Master Java programming language.

topics.title: What is Java?
topics.description: An absolute beginner's introduction to Java, explaining what it is and why it matters.

topics.title: Why use Java?
topics.description: Understanding the real-world applications and use cases of Java in modern engineering.

topics.title: History and Ecosystem
topics.description: A brief look at how Java evolved and where it fits in the broader ecosystem today.

topics.title: Java installation
topics.description: Install a JDK, set JAVA_HOME and PATH, and verify with java -version. Know which LTS version to pick and how multiple JDKs coexist.

topics.title: JDK, JRE, JVM
topics.description: The JVM runs bytecode, the JRE bundles the JVM with libraries, the JDK adds compilers and tools. Interviewers ask this constantly.

topics.title: Compilation
topics.description: javac produces .class files; java loads them through class loaders. Learn classpath, packages on disk and how a main class is located.

topics.title: Syntax
topics.description: Statements, blocks, comments, naming conventions and the structure of a class. Small habits here make code readable for reviewers.

topics.title: Variables and types
topics.description: Eight primitives and reference types, default values, literals and widening versus narrowing conversions.

topics.title: Operators
topics.description: Arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise, ternary and assignment operators with precedence. Integer overflow silently wraps.

topics.title: Control flow
topics.description: if/else, switch (including arrow-form and expressions), loops, break and continue. Modern switch avoids fall-through bugs.

topics.title: Methods
topics.description: Signatures, overloading, varargs, static versus instance and return types. Overload resolution rules trip people up in interviews.

topics.title: Arrays
topics.description: Fixed-length, typed, zero-indexed containers. Multi-dimensional arrays, Arrays utility methods and array covariance quirks.

topics.title: Strings
topics.description: Immutable, pooled, compared with equals not ==. Know the common API and why immutability matters for security and hashing.

topics.title: StringBuilder
topics.description: Mutable string buffer for efficient concatenation. Use it in loops; StringBuffer is the synchronised legacy version.

topics.title: Exceptions
topics.description: Checked versus unchecked exceptions, try/catch/finally, try-with-resources and custom exceptions. Know the hierarchy under Throwable.

topics.title: Error handling
topics.description: Fail fast, wrap with context, never swallow. Errors versus exceptions, and how to design exception boundaries in an application.

topics.title: Wrapper types and autoboxing
topics.description: Integer, Long and friends wrap primitives for generics. Autoboxing hides conversions that cost allocations and break == comparisons.

topics.title: Enums
topics.description: Type-safe constants with fields, methods and per-constant behaviour. EnumMap and EnumSet are fast specialised collections.

topics.title: Classes and Objects
topics.description: A class is a blueprint; an object is an instance on the heap. Fields, methods, this, and object identity versus equality.

topics.title: Constructors
topics.description: Initialise state at creation. Default, overloaded and chained constructors with this(...) and super(...), plus initialiser blocks.

topics.title: Access modifiers
topics.description: public, protected, package-private and private control visibility. They apply to classes, fields, methods and constructors.

topics.title: Encapsulation
topics.description: Hide state behind methods so invariants hold. Getters and setters, immutable objects and defensive copies.

topics.title: Inheritance
topics.description: extends reuses and specialises a class. Method overriding, super calls, and why composition is often preferred.

topics.title: Polymorphism
topics.description: A reference of a supertype can point to any subtype; the runtime type decides which override runs. Overloading is compile-time polymorphism.

topics.title: Abstraction
topics.description: Expose what an object does, hide how. Abstract classes and interfaces model contracts; clients depend on abstractions.

topics.title: Interfaces
topics.description: Pure contracts with abstract, default and static methods. A class can implement many; functional interfaces enable lambdas.

topics.title: Abstract classes
topics.description: Partially implemented classes for shared code with abstract hooks. Template method pattern lives here.

topics.title: Composition
topics.description: Build objects from other objects ("has-a") instead of inheriting ("is-a"). More flexible and testable than deep hierarchies.

topics.title: Nested and inner classes
topics.description: Static nested, inner, local and anonymous classes. Inner classes capture the outer instance, which matters for memory and serialization.

topics.title: Immutability
topics.description: Objects that never change after construction are thread-safe and easy to reason about. Records make immutable data classes trivial.

topics.title: Packages
topics.description: Namespaces that map to directories. Import rules, package-private visibility and naming with reverse domains.

topics.title: Modules
topics.description: The Java Platform Module System (module-info.java) declares exports and requires. Strong encapsulation beyond packages.

topics.title: Java project organization
topics.description: Standard layout: src/main/java, src/test/java, resources, and the build file. Layered packages by feature or by layer.

topics.title: Generics
topics.description: Type parameters for classes and methods give compile-time safety. Bounded types, wildcards and erasure are the interview core.

topics.title: Type safety
topics.description: Catch errors at compile time with generics, enums and final. Avoid raw types and unchecked casts.

topics.title: Collections overview
topics.description: The interfaces (Collection, List, Set, Map, Queue), their main implementations and the complexity of each operation.

topics.title: List
topics.description: Ordered, indexable, allows duplicates. ArrayList versus LinkedList, iteration, sublists and immutable lists.

topics.title: Set
topics.description: No duplicates. HashSet for speed, LinkedHashSet for order, TreeSet for sorting; correctness depends on equals and hashCode.

topics.title: Map
topics.description: Key-value store. HashMap, LinkedHashMap, TreeMap and the useful computeIfAbsent, merge and getOrDefault helpers.

topics.title: Queue and Deque
topics.description: FIFO queues, priority queues and double-ended deques. ArrayDeque replaces Stack and LinkedList for most uses.

topics.title: ArrayList and LinkedList
topics.description: ArrayList is a growable array; LinkedList is a doubly linked list. In practice ArrayList wins almost everywhere.

topics.title: HashSet and TreeSet
topics.description: Hash-based versus tree-based sets: O(1) versus O(log n), unordered versus sorted, plus navigation methods on TreeSet.

topics.title: HashMap and TreeMap
topics.description: HashMap internals (buckets, load factor, treeification) versus TreeMap (red-black tree with ordered navigation).

topics.title: equals and hashCode
topics.description: The contract: equal objects must have equal hash codes. Breaking it corrupts HashMap and HashSet behaviour.

topics.title: Comparable and Comparator
topics.description: Comparable defines natural order inside the class; Comparator defines external orders. Comparator.comparing chains keys.

topics.title: Lambdas
topics.description: Anonymous functions for functional interfaces. Syntax, captured variables must be effectively final, and method references.

topics.title: Functional interfaces
topics.description: Function, Predicate, Supplier, Consumer, BiFunction and primitive specialisations from java.util.function.

topics.title: Streams
topics.description: Declarative pipelines: source, intermediate operations, terminal operation. Laziness, collectors, and when not to use streams.

topics.title: Optional
topics.description: A container that may hold a value, replacing null returns. Use map, orElse, orElseThrow; avoid Optional fields and parameters.

topics.title: File I/O
topics.description: Reading and writing files with java.nio.file.Files and buffered streams, character encodings and try-with-resources.

topics.title: NIO
topics.description: Channels, buffers and selectors for non-blocking I/O, plus the Path and Files API that replaced java.io.File.

topics.title: Serialization
topics.description: Turning objects into bytes: Java native serialization and its pitfalls, versus JSON with Jackson or Gson.

topics.title: Date/time APIs
topics.description: java.time: LocalDate, LocalDateTime, ZonedDateTime, Instant, Duration and formatting. Legacy Date/Calendar are mutable and confusing.

topics.title: Records and sealed classes
topics.description: Records are concise immutable data carriers; sealed classes restrict which classes may extend a type, enabling exhaustive switches.

topics.title: Pattern matching and modern switch
topics.description: instanceof patterns, switch on types with record deconstruction, and guards. Java 21 makes these the idiomatic way to branch on data.

topics.title: Annotations
topics.description: Metadata on code read by compilers, frameworks and tools. Built-in ones like @Override, @FunctionalInterface, and defining your own with retention policies.

topics.title: Threads
topics.description: Creating threads with Thread or Runnable, lifecycle states, daemon threads, and why raw threads are rarely the right abstraction.

topics.title: Synchronization
topics.description: synchronized methods and blocks, intrinsic locks, visibility, and the happens-before relationship that makes data safe across threads.

topics.title: Locks
topics.description: ReentrantLock, ReadWriteLock and conditions offer tryLock, fairness and interruptibility beyond synchronized.

topics.title: Executors
topics.description: Thread pools via ExecutorService: fixed, cached, scheduled, and virtual-thread executors. Submit tasks, shut down cleanly.

topics.title: Futures
topics.description: Future represents an asynchronous result: get with timeout, cancel, and isDone. Callable returns values and throws.

topics.title: CompletableFuture
topics.description: Composable async pipelines: thenApply, thenCompose, thenCombine, exceptionally, allOf. Non-blocking callbacks instead of get.

topics.title: Concurrent collections
topics.description: ConcurrentHashMap, CopyOnWriteArrayList, BlockingQueue and friends give thread safety without global locks.

topics.title: volatile and atomics
topics.description: volatile guarantees visibility, not atomicity; AtomicInteger and friends provide lock-free compare-and-swap operations.

topics.title: Virtual threads
topics.description: Java 21 lightweight threads managed by the JVM. Millions can exist, making blocking code scale like async code.

topics.title: JVM memory
topics.description: Heap (young and old generations), stack per thread, metaspace, and the flags that size them. Where OutOfMemoryError comes from.

topics.title: Garbage collection
topics.description: Automatic memory reclamation: reachability, generational hypothesis, G1 and ZGC, and how to read GC logs.

topics.title: Performance
topics.description: Measure before optimising: JMH microbenchmarks, profilers, avoiding boxing, choosing collections, and JIT warm-up effects.

topics.title: Maven
topics.description: Build lifecycle, pom.xml coordinates, dependency scopes and plugins. The standard for most Java projects.

topics.title: Gradle
topics.description: Groovy or Kotlin DSL builds with tasks, incremental compilation and a daemon. Faster and more flexible than Maven.

topics.title: Testing and debugging
topics.description: JUnit 5, assertions, parameterised tests, Mockito mocks and using a debugger with breakpoints and watches.

topics.title: JDBC
topics.description: Connections, prepared statements, result sets and transactions against a database. Prepared statements prevent SQL injection.

topics.title: SOLID principles
topics.description: Single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation, dependency inversion. The vocabulary of design reviews.

topics.title: Design patterns
topics.description: Singleton, Factory, Builder, Strategy, Observer, Decorator and friends in Java, with their JDK examples.

title: JavaScript and TypeScript
description: Master web programming languages.

code.label: JavaScript, or TypeScript when the topic is TypeScript

topics.title: What is JavaScript?
topics.description: A high-level, interpreted programming language primarily used for web development to make pages interactive.

topics.title: Where is JavaScript used?
topics.description: JavaScript powers the modern web, running in the browser for UI, on servers via Node.js, and even in mobile/desktop apps.

topics.title: History and ECMAScript
topics.description: Created in 10 days in 1995, JavaScript was standardized as ECMAScript. Modern JS is based on ES6 (ES2015) and beyond.

topics.title: JavaScript runtime
topics.description: JavaScript runs inside a host: browsers and Node.js provide the engine (V8), the event loop and APIs. The language itself has no I/O.

topics.title: Browser execution
topics.description: Scripts load via script tags with defer or async, run on the main thread, and share it with rendering. Blocking the thread freezes the page.

topics.title: Variables and types
topics.description: let, const and var scoping, the seven primitive types plus object, typeof quirks and the difference between null and undefined.

topics.title: Operators and type coercion
topics.description: Implicit conversion rules for ==, +, and comparisons cause classic bugs. Use === and know the falsy values.

topics.title: Conditions and loops
topics.description: if/else, switch, ternaries, for, for...of, for...in, while, and the difference between iterating arrays and object keys.

topics.title: Functions and callbacks
topics.description: Function declarations, expressions, arrows, default parameters, rest/spread, and passing functions as callbacks.

topics.title: Destructuring, spread and rest
topics.description: Pull values out of arrays and objects, copy and merge with spread, collect the rest. Everyday syntax in modern codebases.

topics.title: Template literals and strings
topics.description: Backtick strings with interpolation and multi-line text, tagged templates, and the common string methods.

topics.title: Scope and hoisting
topics.description: Function scope for var, block scope for let/const, and how declarations are hoisted with a temporal dead zone.

topics.title: Closures
topics.description: A function remembers the variables of the scope where it was created. Used for private state, factories and memoisation.

topics.title: Lexical environment
topics.description: The internal record of identifiers and their outer references. Explains scope chain lookups and why closures work.

topics.title: this keyword
topics.description: this depends on how a function is called: method, plain call, constructor, or explicit binding. Arrow functions inherit it.

topics.title: call, apply, bind
topics.description: Explicitly set this: call and apply invoke immediately with a this and arguments; bind returns a new function.

topics.title: Arrow functions
topics.description: Concise syntax with lexical this, no arguments object and no prototype. Not suitable as methods or constructors.

topics.title: Objects
topics.description: Property access, computed keys, shorthand, destructuring, spread, Object.keys/entries and property descriptors.

topics.title: Arrays
topics.description: The essential methods: map, filter, reduce, find, some, every, sort (with comparator), flat, and mutating versus non-mutating ones.

topics.title: Prototypes
topics.description: Objects delegate to a prototype chain. Understand __proto__ versus prototype, Object.create and how inheritance actually works.

topics.title: Classes
topics.description: Syntax over prototypes: constructor, methods, getters, static members, private fields (#) and extends/super.

topics.title: DOM manipulation
topics.description: Select, create, modify and remove elements; classList, dataset, and batching changes to limit reflows.

topics.title: Events
topics.description: addEventListener, bubbling and capturing, delegation, preventDefault and stopPropagation, and custom events.

topics.title: Browser APIs
topics.description: fetch, timers, history, geolocation, IntersectionObserver, Web Workers and the Notification API: the platform beyond the DOM.

topics.title: Browser storage
topics.description: localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB and cookies: capacity, persistence, synchronous versus async, and security limits.

topics.title: Cookies and security
topics.description: Cookie attributes (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite), the same-origin policy, CORS, XSS and CSRF and how to prevent them.

topics.title: Map, Set, WeakMap
topics.description: Keyed collections with any key type, insertion order and size. WeakMap and WeakSet hold keys weakly for metadata without leaks.

topics.title: Regular expressions
topics.description: Patterns for matching and replacing text: character classes, quantifiers, groups, flags and the methods that use them.

topics.title: Debounce and throttle
topics.description: Limit how often expensive handlers run: debounce waits for a pause, throttle allows one call per interval.

topics.title: Web Workers
topics.description: Run CPU-heavy work off the main thread with message passing. No DOM access, structured clone for data, transferables for speed.

topics.title: Call stack
topics.description: Synchronous code runs on one call stack. Understanding it explains stack traces, recursion limits and why long tasks block.

topics.title: Event loop
topics.description: The loop that moves callbacks from queues to the empty call stack. Explains ordering of timers, promises and rendering.

topics.title: Tasks and microtasks
topics.description: Promise callbacks (microtasks) run before the next task (timers, I/O). Predicting output order is a favourite interview question.

topics.title: Promises
topics.description: Represent eventual results with then/catch/finally and chaining. Combinators: all, allSettled, race, any.

topics.title: async/await
topics.description: Syntactic sugar over promises: await pauses the async function, try/catch handles rejections, and parallelism needs Promise.all.

topics.title: Fetch
topics.description: The modern HTTP API: Request, Response, headers, JSON bodies, AbortController for cancellation, and the fact that 404 does not reject.

topics.title: HTTP requests
topics.description: Methods, status codes, headers, query strings and bodies. Idempotency, caching headers and content negotiation from the client side.

topics.title: Error handling
topics.description: try/catch with async code, custom Error subclasses, error causes, and global handlers for uncaught errors and rejections.

topics.title: Modules
topics.description: ES modules with import/export, default versus named exports, live bindings, and how they differ from CommonJS require.

topics.title: Package management
topics.description: npm and package.json: dependencies, devDependencies, semver ranges, lockfiles and scripts.

topics.title: Iterators and generators
topics.description: The iteration protocol behind for...of, and generator functions that produce values lazily with yield.

topics.title: Functional programming
topics.description: Pure functions, immutability, composition, currying and avoiding shared state. Makes code testable and predictable.

topics.title: Memory management
topics.description: Garbage collection by reachability, common leak sources (timers, listeners, closures, detached DOM) and DevTools memory profiling.

topics.title: Performance
topics.description: Measure with Performance API and DevTools; reduce work on the main thread, debounce input, virtualise long lists, avoid layout thrashing.

topics.title: Testing
topics.description: Unit tests with Jest or Vitest, mocking modules and timers, and DOM testing with Testing Library.

topics.title: Currying and composition
topics.description: Build functions from smaller ones: compose/pipe, partial application, point-free style, and when it hurts readability.

topics.title: TypeScript setup
topics.description: Install, tsconfig.json, compile with tsc or bundlers, and understand that types vanish at runtime.

topics.title: Types and strict mode
topics.description: Primitive types, arrays, tuples, any versus unknown, and why strictNullChecks catches whole classes of bugs.

topics.title: Interfaces
topics.description: Describe object shapes; support optional and readonly properties, extension and declaration merging.

topics.title: Aliases
topics.description: type aliases name any type, including unions and primitives. Know when to use type versus interface.

topics.title: Unions and intersections
topics.description: A | B accepts either; A & B requires both. Discriminated unions with a literal tag give safe exhaustive handling.

topics.title: Enums and literal types
topics.description: String enums, const enums and literal unions. Literal unions are usually the simpler, safer choice.

topics.title: Generics
topics.description: Type parameters for reusable, type-safe functions and classes. Constraints with extends and defaults.

topics.title: Narrowing and type guards
topics.description: typeof, instanceof, in, equality and user-defined guards (x is T) let the compiler refine types in branches.

topics.title: Utility types
topics.description: Partial, Required, Pick, Omit, Record, ReturnType, Parameters and friends transform existing types.

topics.title: Mapped types
topics.description: Build types by iterating over keys: { [K in keyof T]: ... } with modifiers and key remapping.

topics.title: Conditional types
topics.description: T extends U ? X : Y with inference via infer. Distributive behaviour over unions.

topics.title: Type-safe APIs
topics.description: End-to-end typing: validate inputs with zod, derive types from schemas, and share types between client and server.

topics.title: Advanced TS architecture
topics.description: Project references, path aliases, declaration files, strictness migration and library typing with declaration maps.

title: React and Next.js
description: Master frontend development.

topics.title: What is React?
topics.description: An absolute beginner's introduction to React, explaining what it is and why it matters.

topics.title: Why use React?
topics.description: Understanding the real-world applications and use cases of React in modern engineering.

topics.title: History and Ecosystem
topics.description: A brief look at how React evolved and where it fits in the broader ecosystem today.

topics.title: HTML
topics.description: Semantic elements, document structure, forms and accessibility attributes. Good HTML is the foundation React renders into.

topics.title: CSS
topics.description: Selectors, the box model, flexbox, grid, specificity and the cascade. Plus how React apps usually scope styles.

topics.title: Responsive design
topics.description: Mobile-first layouts with media queries, fluid units, container queries and responsive images.

topics.title: Accessibility
topics.description: Keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA roles, colour contrast and screen reader testing.

topics.title: JSX
topics.description: HTML-like syntax that compiles to createElement calls. Expressions in braces, className, fragments and the rules of JSX.

topics.title: Components
topics.description: Function components as the unit of UI: composition, props in, elements out, and how React calls them during rendering.

topics.title: Props
topics.description: Read-only inputs passed from parent to child. Default values, destructuring, passing callbacks, and prop drilling.

topics.title: Rendering
topics.description: Rendering, committing and re-rendering. What triggers a render, why renders must be pure, and Strict Mode double rendering.

topics.title: State
topics.description: useState holds values across renders. Updates are batched and asynchronous; use functional updates when the new value depends on the old.

topics.title: Events
topics.description: Synthetic events, handler naming, passing arguments, preventDefault and the difference from DOM listeners.

topics.title: Lists
topics.description: Render arrays with map and give each item a stable key so React can reconcile efficiently. Index keys cause bugs with reordering.

topics.title: Conditional rendering
topics.description: Ternaries, && guards, early returns and switching components. Watch for 0 rendering with &&.

topics.title: Forms
topics.description: Controlled inputs tie value to state; uncontrolled use refs. Handling submit, multiple fields and select/checkbox specifics.

topics.title: Validation
topics.description: Client-side validation with libraries like react-hook-form and zod, showing errors, and never trusting the client alone.

topics.title: useState
topics.description: Local state hook: lazy initialisers, updating objects and arrays immutably, and when to split versus merge state.

topics.title: useEffect
topics.description: Synchronise with external systems after render. Dependencies, cleanup, and the common mistakes: missing deps, effects for derived state.

topics.title: useRef
topics.description: A mutable box that persists across renders without causing re-renders. DOM access, timers, previous values.

topics.title: Context API
topics.description: Share values through the tree without props. Providers, useContext, and splitting contexts to limit re-renders.

topics.title: Custom hooks
topics.description: Extract reusable stateful logic into use* functions. They share logic, not state, and follow the rules of hooks.

topics.title: Component composition
topics.description: Compose behaviour with children, render props and slots rather than deep inheritance or prop drilling.

topics.title: State management
topics.description: Local state first, then lifted state, context, or stores (Zustand, Redux Toolkit). Choose based on sharing scope and update frequency.

topics.title: Server-state caching
topics.description: Server data has different needs: caching, refetching, deduplication and mutations. React Query and SWR handle this.

topics.title: useReducer
topics.description: Manage complex state transitions with a reducer function and dispatched actions. Pairs with context for small stores.

topics.title: useMemo and useCallback
topics.description: Cache expensive computations and function identities between renders. Overuse adds cost; measure first.

topics.title: Routing and navigation
topics.description: Client-side routing with React Router or Next.js: nested routes, params, loaders, links and programmatic navigation.

topics.title: Data fetching
topics.description: Fetching in effects versus loaders versus server components. Loading, error and race-condition handling.

topics.title: React rendering
topics.description: Fiber, the virtual DOM, concurrent rendering and transitions. How React interrupts and prioritises work.

topics.title: Reconciliation
topics.description: How React diffs element trees: type comparison, keys, and why changing element type remounts the subtree.

topics.title: Performance
topics.description: Profile first. Then memo, useMemo, useCallback, virtualisation, code splitting and avoiding unnecessary context updates.

topics.title: Testing
topics.description: Testing Library for components, user-event for interactions, mocking network with MSW, and end-to-end tests with Playwright.

topics.title: Error boundaries
topics.description: Class components that catch render errors below them and show a fallback. Do not catch event handler or async errors.

topics.title: Suspense and streaming
topics.description: Suspense shows fallbacks while children load data or code. With server rendering it enables streaming HTML.

topics.title: Portals and refs forwarding
topics.description: Portals render children into another DOM node for modals and tooltips; forwardRef exposes DOM nodes to parents.

topics.title: App Router
topics.description: File-system routing in the app directory with layouts, server components by default and streaming.

topics.title: Routing conventions
topics.description: page, layout, loading, error, not-found, route groups, dynamic and catch-all segments, parallel and intercepting routes.

topics.title: Server Components
topics.description: Render on the server, ship no JavaScript, access data directly. Cannot use state or effects.

topics.title: Client Components
topics.description: Marked with "use client". Needed for interactivity, browser APIs and hooks. Keep them small and at the leaves.

topics.title: Layouts
topics.description: Shared UI that persists across navigations and keeps state. Root layout, nested layouts and templates.

topics.title: Loading states
topics.description: loading.tsx wraps the segment in Suspense for instant loading UI and streaming. Granular Suspense for slow parts.

topics.title: Error handling
topics.description: error.tsx boundaries per segment with reset, global-error for the root, and not-found handling.

topics.title: Route handlers
topics.description: route.ts files export GET, POST and other handlers using Web Request and Response. Replace API routes.

topics.title: Server actions
topics.description: Functions marked "use server" callable from forms and client code. Mutations without API routes, with revalidation.

topics.title: Data access
topics.description: Fetch directly in server components, use a data layer (Drizzle/Prisma), and avoid leaking secrets to the client.

topics.title: Caching
topics.description: Request memoisation, the data cache, full route cache and router cache. Know what is cached by default in your Next version.

topics.title: Revalidation
topics.description: Time-based (revalidate) and on-demand (revalidatePath, revalidateTag) invalidation to keep static pages fresh.

topics.title: Rendering strategies
topics.description: Static, dynamic and streaming rendering; partial prerendering; choosing per route based on data freshness needs.

topics.title: Authentication
topics.description: Sessions or JWTs with Auth.js or a provider, protecting routes in layouts, middleware and the data layer.

topics.title: Authorization
topics.description: What a user may do: roles, ownership checks, and enforcing rules in server actions and route handlers, never only in the UI.

topics.title: Database integration
topics.description: Connecting Postgres via an ORM, connection pooling in serverless, migrations, and keeping queries in the server layer.

topics.title: Middleware
topics.description: Runs before a request completes: redirects, rewrites, auth checks, A/B testing, at the edge with limited APIs.

topics.title: Styling approaches
topics.description: CSS Modules, Tailwind, CSS-in-JS and their fit with server components. Tailwind and Modules work without client JavaScript.

topics.title: Internationalization
topics.description: Locale routing, message catalogues, formatting dates and numbers with Intl, and right-to-left support.

topics.title: SEO
topics.description: Server rendering, metadata, canonical URLs, structured data, sitemaps and robots. Core Web Vitals influence ranking.

topics.title: Metadata
topics.description: The metadata export and generateMetadata for titles, descriptions, Open Graph and Twitter cards, plus dynamic OG images.

topics.title: Images
topics.description: next/image optimises size, format and loading. Sizes, priority, remote patterns and layout shift prevention.

topics.title: Production performance budgets
topics.description: Measure Core Web Vitals, cut JavaScript with server components, stream, cache, and optimise fonts and images.

topics.title: Deployment
topics.description: Deploying to Vercel or a Node host, environment variables, build output, and preview environments.

topics.title: Observability
topics.description: Logging, error tracking (Sentry), analytics and Web Vitals reporting so you know what happens in production.

topics.title: Security
topics.description: CSP headers, input validation, CSRF-safe server actions, secret handling, and dependency updates.

topics.title: Production-grade projects
topics.description: Bring it together: a full app with auth, database, caching, tests, CI and monitoring, deployed and documented.

title: Node.js and Backend Development
description: Master backend development with Node.

topics.title: What is Node.js?
topics.description: An absolute beginner's introduction to Node.js, explaining what it is and why it matters.

topics.title: Why use Node.js?
topics.description: Understanding the real-world applications and use cases of Node.js in modern engineering.

topics.title: History and Ecosystem
topics.description: A brief look at how Node.js evolved and where it fits in the broader ecosystem today.

topics.title: Backend architecture
topics.description: How requests flow from client to server to database and back. Layers (routing, service, data), statelessness and horizontal scaling.

topics.title: HTTP fundamentals
topics.description: Requests and responses, methods, status codes, headers, cookies, keep-alive and HTTP/2 basics from the server perspective.

topics.title: Node.js runtime
topics.description: V8 plus libuv: single-threaded JavaScript with an event loop and a thread pool for I/O. Great for I/O-bound services.

topics.title: Modules and npm
topics.description: CommonJS versus ES modules in Node, package.json exports, scripts, and dependency management.

topics.title: Event loop
topics.description: Phases: timers, pending callbacks, poll, check, close. process.nextTick and microtasks run between phases.

topics.title: Asynchronous I/O
topics.description: Callbacks, promises and async/await for file, network and database operations. Promisify legacy APIs.

topics.title: Streams
topics.description: Readable, Writable, Duplex and Transform streams process data in chunks with backpressure. pipeline handles errors and cleanup.

topics.title: Buffers
topics.description: Raw binary data outside the V8 heap. Encodings, slicing, concatenation and converting to and from strings.

topics.title: Express/Fastify
topics.description: Minimal web frameworks: app setup, routing, middleware chain and plugins. Fastify adds schema validation and speed.

topics.title: Routing
topics.description: Route params, query strings, routers per resource, and ordering rules. RESTful path design.

topics.title: Middleware
topics.description: Functions that see request and response and call next. Body parsing, CORS, auth, logging and error handlers.

topics.title: Request validation
topics.description: Validate bodies, params and queries with zod or JSON Schema before handlers run. Return 400 with useful details.

topics.title: Error handling
topics.description: Central error middleware, custom error classes with status codes, and never leaking stack traces to clients.

topics.title: Logging
topics.description: Structured JSON logs with pino or winston, request ids, log levels and correlation across services.

topics.title: REST APIs
topics.description: Resource-oriented URLs, proper methods and status codes, consistent response envelopes and error formats.

topics.title: Pagination
topics.description: Offset and cursor pagination, limits, total counts and stable ordering. Cursors scale better for large tables.

topics.title: Filtering
topics.description: Query parameters for filters, sorting and field selection, validated and mapped safely to database queries.

topics.title: Versioning
topics.description: URL, header or media-type versioning; deprecation policies and supporting two versions during migration.

topics.title: GraphQL
topics.description: Schema-first APIs where clients ask for exactly the fields they need. Resolvers, the N+1 problem and DataLoader.

topics.title: gRPC
topics.description: Binary RPC over HTTP/2 with protobuf contracts. Fast service-to-service calls with streaming.

topics.title: SQL integration
topics.description: Connecting with pg or mysql2, parameterised queries, pooling, and ORMs versus query builders.

topics.title: Transactions
topics.description: Group writes so they succeed or fail together. BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, isolation, retries on serialization failure.

subtopics.title: Using a client from the pool

topics.title: Data access
topics.description: Repository or DAL pattern: keep queries in one place, return domain objects, and make them testable.

topics.title: Authentication
topics.description: Verifying identity: password login, sessions or tokens, and third-party providers. Rate limit and log attempts.

topics.title: Authorization
topics.description: Roles, permissions and resource ownership checked on every request in middleware and services.

topics.title: Sessions
topics.description: Server-side session stores (Redis), cookie settings, expiry and rotation on privilege change.

topics.title: JWT
topics.description: Signed tokens carrying claims. Short-lived access tokens, refresh tokens, algorithm choice and revocation limits.

topics.title: OAuth
topics.description: Delegated authorization with authorization code + PKCE, scopes, tokens and OpenID Connect for identity.

topics.title: Password hashing
topics.description: bcrypt, scrypt or argon2 with salts and tuned cost. Never store or log plain passwords.

topics.title: Secret management
topics.description: Environment variables, secret managers, rotation, and keeping secrets out of git and logs.

topics.title: ORMs: Prisma and Drizzle
topics.description: Type-safe database access: schema definition, migrations, query builders and where raw SQL still wins.

topics.title: Uploads
topics.description: Multipart parsing with multer or busboy, size limits, type checks and streaming to storage instead of buffering.

topics.title: Object storage
topics.description: S3-compatible storage for files: buckets, keys, presigned URLs for direct upload and download, lifecycle rules.

topics.title: Email
topics.description: Transactional email via providers (SES, Resend), templates, deliverability (SPF, DKIM), and queueing sends.

topics.title: Notifications
topics.description: Push, in-app and SMS notifications: fan-out, preferences, batching and idempotency.

topics.title: Redis
topics.description: In-memory data store for caching, sessions, rate limits, queues and pub/sub. Data structures and expiry.

topics.title: Caching
topics.description: Cache-aside, TTLs, invalidation and stampede protection. Cache at the right layer: HTTP, application or database.

topics.title: Queues
topics.description: Decouple work with message queues (BullMQ, RabbitMQ, SQS): producers, consumers, retries and dead-letter queues.

topics.title: Background jobs
topics.description: Scheduled and delayed work: cron jobs, workers, job status tracking and graceful shutdown of workers.

topics.title: WebSockets
topics.description: Persistent bidirectional connections with ws or Socket.IO: handshake, rooms, heartbeats and scaling with an adapter.

topics.title: Real-time systems
topics.description: Choosing between WebSockets, SSE and polling; presence, ordering and delivery guarantees.

topics.title: Worker threads and clustering
topics.description: Use CPU cores: cluster forks processes; worker_threads share memory for CPU-bound tasks.

topics.title: Rate limiting
topics.description: Token bucket, sliding window and fixed window limits per user or IP, stored in Redis, with proper 429 responses.

topics.title: API security
topics.description: Input validation, output encoding, CORS, helmet headers, authentication on every route and least privilege.

topics.title: Abuse prevention
topics.description: Bot detection, captchas, anomaly detection, blocking, and protecting expensive endpoints.

topics.title: Testing
topics.description: Unit tests for services, integration tests with a test database, and API tests with supertest.

topics.title: Documentation
topics.description: OpenAPI specs, generated docs, examples and keeping docs in sync with code.

topics.title: Debugging
topics.description: Node inspector, logging, reproducing issues, and diagnosing memory leaks and event loop blocks.

topics.title: Modular monoliths
topics.description: One deployable with strict module boundaries. Most teams should start here and split later.

topics.title: Microservices
topics.description: Independent services with their own data, communicating over APIs or events. Costs: distributed failures, consistency, ops.

topics.title: Messaging
topics.description: Event-driven communication: topics, consumers, ordering, idempotency and schema evolution.

topics.title: Reliability
topics.description: Health checks, graceful shutdown, timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers and idempotent endpoints.

topics.title: Scalability
topics.description: Horizontal scaling with load balancers, stateless instances, database read replicas and caching layers.

topics.title: Performance
topics.description: Profiling Node, keeping the event loop free, connection pooling, compression, and measuring p95 latency.

topics.title: Docker
topics.description: Containerising Node: small base images, multi-stage builds, non-root users, .dockerignore and health checks.

topics.title: CI/CD
topics.description: Pipelines that lint, test, build images and deploy with approvals and rollbacks.

topics.title: Production deployment
topics.description: Process managers, environment config, zero-downtime restarts, logs and secrets in real hosting.

topics.title: End-to-end backend projects
topics.description: Build a complete API: auth, CRUD, validation, tests, docs, Docker and deployment, with monitoring.

topics.title: Graceful shutdown
topics.description: Handle SIGTERM: stop accepting connections, finish in-flight requests, close pools, then exit within the platform timeout.

topics.title: TypeScript in Node
topics.description: Run TS with tsx or compile with tsc, strict config, ESM output, path aliases and typed environment variables.

title: SQL, PostgreSQL and MySQL
description: Master relational databases.

topics.title: What is SQL?
topics.description: An absolute beginner's introduction to SQL, explaining what it is and why it matters.

topics.title: Why use SQL?
topics.description: Understanding the real-world applications and use cases of SQL in modern engineering.

topics.title: History and Ecosystem
topics.description: A brief look at how SQL evolved and where it fits in the broader ecosystem today.

topics.title: Relational database fundamentals
topics.description: Tables of rows and columns related by keys. The relational model, declarative queries and why databases beat files.

topics.title: Tables
topics.description: CREATE TABLE with columns, defaults, NOT NULL and identity columns; ALTER and DROP with care.

topics.title: Schemas
topics.description: Namespaces inside a database for organising tables and permissions. search_path and qualified names.

topics.title: Types
topics.description: Numeric, text, boolean, date/time, JSON, arrays and UUID. Choosing types affects storage, correctness and indexing.

topics.title: Keys
topics.description: Primary keys identify rows; foreign keys enforce relationships; natural versus surrogate keys.

topics.title: Constraints
topics.description: NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, FOREIGN KEY and exclusion constraints keep bad data out at the source.

topics.title: SELECT
topics.description: Projection, aliases, expressions, DISTINCT, LIMIT/OFFSET and ordering. The starting point of every query.

topics.title: INSERT
topics.description: Single and multi-row inserts, RETURNING, defaults and upsert with ON CONFLICT.

topics.title: UPDATE
topics.description: Set columns with expressions, update from joins, and always write the WHERE clause first.

topics.title: DELETE
topics.description: Remove rows by condition, delete using joins, and TRUNCATE for whole tables. Soft deletes as an alternative.

topics.title: WHERE
topics.description: Filtering with comparisons, BETWEEN, IN, LIKE, IS NULL and boolean logic. NULL comparisons need special care.

topics.title: ORDER BY
topics.description: Sort by columns or expressions, ascending or descending, with NULLS FIRST/LAST, and why unsorted results are unordered.

topics.title: GROUP BY
topics.description: Aggregate rows into groups with COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX. Every non-aggregated column must be grouped.

topics.title: HAVING
topics.description: Filter groups after aggregation, unlike WHERE which filters rows before it.

topics.title: Aggregate and scalar functions
topics.description: COUNT, SUM, AVG with FILTER, string functions, date arithmetic and COALESCE/NULLIF for null handling.

topics.title: Set operations
topics.description: UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT and EXCEPT combine result sets. UNION removes duplicates and costs more.

topics.title: INNER JOIN
topics.description: Rows with matching keys in both tables. The default join; understand join conditions versus filters.

topics.title: LEFT JOIN
topics.description: All rows from the left table with NULLs where the right has no match. Used for "customers without orders" queries.

topics.title: RIGHT JOIN
topics.description: Mirror of LEFT JOIN. Rarely needed; rewrite as LEFT JOIN by swapping tables for readability.

topics.title: FULL JOIN
topics.description: All rows from both sides, NULL-filled where unmatched. Useful for reconciliations and diffs.

topics.title: Subqueries
topics.description: Queries inside queries: scalar, IN/EXISTS, correlated subqueries and derived tables in FROM.

topics.title: CTEs
topics.description: WITH clauses name intermediate results for readability, and recursive CTEs walk hierarchies.

topics.title: Window functions
topics.description: Aggregates over a window of rows without collapsing them: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG, LEAD, running totals.

topics.title: EXISTS, IN and anti-joins
topics.description: Semi-joins and anti-joins express "has any" and "has none". Know which forms are NULL-safe and index-friendly.

topics.title: JSON in SQL
topics.description: Store and query semi-structured data: JSONB operators, indexing, extracting fields and when to normalise instead.

topics.title: Schema design
topics.description: Model entities and relationships, pick keys, avoid nullable sprawl, and design for the queries you will run.

topics.title: Relationships
topics.description: One-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many and self-references, with referential integrity and cascade behaviour.

topics.title: Normalization
topics.description: 1NF through 3NF (and BCNF) remove redundancy and update anomalies. Denormalise deliberately for read performance.

topics.title: Indexes
topics.description: B-tree indexes speed lookups and sorts at the cost of writes and space. Composite indexes, covering indexes and selectivity.

topics.title: Query execution plans
topics.description: EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows scans, joins, estimated versus actual rows and where time goes.

topics.title: Full-text search
topics.description: tsvector and tsquery, GIN indexes, ranking, and when to move to a dedicated search engine.

topics.title: Transactions
topics.description: BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK and savepoints. All-or-nothing groups of statements.

topics.title: ACID
topics.description: Atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability: the guarantees that make transactions trustworthy.

topics.title: Isolation levels
topics.description: Read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read, serializable, and the anomalies each allows.

topics.title: Locking
topics.description: Row and table locks, SELECT FOR UPDATE, lock queues and how MVCC lets readers avoid blocking writers.

topics.title: Deadlocks
topics.description: Two transactions waiting on each other. Databases detect and abort one; prevent by consistent lock ordering.

topics.title: Concurrency
topics.description: Lost updates, optimistic versus pessimistic control, version columns and idempotent writes.

topics.title: Views
topics.description: Saved queries acting as virtual tables. Simplify access, enforce security, and materialised views cache results.

topics.title: Triggers
topics.description: Functions that fire on INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE. Useful for audit logs; dangerous when they hide logic.

topics.title: Stored procedures
