topics.description: Server-side routines in PL/pgSQL or SQL. Encapsulate logic near data; weigh against application-side code.

topics.title: Migrations
topics.description: Versioned schema changes applied in order by tools (Drizzle, Flyway, Prisma). Forward-only, reviewed, and safe for live data.

topics.title: Schema evolution
topics.description: Changing schemas without downtime: expand-contract, dual writes, and backward-compatible steps.

topics.title: PostgreSQL-specific features
topics.description: JSONB, arrays, full-text search, CTE power, extensions (PostGIS, pg_trgm), and rich index types.

topics.title: MySQL-specific features
topics.description: InnoDB engine, clustered primary keys, auto_increment, and the syntax and behaviour differences from Postgres.

topics.title: Partitioning
topics.description: Split a large table into partitions by range, list or hash to speed queries and maintenance.

topics.title: Replication
topics.description: Streaming replication for standbys, logical replication for selective sync, and replication lag.

topics.title: High availability
topics.description: Failover, connection routing, backups and testing recovery. Managed services automate most of it.

topics.title: Backup
topics.description: Logical dumps (pg_dump) versus physical base backups with WAL archiving for point-in-time recovery.

topics.title: Recovery
topics.description: Restoring dumps, replaying WAL, and rehearsing disaster scenarios with documented runbooks.

topics.title: Pooling
topics.description: Connection poolers (PgBouncer) and application pools limit connections and protect the database.

topics.title: Security
topics.description: Roles and grants, least privilege, row-level security, TLS and auditing.

topics.title: Query optimization
topics.description: Find slow queries with pg_stat_statements, fix with indexes, rewrites, and avoiding N+1 patterns.

topics.title: Practical database projects
topics.description: Design and build a schema for a real domain, seed it, write reports with window functions and tune with EXPLAIN.

title: High-Level System Design (HLD)
description: Master scalable system architectures.

topics.title: What is System Design?
topics.description: An absolute beginner's introduction to System Design, explaining what it is and why it matters.

topics.title: Why use System Design?
topics.description: Understanding the real-world applications and use cases of System Design in modern engineering.

topics.title: History and Ecosystem
topics.description: A brief look at how System Design evolved and where it fits in the broader ecosystem today.

topics.title: Requirements and capacity estimation
topics.description: Clarify functional and non-functional requirements, then estimate users, QPS, storage and bandwidth with back-of-envelope maths.

topics.title: Networking
topics.description: TCP versus UDP, latency versus bandwidth, TLS handshakes, and how many round trips a request costs.

topics.title: DNS
topics.description: Resolves names to IPs through recursive and authoritative servers with TTL caching. Used for routing and failover.

topics.title: HTTP
topics.description: Request semantics, caching headers, keep-alive, HTTP/2 multiplexing and HTTP/3 over QUIC.

topics.title: Reverse proxies
topics.description: Front servers that terminate TLS, route, cache, compress and shield backends. Nginx, Envoy, API gateways.

topics.title: Load balancing
topics.description: Distribute traffic across instances: L4 versus L7, algorithms, health checks, sticky sessions and global load balancing.

topics.title: CDNs
topics.description: Edge caches near users for static and cacheable dynamic content. Cache keys, TTLs, invalidation and origin shielding.

topics.title: Caching
topics.description: Layers (client, CDN, application, database), cache-aside and write-through, eviction policies and hit-rate thinking.

topics.title: Cache invalidation
topics.description: Keeping caches correct: TTLs, event-driven invalidation, versioned keys and avoiding stale reads after writes.

topics.title: SQL/NoSQL selection
topics.description: Relational for transactions and joins; document, key-value, wide-column and graph stores for specific access patterns.

topics.title: Data modeling
topics.description: Model for the queries: keys, denormalisation, and access-pattern-first design in NoSQL.

topics.title: Replication
topics.description: Copies of data for availability and read scaling. Leader-follower, multi-leader and leaderless, with lag and conflicts.

topics.title: Partitioning
topics.description: Splitting data across nodes by key range or hash. Rebalancing, hotspots and secondary indexes across partitions.

topics.title: Sharding
topics.description: Horizontal partitioning of a database across servers: shard keys, routing, cross-shard queries and resharding.

topics.title: Consistent hashing
topics.description: Place nodes and keys on a ring so adding or removing a node moves only nearby keys. Virtual nodes balance load.

topics.title: Distributed ID generation
topics.description: Unique ids without a single point of contention: UUIDs, Snowflake ids, database ranges and their ordering properties.

topics.title: Bloom filters
topics.description: Probabilistic membership test with no false negatives and tunable false positives, in tiny memory.

topics.title: Consistency
topics.description: Strong, eventual and causal consistency; linearizability; and what users actually notice.

topics.title: Availability
topics.description: Measured in nines; achieved with redundancy, failover, health checks and graceful degradation.

topics.title: CAP tradeoffs
topics.description: Under partition you choose consistency or availability. PACELC adds the latency trade-off when there is no partition.

topics.title: Queues
topics.description: Message queues decouple producers and consumers, buffer bursts and enable retries. Delivery semantics matter.

topics.title: Pub/sub
topics.description: Publishers emit to topics; many subscribers receive. Fan-out, topic design and subscriber independence.

topics.title: Event-driven systems
topics.description: Services react to events. Event sourcing, CQRS, sagas and eventual consistency across services.

topics.title: Object storage
topics.description: S3-style storage for blobs: durability, consistency, presigned URLs, versioning and cost tiers.

topics.title: Search
topics.description: Inverted indexes, relevance ranking, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, and syncing search with the primary store.

topics.title: API design: REST, GraphQL, gRPC
topics.description: Choosing an API style by clients and constraints: caching, flexibility, performance and tooling.

topics.title: Real-time delivery: WebSockets, SSE, polling
topics.description: Push versus pull for live updates, connection costs, scaling long-lived connections and fallbacks.

topics.title: Message brokers: Kafka
topics.description: Partitioned, replicated logs with consumer groups. Retention, offsets, ordering per partition and exactly-once processing.

topics.title: Authentication
topics.description: Identity at scale: sessions versus JWTs, SSO, token refresh and centralised identity providers.

topics.title: Authorization
topics.description: Permission models (RBAC, ABAC), policy engines and enforcing at gateway and service.

topics.title: Rate limiting
topics.description: Protect services with per-client limits at the gateway, distributed counters and clear responses.

topics.title: Observability
topics.description: Logs, metrics and traces plus dashboards and alerts. Correlation ids tie a request across services.

topics.title: Reliability
topics.description: Timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers, bulkheads and idempotency to survive partial failure.

topics.title: Failure recovery
topics.description: Backups, replicas, failover automation, chaos testing and post-incident reviews.

topics.title: Multi-region systems
topics.description: Serving users from several regions: data replication, latency routing, failover and consistency across regions.

topics.title: Scalability
topics.description: Vertical versus horizontal, stateless tiers, sharding, caching and async processing as the standard levers.

topics.title: Performance
topics.description: Latency budgets, percentiles, hot paths, connection reuse and measuring under realistic load.

topics.title: Cost optimization
topics.description: Right-sizing, autoscaling, storage tiers, caching to cut compute and egress, and measuring cost per request.

topics.title: URL shortener design
topics.description: Generate short keys, redirect fast, and count clicks at scale. Covers key generation, storage, caching and analytics.

topics.title: Chat application design
topics.description: Real-time messaging with WebSockets, message storage, delivery receipts, presence and group fan-out.

topics.title: News feed design
topics.description: Generate personalised feeds: fan-out on write versus read, ranking, caching and celebrity users.

topics.title: Notification system design
topics.description: Multi-channel notifications with templates, preferences, rate limits, retries and deduplication.

topics.title: E-commerce design
topics.description: Catalog, cart, checkout, inventory and orders with consistency where money moves and caching where it does not.

topics.title: Food delivery design
topics.description: Restaurants, orders, drivers and real-time location. Matching, ETA, and geospatial queries.

topics.title: Video streaming design
topics.description: Upload, transcode to multiple bitrates, store, and serve via CDN with adaptive streaming.

topics.title: Payment system design
topics.description: Idempotent payment APIs, ledger with double-entry, reconciliation with providers and strict consistency.

topics.title: Ride-sharing design
topics.description: Riders and drivers with matching, surge pricing, trip state and live location at scale.

topics.title: Web crawler design
topics.description: Politeness, URL frontier, deduplication, robots.txt and distributed fetching with storage of pages.

topics.title: Typeahead search design
topics.description: Prefix suggestions in milliseconds: tries with precomputed top-k, caching and data pipelines updating frequencies.

topics.title: Google Drive design
topics.description: File sync with chunking, deduplication, metadata database, conflict handling and change notifications.

title: Low-Level System Design (LLD)
description: Master object-oriented design and design patterns.

topics.title: What is Low-Level Design?
topics.description: An absolute beginner's introduction to Low-Level Design, explaining what it is and why it matters.

topics.title: Why use Low-Level Design?
topics.description: Understanding the real-world applications and use cases of Low-Level Design in modern engineering.

topics.title: History and Ecosystem
topics.description: A brief look at how Low-Level Design evolved and where it fits in the broader ecosystem today.

topics.title: OOP principles
topics.description: Encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance and polymorphism as design tools, and how they show up in a low-level design interview.

topics.title: SOLID
topics.description: Five principles for maintainable object design, each with a concrete refactoring you can show in an interview.

topics.title: UML class diagrams
topics.description: Classes, attributes, methods and relationships (association, aggregation, composition, inheritance) with multiplicities.

topics.title: Sequence diagrams
topics.description: Show object interactions over time: lifelines, messages, activations and alt/loop fragments.

topics.title: State diagrams
topics.description: States, transitions, guards and actions for objects with lifecycles such as orders or connections.

topics.title: Interfaces
topics.description: Define contracts between components so implementations can vary and tests can substitute fakes.

topics.title: Composition
topics.description: Assemble behaviour from parts with delegation; favour it over inheritance hierarchies.

topics.title: Cohesion and coupling
topics.description: High cohesion inside modules, low coupling between them. Recognise and fix feature envy and shotgun surgery.

topics.title: Domain modeling
topics.description: Entities, value objects, aggregates and invariants. Model the business language, not the database.

topics.title: Object responsibilities
topics.description: Assign responsibilities with GRASP: information expert, creator, controller, low coupling.

topics.title: Creational patterns overview
topics.description: Singleton, Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder and Prototype: controlling how objects are created.

topics.title: Structural patterns overview
topics.description: Adapter, Decorator, Facade, Proxy, Composite, Bridge, Flyweight: composing objects into larger structures.

topics.title: Behavioral patterns overview
topics.description: Strategy, Observer, Command, State, Template Method, Chain of Responsibility, Iterator, Mediator: object interaction.

topics.title: Singleton
topics.description: One instance with global access. Thread-safe implementations, and why dependency injection usually replaces it.

topics.title: Factory Method and Abstract Factory
topics.description: Defer instantiation to subclasses or factories so clients depend only on abstractions.

topics.title: Builder
topics.description: Construct complex objects step by step with a fluent API; validate at build time.

topics.title: Strategy
topics.description: Encapsulate interchangeable algorithms behind an interface and select at runtime.

topics.title: Observer
topics.description: Subjects notify subscribers of changes. Event systems, listeners and the pitfalls of memory leaks.

topics.title: Decorator
topics.description: Wrap objects to add behaviour dynamically without subclassing. Streams, middleware and UI wrappers.

topics.title: Command
topics.description: Encapsulate a request as an object with execute and undo. Enables queues, macros and history.

topics.title: State
topics.description: Encapsulate state-specific behaviour in classes and switch the current state object on transitions.

topics.title: Adapter and Facade
topics.description: Adapter converts one interface to another; Facade simplifies a subsystem behind one entry point.

topics.title: Proxy
topics.description: A stand-in controlling access: lazy loading, caching, access control, remote calls.

topics.title: Template Method
topics.description: Define the skeleton of an algorithm in a base class and let subclasses fill in steps.

topics.title: Chain of Responsibility
topics.description: Pass a request along handlers until one handles it. Middleware, approval workflows and validation chains.

topics.title: Error handling
topics.description: Exceptions versus result types, validation at boundaries, and designing failures into the object model.

topics.title: State machines
topics.description: Explicit states and transitions prevent invalid behaviour. Implement with enums, tables or the State pattern.

topics.title: Concurrency
topics.description: Designing objects used by many threads: immutability, confinement, locks and thread-safe collections.

topics.title: Thread safety
topics.description: Race conditions, atomicity, visibility and how to reason about invariants under concurrent access.

topics.title: Clean architecture
topics.description: Dependencies point inward: entities, use cases, adapters, frameworks. Business rules stay framework-free.

topics.title: Testability
topics.description: Design for tests: dependency injection, small units, deterministic behaviour and clear seams.

topics.title: Parking lot design
topics.description: Vehicles, spots, levels, tickets and payments with extensible vehicle types and pricing strategies.

topics.title: Elevator design
topics.description: Requests, scheduling algorithm, elevator state machine and dispatch across multiple cars.

topics.title: Library management design
topics.description: Books, copies, members, loans, reservations, fines and search.

topics.title: Vending machine design
topics.description: States (idle, has money, dispensing), inventory, payments and change with a state machine.

topics.title: Splitwise design
topics.description: Users, groups, expenses, split strategies and debt simplification.

topics.title: Rate limiter design
topics.description: Token bucket, leaky bucket and sliding window implementations with thread safety and configurable rules.

topics.title: Logging framework design
topics.description: Levels, appenders, formatters, async logging and configuration, using Chain of Responsibility or Observer.

topics.title: Cache design

title: Advanced SQL
description: SQL beyond joins and GROUP BY for analytics and pipeline work: lateral and anti joins, window frames, recursive CTEs, JSON and arrays, gaps-and-islands, MERGE, EXPLAIN, indexing, partitioning, materialised views, locking for loads, and testable SQL.

categories.title: Advanced Joins and Set Operations
categories.description: Join forms that the basic track skips, and the set operators that combine whole result sets.

topics.title: LATERAL joins
topics.description: A LATERAL subquery can reference columns from tables to its left, so it runs once per outer row. It replaces correlated subqueries that must return several columns or rows, such as the latest three orders per customer.

subtopics.title: CROSS JOIN LATERAL versus LEFT JOIN LATERAL

topics.title: Semi-joins and anti-joins
topics.description: EXISTS and NOT EXISTS express "has at least one match" and "has no match" without duplicating rows the way a join does. Anti-joins written with NOT IN silently return nothing when the subquery yields a NULL.

subtopics.title: The NOT IN and NULL trap
LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL versus NOT EXISTS

topics.title: Self-joins and non-equi joins
topics.description: Joining a table to itself for pairs, predecessors and hierarchies, and joining on inequalities or BETWEEN for ranges, bands and versioned lookups. Non-equi joins cannot use hash joins, so their cost profile differs.

subtopics.title: Avoiding duplicate pairs with a < b

topics.title: UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT
topics.description: Set operators combine whole result sets by position, not by name. UNION deduplicates and costs a sort or hash, UNION ALL does not; INTERSECT and EXCEPT compare complete rows and treat NULLs as equal, unlike joins.

topics.title: Join order and query shape
topics.description: How the optimiser reorders inner joins but not outer joins, why filtering before joining shrinks intermediate results, and how join_collapse_limit and CTE boundaries change what the planner is allowed to reorder.

categories.title: Window Functions in Depth
categories.description: Frames, ordering subtleties and the analytic functions that drive most reporting SQL.

topics.title: Window frames: ROWS, RANGE and GROUPS
topics.description: The frame clause decides which rows an aggregate sees relative to the current row. The default RANGE frame includes peers with equal ORDER BY values, which is why running sums over duplicate dates look wrong until you switch to ROWS.

subtopics.title: Default frame with and without ORDER BY
RANGE with numeric and interval offsets

topics.title: Ranking and distribution functions
topics.description: ROW_NUMBER, RANK and DENSE_RANK handle ties differently; NTILE buckets rows; PERCENT_RANK and CUME_DIST give relative positions. Choosing the wrong one silently changes top-N and percentile reports.

topics.title: Offset and value functions
topics.description: LAG and LEAD read neighbouring rows, FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE and NTH_VALUE read from the frame edges. LAST_VALUE surprises people because the default frame ends at the current row, so it returns the current value.

subtopics.title: LAG and LEAD with offsets and defaults

topics.title: Running totals, moving averages and cumulative shares
topics.description: Combining SUM, AVG and COUNT with frames to build cumulative sums, trailing windows, share-of-total and running distinct counts, and the PARTITION BY choices that reset them per customer, month or product.

topics.title: Named windows and filtering window results
topics.description: The WINDOW clause defines a window once for reuse; window functions run after WHERE and HAVING, so filtering on their output needs a subquery or CTE. FILTER (WHERE ...) restricts which rows feed an aggregate, including window aggregates.

subtopics.title: Evaluation order and why WHERE cannot see windows
Filtering window output through a CTE

categories.title: Recursive CTEs and Hierarchies
categories.description: Iteration inside a single statement: trees, graphs and generated sequences.

topics.title: Recursive CTE mechanics
topics.description: WITH RECURSIVE runs an anchor query, then repeats the recursive member on the previous iteration only until it returns no rows. Knowing that each step sees just the last batch explains both its power and its termination rules.

topics.title: Trees, paths and levels
topics.description: Walking parent-child tables such as org charts, categories and bills of materials: computing depth, building a materialised path string or array for ordering, and rolling quantities up the tree.

subtopics.title: Ordering a tree by path array

topics.title: Graph traversal and cycle detection
topics.description: Reachability and shortest paths over edge tables, why cycles make a recursive CTE loop forever, and the CYCLE clause (PostgreSQL 14+) or an explicit visited array that stops it.

subtopics.title: Detecting cycles with a visited array
Shortest path with depth and LIMIT

topics.title: Generating series and calendar tables
topics.description: generate_series builds numbers, dates and timestamps on the fly, which lets you left-join to find missing days, build calendar dimensions, and densify sparse metrics before charting.

subtopics.title: Filling gaps with a LEFT JOIN
Recursive CTEs when generate_series is unavailable

categories.title: Semi-structured and Text Data
categories.description: JSON, arrays, strings and regular expressions inside the database.

topics.title: JSONB operators and indexing
topics.description: jsonb stores parsed binary JSON with operators for path access (->, ->>, #>>), containment (@>), key existence (?) and jsonpath queries, and GIN indexes make containment queries fast without normalising the data first.

topics.title: Building and unnesting JSON
topics.description: Turning rows into JSON with jsonb_build_object and jsonb_agg, and JSON back into rows with jsonb_array_elements, jsonb_each and jsonb_to_recordset, so API payloads and event logs can be shredded into relational form.

topics.title: Arrays and unnest
topics.description: PostgreSQL arrays as multi-valued columns: constructors, ANY and ALL, array_agg with ORDER BY, unnest WITH ORDINALITY to keep positions, and where arrays beat a junction table and where they do not.

topics.title: String functions and aggregation
topics.description: string_agg, split_part, format, concat_ws, position and substring with the right NULL behaviour, plus case-folding and trimming for joins on messy text keys.

subtopics.title: Normalising keys with lower and btrim

topics.title: Regular expressions in SQL
topics.description: The ~ and ~* operators, regexp_replace, regexp_matches, regexp_split_to_table and (PostgreSQL 15+) regexp_count and regexp_substr, with the performance caveat that regex predicates cannot use ordinary B-tree indexes.

categories.title: Temporal Queries and Sequences
categories.description: Dates, intervals, sessions and the classic gaps-and-islands family.

topics.title: Timestamps, time zones and intervals
topics.description: timestamptz stores an instant and renders it in the session zone; timestamp stores wall-clock text. AT TIME ZONE converts between them, and interval arithmetic across DST boundaries and month ends is where reports go wrong.

topics.title: Bucketing with date_trunc and date_bin
topics.description: Rolling events into hours, days, weeks or arbitrary 15-minute bins with date_trunc and date_bin, choosing the week start, and why bucketing in the query beats bucketing in the BI tool.

subtopics.title: Bucketing in the session time zone

topics.title: Gaps and islands
topics.description: Finding runs of consecutive values or dates (islands) and the holes between them (gaps) using the ROW_NUMBER difference trick or LAG-based change flags, the pattern behind streaks, outages and contiguous-booking reports.

subtopics.title: Change flags with LAG plus running SUM
Islands over dates versus over integers

topics.title: Sessionisation
topics.description: Splitting event streams into sessions when the gap between consecutive events exceeds a timeout: flag new sessions with LAG, number them with a running SUM, then aggregate per session for duration and event counts.

subtopics.title: New-session flags with LAG and a threshold

topics.title: Range types and point-in-time joins
topics.description: daterange and tstzrange hold validity intervals; the && overlap operator, @> containment and exclusion constraints replace fragile pairs of start/end columns, and as-of joins pick the version valid at a given moment.

categories.title: Reshaping and Merging Data
categories.description: Pivoting, unpivoting and writing data in idempotent, conflict-aware ways.

topics.title: Pivoting with conditional aggregation
topics.description: Turning rows into columns with SUM(CASE WHEN ...) or the FILTER clause, the crosstab function from the tablefunc extension, and why a dynamic column list needs application code or PL/pgSQL.

topics.title: Unpivoting with VALUES and LATERAL
topics.description: Turning wide columns back into rows with CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES (...), (...)), or with unnest over parallel arrays, so metric columns become a tidy (key, value) table for further analysis.

subtopics.title: When to unpivot in SQL versus in code

topics.title: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upserts
topics.description: ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET ... with the EXCLUDED pseudo-table gives atomic upserts, DO NOTHING gives idempotent inserts, and both need a unique index or constraint to arbitrate on.

topics.title: The MERGE statement
topics.description: MERGE (PostgreSQL 15+) matches a source against a target and applies INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE per branch in one statement, which expresses dimension maintenance and SCD loads more readably than separate statements.

subtopics.title: MATCHED, NOT MATCHED and NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE
Duplicate source rows and MERGE errors

categories.title: Query Planning and Performance
categories.description: Reading plans, feeding the planner good statistics and choosing physical structures for analytical queries.

topics.title: Reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE
topics.description: How to read a plan tree from the innermost node outward, compare estimated and actual rows, spot buffers and spills to disk, and use EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT TEXT) as the first step of every tuning session.

subtopics.title: Plan tree structure and node costs

topics.title: Scan and join strategies
topics.description: Sequential, index, index-only and bitmap scans, and nested loop, hash and merge joins: when the planner picks each, and what row counts and memory settings tip the decision.

subtopics.title: Seq scan versus index scan crossover
Index-only scans and the visibility map
Nested loop, hash join and merge join

topics.title: Statistics and row estimates
topics.description: ANALYZE samples tables into pg_statistic, most-common-values and histograms drive estimates, and CREATE STATISTICS fixes correlated columns and functional dependencies that otherwise mislead the planner by orders of magnitude.

topics.title: Indexing strategies for analytics
topics.description: Composite index column order, covering indexes with INCLUDE, partial indexes for hot subsets, expression indexes for computed predicates, and BRIN for huge append-only tables where B-trees are too big.

topics.title: Table partitioning and pruning
topics.description: Declarative range, list and hash partitioning, how partition pruning removes partitions at plan or execution time, partition-wise joins, and the maintenance win of dropping old partitions instead of deleting rows.

topics.title: Materialised views
topics.description: Precomputing expensive aggregates into a materialised view, refreshing it fully or CONCURRENTLY with a unique index, and designing incremental refresh by hand when the built-in refresh is too slow.

topics.title: Rewriting slow queries
topics.description: Common rewrites that change plans: making predicates sargable, replacing OR with UNION ALL, turning correlated subqueries into joins or LATERAL, pre-aggregating before joining, and using EXISTS instead of DISTINCT after a join.

subtopics.title: LIMIT with ORDER BY and indexes

categories.title: Transactions and Locking for Pipelines
categories.description: Loading data safely while readers and other jobs keep running.

topics.title: Atomic loads with staging and swaps
topics.description: Loading into a staging table and swapping it in with ALTER TABLE RENAME inside one transaction gives readers an all-or-nothing switch, and truncating instead of deleting keeps the table small and fast.

topics.title: Row locks and SKIP LOCKED queues
topics.description: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE takes row locks that serialise writers; adding SKIP LOCKED lets many workers pull disjoint batches from a job table, which is the standard way to build a work queue in PostgreSQL.

subtopics.title: Claiming a batch with UPDATE ... RETURNING

topics.title: Advisory locks and singleton jobs
topics.description: pg_advisory_lock and pg_try_advisory_xact_lock coordinate application-level mutual exclusion, so two schedulers cannot run the same load at once and a job can hold a named lock without touching any row.

subtopics.title: Deriving lock keys from job names

topics.title: MVCC, long transactions and bloat
topics.description: Multi-version concurrency keeps old row versions until no transaction needs them; long-running loads and idle-in-transaction sessions block vacuum, inflate tables and stall index-only scans, so pipeline transactions must stay short.

categories.title: SQL Style, Testing and Maintainability
categories.description: Writing SQL that other people, and future you, can read, review and trust.

topics.title: Formatting and naming conventions
topics.description: Consistent keyword case, one clause per line, leading commas or trailing commas but not both, snake_case identifiers, explicit aliases and no SELECT *, enforced with a formatter such as sqlfluff so reviews focus on logic.

topics.title: Structuring queries with CTEs and views
topics.description: Breaking a 200-line query into named CTE steps that each answer one question, deciding when a step deserves a view or a table, and the readability versus performance trade-off of MATERIALIZED CTEs.

subtopics.title: Views for reuse and access control

topics.title: Testing SQL
topics.description: Asserting query results with small fixture tables, checking invariants such as uniqueness, referential completeness and row-count deltas, and using pgTAP or a pytest harness so SQL changes get regression coverage like any code.

subtopics.title: Invariant checks: unique, not null, totals
Comparing before and after result sets

topics.title: Dynamic SQL and PL/pgSQL safely
topics.description: DO blocks and functions for loops over partitions or dynamic column lists, EXECUTE with format() and %I/%L quoting to prevent injection, and keeping dynamic SQL to the few cases plain SQL cannot express.

categories.title: Projects and Interview Preparation
categories.description: End-to-end SQL work on realistic data, then the questions interviewers ask about it.

topics.title: Project: web analytics from raw events
topics.description: Load a clickstream table of page views, sessionise it with a 30-minute timeout, compute daily active users, retention cohorts and funnel conversion with window functions, and expose the results as materialised views refreshed by a script.

topics.title: Project: hierarchical reporting
topics.description: Model an organisation and a bill of materials as parent-child tables, then write recursive CTEs that produce indented org charts, roll up salaries and component costs, detect cycles and expose paths for filtering.

subtopics.title: Recursive walk with depth and path

topics.title: Project: incremental MERGE pipeline
topics.description: Build a partitioned fact table fed from a staging table: dedupe the source, MERGE inserts and updates with a change hash, add a partition per month automatically, and measure plans before and after adding indexes.

topics.title: Project: query tuning lab
topics.description: Take five deliberately slow queries against a multi-million-row dataset, capture EXPLAIN ANALYZE output, fix each with statistics, indexes, rewrites or partitioning, and document the before-and-after timings and plans.

subtopics.title: Apply one fix at a time

topics.title: Advanced SQL interview questions
topics.description: The questions that separate candidates: RANK versus DENSE_RANK, window frames, NOT IN with NULLs, when a CTE is materialised, how a hash join works, why an index is ignored, and how to make a load idempotent.

topics.title: Whiteboard SQL problems
topics.description: Timed practice on the recurring problems: top-N per group, consecutive-day streaks, running totals, deduplicating with ROW_NUMBER, year-over-year comparisons with LAG, and median with PERCENTILE_CONT.

title: AI Agents and Agentic Workflows
description: Designing LLM agents that perceive, plan and act: tool schemas and MCP, planning and decomposition, graph and state-machine orchestration, memory and checkpoints, human approval, error recovery, tracing, evaluation, sandboxing, cost control, multi-agent patterns and the LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK and Claude Agent SDK ways of building them.

code.label: Python with the usual libraries (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, torch)

categories.title: Agent Foundations
categories.description: What turns a model call into an agent and when that is the wrong choice.

topics.title: What makes an LLM an agent
topics.description: An agent is a model that chooses its next action from observations, calls tools and loops until a goal is met; the difference from a chatbot is that the model controls the flow, which brings power and unpredictability.

topics.title: The perceive-plan-act loop
topics.description: Each iteration reads the current state and tool results, decides on a plan or the next step, executes an action and feeds the result back; every agent framework is a variation of this loop with different guard rails.

topics.title: Workflows versus autonomous agents
topics.description: A workflow fixes the sequence of LLM and tool steps in code; an agent lets the model choose; workflows are cheaper, testable and predictable, so they should be the default until the task genuinely needs open-ended decisions.

topics.title: When not to build an agent
topics.description: Tasks with deterministic logic, strict compliance paths or tight latency budgets are better served by code and a single model call; recognising these early avoids expensive, fragile systems that a script would have replaced.

categories.title: Tool Use and Tool Schemas
categories.description: Giving the model capabilities it can call reliably.

topics.title: Function calling and tool schemas
topics.description: A tool is declared to the model as a name, description and JSON Schema of parameters; the model returns a structured call, your code runs it and returns the result, so the schema is the contract that decides how well the model uses it.

topics.title: Writing tool descriptions the model understands
topics.description: The description is read like documentation by the model: say what the tool does, when to use it and when not to, name units and formats, and keep the parameter set small; poor descriptions are the top cause of wrong tool calls.

topics.title: Executing tools and returning results
topics.description: Tool results should be concise, structured and truncated to a token budget, with ids and pagination for large data; what you return shapes the next reasoning step as much as the prompt does.

topics.title: Tool errors as information
topics.description: A failing tool should return a clear, actionable error message to the model rather than crash the loop; well-phrased errors let the model correct its arguments or choose another approach on the next step.

subtopics.title: Error messages the model can act on

topics.title: Model Context Protocol for tools
topics.description: MCP standardises how a client such as an agent discovers and calls tools, resources and prompts exposed by a server over stdio or HTTP, so one integration can serve many agents and hosts instead of bespoke adapters.

categories.title: Planning and Decomposition
categories.description: How agents reason about what to do next.

topics.title: ReAct: reasoning interleaved with actions
topics.description: The ReAct pattern alternates a short reasoning step with a tool call and an observation, so the model grounds each decision in fresh evidence; it is the base loop most tool-using agents run today.

topics.title: Plan-then-execute and task decomposition
topics.description: Asking the model to write a plan of sub-tasks first, then executing each with fresh context, keeps long tasks on track and lets you show progress, replan on failure and parallelise independent steps.

topics.title: Reflection and self-critique
topics.description: Having the model review its own output or a tool result against explicit criteria before continuing catches many errors cheaply; it works best with concrete checks such as tests or schema validation rather than vague "is this good".

topics.title: Routing and classification steps
topics.description: A cheap classification step that sends a request to a specialised prompt, model or sub-workflow improves accuracy and cost; routing is the simplest agentic pattern and often removes the need for a general agent.

categories.title: Workflow Orchestration
categories.description: Structuring multi-step LLM work as explicit graphs and state machines.

topics.title: Prompt chaining and parallelisation
topics.description: Chaining splits a task into sequential calls with checks between them; parallelisation runs independent calls at once and merges results or votes; both are workflow patterns with fixed control flow that are easy to test.

topics.title: Orchestrator-worker pattern
topics.description: A central model breaks a task into sub-tasks, delegates each to worker calls with focused context and synthesises the results; it suits tasks where the sub-tasks cannot be known in advance, such as multi-file code changes.

topics.title: Graph-based orchestration
topics.description: Modelling an agent as nodes that transform a shared state and edges that decide the next node, as LangGraph does, makes the control flow explicit, resumable and visualisable instead of hidden inside a loop.

topics.title: State machines for agent control
topics.description: Explicit states such as gathering, drafting, awaiting approval and done, with allowed transitions, stop an agent from wandering; each state has its own prompt, tools and exit conditions, which makes behaviour auditable.

topics.title: Evaluator-optimiser loops
topics.description: One call produces a draft, another evaluates it against criteria and returns feedback, and the loop repeats until the evaluator accepts or a budget runs out; it works when evaluation is easier than generation.

categories.title: State Management and Memory
categories.description: What the agent remembers within a run and across runs.

topics.title: Designing agent state
topics.description: State holds the messages, intermediate results, plan and metadata a run needs; typing it explicitly, keeping it serialisable and separating scratch from durable fields makes runs resumable and debuggable.

topics.title: Managing the context window during a run
topics.description: Long runs fill the context with tool output; trimming old results, summarising completed steps and storing large artefacts outside the prompt keep the agent effective past the point where naive appending fails.

topics.title: Long-term memory stores
topics.description: Memory across sessions lives in a database: facts about the user, past outcomes and learned preferences retrieved by key or by embedding; deciding what to write, when to forget and how to avoid contaminating runs is the hard part.

topics.title: Checkpoints and resumable runs
topics.description: Persisting state after each node lets a run survive crashes, pause for human input and be replayed from any point; checkpointing is what turns an agent script into a durable process.

categories.title: Execution Control and Safety Rails
categories.description: Keeping multi-step runs bounded, correct and under human control.

topics.title: Multi-step execution and loop limits
topics.description: Every loop needs a maximum number of steps, a token budget and a wall-clock limit; without them a confused agent burns money and time, and with them failures become clean, reportable events.

topics.title: Human approval and interrupts
topics.description: Actions with real consequences, such as sending email or spending money, pause the run, present the proposed action and wait for approval; interrupts require checkpointed state and a resume path that carries the decision.

subtopics.title: Interrupt before or after a node

topics.title: Error recovery and retries
topics.description: Transient failures get bounded retries with backoff in code; semantic failures go back to the model with the error; persistent failures trigger fallbacks or escalation; a policy per error class keeps runs from either dying or looping.

topics.title: Idempotency and side effects
topics.description: Retries and replays can execute a tool twice, so writes need idempotency keys, dry-run modes and compensating actions; reads and writes should be separated so planning can happen without touching the world.

topics.title: Timeouts, cancellation and cleanup
topics.description: Users cancel, tools hang and budgets expire mid-run; propagating cancellation to in-flight tool calls, releasing resources and recording a partial result prevent zombie processes and inconsistent state.

categories.title: Observability and Evaluation of Agents
categories.description: Seeing what an agent did and measuring whether it works.

topics.title: Tracing agent runs
topics.description: A trace captures every model call, tool call, arguments, results, latency and cost as a tree of spans; without it a failed run is unexplainable, and with it you can replay, compare and bill accurately.

subtopics.title: Spans for model and tool calls

topics.title: Evaluating task success and trajectories
topics.description: Agent evals check the final outcome against a goal and the trajectory against expectations, such as which tools were called and in what order; outcome-only scoring misses dangerous paths that happened to succeed.

topics.title: Simulated environments and test harnesses
topics.description: Running agents against mocked tools, sandboxed copies of systems and scripted users lets you test many scenarios deterministically and cheaply before touching production data.

topics.title: Debugging failed agent runs
topics.description: Reading the trace to find the first wrong step, checking whether the prompt, tool description, tool result or state was at fault, then adding a regression case, is the standard loop for improving agents.

subtopics.title: Prompt versus tool versus state faults

categories.title: Security, Cost and Latency
categories.description: Bounding what an agent can do and what it can spend.

topics.title: Security boundaries and least privilege
topics.description: An agent should hold only the credentials and tools its task needs, scoped per user and per run; permissions are enforced in the tool layer, never by the prompt, because the model can be persuaded to ignore instructions.

topics.title: Sandboxing code execution
topics.description: Agents that run generated code need containers or microVMs with no network by default, resource limits, ephemeral filesystems and no access to host secrets; the sandbox is what makes code execution a safe tool.

topics.title: Prompt injection against agents
topics.description: Web pages, emails and documents an agent reads can contain instructions that hijack it into exfiltrating data or taking actions; treating all tool output as untrusted, confirming risky actions and limiting data flow are the defences.

topics.title: Cost control for agents
topics.description: Agents multiply calls, so cost is managed with per-run token budgets, smaller models for routine steps, prompt caching of stable prefixes, trimmed tool results and monitoring of cost per completed task.

topics.title: Latency control for agents
topics.description: Sequential steps add up; parallel tool calls, streaming intermediate progress, speculative or cached results and cutting unnecessary reflection rounds keep agents responsive enough for interactive use.

categories.title: Multi-Agent Patterns and Frameworks
categories.description: Coordinating several agents and the toolkits that package these ideas.

topics.title: Multi-agent patterns
topics.description: Supervisor agents delegate to specialists, handoff patterns pass a conversation between agents, and debate or committee patterns compare outputs; each adds coordination cost that must be justified by better results.

topics.title: Subagents and context isolation
topics.description: Spawning a subagent with its own fresh context for a bounded subtask keeps the main agent's context clean and lets work run in parallel; the subagent returns a summary, not its whole transcript.

topics.title: LangGraph
topics.description: LangGraph builds agents as state graphs with typed state, nodes, conditional edges, checkpointers for persistence and interrupts for human input; it is the framework to know for explicit, resumable orchestration.

topics.title: OpenAI Agents SDK
topics.description: The OpenAI Agents SDK models agents with instructions, tools and handoffs, adds guardrails that run alongside the agent, and traces every run; it favours a small set of primitives over a graph abstraction.

topics.title: Claude Agent SDK concepts
topics.description: The Claude Agent SDK packages the agent loop used by Claude Code: tools including file and shell access, MCP servers, permission modes, hooks around tool calls, subagents and session persistence, so you build on a proven loop rather than writing one.

subtopics.title: Subagents and sessions in the SDK

topics.title: Project: research assistant agent
topics.description: Build an agent that plans a research question, searches the web and a local document store through tools, reads and summarises sources, tracks what it has covered in state and produces a cited report with a step budget.

subtopics.title: Plan and execute with a step budget

topics.title: Project: approval-gated operations agent
topics.description: An agent that triages incoming support tickets, drafts replies and proposed account actions, then pauses for human approval before any write; use a graph with checkpoints so a run can be resumed hours later.

topics.title: Project: coding agent in a sandbox
topics.description: An agent that takes a task description, edits files and runs tests inside a container with no network, iterates until tests pass or a budget is hit, and opens a summary of changes; include traces and a scenario test suite.

topics.title: Project: multi-agent data analysis
topics.description: A supervisor agent that routes analysis questions to a SQL agent and a charting agent with isolated contexts, merges their outputs into a report, and is evaluated on a scenario suite with mocked databases.

topics.title: AI agents interview questions
topics.description: Expect questions on the agent loop, tool schema design, workflows versus agents, handling tool failures, human-in-the-loop design, memory strategies, prompt injection defences, evaluating agents and controlling cost.

topics.title: Agent system design exercise
topics.description: Design an agent that resolves customer refund requests end to end across CRM, payments and email, with a 2 percent error tolerance, full audit trail and human approval above a threshold; specify tools, states, checkpoints, evals and cost controls.

title: AI Engineering Foundations
description: The mental models an AI engineer needs before touching a framework: what AI, ML and deep learning actually are, how an AI application is put together, how data and models move through their lifecycles, how to pick between building, calling and fine-tuning a model, and how to evaluate, budget, secure and ship one responsibly.

code.label: Python with the usual libraries (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, torch)

categories.title: What AI Is and Is Not
categories.description: Precise vocabulary so every later decision rests on the right distinctions.

topics.title: AI, machine learning and deep learning
topics.description: AI is the goal of machines performing tasks that need intelligence; ML is learning a function from data instead of writing rules; deep learning is ML with many-layered neural networks. Knowing which layer a problem sits in decides tooling, data needs and cost.

subtopics.title: AI as a goal, ML as a method

topics.title: Rule-based systems versus learned models
topics.description: Hand-written rules are transparent and cheap when the logic is small and stable; learned models win when the rules are unknown, fuzzy or change with the data. Most real products combine both, with rules as guardrails around a model.

subtopics.title: Signs a rule system should become a model

topics.title: Supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning
topics.description: The three learning set-ups differ by what signal the algorithm gets: labelled targets, no labels, or rewards from actions. Recognising the set-up tells you what data to collect and which family of algorithms applies.

subtopics.title: Rewards and policies in reinforcement learning
Matching a business problem to a set-up

topics.title: Discriminative versus generative models
topics.description: A discriminative model predicts a label or number from an input; a generative model produces new content such as text, images or audio. The distinction changes how you evaluate (accuracy versus quality and faithfulness) and how outputs can fail.

subtopics.title: Why generative outputs are harder to score
Combining a generator with a classifier

topics.title: Why AI works now: data, compute and transformers
topics.description: The current wave comes from three things arriving together: web-scale datasets, GPUs that make matrix multiplication cheap, and the transformer architecture that scales predictably. Understanding this explains why capabilities and costs move the way they do.

categories.title: Anatomy of an AI Application
categories.description: The four moving parts of any AI product: model, data, serving and feedback.

topics.title: The four parts: model, data, serving, feedback
topics.description: Every AI application is a model that turns inputs into outputs, the data that shaped it, the serving layer that puts it in a request path, and the feedback loop that tells you how it is doing. Diagramming these first prevents building a great model nobody can call.

subtopics.title: Model as a function with weights
Data that trains and data that flows

topics.title: Where the model sits in a request path
topics.description: A model call is one step in a chain: validate input, fetch context, call the model, post-process, log and respond. Placing it deliberately decides latency, cost and what can be cached or retried.

subtopics.title: Calling a model from an API handler

topics.title: Inputs: features, prompts and context
topics.description: Classic models consume engineered feature vectors; language models consume prompts assembled from instructions, retrieved context and user text. Both are input contracts that must be versioned and tested because a silent change breaks the model without any error.

topics.title: Outputs: post-processing, thresholds and guardrails
topics.description: Raw model output is rarely the final answer: probabilities need thresholds, generated text needs parsing and safety checks, and rejected outputs need a fallback. The post-processing layer is where product behaviour is actually tuned.

topics.title: Feedback loops and data flywheels
topics.description: Logged predictions, user corrections and outcomes become tomorrow's training and evaluation data. Designing that capture from day one turns usage into a compounding advantage and exposes failures before they reach a dashboard.

categories.title: Data and Model Lifecycles
categories.description: How data becomes a model and how a model ages.

topics.title: Data collection and labelling
topics.description: Models are limited by the data they see, so sourcing, sampling and labelling are engineering work: writing labelling guidelines, measuring inter-annotator agreement and deciding what a representative sample is.

topics.title: Train, validation and test splits
topics.description: The training set fits parameters, the validation set steers choices, and the test set gives one honest final score. Splitting by time or by group instead of at random is what keeps that final score honest.

topics.title: Data quality and leakage
topics.description: Duplicates, mislabelled rows and features that secretly encode the target produce models that look brilliant offline and fail in production. Leakage is the most common cause of a too-good-to-be-true result.

topics.title: Training versus inference
topics.description: Training runs backward passes over a whole dataset for hours on accelerators; inference runs a forward pass per request in milliseconds. They have different hardware, cost, latency and reliability profiles, and confusing them leads to mis-sized systems.

subtopics.title: Compute and memory at each stage

topics.title: Model versioning and lineage
topics.description: A model artefact is only reproducible if you can name the code, data snapshot, hyperparameters and environment that made it. A model registry ties these together so rollbacks and audits are possible.

topics.title: Drift and retraining triggers
topics.description: The world changes after deployment: input distributions shift and the relationship to the target changes. Monitoring drift and defining when to retrain keeps a model from decaying quietly.

categories.title: Choosing a Model: Build, Call or Fine-tune
categories.description: The decision that shapes a project's budget, timeline and risk.

topics.title: Calling a hosted model API
topics.description: A hosted API gives instant access to a strong model with no training, at the cost of per-call pricing, vendor dependence and sending data outside your boundary. It is the default first step for most language and vision tasks.

topics.title: Training your own model
topics.description: Training from scratch fits the model exactly to your data and keeps everything in-house, but demands labelled data, ML expertise and ongoing maintenance. It shines for tabular problems, tight latency budgets and domains far from public data.

subtopics.title: When tabular models beat large models
Full control over latency and cost

topics.title: Fine-tuning a pretrained model
topics.description: Fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model with a smaller labelled set, giving domain behaviour without training from scratch. It is worth it for style, format and specialised vocabulary, and much less so for injecting facts that retrieval can supply.

subtopics.title: Data needed to see a gain

topics.title: Open-weights versus proprietary models
topics.description: Open-weights models can be self-hosted, inspected and fine-tuned freely; proprietary models are often stronger and simpler to consume. Licence terms, hosting capacity and compliance decide which is viable.

topics.title: The decision matrix: cost, data, control, latency
topics.description: Score the options on data available, latency budget, cost per prediction, need for control and time to market, then start with the cheapest option that meets the bar. Most teams move from API to fine-tuned or custom models only when volume or requirements justify it.

categories.title: Evaluation Fundamentals
categories.description: You cannot improve what you cannot measure, and most AI failures are measurement failures.

topics.title: Offline metrics and what they hide
topics.description: Accuracy, F1, RMSE and BLEU summarise performance on a held-out set, but a single number hides class imbalance, subgroup failures and whether errors matter equally. Pick metrics that reflect the decision the model supports.

subtopics.title: Choosing a metric from the decision

topics.title: Baselines and sanity checks
topics.description: A majority-class predictor, a simple heuristic or last week's value tells you whether a model adds any value. Beating a baseline is the minimum bar and often reveals leakage or a broken split when the gap is implausibly large.

subtopics.title: Implausible gains as a warning sign
Sanity checks on a tiny sample

topics.title: Evaluation sets and golden data
topics.description: A curated, versioned evaluation set with known answers is the most valuable asset in an AI project. It should cover normal cases, edge cases and past failures, and be refreshed as feedback arrives without ever leaking into training.

subtopics.title: Covering edge cases and past failures
Keeping eval data out of training

topics.title: Human evaluation and rubrics
topics.description: For generative outputs, humans scoring against a written rubric is the ground truth that automatic metrics approximate. Clear criteria, calibration rounds and agreement checks make those scores usable.

topics.title: Online evaluation and A/B tests
topics.description: Offline scores predict but do not prove product impact. Shadow deployments, canaries and A/B tests measure the model on real traffic against the metric the business cares about, with guardrail metrics to catch harm.

categories.title: Latency, Cost and Reliability
categories.description: The engineering constraints that decide whether a model can ship.

topics.title: Latency budgets and where time goes
topics.description: End-to-end latency is network, queueing, pre-processing, model compute and post-processing added together. Measuring each segment at p50 and p99 shows what to optimise and whether a model can fit an interactive budget at all.

subtopics.title: Time to first token in streaming

topics.title: Token and compute cost models
topics.description: Hosted models charge per input and output token; self-hosted models cost GPU-hours regardless of load. Estimating cost per request and per month from expected traffic prevents a prototype that is unaffordable at scale.

subtopics.title: Cost per request and per user
Prompt length as a cost lever

topics.title: Caching, batching and routing
topics.description: Reusing identical or similar responses, grouping requests into batches and sending easy requests to smaller models cut both latency and cost. Each has a correctness trade-off that must be checked against the evaluation set.

topics.title: Timeouts, retries and fallbacks
topics.description: Model calls fail: providers rate-limit, GPUs run out of memory, networks drop. Bounded retries with backoff, sensible timeouts and a defined fallback answer keep the product working when the model does not.

topics.title: Rate limits and quotas
topics.description: Providers cap requests and tokens per minute; your own GPUs cap concurrent batches. Client-side limiting, queueing and quota planning per feature avoid cascading failures when traffic spikes.

topics.title: Observability for AI systems
topics.description: Beyond uptime, an AI system needs traces of each model call with inputs, outputs, latency, cost and quality signals. This is what lets you debug a bad answer a week later and see drift before users complain.

subtopics.title: Tracing a model call end to end
Alerting on cost and error spikes

categories.title: Privacy, Safety and Responsible Use
categories.description: The failure modes that hurt people and companies, and how engineers reduce them.

topics.title: PII and data minimisation
topics.description: Personal data in prompts, logs and training sets creates legal and ethical exposure. Collect only what the task needs, redact before logging, and know which providers retain or train on what you send.

topics.title: Prompt injection and untrusted input
topics.description: Any text a model reads, including documents and web pages, can contain instructions that hijack its behaviour. Treat model input as untrusted, limit what tools the model can trigger and validate outputs before acting on them.

topics.title: Bias, fairness and representativeness
topics.description: Models reproduce the patterns in their data, including historical discrimination and under-representation. Measuring performance per subgroup and choosing a fairness definition explicitly are engineering tasks, not afterthoughts.

topics.title: Hallucination and grounding
topics.description: Generative models produce fluent text that can be false. Grounding answers in retrieved sources, asking for citations, constraining outputs and measuring faithfulness turn confident fiction into a checkable claim.

topics.title: Governance: model cards, audits and regulation
topics.description: Documenting what a model is for, how it was evaluated and where it fails, plus keeping audit trails, is now expected by customers and regulators such as the EU AI Act. Lightweight documentation done early is far cheaper than a retrofit.

categories.title: The AI Engineering Role and Workflow
categories.description: What the job is day to day and how work moves from idea to production.

topics.title: AI engineer, ML engineer and data scientist
topics.description: Data scientists explore data and build models; ML engineers productionise training and serving; AI engineers build products on top of models, often pretrained ones, with a focus on prompts, retrieval, evaluation and integration. Knowing the boundaries clarifies what to learn.

topics.title: From idea to prototype: the notebook-first loop
topics.description: Start with a small dataset and a notebook, get a baseline in a day, then iterate on data and prompts before touching architecture. The fastest teams shorten the loop between a change and a measured result.

topics.title: Experiment tracking and reproducibility
topics.description: Every run should record its config, data version, metrics and artefacts so results can be compared and reproduced weeks later. Tools such as MLflow or Weights & Biases do this, but a disciplined folder and CSV is better than nothing.

topics.title: Defining success with stakeholders
topics.description: Translate a business goal into a measurable target, agree what "good enough" means and what failures are unacceptable before building. This avoids shipping a model that meets a metric nobody cares about.

topics.title: Shipping and iterating an AI feature
topics.description: Release behind a flag, roll out gradually, watch quality and cost dashboards, collect feedback, and schedule the next improvement. An AI feature is never finished; the process is the product.

topics.title: Project: support ticket classifier with scikit-learn
topics.description: Build a classifier that routes support tickets to teams: split data properly, compute a majority baseline, train TF-IDF plus logistic regression, report per-class precision and recall, pick thresholds per team and write a short model card.

topics.title: Project: image classifier with a pretrained torchvision model
topics.description: Fine-tune a pretrained ResNet on a small labelled image set with PyTorch: load and augment data, replace the head, train with a validation loop, measure accuracy and a confusion matrix, and export the model for inference.

topics.title: Project: document question-answering over an LLM API
topics.description: Build a small assistant that answers questions from a folder of documents: chunk and embed text, retrieve relevant chunks, prompt a hosted model with citations, add timeouts and retries, and evaluate on a golden set of 30 questions.

topics.title: Project: evaluation harness for a model endpoint
topics.description: Write a reusable harness that runs a versioned evaluation set against any model endpoint, records latency, cost and scores per example, compares two runs side by side, and fails a CI job when quality drops below a threshold.

subtopics.title: Load and version the eval set

topics.title: AI foundations interview questions
topics.description: The questions that test whether you think like an engineer: ML versus deep learning, leakage, why a test set is sacred, API versus fine-tune trade-offs, drift, and how to evaluate a generative model.

topics.title: Designing an AI system in an interview
topics.description: A structured way to answer "design a system that does X with AI": clarify the decision and success metric, sketch model, data, serving and feedback, choose a model strategy, then cover evaluation, latency, cost, privacy and failure modes.

title: AI Infrastructure and Deployment
description: The platform under AI systems: GPUs and accelerators, CUDA and drivers, CUDA-enabled containers, Kubernetes GPU scheduling with KServe and Ray Serve, SageMaker, Vertex AI and Azure ML, storage and data lakes for training data, networking and secrets, Terraform for ML stacks, distributed training clusters, spot-instance cost control, security, compliance and deployment pipelines.

categories.title: GPUs and Accelerators
categories.description: What the hardware is and how to tell whether it is being used.

topics.title: GPU architecture for machine learning
topics.description: Streaming multiprocessors, tensor cores, HBM and the memory hierarchy, and why ML workloads are usually memory-bandwidth bound: the mental model behind every utilisation and sizing decision.

topics.title: Choosing accelerators
topics.description: NVIDIA data-centre GPUs, AMD Instinct with ROCm, Google TPUs, AWS Inferentia and Trainium, and consumer cards, compared on memory, interconnect, software maturity and price per unit of work.

topics.title: CUDA toolkit, drivers and compatibility
topics.description: The layering of kernel driver, CUDA runtime, cuDNN and framework builds, the compatibility matrix that decides which PyTorch wheel works with which driver, and how to diagnose "CUDA not available".

topics.title: GPU monitoring with nvidia-smi and DCGM
topics.description: Reading utilisation, memory, temperature and power with nvidia-smi, exporting fleet metrics with the DCGM exporter, and spotting the classic signs of a data-loading bottleneck or an idle reserved GPU.

topics.title: Numeric precision and hardware
topics.description: fp32, tf32, fp16, bf16, fp8 and int8: what each costs in memory and accuracy, which GPUs support them natively, and why bf16 became the default for training and fp8 matters for the newest hardware.

topics.title: CUDA base images and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit
topics.description: How containers get GPU access: the toolkit injects the host driver at runtime, nvidia/cuda and framework images supply the CUDA runtime, and --gpus selects devices, so the driver never lives in the image.

topics.title: Building lean ML images
topics.description: Multi-stage builds, pinned dependency layers ordered for cache hits, no notebooks or datasets in the image, and a base image chosen for size, since a 15 GB image slows every deploy and autoscale event.

subtopics.title: What never belongs in the image

topics.title: Registries, scanning and image provenance
topics.description: Pushing to ECR, GCR or GHCR, scanning images for vulnerabilities, signing them, pinning by digest in deployments, and cleanup policies so the registry does not fill with stale multi-gigabyte images.

topics.title: Local GPU stacks with Docker Compose
topics.description: A Compose file that runs a model server, a vector database and a tracking server with GPU reservations, shared volumes for weights and a network, mirroring production closely enough to catch integration bugs.
