topics.description: Upstream retries create duplicates and network paths reorder events; dedupe by id with bounded state, and per-key reordering buffers that release events in event-time order after a delay.

categories.title: Testing and Monitoring Streaming Jobs
categories.description: Proving a job is right and knowing when it stops being right.

topics.title: Unit testing operators and functions
topics.description: Testing window and state logic with test harnesses that feed events with explicit timestamps and watermarks, asserting outputs per firing without running a cluster.

topics.title: Integration tests with embedded Kafka and mini-clusters
topics.description: Running the job against a local Kafka in Docker or a mini-cluster with recorded input and expected output, including a failure injection to verify recovery from a checkpoint.

topics.title: Consumer lag and end-to-end latency
topics.description: Lag per partition shows the job is falling behind; end-to-end latency (event time to output time) shows what users experience; alerting on both trend and absolute values.

topics.title: Checkpoint health and job metrics
topics.description: Checkpoint duration, size and failure count, restart counts, watermark progress per operator and state size; the dashboard a streaming team watches and what each anomaly usually means.

topics.title: Project: clickstream sessionisation
topics.description: Consume page-view events from Kafka, sessionise them per user with a 30-minute gap, compute session length and page count, route late events to a side topic, and write sessions to Postgres idempotently with PyFlink or Spark.

subtopics.title: Handle late events via side output

topics.title: Project: real-time fraud rules with state
topics.description: A keyed stream of card transactions with rules such as more than five transactions in two minutes or two countries within an hour, using keyed state and timers, exactly-once output to Kafka, and tests with a harness.

topics.title: Project: batch and stream metrics that agree
topics.description: Compute hourly revenue both as a Spark batch job over Parquet and as a streaming job with tumbling windows and watermarks, compare results, quantify late-data differences, and document a reconciliation process.

topics.title: Project: stream enrichment with a temporal join
topics.description: Join a stream of orders to a CDC changelog of product prices using a temporal join in Flink SQL so each order uses the price valid at order time, then land results to Parquet with exactly-once file commits.

topics.title: Streaming interview questions
topics.description: Explaining watermarks, why event time matters, window types and their state cost, exactly-once boundaries, how checkpoints work, backpressure diagnosis, and when batch is the better answer.

topics.title: Streaming system design walkthroughs
topics.description: Design exercises done aloud: real-time leaderboard, anomaly detection on sensor data, and order-to-shipment tracking, covering keys, windows, state, guarantees, late data and scale numbers.

subtopics.title: Deriving keys and windows from requirements

title: Business Metrics and KPIs
description: How to design, define, compute and review the numbers a business runs on: leading and lagging indicators, north-star metrics and metric trees, revenue, growth, retention, LTV and CAC, unit economics, operational KPIs, metric dictionaries, the classic pitfalls, and KPI reviews that lead to decisions.

code.label: SQL or spreadsheet formulas, whichever fits

categories.title: Metric Design Foundations
categories.description: What separates a useful metric from a number on a slide.

topics.title: Measures, metrics and KPIs
topics.description: A measure is a raw count or sum, a metric puts it in context (per user, per month, as a rate), and a KPI is a metric someone is accountable for. Keeping the three apart stops every number on a dashboard from being called a KPI.

subtopics.title: What makes a metric a KPI
How many KPIs a team can hold

topics.title: Leading versus lagging indicators
topics.description: Lagging indicators (revenue, churn) confirm what already happened; leading indicators (trial sign-ups, usage depth) move earlier and predict them. Pairing each lagging KPI with leading drivers is what lets a team act before the quarter closes.

subtopics.title: Finding leading indicators with lagged correlation
Pairing each KPI with its drivers

topics.title: Input versus output metrics
topics.description: Output metrics (revenue, retention) are what the business wants but nobody can move directly; input metrics (calls made, pages shipped, delivery time) are the controllable levers. Teams should be judged on outputs but managed with inputs.

subtopics.title: Outputs are results, inputs are levers

topics.title: Counts, rates, ratios and averages
topics.description: The four shapes a metric takes and how each misleads: counts grow with the business, rates need a clear denominator, ratios hide both terms, and averages hide distributions. Choosing the shape is the first design decision.

subtopics.title: Medians and percentiles instead of means

categories.title: North-Star Metrics and Metric Trees
categories.description: One number that captures value delivered, and the tree of drivers underneath it.

topics.title: Choosing a north-star metric
topics.description: A north-star metric measures the value customers get, leads revenue, and can be moved by the teams that own it: nights booked for Airbnb, weekly active teams for Slack. Picking the wrong one (revenue, sign-ups) optimises the company for the wrong behaviour.

subtopics.title: Criteria for a good north star

topics.title: Building a metric tree
topics.description: Decompose the north star into multiplicative or additive drivers (active users x sessions per user x conversion x order value) until each leaf is owned by a team. The tree makes trade-offs explicit and turns "grow revenue" into concrete levers.

topics.title: Driver analysis: explaining a change
topics.description: When a KPI moves, attribute the change to its drivers: hold each driver at its previous value and measure the effect of moving one at a time, then reconcile the residual interaction term. This is the SQL or spreadsheet workhorse behind "why did revenue drop 8%?".

topics.title: Guardrail and counter-metrics
topics.description: Every metric a team pushes can be gamed or can damage something else, so pair it with a guardrail that must not degrade: conversion rate with refund rate, support speed with resolution quality. Guardrails are how you keep a target from becoming a trap.

categories.title: Revenue and Growth Metrics
categories.description: The recurring, transactional and growth numbers every finance and leadership team asks for.

topics.title: MRR and ARR
topics.description: Monthly and annual recurring revenue normalise subscription contracts to a run rate: a $1,200 annual plan is $100 MRR. MRR excludes one-off fees and usage that does not recur, and its month-over-month change is the heartbeat of a subscription business.

subtopics.title: Normalising contracts to monthly run rate
Computing MRR from a subscriptions table

topics.title: MRR movements: new, expansion, contraction and churn
topics.description: MRR at month end equals last month plus new, plus expansion, minus contraction, minus churned, plus reactivation. Splitting the delta this way shows whether growth comes from new logos or from existing customers, and which bucket is leaking.

subtopics.title: Quick ratio of growth to loss

topics.title: ARPU, ARPA and average selling price
topics.description: Average revenue per user (or per account) divides revenue by the count of active payers in the period; average selling price divides new bookings by new deals. Each needs a precise denominator, and each is a mean that segments or medians often explain better.

subtopics.title: Segmenting ARPU by plan and region

topics.title: GMV, take rate and net revenue
topics.description: Marketplaces and payment businesses report gross merchandise value (total transaction value) and the take rate (their share of it). Net revenue is what the company keeps, and confusing GMV with revenue overstates a business by an order of magnitude.

subtopics.title: GMV definition and what it includes

topics.title: Growth rates: MoM, YoY and compounding
topics.description: Month-over-month growth is noisy and seasonal, year-over-year removes seasonality but lags, and compound monthly growth rate summarises a period. Reporting the right one, and the base it is computed from, keeps growth claims honest.

categories.title: Retention, Churn and Engagement
categories.description: Whether customers stay, and how deeply they use what they bought.

topics.title: Customer churn and logo churn
topics.description: Churn rate is customers lost in a period divided by customers at the start of it. The denominator, the treatment of customers who joined mid-period, and the period length all change the number, so churn is only comparable when its definition is fixed.

topics.title: Revenue churn and net revenue retention
topics.description: Gross revenue retention measures how much of a cohort's starting MRR survives without counting upsell; net revenue retention adds expansion and can exceed 100%. NRR above 100% means the existing base grows on its own, which is why investors watch it.

topics.title: Cohort retention curves
topics.description: Group customers by their start month and track the share still active at month 1, 2, 3 and beyond. A curve that flattens shows a retained core; one that keeps sliding means the product leaks. Comparing cohorts shows whether retention improves for newer users.

subtopics.title: Building a cohort table in SQL

topics.title: Active users: DAU, WAU, MAU and stickiness
topics.description: Active-user metrics count distinct users who did a qualifying action in a window; the qualifying action decides everything. DAU/MAU (stickiness) shows how many days a month typical users show up, and is a better health signal than MAU alone.

categories.title: Customer Economics
categories.description: What a customer costs to win, what they are worth, and whether the maths works.

topics.title: Customer acquisition cost
topics.description: CAC is sales and marketing spend divided by new customers acquired in the same window. Whether it includes salaries, tooling and brand spend, and whether organic customers are in the denominator, changes CAC by multiples, so the definition must be written down.

subtopics.title: Matching spend window to acquisition window

topics.title: Customer lifetime value
topics.description: LTV estimates the gross profit a customer generates over their lifetime: ARPU x gross margin / churn rate in the simple model, or the sum of a cohort's margin curve for something more honest. Its assumptions (constant churn, infinite horizon) are where most LTV numbers go wrong.

subtopics.title: Simple LTV from ARPU, margin and churn

topics.title: LTV:CAC and payback period
topics.description: LTV:CAC compares value created with cost to acquire (3:1 is the conventional benchmark); CAC payback is the months of contribution margin needed to recover CAC. Payback matters more for cash-constrained businesses because it says when the money comes back.

subtopics.title: Why payback beats LTV:CAC for cash

topics.title: Contribution margin and unit economics
topics.description: Unit economics asks whether one unit (an order, a ride, a subscriber) makes money after its variable costs: price minus COGS, payment fees, delivery, support. A business with negative contribution margin loses more as it grows, whatever the top line says.

categories.title: Operational Metrics
categories.description: The KPIs of teams that ship, serve, stock and sell.

topics.title: Throughput, cycle time and lead time
topics.description: Throughput is units completed per period, cycle time is how long each takes from start to done, and lead time adds queueing before work starts. Little's law links them (WIP = throughput x cycle time), which is why cutting work in progress speeds delivery.

topics.title: Service metrics: SLA, resolution time, CSAT and NPS
topics.description: Support and service teams track first response time, resolution time against an SLA, ticket backlog, CSAT after each interaction and NPS across the base. Each has a known distortion: NPS depends on who answers, CSAT on when it is asked.

topics.title: Inventory and supply metrics
topics.description: Inventory turnover, days of inventory, stock-out rate and fill rate show whether stock is working or sitting. Turnover that is too high means lost sales from stock-outs; too low means cash tied up and write-offs, so the pair must be read together.

subtopics.title: Inventory turnover and days on hand

topics.title: Sales pipeline metrics
topics.description: Pipeline coverage, stage conversion rates, win rate, average deal size and sales cycle length together forecast bookings: pipeline x win rate / cycle length is the velocity of revenue. Analysts keep these honest by fixing stage definitions and snapshotting the pipeline.

categories.title: Defining Metrics Precisely
categories.description: Turning a metric name into a definition two analysts would compute identically.

topics.title: Writing a metric definition
topics.description: A usable definition states the numerator, denominator, grain, filters, time window, source tables and known exclusions, plus the SQL that computes it. "Active users" without those is a debate waiting to happen every time two dashboards disagree.

topics.title: Grain, filters and time windows
topics.description: The same metric changes with grain (per user, per account, per order), with filters (test accounts, internal users, refunds) and with the window (calendar month, trailing 28 days). Naming these explicitly is how a "monthly active users" number becomes reproducible.

topics.title: Metric dictionaries and ownership
topics.description: A metric dictionary (or semantic layer) is the single catalogue of definitions, owners, source queries and dashboards using each metric. It is the reference that ends "which number is right?" arguments and the place a new analyst learns the business.

topics.title: Versioning and changing a metric
topics.description: Definitions change when the product or data changes; without versioning, history silently breaks. Treat a change like a release: new version, restated history where possible, an annotation on every chart, and a note on which reports moved.

categories.title: Metric Pitfalls and Judgement
categories.description: The ways a correct calculation still gives the wrong answer.

topics.title: The trouble with averages
topics.description: Means are pulled by outliers and hide bimodal populations: an average session of 8 minutes may be mostly 30-second bounces and a few hour-long users. Medians, percentiles and histograms describe what typical customers actually do.

topics.title: Vanity metrics
topics.description: Cumulative sign-ups, page views and app downloads go up and to the right regardless of health, so they flatter without informing. Actionable metrics are comparable, rate-based, tied to a decision, and can go down when something is wrong.

topics.title: Simpson's paradox and mix shifts
topics.description: An aggregate can move opposite to every segment when the mix changes: conversion falls overall while rising in each channel because a low-converting channel grew. Always check the mix before explaining a change in a blended rate.

subtopics.title: Simpson's paradox with a worked example

topics.title: Goodhart's law and gaming
topics.description: When a measure becomes a target it stops being a good measure: call centres hit handle-time targets by hanging up, sales hits bookings with discounts that never renew. Anticipate the gaming path for every KPI and add the guardrail that closes it.

topics.title: Seasonality, denominators and small numbers
topics.description: Weekly, monthly and annual cycles, holidays and month lengths create moves that look like trends; rates on tiny denominators swing wildly. Comparing like with like (YoY, same-weekday, minimum sample thresholds) keeps reviews from chasing noise.

categories.title: Reporting Cadence and KPI Reviews
categories.description: Turning metrics into a rhythm of decisions.

topics.title: Choosing the reporting cadence
topics.description: Match cadence to how fast the metric moves and how fast anyone can act: daily for operations and incidents, weekly for growth levers, monthly for finance, quarterly for strategy. Reporting a slow metric daily creates noise-chasing; reporting a fast one monthly hides problems.

topics.title: Targets, thresholds and OKRs
topics.description: A target turns a metric into a commitment; setting it needs a baseline, a trend, a stretch and a rationale. OKRs frame outcomes with measurable key results, and thresholds (red, amber, green) let a review focus on what is off track.

topics.title: Running a KPI review
topics.description: A good review follows a fixed agenda: what moved, why (from the metric tree), what we will do, and what we decided last time. The analyst's role is to pre-investigate the big moves so the meeting spends its time on decisions, not on reading numbers aloud.

topics.title: Anomalies and written commentary
topics.description: Flag moves that exceed normal variation, separate data issues from real change, and write commentary that leads with the answer: what changed, by how much, why, and what it means. Numbers without narrative get ignored; narrative without numbers gets doubted.

categories.title: Projects and Interview Preparation
categories.description: End-to-end deliverables an analyst would hand to a leadership team, then the questions interviews ask about them.

topics.title: Project: metric dictionary for a subscription business
topics.description: Write the dictionary for a SaaS company from a sample subscriptions and events schema: MRR and its movements, churn, NRR, MAU, CAC and LTV, each with owner, grain, exclusions, reference SQL and a worked value for one month, then reconcile the MRR bridge to the totals.

subtopics.title: Write each definition with reference SQL
Compute a worked month and reconcile
Publish with owners and review dates

topics.title: Project: north-star metric tree with driver SQL
topics.description: Pick a north star for an e-commerce dataset, build a three-level metric tree, and write the SQL that computes every leaf monthly; then explain one month's change with a driver bridge and a waterfall chart that reconciles to the total.

subtopics.title: Choose and justify the north star
Draw the tree and map owners

topics.title: Project: monthly KPI pack
topics.description: Produce a repeatable monthly pack from a retail dataset: one page of headline KPIs with MoM, YoY and target variance, a page per metric-tree branch, RAG status, and answer-first commentary on the three largest moves, built so next month is a refresh, not a rebuild.

topics.title: Project: churn and LTV cohort workbook
topics.description: From a subscriptions table, build monthly cohorts, retention and revenue retention triangles, churn by plan and acquisition channel, cohort LTV curves capped at 36 months, and a CAC payback comparison by channel with a written recommendation on where to spend.

subtopics.title: Segment churn by plan and channel

topics.title: Business metrics interview questions
topics.description: Definitions and calculations interviewers expect fluently: MRR from a contract, churn to annual, LTV from ARPU and churn, NRR versus GRR, CAC payback, DAU/MAU, why averages mislead, and the difference between a north star and a KPI.

subtopics.title: Explaining a metric to a non-analyst

topics.title: Metric case questions
topics.description: Open-ended cases: "revenue dropped 10% last week, what do you do?", "how would you measure the success of feature X?", "define the KPIs for a food delivery app". A structured answer checks data, decomposes with a tree, segments, then proposes metrics with guardrails.

title: C Programming
description: C from the first compiled program to systems code you can trust: the toolchain, pointers and arrays, manual memory management, structs and hand-built data structures, stdio and POSIX I/O, pthreads and atomics, sanitizers, secure coding, and projects such as a shell, an HTTP server and a memory allocator.

categories.title: Environment and Tooling
categories.description: A compiler, a build tool and a debugger before the first pointer.

topics.title: Installing a C toolchain
topics.description: Getting gcc or clang (and MSVC or MinGW on Windows), checking the version, choosing a C standard, and understanding what the compiler, assembler and linker each contribute to an executable.

topics.title: Compiling and linking from the command line
topics.description: The four stages behind gcc main.c: preprocessing, compiling to assembly, assembling to object files and linking, plus the flags every build should use: -Wall -Wextra -g and an optimisation level.

topics.title: Make and Makefiles
topics.description: Describing a build as targets, prerequisites and recipes so only changed files are recompiled; pattern rules, variables such as CC and CFLAGS, and automatic header dependency tracking with -MMD.

topics.title: Anatomy of a C program
topics.description: What main, #include <stdio.h>, function declarations and return codes each do, how execution starts and ends, and why a C file is a flat list of declarations rather than a class hierarchy.

topics.title: The preprocessor and macros
topics.description: Textual substitution before compilation: #include, object-like and function-like #define, conditional compilation with #if and #ifdef, include guards, and the parenthesisation and double-evaluation traps of macros.

topics.title: Integer and floating types
topics.description: char, short, int, long, their unsigned forms and float, double and long double: implementation-defined sizes, sizeof, limits.h, and why stdint.h types like int32_t and size_t make intent and portability explicit.

topics.title: Storage classes, scope and lifetime
topics.description: Where a variable lives and how long: block scope automatics on the stack, static storage for file-local and persistent values, extern for sharing across files, and why uninitialised automatics hold garbage.

topics.title: Conversions, promotions and casts
topics.description: The implicit rules that turn char into int, mix signed with unsigned and truncate on assignment, the usual arithmetic conversions, and when an explicit cast is needed versus when it hides a bug.

subtopics.title: Explicit casts and when to avoid them

topics.title: Arithmetic, bitwise and logical operators
topics.description: Integer division and modulo with negatives, shifts and masks for flags, the difference between & and &&, precedence traps like a & b == c, and the compound assignment and increment forms.

subtopics.title: Bitwise AND, OR, XOR and NOT

topics.title: Undefined behaviour and sequence points
topics.description: Why C compilers may assume signed overflow, out-of-bounds access and uninitialised reads never happen, how that assumption produces baffling optimised code, and the modification-order rules that make i = i++ meaningless.

topics.title: Conditions and switch
topics.description: if/else chains, the integer-only nature of switch, fallthrough as both a feature and a bug, default placement, and why every non-zero value is true while assignment inside a condition is a classic typo.

subtopics.title: if, else and truthiness of integers

topics.title: Loops and jumps
topics.description: for, while and do-while, loop variables declared in the for header since C99, break and continue, and the legitimate uses of goto for error cleanup versus the spaghetti it is famous for.

topics.title: Functions, prototypes and the call stack
topics.description: Declaring prototypes in headers, pass-by-value semantics that copy every argument, returning values, recursion, stack frames and why returning the address of a local variable is a bug.

topics.title: Pointer fundamentals
topics.description: Addresses as values: declaring pointers, & and *, NULL, pointer types and why they matter, pointers to pointers, and reading declarations like int *const p from the inside out.

topics.title: Arrays and pointer decay
topics.description: Fixed-size arrays laid out contiguously, how an array name decays to a pointer to its first element in most expressions, why a function cannot receive an array by value, and where sizeof stops working.

topics.title: Pointer arithmetic and bounds
topics.description: Adding integers to pointers moves by element size, subtracting pointers gives an element count, one-past-the-end is the only legal out-of-range pointer, and iterating with pointers versus indices.

topics.title: Multidimensional arrays and arrays of pointers
topics.description: Row-major 2D arrays, passing them to functions with the inner dimension fixed, the difference between int m[3][4] and int *rows[3], variable-length arrays, and building jagged arrays on the heap.

topics.title: Function pointers and callbacks
topics.description: Storing and calling functions through pointers, the declaration syntax and typedefs that tame it, passing comparators to qsort and bsearch, dispatch tables, and callbacks with a void * context argument.

topics.title: The stack and the heap
topics.description: Automatic variables live in stack frames that vanish on return; heap memory lives until freed. Stack size limits, why large or dynamically sized buffers go on the heap, and how to picture a process address space.

topics.title: malloc, calloc, realloc and free
topics.description: Requesting bytes from the allocator, zero-initialisation with calloc, growing with realloc and its move semantics, checking for NULL, and the sizeof(*p) idiom that keeps allocation sizes correct.

subtopics.title: free and setting pointers to NULL

topics.title: Memory bugs: leaks, double free and use after free
topics.description: The bug classes that make C infamous, how each corrupts the heap or leaks, why they often appear far from the cause, and the discipline (single owner, free at one place, NULL after free) that prevents them.

subtopics.title: Use after free and dangling pointers

topics.title: Ownership conventions in C APIs
topics.description: Without a compiler enforcing ownership, C code documents it: who frees what, create/destroy function pairs, returning heap memory versus filling a caller buffer, and const to signal borrowed data.

topics.title: Alignment, padding and struct layout
topics.description: Why the compiler inserts padding between struct members, how member order changes sizeof, alignof and _Alignas in C11, and why unaligned access is undefined on some architectures.

topics.title: Structs and typedef
topics.description: Grouping fields into a value type, initialising with designated initialisers, copying by assignment, passing by pointer to avoid copies, the -> operator, and typedef to give the struct a clean name.

topics.title: Unions, enums and bit-fields
topics.description: Unions overlay members on the same bytes, enums name integer constants, and bit-fields pack flags: how tagged unions model variants safely, and where type punning through unions is allowed.

topics.title: Linked lists in C
topics.description: Building singly and doubly linked lists from heap nodes, insertion and deletion with pointer-to-pointer tricks, traversal, freeing every node, and the intrusive list pattern used in kernels.

subtopics.title: Insert and delete with pointer to pointer

topics.title: Dynamic arrays and growth
topics.description: A struct of pointer, length and capacity that doubles with realloc for amortised O(1) append, with bounds-checked access, shrink-to-fit, and why doubling beats growing by a constant.

topics.title: Hash tables in C
topics.description: A hash function, an array of buckets, and either chaining or open addressing to resolve collisions; load factor and resizing, string keys with FNV-1a, and deletion with tombstones.

subtopics.title: Hash functions for strings and integers

topics.title: Opaque types and encapsulation
topics.description: Hiding a struct definition behind an incomplete type in the header so callers use only the API: why this preserves ABI, the handle pattern, and how it gives C the information hiding OOP promises.

topics.title: C strings and string.h
topics.description: A string is a char array ended by a null byte: string literals and their immutability, strlen versus sizeof, strcpy, strcat, strcmp and strtok, and why every one of them trusts the terminator.

topics.title: Safe string handling with bounded functions
topics.description: Avoiding overflow by always passing a size: snprintf as the universal safe builder, the strncpy trap of no terminator, strlcpy and memcpy with explicit lengths, and tracking lengths explicitly instead of rescanning.

topics.title: Parsing numbers and characters
topics.description: ctype.h classification and case conversion, strtol and strtod with their end-pointer and errno reporting, why atoi is unsafe, and tokenising input by hand without strtok.

topics.title: printf and scanf formatting
topics.description: Format specifiers and length modifiers, width and precision, the PRId64 macros for fixed-width types, and why scanf with %s is dangerous while fgets plus sscanf is the safer pattern.

topics.title: Return codes and errno
topics.description: C signals failure through return values: -1 or NULL plus a global errno, perror and strerror for messages, checking every call, and designing your own functions to return status separately from results.

subtopics.title: errno and when it is set

topics.title: Cleanup with goto and early return
topics.description: Handling multiple resources without exceptions: the single-exit pattern with goto labels that unwind in reverse order, initialising pointers to NULL so cleanup is always safe, and keeping error paths tested.

subtopics.title: Initialising to NULL for safe cleanup

topics.title: File I/O with stdio
topics.description: FILE * streams: fopen modes, fgets for lines, fread and fwrite for blocks, fseek and ftell, buffering and fflush, and always checking fclose because writes can fail at the end.

topics.title: Binary files and endianness
topics.description: Writing structs directly is fast but non-portable: padding, endianness and type sizes differ. Serialising field by field with fixed-width types and explicit byte order, and reading headers safely.

topics.title: Command-line arguments and environment
topics.description: argc and argv, parsing options with getopt, reading environment variables with getenv, exit codes and EXIT_FAILURE, and writing diagnostics to stderr so pipelines stay clean.

topics.title: Headers and translation units
topics.description: Each .c file compiles alone; headers carry declarations shared between them. Declaration versus definition, the one-definition rule, extern variables, inline functions in headers and what to keep private with static.

topics.title: Static and shared libraries
topics.description: Bundling object files into a .a archive linked at build time or a .so/.dll loaded at run time, -l and -L flags, link order, symbol visibility, and how the dynamic loader finds libraries.

topics.title: CMake for C projects
topics.description: Describing targets, sources, include directories and link dependencies in CMakeLists.txt, out-of-source builds, Debug and Release configurations, and finding system libraries with find_package.

topics.title: The C standard library map
topics.description: Knowing what exists so you do not rewrite it: stdlib for memory and conversion, string, stdio, math, time, ctype, assert, limits, stdint, stdbool and errno, and which functions are traps.

topics.title: C standards and portability
topics.description: What changed from C89 through C99, C11, C17 and C23 (mixed declarations, VLAs, _Generic, threads, nullptr, #embed), feature test macros for POSIX, and writing code that compiles cleanly on gcc, clang and MSVC.

topics.title: Designing C APIs
topics.description: Naming with a prefix, init and destroy pairs, returning status codes with out-parameters, const-correctness, avoiding hidden global state, and versioning headers so callers can depend on them.

topics.title: Generic code with void pointers and macros
topics.description: C has no templates, so generic containers pass void * with an element size, macros generate type-specific code, X macros keep enums and strings in sync, and _Generic dispatches on type.

topics.title: POSIX system calls
topics.description: Below stdio: open, read, write and close with file descriptors, short reads and writes, stat, directory listing, and mmap for mapping files into memory; what a system call costs versus a library call.

topics.title: Signals and time
topics.description: Registering handlers with sigaction, the tiny set of async-signal-safe functions, the volatile sig_atomic_t flag pattern, and measuring time with clock_gettime and monotonic clocks.

topics.title: Threads with pthreads
topics.description: Creating threads with pthread_create, passing arguments through a struct, joining and detaching, thread-local storage, and why sharing stack variables with a thread that outlives the function is a bug.

topics.title: Mutexes and condition variables
topics.description: Protecting shared state with pthread_mutex, spotting data races, waiting for a condition without spinning, the spurious-wakeup loop, and ordering locks to avoid deadlock.

topics.title: C11 atomics and memory ordering
topics.description: stdatomic.h for lock-free counters and flags, why volatile is not a synchronisation tool, acquire and release semantics, and the cases where seq_cst is the only ordering you should use.

topics.title: Processes, pipes and IPC
topics.description: fork to duplicate a process, exec to replace its image, wait to collect status, pipes and dup2 to connect stdout to stdin, and shared memory for higher-bandwidth inter-process communication.

topics.title: Unit testing in C
topics.description: Structuring code so functions are testable, a minimal assert-based harness, frameworks such as Unity, CMocka and Check, running tests from make or ctest, and testing failure paths with injected allocators.

subtopics.title: Test targets in make and ctest

topics.title: Debugging with gdb
topics.description: Breakpoints, stepping, printing variables and structs, backtraces after a segfault, watchpoints for corrupted values, examining memory, and loading core dumps to debug crashes after the fact.

topics.title: Sanitizers and Valgrind
topics.description: AddressSanitizer for overflows and use-after-free, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, ThreadSanitizer for races, and Valgrind memcheck for leaks on unmodified binaries: what each catches and its cost.

topics.title: Profiling with perf and gprof
topics.description: Measuring before optimising: sampling with perf, call-graph profiles with gprof, flame graphs, and separating hot loops from allocation overhead and I/O waits.

topics.title: Cache-friendly data layout
topics.description: Why memory access patterns dominate performance: cache lines, sequential versus random access, struct-of-arrays versus array-of-structs, false sharing between threads, and prefetch-friendly loops.

topics.title: Compiler optimisations, inline and restrict
topics.description: What -O2 and -O3 do, inline as a hint, restrict to promise no aliasing, link-time optimisation, reading generated assembly with -S or Compiler Explorer, and why UB-free code optimises better.

topics.title: Buffer overflows
topics.description: How writing past an array corrupts adjacent variables and return addresses, stack smashing, the gets and strcpy culprits, and the defences: bounded functions, stack canaries, ASLR and non-executable stacks.

topics.title: Integer overflow and signed-unsigned pitfalls
topics.description: Size calculations that wrap to small values, negative lengths becoming huge when converted to size_t, checked arithmetic with __builtin_add_overflow, and validating lengths before allocating or indexing.

topics.title: Format strings and input validation
topics.description: Why printf(user_input) lets attackers read and write memory, always using a literal format string, validating and bounding every external input, and treating file contents and network bytes as hostile.

subtopics.title: Treating file and network data as hostile

topics.title: Hardening flags and fuzzing
topics.description: Compiler defences (-fstack-protector, _FORTIFY_SOURCE, -D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS, PIE, RELRO), warnings as errors, static analysis with clang-tidy and cppcheck, and coverage-guided fuzzing with libFuzzer or AFL.

topics.title: Project: Unix shell
topics.description: Build a shell that reads a line, tokenises it, runs commands with fork and exec, supports pipes, redirection and background jobs, handles Ctrl-C without dying, and implements cd and exit as builtins.

topics.title: Project: HTTP server with sockets
topics.description: Write a static-file HTTP/1.0 server with socket, bind, listen and accept, parse request lines and headers safely, serve files with correct status codes and content types, and handle many clients with threads or poll.

topics.title: Project: memory allocator
topics.description: Implement malloc, free and realloc on top of sbrk or mmap with a free list, block headers, splitting and coalescing, alignment guarantees, and a test suite that compares against the system allocator.

topics.title: Project: persistent key-value store
topics.description: Build a command-line store that appends set and delete records to a log, rebuilds an in-memory hash table on start, compacts the log, and survives crashes mid-write thanks to checksums and fsync.

topics.title: Project: JSON parser
topics.description: Write a recursive-descent JSON parser producing a tagged-union value tree, with a tokenizer, UTF-8 string unescaping, number parsing, precise error positions, a serialiser back to text, and fuzz testing.

topics.title: C interview questions
topics.description: The questions that keep coming up: pointers versus arrays, malloc versus calloc, stack versus heap, undefined behaviour, static and extern, struct padding, const placement, volatile, and how C compares to C++ and Rust.

topics.title: Coding interviews in C
topics.description: Solving problems fast without a standard container library: hand-rolled stacks and queues, in-place array tricks, string reversal and two-pointer scans, bit manipulation, and managing memory without leaks under time pressure.

subtopics.title: Array and string manipulation in place

title: CI/CD
description: Continuous integration and delivery as engineers actually run it: pipeline anatomy, GitHub Actions in depth with GitLab CI and Jenkins for comparison, build, test and artifact stages, container image pipelines, security scanning, rolling, blue/green and canary deployments, GitOps, feature flags, versioning, pipeline performance and monorepos. Docker, Kubernetes and Terraform basics live in their own tracks.

code.label: shell, YAML, HCL or Dockerfile, whichever fits

categories.title: CI Principles and Pipeline Anatomy
categories.description: What a pipeline is for, what its stages are, and the working habits that make it pay off.

topics.title: Continuous integration principles
topics.description: Why integrating to a shared mainline many times a day with an automated build and test on every push catches conflicts and regressions in minutes instead of weeks, and the discipline (small commits, green builds, fix-forward first) that makes it work.

subtopics.title: CI versus CD versus continuous deployment

topics.title: Anatomy of a pipeline
topics.description: The stages almost every pipeline shares: checkout, dependency install, build, static checks, tests, packaging, publish and deploy, how they are ordered so cheap checks fail first, and how artifacts flow from one stage to the next.

subtopics.title: Triggers: push, PR, tag and schedule
Pipeline status as a merge gate

topics.title: Trunk-based development and branching for CI
topics.description: How trunk-based development with short-lived branches and pull requests keeps integration continuous, why long-lived release branches multiply merge pain, and how branch protection rules enforce that only green, reviewed code lands.

topics.title: Choosing a CI system
topics.description: The trade-offs between hosted (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Buildkite) and self-managed (Jenkins, Tekton) systems: runner control, cost per minute, ecosystem, secrets handling and lock-in, and how to evaluate one against your repository layout and compliance needs.

categories.title: GitHub Actions
categories.description: The most widely used hosted CI, from the first workflow file to reusable, cached, secure multi-job pipelines.

topics.title: Workflow files, triggers and events
topics.description: How a YAML file under .github/workflows declares when it runs (push, pull_request, schedule, workflow_dispatch, release), how filters on branches, paths and tags narrow it, and how the github context exposes the event payload to steps.

topics.title: Jobs, steps, runners and dependencies
topics.description: How jobs run in parallel on fresh runners unless needs: orders them, how steps share a filesystem but not a shell, how outputs pass between steps and jobs, and how runs-on picks ubuntu, windows, macos or a labelled self-hosted machine.

subtopics.title: Jobs run in parallel by default

topics.title: Matrix builds
topics.description: Running one job definition across combinations of versions, operating systems or shards with strategy.matrix, adding include and exclude entries for special cases, and using fail-fast and max-parallel to control cost and noise.

topics.title: Caching dependencies and build outputs
topics.description: How actions/cache keys a tarball on a hash of lockfiles, why restore-keys give partial hits, what the 10 GB per-repo limit and eviction mean, and when setup-node or setup-python built-in caching is enough versus caching Docker layers or Gradle outputs.

topics.title: Secrets, variables and OIDC to cloud
topics.description: Where repository, environment and organisation secrets live, how they are masked in logs, why fork PRs cannot read them, and how OIDC lets a job assume an AWS, Azure or GCP role with a short-lived token instead of storing long-lived keys.

topics.title: Reusable workflows and composite actions
topics.description: Two ways to stop copy-pasting YAML: reusable workflows called with workflow_call that run whole jobs with inputs and secrets, and composite actions that bundle steps, plus when to write a JavaScript or Docker action instead.

topics.title: Self-hosted runners and concurrency
topics.description: Registering runners on your own VMs or Kubernetes (actions-runner-controller), labelling and grouping them, why ephemeral runners are safer than persistent ones, and using concurrency groups to cancel superseded runs and serialise deployments.

categories.title: GitLab CI and Jenkins
categories.description: Enough of the two other big systems to read their pipelines, migrate between them and answer comparison questions.

topics.title: GitLab CI: stages, jobs and runners
topics.description: How .gitlab-ci.yml declares stages and jobs, how rules: and only/except select when jobs run, how GitLab runners with executors (shell, docker, kubernetes) pick up jobs, and how artifacts, cache and needs: build a DAG pipeline.

topics.title: GitLab environments, review apps and Auto DevOps
topics.description: How GitLab ties jobs to environments with deployment tracking and stop jobs, spins up per-merge-request review apps, protects production environments with approvals, and what Auto DevOps generates for you out of the box.

topics.title: Jenkins: pipelines, agents and shared libraries
topics.description: The controller-and-agent model, declarative versus scripted Jenkinsfile syntax, how stages, agents and post blocks work, how shared libraries centralise pipeline logic, and why plugin sprawl and controller upgrades are the main operational burden.

subtopics.title: Shared libraries with vars/ and src/

categories.title: Build, Test and Artifacts
categories.description: The stages that turn a commit into a verified, versioned, stored artifact.

topics.title: Build stages and reproducible builds
topics.description: Making a build produce the same output from the same input: pinned toolchains, lockfiles, hermetic containers, deterministic timestamps and build metadata (commit SHA, build number) embedded so any artifact can be traced back to its source.

subtopics.title: Building inside a fixed container image

topics.title: Test stages: unit, integration and end-to-end in CI
topics.description: Layering tests so unit tests gate every push, integration tests run against service containers (Postgres, Redis via services: or Testcontainers), and slower end-to-end suites run on merge or nightly, with reports published as JUnit XML and coverage.

topics.title: Flaky tests and test quarantine
topics.description: Why nondeterministic tests destroy trust in CI, how to detect them (rerun analysis, flake dashboards), the quarantine pattern that removes them from the merge gate without deleting them, and the usual root causes: shared state, timing, ordering and network.

topics.title: Artifact management and registries
topics.description: Storing build outputs in a versioned registry (Artifactory, Nexus, GitHub Packages, cloud artifact registries) rather than rebuilding per environment, retention and cleanup policies, immutability of released versions, and promoting one artifact through environments.

subtopics.title: Artifact registries: Artifactory, Nexus, GitHub Packages

topics.title: Container image pipelines
topics.description: Building images in CI with docker buildx or Kaniko, multi-stage Dockerfiles to keep runtime images small, layer caching via registry cache exports, tagging by commit SHA and semver, pinning deployments to digests, and multi-architecture builds. Dockerfile basics are in the Docker track.

categories.title: Security in the Pipeline
categories.description: Shifting scanning left and hardening the pipeline itself, which is now a prime attack target.

topics.title: SAST in the pipeline
topics.description: Static analysis with Semgrep, CodeQL, SonarQube or Bandit on every pull request, tuning rule sets to cut noise, surfacing findings as PR annotations, and choosing between blocking and advisory severities so the gate is respected rather than bypassed.

topics.title: Dependency and licence scanning
topics.description: Catching vulnerable or badly licensed third-party packages with Dependabot, Renovate, OSV-Scanner, Snyk or Trivy fs, automating upgrade pull requests, and handling the flood of alerts with severity thresholds, reachability and grouping.

topics.title: Container image scanning and SBOMs
topics.description: Scanning built images with Trivy or Grype for OS and language package CVEs, generating a software bill of materials with Syft in SPDX or CycloneDX, failing on critical findings, and choosing minimal base images (distroless, Alpine, Chainguard) to shrink the attack surface.

topics.title: Supply chain security: signing and provenance
topics.description: Signing images and artifacts with Sigstore cosign using keyless OIDC identities, attaching SLSA provenance attestations that record how and where the artifact was built, and verifying signatures at deploy time with admission policies.

topics.title: Hardening the pipeline itself
topics.description: Treating the pipeline as production: least-privilege tokens, pinning actions to commit SHAs, avoiding script injection through untrusted inputs like PR titles, isolating fork builds, protecting the runner, and auditing who can change workflow files.

categories.title: Deployment Strategies and Environments
categories.description: Getting the artifact into production safely, with a way back.

topics.title: Rolling deployments
topics.description: Replacing instances a few at a time so capacity never drops to zero, how maxSurge and maxUnavailable tune the pace, why readiness checks gate each step, and the version-skew window where old and new code run side by side.

topics.title: Blue/green deployments
topics.description: Running two full environments and switching traffic at the load balancer or DNS in one step, which gives instant rollback and no mixed versions at the cost of double capacity and careful handling of database and session state.

subtopics.title: Switching at load balancer or DNS

topics.title: Canary releases and progressive delivery
topics.description: Sending a small slice of traffic to the new version, comparing its error rate and latency against the baseline, and promoting or aborting automatically with Argo Rollouts or Flagger driven by Prometheus metrics.

subtopics.title: Traffic splitting by weight or header

topics.title: Environments, gates and approvals
topics.description: Modelling dev, staging and production as environments with their own secrets, protection rules, required reviewers and wait timers, so a deploy to production needs a human sign-off while lower environments deploy automatically.

subtopics.title: Audit trail of who approved what

topics.title: Database migrations in deployments
topics.description: Why schema changes are the hardest part of deploying: the expand-and-contract pattern for backward-compatible migrations, running migrations as a separate step or job before the app rolls out, and keeping rollback possible when data has changed.

topics.title: Rollbacks and hotfix paths
topics.description: Designing the way back before you need it: redeploying the previous artifact by version, automatic rollback on failed health checks, hotfix branches cut from the released tag, and the difference between rolling back code and rolling back a bad migration.

subtopics.title: Hotfix branch from a release tag

categories.title: GitOps, Feature Flags and Releases
categories.description: Declarative delivery, decoupling deploy from release, and versioning what you ship.

topics.title: GitOps delivery with Argo CD and Flux
topics.description: The GitOps model where a controller in the cluster continuously reconciles live state to manifests in a Git repo, so CI only updates a version in Git and the cluster pulls the change, giving an audit trail, drift detection and easy rollback via git revert.

topics.title: Feature flags and decoupling deploy from release
topics.description: Shipping code dark behind a flag so deployment and release are separate decisions, targeting rules and percentage rollouts, kill switches for incidents, the OpenFeature standard and tools like LaunchDarkly, Unleash and Flagsmith, and cleaning up stale flags.

topics.title: Semantic versioning and release tagging
topics.description: What major, minor and patch promise to consumers, how pre-release and build metadata work, why tags rather than branches mark releases, and how CI can derive the version from tags or from commit history.

subtopics.title: Git tags as the release marker

topics.title: Conventional commits and automated changelogs
topics.description: Structuring commit messages as feat:, fix: and BREAKING CHANGE so tools like semantic-release, release-please or git-cliff can compute the next version, write the changelog and cut the GitHub release without a human editing files.

topics.title: Publishing packages from CI
topics.description: Releasing libraries to npm, PyPI, Maven Central or a private registry from a tag-triggered workflow, using trusted publishing (OIDC) where the registry supports it, provenance attestations, and dry runs to catch a broken publish before it is immutable.

categories.title: Pipeline Engineering
categories.description: Making pipelines fast, testable and observable at scale.

topics.title: Pipeline performance and parallelism
topics.description: Finding where the minutes go with per-step timings, then cutting them: parallel jobs, test sharding, dependency and layer caching, shallow clones, skipping unchanged work, bigger runners for hot paths, and cancelling superseded runs.

topics.title: Monorepo pipelines
topics.description: Building only what changed in a repository with many packages: affected-graph tools (Nx, Turborepo, Bazel, Pants), path filters as a simpler first step, remote build caches, and one workflow that fans out into per-package jobs.

subtopics.title: Affected detection from the dependency graph
Path filters as a first step

topics.title: Testing pipeline-as-code
topics.description: Catching YAML mistakes before they hit main: actionlint and yamllint, running workflows locally with act, GitLab CI lint, Jenkins pipeline unit tests, and testing shared workflows in a sandbox repository before rolling them out.

topics.title: Pipeline observability and DORA metrics
topics.description: Exporting pipeline durations, failure rates and queue times to dashboards, tracing long builds, and reporting the four DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore) from pipeline and incident data to show whether delivery is improving.

subtopics.title: Deriving lead time from commits and deploys

topics.title: Ephemeral preview environments
topics.description: Spinning up a full environment per pull request with its own URL so reviewers and QA can test the change, using namespaces on Kubernetes or platforms like Vercel, tearing it down on close, and seeding data so the preview is useful.

categories.title: Projects and Interview Preparation
categories.description: End-to-end pipelines to build and the questions interviewers ask about them.

topics.title: Project: full GitHub Actions pipeline for a web service
topics.description: Build a workflow for a containerised API that lints, runs unit tests with a Postgres service container, builds a multi-arch image with registry caching, scans it with Trivy, signs it with cosign, pushes it by digest and deploys to a staging environment via OIDC with a required approval for production.

subtopics.title: Design the stages and job graph
Build, scan and sign the image

topics.title: Project: GitOps delivery with canary rollouts
topics.description: Set up a config repository watched by Argo CD, have CI bump the image tag with a commit, and deploy the service with an Argo Rollouts canary that promotes on a Prometheus error-rate query and aborts on failure, then demonstrate rollback with git revert.

subtopics.title: Create the config repo and Argo CD app
Automate the tag bump from CI
Write the Rollout and analysis template

topics.title: Project: monorepo pipeline with affected builds
topics.description: Take a monorepo of three services and two shared libraries, wire up Nx or Turborepo affected detection, fan out per-package jobs dynamically, add a remote cache, and show that a change to one library tests only its consumers while a docs-only change runs nothing.

subtopics.title: Set up the workspace and graph

topics.title: Project: automated releases with changelogs and package publishing
topics.description: Adopt conventional commits enforced by commitlint, use release-please to open release PRs that bump versions and write the changelog, publish the package to npm or PyPI with trusted publishing on merge, and attach provenance and a GitHub release with the built artifacts.

topics.title: CI/CD design questions
topics.description: How to answer design prompts like "design the delivery pipeline for a microservice platform": stages, gates, artifact flow, environments, deployment strategy, rollback, security scanning, and the trade-offs you would raise before choosing.

topics.title: CI/CD interview questions
topics.description: The questions engineers get asked about delivery: CI versus CD, how caching works, why build once and promote, how to handle secrets, flaky tests, migrations, GitOps versus push deploys, and how DORA metrics are measured.

title: Cloud Data Platforms
description: The managed building blocks of a cloud data platform across AWS, GCP and Azure: object storage and lakes, warehouses, lakehouses, managed orchestration and ETL, serverless query engines, streaming services, IAM, networking, cost control, infrastructure as code and migrations.

code.label: shell, SQL and Terraform, whichever fits

categories.title: Object Storage and Data Lakes
categories.description: The cheapest, most durable layer, and the foundation everything else reads from.

topics.title: S3, GCS and ADLS compared
topics.description: Object storage stores immutable blobs under keys with no real directories; the three providers differ in consistency history, hierarchical namespace (ADLS Gen2), storage classes and access APIs, but the lake patterns are the same.

topics.title: Lake layout: zones, prefixes and partitions
topics.description: Raw, cleaned and curated zones as separate prefixes or buckets, Hive-style partition paths (dt=2024-01-01), and naming that keeps listing cheap and access policies simple.

subtopics.title: Bucket per zone versus per domain

topics.title: File formats and table formats
topics.description: Parquet and ORC for columnar analytics, Avro for row-oriented streaming, and table formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Hudi) that add ACID transactions, schema evolution and time travel on top of files.

topics.title: Lifecycle rules, versioning and replication
topics.description: Lifecycle policies move objects to cold tiers and expire them, versioning protects against accidental deletes, and cross-region replication supports DR; each affects cost and must be set deliberately per zone.

topics.title: Working with storage from the shell
topics.description: aws s3, gsutil and gcloud storage, az storage: syncing folders, copying with parallelism, listing large prefixes efficiently, presigned URLs, and scripting uploads in CI.

categories.title: Cloud Data Warehouses
categories.description: Managed analytical databases and what makes each one different.

topics.title: Snowflake architecture and virtual warehouses
topics.description: Storage, compute and cloud services are separated; virtual warehouses are independent compute clusters sized by T-shirt sizes, billed per second while running, with auto-suspend and multi-cluster scaling.

topics.title: BigQuery: slots, partitioning and clustering
topics.description: Serverless with on-demand pricing per byte scanned or reserved slots; partitioning by date and clustering by columns cut bytes scanned, and the dry-run flag tells you cost before running.

topics.title: Redshift and Synapse
topics.description: Redshift as a provisioned or serverless MPP cluster with distribution and sort keys, Spectrum for querying S3; Synapse dedicated SQL pools with distribution styles and serverless pools over ADLS.

topics.title: Loading data into a warehouse
topics.description: Bulk loading from object storage (COPY INTO, LOAD DATA, COPY from S3), staged files, external tables, and streaming inserts; why bulk loads beat row inserts and how to make loads idempotent.

topics.title: Choosing a warehouse
topics.description: A comparison by pricing model, ecosystem fit, concurrency, governance features and lock-in; how to run a fair proof of concept with representative queries and data.

categories.title: Lakehouse Platforms
categories.description: Warehouse features on lake storage, mainly through Databricks.

topics.title: Databricks workspace and clusters
topics.description: Workspaces, notebooks, jobs, all-purpose versus job clusters, serverless compute and cluster policies; how the control plane and data plane split across the vendor and your cloud account.

topics.title: Delta Lake on Databricks
topics.description: Delta tables with ACID commits, MERGE, time travel, OPTIMIZE and Z-ORDER, VACUUM for old files, and change data feed; the medallion (bronze, silver, gold) layering it enables.

topics.title: Unity Catalog
topics.description: A cross-workspace catalogue with three-level namespaces, table and column grants, lineage capture, and external locations that map storage credentials to lake paths.

topics.title: Open table formats across engines
topics.description: Iceberg and Delta read by Spark, Trino, Snowflake, BigQuery and Athena; catalogues (Glue, Iceberg REST, Unity) as the shared metadata point; avoiding lock-in by choosing open formats.

subtopics.title: Catalogue as the point of truth

categories.title: Managed Orchestration and ETL Services
categories.description: The provider-native tools for moving and transforming data.

topics.title: AWS Glue
topics.description: Serverless Spark jobs, crawlers that populate the Glue Data Catalog, job bookmarks for incremental runs, and Glue Studio; DPU pricing and when a plain Spark job on EMR is cheaper.

topics.title: Google Cloud Dataflow and Dataproc
topics.description: Dataflow runs Apache Beam pipelines serverlessly for batch and streaming with autoscaling; Dataproc is managed Spark and Hadoop; templates and when to pick each.

topics.title: Azure Data Factory and Synapse pipelines
topics.description: Pipelines of activities with copy activity, mapping data flows on Spark, integration runtimes (Azure, self-hosted) for on-prem access, triggers and parameterisation.

topics.title: Managed Airflow and workflow services
topics.description: MWAA, Cloud Composer, Step Functions and Cloud Workflows: when a managed Airflow is worth its baseline cost, and when a lighter state-machine service fits event-driven glue.

topics.title: Serverless functions in data pipelines
topics.description: Lambda, Cloud Functions and Azure Functions triggered by storage events to validate, route or kick off jobs; limits on runtime and memory, and why heavy transforms belong elsewhere.

subtopics.title: Retries and dead-letter queues for functions

categories.title: Serverless Query Engines
categories.description: SQL directly on the lake, paying per query.

topics.title: Amazon Athena
topics.description: Presto/Trino-based SQL over S3 using the Glue Data Catalog, billed per TB scanned; partition projection, columnar formats and compression as the levers that make it cheap.

topics.title: Trino and Starburst
topics.description: A distributed SQL engine that federates across object storage, warehouses and databases through connectors; coordinator and workers, memory limits, and running it yourself versus managed.

topics.title: BigQuery external tables and BigLake
topics.description: Querying GCS files as external tables, BigLake for fine-grained access on lake data, and the performance gap between external and native tables.

topics.title: Query cost control and result caching
topics.description: Workgroups with per-query byte limits, result caching, materialised views, and query auditing so ad-hoc analysts cannot accidentally scan petabytes.

categories.title: Streaming Services
categories.description: Managed event ingestion without running Kafka yourself.

topics.title: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and Firehose
topics.description: Shards as the unit of throughput and ordering, on-demand versus provisioned capacity, enhanced fan-out consumers, and Firehose for delivering streams to S3, Redshift or OpenSearch with buffering.

topics.title: Google Pub/Sub
topics.description: Topics and subscriptions with at-least-once delivery, ack deadlines, ordering keys, dead-letter topics, and Pub/Sub to BigQuery subscriptions that skip a pipeline entirely.

topics.title: Azure Event Hubs
topics.description: Partitioned event ingestion with a Kafka-compatible endpoint, consumer groups, throughput units, capture to storage, and its place next to Service Bus for messaging.

topics.title: Managed Kafka: MSK and Confluent Cloud
topics.description: MSK provisioned and serverless, Confluent Cloud with Schema Registry and connectors included; comparing operational burden, pricing per throughput and feature sets against native services.

categories.title: Identity, Access and Networking
categories.description: Locking the platform down without blocking the people who need it.

topics.title: IAM for data services
topics.description: Principals, roles and policies; service accounts and instance roles for jobs instead of keys; least-privilege policies scoped to bucket prefixes, datasets or tables, and how to read a deny.

topics.title: Warehouse access control
topics.description: Role hierarchies in Snowflake, dataset and table IAM in BigQuery, row and column level security, dynamic data masking, and mapping business roles to warehouse roles.

topics.title: Encryption and key management
topics.description: Encryption at rest by default, customer-managed keys in KMS, Cloud KMS or Key Vault for compliance, TLS in transit, and what key rotation and revocation actually do to data access.

topics.title: Networking for data services
topics.description: VPCs and subnets, private endpoints to storage and warehouses so traffic never crosses the internet, NAT and egress costs, and firewall rules for Spark clusters reaching databases.

categories.title: Cost Management
categories.description: The bill is a design input, not an afterthought.

topics.title: Where data platform money goes
topics.description: Compute hours, bytes scanned, storage tiers, egress, and idle resources; reading the billing export and tagging resources so cost can be attributed to teams and pipelines.

topics.title: Optimising compute spend
topics.description: Auto-suspend and right-sizing warehouses, job clusters and spot instances for Spark, reserved capacity for steady workloads, and scheduling heavy jobs off-peak.

topics.title: Optimising storage and query spend
topics.description: Columnar formats, partitioning, clustering, lifecycle tiers, compaction, and query patterns that avoid SELECT * so bytes scanned and stored both shrink.

topics.title: Budgets, alerts and FinOps practices
topics.description: Budgets with alerts, anomaly detection, showback reports per team, and a monthly review loop that turns cost findings into pipeline changes.

categories.title: Infrastructure as Code and Migration
categories.description: Repeatable platforms and moving onto them.

topics.title: Terraform for data platforms
topics.description: Providers for AWS, GCP, Azure, Snowflake and Databricks; modules for buckets, IAM, warehouses and clusters; remote state, workspaces per environment and plan review in pull requests.

topics.title: Environments and promotion
topics.description: Dev, staging and prod platforms from the same modules with different variables; separate accounts or projects for blast radius, and promoting changes through pull requests.

topics.title: Migration patterns
topics.description: Lift-and-shift, re-platform and rebuild; running old and new in parallel with reconciliation, migrating consumers last, and cutover with a rollback path.

topics.title: On-premises to cloud data movement
topics.description: Bulk transfer services (Snowball, Transfer Appliance, Data Box), online transfer with DataSync or Storage Transfer Service, database migration services with CDC, and bandwidth maths.

topics.title: Project: a lake and Athena stack in Terraform
topics.description: Provision raw and curated S3 buckets with lifecycle rules, a Glue database and crawler, an Athena workgroup with a byte limit, and IAM roles for a loader and an analyst, then load sample data and query it.

subtopics.title: Scope IAM for loader and analyst

topics.title: Project: BigQuery warehouse with cost controls
topics.description: Create datasets per environment, partitioned and clustered tables loaded from GCS, a scheduled query for a daily aggregate, custom quotas and a budget alert, and a report of bytes billed before and after clustering.

topics.title: Project: streaming ingestion with Kinesis and Firehose
topics.description: A producer script writes events to a Kinesis stream, Firehose converts them to Parquet partitioned by hour into S3, a Glue table exposes them, and a Lambda validates each batch and reports bad records.

topics.title: Project: lakehouse medallion on Databricks
topics.description: Bronze, silver and gold Delta tables from raw JSON with a job cluster, Unity Catalog grants for two groups, OPTIMIZE and VACUUM scheduled, and a comparison of query time before and after Z-ORDER.

topics.title: Cloud data platform interview questions
topics.description: Comparing warehouses, lake versus lakehouse, when to use Glue, Dataflow or Data Factory, IAM least privilege, cost levers, private networking, and how you have run a migration.

topics.title: Designing a platform in an interview
topics.description: Given a company profile, sketch the storage, ingestion, processing, serving and governance layers on one cloud, with the services chosen, the IAM model, the cost model and the migration path defended.
