title: Computer Vision
description: Images as arrays through classical filtering, CNNs, detection, segmentation, vision transformers and CLIP, with the datasets, labelling, evaluation and deployment work that turns a model into a working vision system.

code.label: Python with the usual libraries (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, torch)

categories.title: Images as Data
categories.description: What a picture is once it is in memory.

topics.title: Images as NumPy arrays
topics.description: A raster image is a height by width by channels array of integers or floats; how indexing, slicing, dtype and value range (0-255 versus 0-1) work, and why channel order (HWC versus CHW, RGB versus BGR) causes so many bugs.

topics.title: Colour spaces and channels
topics.description: RGB, grayscale, HSV and LAB and what each separates: HSV isolates hue for colour-based masking, LAB approximates perceptual distance, and grayscale conversion weights channels by luminance.

topics.title: Loading and manipulating images with OpenCV and PIL
topics.description: Reading, resizing, cropping, rotating and saving images with OpenCV and Pillow, how interpolation choices change results, and converting between PIL, NumPy and torch tensors without silent channel or range errors.

topics.title: Histograms and contrast
topics.description: Counting pixel intensities to understand exposure, stretching and equalising histograms to improve contrast, and CLAHE for local equalisation that does not blow out bright regions.

categories.title: Classical Image Processing
categories.description: Filters and geometry that still power preprocessing and simple pipelines.

topics.title: Convolution and filtering kernels
topics.description: Sliding a small kernel over an image to blur, sharpen or detect structure: box and Gaussian blur, padding modes, separable filters and why this is the same operation a CNN learns.

topics.title: Edge detection with Sobel and Canny
topics.description: Gradients as edge evidence: Sobel operators estimate horizontal and vertical derivatives, magnitude and direction combine them, and Canny adds non-maximum suppression and hysteresis thresholds for thin, connected edges.

topics.title: Geometric transforms and warping
topics.description: Translation, rotation, scaling, affine and perspective transforms as matrices, applying them with cv2.warpAffine and warpPerspective, and using homographies to rectify documents or stitch panoramas.

topics.title: Thresholding and morphology
topics.description: Turning grayscale into binary masks with global, Otsu and adaptive thresholds, then cleaning them with erosion, dilation, opening and closing, and extracting connected components and contours.

topics.title: Feature descriptors and matching
topics.description: Keypoint detectors and descriptors (SIFT, ORB) that describe local patches invariantly to scale and rotation, matching them between images with ratio tests, and RANSAC to reject bad matches when estimating a transform.

categories.title: Convolutional Networks
categories.description: The architectures that learn their own filters.

topics.title: Convolution layers, receptive fields and pooling
topics.description: How stacked convolutions grow the receptive field, what stride, padding and dilation do to output size, and why pooling and strided convolutions trade resolution for invariance and compute.

topics.title: Building a CNN in PyTorch
topics.description: Assembling nn.Conv2d, BatchNorm2d, ReLU and pooling into a classifier, writing the training loop with DataLoader, and checking shapes, parameter counts and a first overfit on a tiny batch.

subtopics.title: Overfitting a single batch as a check

topics.title: ResNet and residual connections
topics.description: Skip connections let a block learn a residual on top of identity, which makes very deep networks trainable; bottleneck blocks, downsampling shortcuts and the ResNet-18 to ResNet-152 family.

topics.title: EfficientNet and compound scaling
topics.description: Scaling depth, width and resolution together with a single coefficient, the MBConv block with squeeze-and-excitation, and the accuracy-per-FLOP curve that made EfficientNet a default backbone.

topics.title: MobileNet and depthwise separable convolutions
topics.description: Splitting a convolution into a per-channel depthwise pass and a 1x1 pointwise mix cuts compute by roughly the kernel area, which is how MobileNet and similar models run on phones.

categories.title: Training Vision Models
categories.description: The recipes that separate a paper result from a stalled run.

topics.title: Data augmentation
topics.description: Random crops, flips, colour jitter, RandAugment, Mixup and CutMix as regularisers that teach invariances, applied with torchvision transforms or Albumentations, and the augmentations that break for certain tasks.

topics.title: Transfer learning and fine-tuning
topics.description: Starting from ImageNet-pretrained weights, replacing the head, choosing between freezing the backbone and fine-tuning end to end, using lower learning rates for pretrained layers, and matching the normalisation statistics.

subtopics.title: Pretrained backbones from timm and torchvision

topics.title: Learning rate schedules and training recipes
topics.description: Warmup, cosine decay and one-cycle schedules, label smoothing, weight decay and EMA weights: the standard modern recipe and how to find a learning rate with a range test.

topics.title: Class imbalance and label noise
topics.description: Weighted sampling, class-weighted losses and focal loss for rare classes, and finding mislabelled images with loss ranking or confident-learning tools before they poison training.

topics.title: Mixed precision and GPU throughput
topics.description: torch.autocast and GradScaler for float16 or bfloat16 training, channels_last memory format, DataLoader workers and pinned memory, and profiling to find whether the GPU or the input pipeline is the bottleneck.

categories.title: Image Classification
categories.description: The first task and still the backbone of the rest.

topics.title: Multi-class and multi-label classification
topics.description: Softmax with cross-entropy for one label per image versus sigmoid with binary cross-entropy for several, building the dataset and loss for each, and choosing thresholds per label.

topics.title: Fine-grained recognition and metric learning
topics.description: When classes differ by tiny details (bird species, product SKUs) or new classes appear constantly, train an embedding with triplet or ArcFace loss and classify by nearest neighbour instead of a fixed head.

topics.title: Self-supervised pretraining
topics.description: Learning visual features without labels: contrastive methods (SimCLR, MoCo), self-distillation (DINO) and masked autoencoders (MAE), and when self-supervised backbones beat ImageNet weights for your domain.

categories.title: Object Detection
categories.description: Finding what is where.

topics.title: Bounding boxes, anchors and NMS
topics.description: Box formats (xyxy, xywh, normalised), anchor boxes as priors for regression, IoU for matching predictions to ground truth, and non-maximum suppression to collapse duplicate detections.

topics.title: Two-stage detectors: Faster R-CNN
topics.description: A region proposal network suggests candidate boxes, RoI pooling or RoIAlign crops features for each, and a second head classifies and refines them; accurate, slower, and available in torchvision.

topics.title: One-stage detectors: YOLO and RetinaNet
topics.description: Predicting classes and boxes directly from a grid of feature cells in a single pass, the anchor-free heads of recent YOLO versions, and focal loss in RetinaNet to handle the flood of background cells.

topics.title: DETR and transformer-based detection
topics.description: Treating detection as set prediction: learned object queries attend over image features, Hungarian matching pairs predictions with targets, and NMS disappears; the convergence fixes in Deformable DETR and RT-DETR.

topics.title: Training a detector on a custom dataset
topics.description: Converting annotations to the format a framework expects, fine-tuning an Ultralytics YOLO or torchvision Faster R-CNN, validating mAP, and the common failures: wrong box normalisation, class id offsets, tiny objects.

categories.title: Segmentation
categories.description: Labelling every pixel.

topics.title: Semantic segmentation with U-Net and DeepLab
topics.description: Predicting a class per pixel with an encoder-decoder, the U-Net skip connections that recover fine detail, atrous convolutions in DeepLab for wide context, and per-pixel cross-entropy training.

topics.title: Instance segmentation with Mask R-CNN
topics.description: Extending Faster R-CNN with a mask head that predicts a binary mask per detected object, RoIAlign to keep masks pixel-accurate, and how instance differs from semantic and panoptic segmentation.

topics.title: Promptable segmentation with Segment Anything
topics.description: SAM segments any object from a point, box or mask prompt using a heavy image encoder and a light prompt decoder; using it for zero-shot masks, fast annotation and as a component in pipelines.

topics.title: Segmentation losses
topics.description: Cross-entropy alone fails on small foregrounds; Dice and IoU losses optimise overlap directly, combined losses stabilise training, and boundary-aware losses sharpen edges.

categories.title: Vision Transformers and Multimodal Models
categories.description: Attention replaces convolution, and text joins the picture.

topics.title: ViT: patches as tokens
topics.description: Splitting an image into 16x16 patches, linearly embedding each as a token with a position embedding, and running a standard transformer encoder; why ViT needs lots of data or strong pretraining to beat CNNs.

topics.title: Swin and hierarchical vision transformers
topics.description: Windowed attention with shifted windows keeps cost linear in image size while building a feature pyramid, which makes Swin a drop-in backbone for detection and segmentation.

topics.title: CLIP and contrastive image-text pretraining
topics.description: Training an image encoder and a text encoder so matching pairs have high cosine similarity across a batch, which yields a shared embedding space usable for retrieval and zero-shot classification.

topics.title: Zero-shot classification and retrieval with CLIP
topics.description: Classifying by comparing an image embedding with text embeddings of prompts like "a photo of a {label}", prompt ensembling, and building image search where the query is text or another image.

topics.title: Vision-language models
topics.description: Models that generate text from images (BLIP-2, LLaVA, PaliGemma): a vision encoder, a projector and a language model, used for captioning, visual question answering and document understanding.

subtopics.title: Vision encoder plus projector plus LLM

categories.title: Evaluation
categories.description: Metrics that match the task.

topics.title: Intersection over union
topics.description: IoU as the overlap ratio between predicted and true regions for boxes and masks, computing it correctly with edge cases, and choosing the IoU threshold that defines a true positive.

topics.title: Precision-recall curves and mAP
topics.description: Ranking detections by confidence, tracing precision against recall, averaging precision per class and across IoU thresholds as in COCO mAP@[.5:.95], and reading the metrics tools like pycocotools print.

subtopics.title: COCO mAP at multiple IoU thresholds

topics.title: Segmentation metrics
topics.description: Pixel accuracy is dominated by background; mean IoU per class and Dice reflect what matters, boundary F-score captures edge quality, and panoptic quality combines recognition and segmentation.

topics.title: Classification metrics, calibration and error analysis
topics.description: Top-1 and top-5 accuracy, confusion matrices and per-class recall, calibration with reliability diagrams and temperature scaling, and Grad-CAM to see what the model looked at when it was wrong.

categories.title: Datasets and Labelling
categories.description: Where the real cost of a vision project lives.

topics.title: Standard datasets and benchmarks
topics.description: ImageNet, COCO, Pascal VOC, Cityscapes and Open Images: what each labels, their licences, and how to load them through torchvision or Hugging Face datasets for pretraining and benchmarking.

subtopics.title: ImageNet and its role in pretraining

topics.title: Annotation formats
topics.description: COCO JSON with images, annotations and categories arrays, Pascal VOC XML per image, YOLO txt per image, and mask formats (PNG index masks, RLE); converting between them without losing boxes.

subtopics.title: Mask encodings: index PNG and RLE

topics.title: Labelling tools and workflows
topics.description: Setting up CVAT or Label Studio, writing guidelines with examples of hard cases, model-assisted pre-labelling with SAM or a current model, review passes and measuring annotator agreement.

topics.title: Dataset quality, bias and splits
topics.description: Duplicate and near-duplicate leakage between splits, splitting by scene or capture session rather than by image, spotting spurious correlations (backgrounds, watermarks) and checking coverage across conditions.

categories.title: Deployment Considerations
categories.description: From a notebook to a camera feed.

topics.title: Exporting models with TorchScript and ONNX
topics.description: Tracing or scripting a model, exporting to ONNX with dynamic batch axes, verifying outputs match, and running with ONNX Runtime or TensorRT; the ops and preprocessing steps that do not export.

topics.title: Quantisation and pruning for edge devices
topics.description: Post-training and quantisation-aware int8 to shrink and speed up models, structured pruning, and the accuracy checks needed before shipping to phones, Jetson boards or browsers.

topics.title: Real-time video pipelines
topics.description: Decoding frames, batching or skipping to hit a frame budget, running detection then tracking (ByteTrack, DeepSORT) to keep identities, and measuring end-to-end latency including preprocessing.

topics.title: Monitoring vision models in production
topics.description: Detecting drift in image statistics, lighting and camera changes, logging low-confidence samples for relabelling, and closing the loop with periodic retraining and shadow evaluation.

topics.title: Project: image classifier with transfer learning
topics.description: Fine-tune a pretrained ResNet or EfficientNet on a small custom dataset, use augmentation and a cosine schedule, report accuracy with a confusion matrix and Grad-CAM, and export to ONNX with a script that runs on a folder.

topics.title: Project: custom object detector
topics.description: Label a few hundred images in CVAT for two or three classes, train an Ultralytics YOLO model, evaluate mAP per class, run it on a webcam stream with a tracker, and document what failed and why.

subtopics.title: Label and export in YOLO format

topics.title: Project: background removal service
topics.description: Build a segmentation model or use SAM plus a matting refinement to cut subjects from photos, expose it as an API that returns a PNG with alpha, and measure IoU and edge quality on a held-out set.

subtopics.title: Serve as an API with alpha output

topics.title: Project: CLIP-powered image search
topics.description: Embed a photo collection with CLIP, store vectors in FAISS, support text and image queries, add zero-shot tag suggestions, and build a small web UI that returns results in under a second.

topics.title: Computer vision interview questions
topics.description: Receptive fields and output sizes, why ResNets train, one-stage versus two-stage detectors, how NMS and mAP work, CNN versus ViT trade-offs, and how to handle small data and class imbalance.

topics.title: Practical vision coding exercises
topics.description: Implement IoU and NMS in NumPy, compute conv output shapes by hand, write a Dataset class with augmentation, and debug a training run whose loss is flat or whose validation accuracy is stuck at chance.

title: C++
description: Modern C++ from the compiler flags up: value semantics, RAII and smart pointers, classes and templates, the STL and ranges, move semantics, C++11 to C++23 features, multithreading, performance engineering, competitive programming, and projects such as a vector clone, a thread pool and an HTTP server.

categories.title: Environment and Tooling
categories.description: A modern compiler, a build system and the tools that catch mistakes before you run.

topics.title: Installing a compiler and CMake
topics.description: Getting gcc, clang or MSVC with C++20 support, installing CMake and Ninja, checking versions, and choosing the standard with -std=c++20 so the features you learn actually compile.

subtopics.title: gcc, clang and MSVC support levels
Verifying the setup with a test build

topics.title: Compilation model and compiler flags
topics.description: Translation units, headers pasted by the preprocessor, object files and linking, plus the flags that matter: -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic, -O2 versus -O0 -g, and why a warning-free build is the baseline.

topics.title: Editors, formatters and static tools
topics.description: clang-format for one canonical style, clang-tidy for modernisation and bug checks, compile_commands.json so editors understand the build, and language servers like clangd for navigation and diagnostics.

topics.title: Anatomy of a C++ program
topics.description: main, #include <iostream>, namespaces and using declarations, std::cout versus printf, and the split between declarations in headers and definitions in source files that shapes every project.

topics.title: Fundamental types, auto and initialisation
topics.description: Integer and floating types, bool and char, brace initialisation that rejects narrowing, the difference between int x; int x{}; and int x = 0;, and auto for deduced types without losing readability.

topics.title: const, constexpr and references
topics.description: const for values that must not change, constexpr for values computed at compile time, lvalue references as aliases, const references for cheap read-only parameters, and why references cannot be reseated.

topics.title: Operators and expressions
topics.description: Arithmetic and integer division, bitwise operators, precedence, integer promotion and mixed signed-unsigned comparisons, the three-way comparison operator <=>, and the sequencing rules that make some expressions undefined.

topics.title: Conditions, switch and init-statements
topics.description: if/else and switch, C++17 if-with-initialiser to scope a variable to the condition, if constexpr for compile-time branches, enum class in switch, and [[fallthrough]] to mark intentional fallthrough.

topics.title: Loops and range-for
topics.description: for, while and do-while, range-based for over containers and arrays, choosing auto, auto& or const auto& in the loop head to avoid copies, and iterating with indices when you need the position.

subtopics.title: break, continue and labels via flags

topics.title: Functions, overloading and default arguments
topics.description: Declaring and defining functions, overload resolution by parameter types, default arguments, inline and constexpr functions, trailing return types, and [[nodiscard]] to stop callers ignoring results.

topics.title: Lambdas and captures
topics.description: Anonymous function objects: capture by value or reference, mutable lambdas, generic lambdas with auto parameters, storing lambdas in std::function versus templates, and the dangling-reference capture trap.

subtopics.title: Capture by value and by reference

topics.title: Raw pointers, arrays and the free store
topics.description: Addresses, dereferencing and nullptr, C-style arrays and decay, new and delete with their array forms, and why every raw new is a leak waiting to happen when an exception or early return skips delete.

topics.title: RAII and deterministic destruction
topics.description: Resource Acquisition Is Initialisation: acquire in the constructor, release in the destructor, and let scope exit, including exceptions, clean up. The idiom behind smart pointers, lock guards and file streams.

topics.title: unique_ptr
topics.description: Sole ownership with zero overhead: make_unique, move-only semantics, transferring ownership through returns and parameters, custom deleters, and how it replaces almost every new/delete pair.

topics.title: shared_ptr and weak_ptr
topics.description: Reference-counted shared ownership with make_shared, the control block and its atomic cost, weak_ptr to break cycles and observe without owning, and why shared_ptr is not the default choice.

topics.title: Rule of zero, three and five
topics.description: If a class manages a resource it needs a destructor, copy and move operations; if it uses RAII members it needs none. The rule of zero as the goal, =default and =delete, and what the compiler generates.

topics.title: Classes, constructors and destructors
topics.description: Members, access specifiers, member initialiser lists, delegating and explicit constructors, static members, and const member functions that document which operations observe versus mutate.

subtopics.title: Access specifiers and struct versus class

topics.title: Copy and move semantics
topics.description: Copy constructors and assignment that duplicate resources, move constructors that steal them, rvalue references, std::move as a cast, and the moved-from state a class must leave valid.

topics.title: Operator overloading
topics.description: Making types feel built-in: arithmetic and comparison operators, member versus free functions, operator<< for streams, defaulted <=> and ==, subscript and call operators, and the operators you should not overload.

topics.title: Inheritance and virtual functions
topics.description: Public inheritance as is-a, virtual dispatch through vtables, override and final, virtual destructors for polymorphic deletion, and object slicing when a derived object is copied into a base.

topics.title: Abstract classes and interfaces
topics.description: Pure virtual functions to define interfaces, factories returning unique_ptr<Base>, dependency injection through interfaces for testability, and dynamic_cast as a last resort.

topics.title: Value semantics and composition
topics.description: C++ prefers values to hierarchies: types that copy and compare like ints, composition over inheritance, std::variant as a closed alternative to virtual dispatch, and where polymorphism still earns its place.

topics.title: Function and class templates
topics.description: Writing code once for many types: template parameters, instantiation on use, why definitions live in headers, non-type template parameters, and how the compiler type-checks at instantiation time.

topics.title: Specialisation and argument deduction
topics.description: Full and partial specialisation to customise templates for particular types, how arguments are deduced from calls, class template argument deduction in C++17, and when overloading beats specialisation.

topics.title: Variadic templates and fold expressions
topics.description: Parameter packs that accept any number of arguments, expanding packs with ..., fold expressions for sums and prints, sizeof..., and perfect forwarding of packs into constructors and emplace.

topics.title: Concepts and constraints
topics.description: C++20 concepts express what a template requires, turning pages of instantiation errors into one clear message: requires clauses, standard concepts, defining your own, and constrained auto.

topics.title: Type traits and SFINAE
topics.description: Inspecting and transforming types at compile time with <type_traits>, substitution failure as an overload filter, enable_if and void_t idioms in pre-C++20 code, and reading the older library code you will meet.

topics.title: constexpr and compile-time programming
topics.description: constexpr functions and variables that run at compile time, consteval for immediate functions, constexpr containers and algorithms in C++20, and using static_assert to check computed values.

topics.title: Sequence containers
topics.description: std::vector as the default container with its capacity and reallocation rules, std::array for fixed sizes, deque for both ends, list and forward_list for stable nodes, and iterator invalidation on each.

topics.title: Associative containers and hashing
topics.description: map and set as balanced trees with ordered iteration, unordered_map and unordered_set with hashing, custom comparators and hash functions, heterogeneous lookup, and the try_emplace and insert_or_assign helpers.

topics.title: Iterators and iterator categories
topics.description: The glue between containers and algorithms: begin and end, input through random-access categories and what each allows, iterator adaptors like back_inserter and reverse_iterator, and writing an iterator for your type.

topics.title: Algorithms
topics.description: The <algorithm> and <numeric> toolkit: sort, stable_sort and partial_sort, find_if and count_if, transform and accumulate, the erase-remove idiom and its C++20 replacement, and binary search on sorted ranges.

topics.title: Ranges and views
topics.description: C++20 ranges: algorithms that take whole containers, lazy views such as filter, transform and take composed with |, projections, and how views avoid building intermediate containers.

topics.title: Utilities: pair, tuple, optional and variant
topics.description: Vocabulary types for values without custom structs: pair and tuple with structured bindings, optional for maybe-a-value, variant with std::visit for type-safe unions, and any for the rare open case.

topics.title: std::string and string_view
topics.description: Owning strings with small-string optimisation, non-owning string_view for parameters and slices, the dangling view trap, substr and find, and converting to and from C strings.

topics.title: Text conversions and parsing
topics.description: Numbers to text and back with to_string, stoi and the faster, locale-free from_chars and to_chars, splitting strings, std::regex for patterns and its performance cost, and character classification.

topics.title: Streams, files and formatting
topics.description: ifstream and ofstream, reading lines with getline, stringstream for parsing, stream state and error checking, std::format for type-safe formatting and std::print in C++23 as the modern replacement for iostream output.

topics.title: Exceptions: throw, try and catch
topics.description: Throwing objects derived from std::exception, catching by const reference, the standard exception hierarchy, stack unwinding and destructors, and rethrowing with throw; to preserve the original.

topics.title: Exception safety and noexcept
topics.description: The basic, strong and no-throw guarantees, why destructors and move operations should be noexcept, how vector chooses copy over move when a move may throw, and designing functions so partial failure leaves state valid.

topics.title: Error codes, optional and expected
topics.description: When exceptions are the wrong tool: returning std::optional for absent values, std::error_code for system errors, and C++23 std::expected<T, E> that carries a value or an error in one type.

subtopics.title: Monadic operations on optional and expected

topics.title: Assertions and static_assert
topics.description: assert for runtime invariants stripped in release builds, static_assert for compile-time checks on types and constants, [[assume]] and contracts as they arrive, and where validation belongs instead of assertions.

topics.title: Headers, the ODR and linking
topics.description: Include guards and #pragma once, the one-definition rule and inline variables, forward declarations to cut compile times, static versus shared libraries, and reading undefined-reference linker errors.

topics.title: C++20 modules
topics.description: Named modules that replace textual inclusion: export declarations, module partitions, import std, compiler and CMake support, and why modules cut build times and stop macro leakage.

topics.title: CMake for C++ projects
topics.description: Targets with sources, include directories and compile features, PUBLIC and PRIVATE propagation, presets, tests with CTest, and structuring a repository with libraries, executables and tests.

topics.title: vcpkg, Conan and dependencies
topics.description: Fetching third-party libraries reproducibly: vcpkg manifests and Conan recipes integrated with CMake, versions and lock files, FetchContent for small dependencies, and building in CI from a clean machine.

topics.title: std::thread and jthread
topics.description: Launching threads with callables and arguments, join versus detach, C++20 jthread that joins automatically and supports stop tokens, thread_local storage and hardware_concurrency.

topics.title: Mutexes and lock guards
topics.description: Data races and why they are undefined behaviour, std::mutex with lock_guard and unique_lock, scoped_lock for several mutexes without deadlock, shared_mutex for readers, and keeping critical sections small.

topics.title: Condition variables and producer-consumer
topics.description: Waiting for a state change without spinning: condition_variable with a predicate to handle spurious wakeups, notify_one versus notify_all, and a thread-safe bounded queue as the building block for pipelines.

topics.title: Atomics and the memory model
topics.description: std::atomic for lock-free counters and flags, compare_exchange loops, memory orders from relaxed to seq_cst, acquire-release pairs, and why most code should use the default ordering.

topics.title: async, futures and parallel algorithms
topics.description: std::async and futures for returning results from background work, promise for hand-off, packaged_task, the launch policy trap, and execution policies that parallelise standard algorithms.

topics.title: Coroutines
topics.description: C++20 coroutines as a language mechanism: co_await, co_yield and co_return, the promise_type and awaitable protocol, writing a generator, and why libraries like cppcoro and std::generator in C++23 supply the usable pieces.

topics.title: C++11 and C++14 essentials
topics.description: The features that reset the language: auto, range-for, nullptr, enum class, uniform initialisation, lambdas, smart pointers, move semantics, generic lambdas and make_unique, and the older idioms they replace.

subtopics.title: C++14 generic lambdas and return deduction

topics.title: C++17 essentials
topics.description: Structured bindings, if constexpr, inline variables, std::optional, variant and string_view, std::filesystem, class template argument deduction, and parallel algorithms.

topics.title: C++20 essentials
topics.description: Concepts, ranges, coroutines and modules as the big four, plus the spaceship operator, designated initialisers, std::span, std::format, consteval and constinit, and jthread.

topics.title: C++23 additions
topics.description: std::expected, std::print and println, deducing this, std::mdspan for multidimensional views, std::generator, flat_map and flat_set, and if consteval, with notes on compiler support.

topics.title: Move semantics in depth and copy elision
topics.description: Value categories (lvalue, prvalue, xvalue), when the compiler moves automatically, return value optimisation and why std::move on a return is a pessimisation, forwarding references and perfect forwarding.

subtopics.title: Pass by value and move idiom

topics.title: Cache-friendly design and allocation strategy
topics.description: Contiguous data beats pointer chasing: struct-of-arrays layouts, avoiding per-element allocation, reserve, small buffer optimisation, polymorphic memory resources and arena allocators for hot paths.

subtopics.title: Struct of arrays versus array of structs

topics.title: Profiling, benchmarking and reading assembly
topics.description: Measuring first with perf, Instruments or VTune, microbenchmarks with Google Benchmark and the pitfalls of dead-code elimination, and using Compiler Explorer to see what the optimiser did to your code.

topics.title: Unit testing with GoogleTest and Catch2
topics.description: Writing test cases and assertions, fixtures and parameterised tests, running with CTest, mocking interfaces with GoogleMock, and structuring code so logic is testable without I/O.

topics.title: Debugging with gdb and lldb
topics.description: Breakpoints and stepping, printing STL containers with pretty printers, backtraces through templates and lambdas, watchpoints, core dumps, and debugging optimised builds.

topics.title: Sanitizers, static analysis and fuzzing
topics.description: AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and ThreadSanitizer builds in CI, clang-tidy and cppcheck for static findings, and libFuzzer harnesses for parsers and decoders.

topics.title: Undefined behaviour and lifetime bugs
topics.description: Dangling references from temporaries, iterator invalidation, signed overflow, out-of-bounds access, uninitialised reads, and how the optimiser exploits UB to produce code that seems impossible.

topics.title: Secure coding in C++
topics.description: Bounds-checked access with at and span, avoiding C-style buffers, integer overflow checks, validating untrusted input, hardened builds with _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS and stack protectors, and the C++ Core Guidelines.

subtopics.title: Replacing C buffers with span and string_view

topics.title: Project: std::vector clone
topics.description: Implement a Vector<T> with capacity growth, placement new and manual destruction, strong exception safety on push_back, move-aware reallocation, iterators that work with standard algorithms, and a GoogleTest suite.

topics.title: Project: thread pool and job scheduler
topics.description: Build a fixed-size thread pool with a thread-safe task queue, futures for results, graceful shutdown with jthread and stop tokens, task priorities, and a benchmark against std::async.

topics.title: Project: HTTP server
topics.description: Write an HTTP/1.1 server with non-blocking sockets and epoll or Asio, a safe request parser, routing, static files and keep-alive, RAII wrappers for every OS handle, and load tests under sanitizers.

subtopics.title: Event loop with epoll or Asio

topics.title: Project: expression evaluator
topics.description: Build a calculator that tokenises input, parses with precedence climbing into a variant-based AST, evaluates with std::visit, supports variables and functions, reports errors with positions, and has fuzz and unit tests.

topics.title: Competitive programming in C++
topics.description: Why C++ dominates contests: fast I/O with sync_with_stdio(false), bits/stdc++.h and typedefs, STL tricks such as priority_queue and lower_bound, avoiding TLE with the right complexity, and debugging with assertions.

subtopics.title: Common pitfalls: overflow and recursion depth

topics.title: C++ interview questions
topics.description: The questions that keep coming up: RAII, smart pointer differences, virtual destructors, the rule of five, std::move, templates versus virtual functions, vector versus list, and undefined behaviour examples.

topics.title: Coding interviews in C++
topics.description: Solving problems fast: unordered_map and set for lookups, sorting with custom comparators, two pointers and sliding windows, priority queues, string building without quadratic concatenation, and reasoning about STL complexity aloud.

title: C#
description: Modern C# on .NET from the dotnet CLI to idiomatic, tested code: the type system, LINQ, generics, records, pattern matching, nullable reference types, delegates and events, async/await, dependency injection, an ASP.NET Core overview, buildable projects and interview practice.

categories.title: Environment and Tooling
categories.description: The .NET SDK, the dotnet CLI and a project layout you can build and run from any terminal.

topics.title: Installing the .NET SDK and dotnet CLI
topics.description: What the SDK contains versus the runtime, how global.json pins an SDK version, and the dotnet new, build, run and test commands that drive every project without an IDE.

topics.title: Projects, solutions and the csproj file
topics.description: How the SDK-style csproj declares the target framework, output type and properties, how a solution file groups projects, and why implicit usings and nullable are switched on in the project file.

topics.title: NuGet packages and package references
topics.description: Adding libraries with dotnet add package, how PackageReference and the lock file record versions, transitive dependencies, and restoring packages in CI.

topics.description: Roslyn analyzers report style and correctness problems at compile time; .editorconfig settings and dotnet format keep the code base consistent whether you use Visual Studio, Rider or VS Code.

topics.title: Top-level statements and Program.cs
topics.description: Since C# 9 a program can start with plain statements instead of a Main method; how the compiler generates the entry point, where args come from, and when an explicit Main is still clearer.

topics.title: Namespaces, usings and file organisation
topics.description: File-scoped namespaces, using directives, global usings and static usings, and the convention of one type per file mirrored by the folder structure.

topics.title: Variables, var and value versus reference types
topics.description: Declaring with explicit types or var, definite assignment rules, and the split between value types copied on assignment and reference types shared through references.

topics.title: Numeric types, char, bool and conversions
topics.description: int, long, double, decimal and their ranges, checked and unchecked overflow, implicit versus explicit casts, and Parse versus TryParse for text input.

topics.title: Operators and expressions
topics.description: Precedence, the conditional operator, null-coalescing ?? and ??=, null-conditional ?., is and as, and switch expressions as expressions rather than statements.

topics.title: Conditions and loops
topics.description: if/else, the switch statement with case guards, for, foreach over any IEnumerable, while and do-while, and break, continue and goto case.

topics.title: Methods, parameters and overloading

topics.title: Expression-bodied members and local functions
topics.description: Writing one-expression methods and properties with =>, nesting helper functions inside a method, and static local functions that cannot capture locals.

topics.title: Pattern matching

topics.title: Iterators with yield

topics.title: Arrays and indices

topics.title: IEnumerable and deferred execution

topics.title: LINQ query and method syntax

subtopics.title: First, Single and their OrDefault variants

topics.title: Grouping, joining and aggregating with LINQ

topics.title: String immutability and StringBuilder

topics.title: Interpolation, formatting and culture
topics.description: Interpolated strings with alignment and format specifiers, composite formatting, raw string literals, and why CultureInfo changes how numbers and dates render.

topics.title: Common string methods
topics.description: Split, Trim, Replace, Contains, StartsWith, IndexOf and Substring, ordinal versus culture-aware comparison, and case-insensitive equality done properly.

topics.title: Regular expressions in .NET
topics.description: System.Text.RegularExpressions: Match, Matches, Replace and IsMatch, named groups, RegexOptions, timeouts against catastrophic backtracking, and source-generated regexes.

topics.title: Encodings, spans and parsing text

topics.title: Exceptions and try, catch, finally
topics.description: Throwing and catching, the exception class hierarchy, finally for cleanup, catching specific types first, and why swallowing Exception hides bugs.

topics.title: Classes, constructors and properties

topics.title: Structs, records and value semantics

topics.title: Inheritance, virtual and abstract members
topics.description: Base and derived classes, virtual and override, abstract classes that cannot be instantiated, sealed to stop further overriding, and the new modifier for hiding.

topics.title: Interfaces and default implementations

topics.title: Generics and constraints
topics.description: Generic classes and methods, where constraints (class, struct, new(), interface, notnull), covariance and contravariance with out and in, and how generics avoid boxing.

topics.title: Delegates, lambdas and events

topics.title: Extension methods, indexers and operator overloading

topics.title: The garbage collector and object lifetimes
topics.description: Generational garbage collection, the large object heap, finalisers versus deterministic cleanup, weak references, and reading allocation counts to find churn.

topics.title: IDisposable and using
topics.description: Deterministic release of files, sockets and database connections through Dispose, using statements and declarations, the dispose pattern, and IAsyncDisposable.

topics.title: Span, Memory and stackalloc
topics.description: Span<T> and Memory<T> as views over arrays, strings and native memory, stackalloc for small buffers, ArrayPool for reuse, and the ref struct rules that keep spans safe.

topics.title: Threads, Task and the thread pool

topics.title: async and await

topics.description: BenchmarkDotNet for trustworthy measurements, allocation-free patterns with Span and struct enumerators, string and LINQ hot spots, and tiered JIT and ReadyToRun effects.

topics.title: Security fundamentals for .NET code

categories.title: Sound Null Safety and Functions
categories.description: The type system that removes null errors, and Dart's flexible function syntax.

topics.title: Nullable types and sound null safety
topics.description: String and String? are distinct types checked by the compiler and trusted by the runtime, so a non-nullable variable can never hold null; how soundness lets the compiler skip null checks and why Dart 3 dropped unsound mode.

topics.title: Null-aware operators and flow analysis
topics.description: ?. for safe calls, ?? and ??=, the ! bang to assert non-null, and type promotion where the compiler narrows a local after a null check but not a field, which is why copying to a local or using a pattern is needed.

topics.title: required, late and nullability in classes
topics.description: required for named parameters that must be passed, late for fields set after construction or expensive lazy initialisation, and choosing nullable fields versus defaults so classes stay sound.

topics.title: Functions, optional and named parameters
topics.description: Positional optional parameters in square brackets, named parameters in braces with defaults or required, arrow syntax for one-expression bodies, and functions as first-class values with typed signatures.

topics.title: Closures and lexical scope
topics.description: Anonymous functions capture variables from their lexical scope by reference, loops create a fresh variable per iteration, and closures power callbacks, builders and stateful helpers throughout Flutter.

topics.title: Higher-order functions and callbacks
topics.description: Passing functions to map, where and forEach, returning functions, tear-offs like list.forEach(print), and designing callback parameters such as onPressed with typedefs and nullable function types.

topics.title: Records, patterns and destructuring
topics.description: Dart 3 patterns destructure records, lists, maps and objects in variable declarations, switch cases and if-case statements, with guards and exhaustiveness for sealed hierarchies, replacing chains of type checks.

topics.title: Lists
topics.description: Growable and fixed-length lists, literals with type inference, indexing, add and insert costs, sublist and getRange, List.generate and List.filled, typed lists like Uint8List, and unmodifiable views.

topics.title: Sets and maps
topics.description: Set literals and the {} ambiguity with maps, contains and set algebra, Map literals with typed keys, null-returning lookups, putIfAbsent and update, and insertion-ordered iteration of the default implementations.

subtopics.title: Set literals and the empty {} trap

topics.title: Collection if, for and spread
topics.description: Building collections declaratively with if and for inside literals, spread and null-aware spread, and why this style dominates Flutter widget lists.

topics.title: Iterable and lazy methods
topics.description: map, where, expand, take and skip return lazy Iterables evaluated on demand, fold and reduce aggregate, toList materialises, and sync* generators with yield produce sequences without building lists.

topics.title: Strings and StringBuffer
topics.description: Immutable UTF-16 strings with interpolation, multi-line and raw literals, adjacent-literal concatenation, common methods like split and trim, runes for code points, and StringBuffer for building large text.

topics.title: Parsing and RegExp
topics.description: int.parse and int.tryParse, double.parse, RegExp with hasMatch, firstMatch and allMatches, named groups, and replaceAllMapped for transformations.

topics.title: Exceptions, try, on, catch and finally
topics.description: Exception for recoverable failures versus Error for bugs, on to filter by type and catch to bind the object and stack trace, finally for cleanup, rethrow to preserve the trace, and that Dart has no checked exceptions.

topics.title: Custom exceptions and assert
topics.description: Implementing Exception with a message and toString, modelling failures with sealed classes, assert statements that run only in debug mode, and ArgumentError and StateError for contract violations.

topics.title: Libraries, imports and exports
topics.description: package: imports versus relative imports, show and hide, prefixes for name clashes, deferred loading for web, export to build a public API from several files, and part directives for code generation.

topics.title: Packages with pub
topics.description: pubspec.yaml declares dependencies with caret constraints, dart pub add and get resolve them into pubspec.lock, dev_dependencies stay out of production, and publishing to pub.dev requires a score-friendly layout.

subtopics.title: dart pub add, get and upgrade

topics.title: Files and directories with dart:io
topics.description: File.readAsString and readAsLines for whole files, openRead for streaming large files as bytes, writeAsString and IOSink, Directory listing, path manipulation with package:path, and Platform for OS details.

topics.title: JSON and encoding with dart:convert
topics.description: jsonDecode into dynamic maps and lists, jsonEncode from maps, fromJson and toJson conventions, utf8 and base64 codecs, and generated serialisation with json_serializable or freezed.

topics.title: Command-line apps and processes
topics.description: Reading arguments with package:args, stdin and stdout, exitCode, environment variables via Platform.environment, running other programs with Process.run and Process.start, and dart compile exe for distribution.

topics.title: Classes, constructors and initialiser lists
topics.description: Initialising formals with this.x, named and redirecting constructors, factory constructors that can return cached or subtype instances, const constructors, initialiser lists that run before the body, and super parameters.

topics.title: Getters, setters and operator overloading
topics.description: Computed properties with get and set that look like fields, the uniform access principle, overloading operators such as +, == and [], and the rule that overriding == requires hashCode.

topics.title: Inheritance, abstract classes and implicit interfaces
topics.description: extends for subclassing with super calls, abstract classes with unimplemented members, every class defining an implicit interface you can implement, @override annotations, and covariant parameters.

topics.title: Mixins
topics.description: mixin declarations that add behaviour to many classes without inheritance, applying several with with, the on clause to require a superclass, linearisation order when mixins override the same member, and mixin class.

topics.title: Class modifiers and sealed classes
topics.description: Dart 3 modifiers control how a class is used outside its library: sealed for exhaustive subtypes, final to forbid subtyping, base to forbid implements, interface to forbid extends, and abstract combinations.

topics.title: Enhanced enums
topics.description: Enums with fields, constructors, methods and interfaces, values and byName lookup, the index property, using enums in switch expressions, and when a sealed class fits better.

topics.title: Extension methods and extension types
topics.description: Extensions add methods and getters to existing types statically, named extensions can be imported selectively, and extension types (Dart 3.3) wrap a representation type with zero runtime cost for type-safe APIs.

topics.title: Generics and type inference
topics.description: Generic classes and methods with bounded type parameters, covariance of Dart generics and its runtime checks, type inference from constructors and literals, and checking instantiated types with is at runtime.

topics.title: The Dart VM and garbage collection
topics.description: A generational collector with a fast young space for short-lived objects, each isolate owning its own heap, allocation cost as the thing to minimise, and how const objects avoid allocation entirely.

topics.title: Disposing subscriptions, controllers and sinks
topics.description: StreamSubscriptions, StreamControllers, Timers and IOSinks hold resources until cancelled or closed; the dispose pattern in Flutter State objects and try/finally in scripts prevent leaks and stray callbacks.

topics.title: Immutability, equality and value classes
topics.description: Immutable objects with final fields and const constructors, structural equality by overriding == and hashCode or using equatable, and freezed for generated value classes with copyWith and unions.

categories.title: Asynchronous Programming and Isolates
categories.description: The single-threaded event loop, Futures, Streams and isolates for true parallelism.

topics.title: The event loop and microtasks
topics.description: Dart runs one isolate on a single thread with an event queue and a higher-priority microtask queue; why long synchronous work freezes everything, and how await schedules continuations.

subtopics.title: Why synchronous work blocks the UI

topics.title: Futures and async/await
topics.description: A Future completes once with a value or error, async functions return Futures and await unwraps them, Future.wait runs work in parallel, timeout adds deadlines, and errors propagate to try/catch around await.

subtopics.title: Error handling with try/catch around await

topics.title: Streams
topics.description: A Stream delivers many values over time; single-subscription versus broadcast streams, listen with onError and onDone, await for consumption, StreamController to produce events, and async* generators.

topics.title: Stream transformations
topics.description: map, where, asyncMap, expand, take and distinct on streams, transform with StreamTransformer, combining and debouncing with rxdart, and handling backpressure with pause and resume.

subtopics.title: first, last and toList on streams

topics.title: Isolates and parallelism
topics.description: Isolates run Dart code on separate threads with separate heaps; Isolate.run offloads a function and returns its result, Isolate.spawn with SendPort and ReceivePort handles long-lived workers, and Flutter's compute wraps it.

topics.title: Cancellation, Completers and timeouts
topics.description: Futures cannot be cancelled directly, so CancelableOperation from package:async, subscription cancel, timeout and Completer for bridging callback APIs into Futures are the tools.

topics.title: Zones and uncaught async errors
topics.description: runZonedGuarded catches errors escaping async code that no try/catch sees, zones carry values and intercept print and timers, and Flutter and crash reporters rely on them for global error handling.

topics.title: Unit tests with package:test
topics.description: test and group blocks, expect with matchers like equals, throwsA and isA, setUp and tearDown, tags and skip, and running with dart test including filtering by name.

topics.title: Mocking with mockito and mocktail
topics.description: mocktail creates mocks without code generation using when and verify, mockito with build_runner for generated mocks, registerFallbackValue for custom types, and fakes behind abstract classes.

topics.title: Testing async code and streams
topics.description: Awaiting Futures in tests, expectLater with emitsInOrder and emitsError for streams, fakeAsync and FakeAsync to control time, and testing timeouts without real waiting.

topics.title: Debugging with DevTools
topics.description: Breakpoints and the debugger() call, the Dart DevTools suite for CPU profiling, memory snapshots and the network view, logging with dart:developer log, and reading async stack traces.

topics.title: Compilation targets and build_runner
topics.description: dart compile exe for native CLIs, js and wasm for the web with tree shaking, aot-snapshot for servers, build_runner for code generation, and the environment declarations that String.fromEnvironment reads.

topics.title: Performance tuning
topics.description: Profiling before guessing, avoiding allocation in hot loops, const and final for cheap objects, typed_data for numeric work, keeping the main isolate free of heavy computation, and benchmark_harness for micro-benchmarks.

topics.title: Secure Dart code
topics.description: Validating and bounding input, avoiding dynamic where types can be checked, Random.secure for tokens, keeping secrets in the environment or platform secure storage, and dart pub outdated for vulnerable dependencies.

categories.title: Dart for Flutter and Servers
categories.description: The Dart features Flutter builds on, plus HTTP on both ends; full Flutter coverage lives in track-flutter.

topics.title: Widgets and the widget tree
topics.description: StatelessWidget and StatefulWidget as immutable descriptions, build returning a tree, BuildContext as the position in that tree, keys for identity, and how const constructors and named parameters shape widget code.

topics.title: State, setState and the widget lifecycle
topics.description: State objects persist across rebuilds, setState schedules a rebuild, initState and dispose bracket resource use, didUpdateWidget handles new configuration, and async work must check mounted.

topics.title: Layout with Row, Column and ListView
topics.description: Rows and columns with main and cross axis alignment, Expanded and Flexible for space, Padding and SizedBox, ListView.builder for long lists, and reading the constraints-go-down sizes-go-up model.

subtopics.title: Constraints go down, sizes go up

topics.title: State management with ChangeNotifier and Riverpod
topics.description: Lifting state up, ChangeNotifier with provider for observable models, Riverpod providers and ref.watch for compile-safe dependencies, and choosing a pattern that keeps widgets free of business logic.

topics.title: HTTP with package:http and shelf servers
topics.description: Making requests with package:http or dio, decoding JSON responses into models, handling status codes and timeouts, and serving HTTP from Dart with shelf and shelf_router for small backends.

topics.title: Platform channels and FFI
topics.description: Calling platform code from Dart through MethodChannel, EventChannel for streams from native, dart:ffi for C libraries with ffigen, and when a package already wraps the platform for you.

subtopics.title: Choosing a package versus custom bridging

topics.title: Project: command-line note keeper
topics.description: Build a CLI with package:args subcommands that stores notes as JSON with dart:convert, models commands with a sealed class and patterns, searches with RegExp, and ships as a dart compile exe binary with package:test coverage.

subtopics.title: Test and compile to a binary

topics.title: Project: Flutter weather app
topics.description: A Flutter app fetching forecasts with package:http, models decoded from JSON, a ChangeNotifier or Riverpod view model with loading, success and error states as a sealed class, and widget tests with a fake client.

subtopics.title: Widget tests with a fake client

topics.title: Project: shelf REST API with SQLite
topics.description: A Dart backend using shelf_router for CRUD routes, sqlite3 or postgres packages for storage, JSON request validation, middleware for logging and errors, integration tests with an in-process server, and a Docker image.

topics.title: Project: concurrent file processor with isolates
topics.description: Process a folder of large CSV files by streaming each with dart:io, parsing in a pool of isolates, merging results through a Stream, reporting progress, and comparing timings against a single-isolate run.

topics.title: Dart interview questions
topics.description: What interviewers ask: final versus const, sound null safety and promotion, mixins versus inheritance, factory constructors, the event loop and microtasks, Futures versus Streams, isolates versus threads, and why Flutter chose Dart.

topics.title: Coding interviews in Dart
topics.description: Solving problems fast in Dart: stdin parsing, List and Map with putIfAbsent, StringBuffer output, sorting with comparators and compareTo, a priority queue from package:collection, and avoiding hidden O(n) list operations.

title: Data Cleaning
description: Turning raw exports into trustworthy tables: profiling, missing data mechanisms and imputation, duplicates and entity resolution, outliers, dates, numbers and currencies, text and category normalisation, units and cross-field checks, schema validation with pandera and Great Expectations, and pipelines you can rerun and explain.

code.label: Python with the usual libraries (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, torch)

categories.title: Profiling Raw Data
categories.description: Finding out what you actually received before changing anything.

topics.title: The first look at a raw file
topics.description: Before pandas: open the file in a text viewer, check the encoding, delimiter, header rows, quoting and line endings, count rows with a shell tool, and look at the last lines. Half of all load failures are visible in the first hundred bytes.

subtopics.title: Row counts before and after load
Comparing to the data provider description

topics.title: Column-level profiling
topics.description: For every column: dtype as loaded versus intended, null count, distinct count, min, max, most common values and a sample of odd ones. A one-screen profile table per dataset catches most problems before they hit a model.

topics.title: Cardinality, keys and grain
topics.description: Which columns identify a row, whether the supposed key is unique, and what one row represents (an order, an order line, a daily snapshot). Getting the grain wrong makes every later aggregation double count.

subtopics.title: Row grain and what one row means

topics.title: Automated profiling reports
topics.description: ydata-profiling, sweetviz and D-Tale generate interactive reports with distributions, correlations, missingness and warnings in one call. They are a starting checklist, not a substitute for reading the columns yourself.

topics.title: Missingness mechanisms: MCAR, MAR and MNAR
topics.description: Values missing completely at random can be dropped safely; missing at random depends on other observed columns and can be imputed from them; missing not at random depends on the hidden value itself and biases everything unless modelled.

topics.title: Visualising and testing missingness
topics.description: Missingness matrices and heatmaps from missingno show whether gaps cluster by row, column or time, and comparing other columns between rows with and without the value tests whether missingness is related to them.

subtopics.title: Comparing groups with and without values

topics.title: Deletion strategies
topics.description: Listwise deletion drops any row with a gap and can throw away most of a dataset; column deletion removes fields that are mostly empty; pairwise deletion uses what exists per calculation. Each is a bias and sample-size trade-off.

topics.title: Simple imputation
topics.description: Mean, median and mode fills, constant sentinels with an indicator column, forward and backward fills for ordered data, and group-wise fills that respect structure. Always add a was_missing flag so models can use the information.

topics.title: Model-based imputation
topics.description: KNNImputer fills from similar rows, IterativeImputer models each column from the others in rounds, and multiple imputation keeps uncertainty by producing several completed datasets. Fit imputers on training data only to avoid leakage.

topics.title: Exact duplicates
topics.description: duplicated and drop_duplicates with subset and keep find repeated rows or repeated keys; the harder question is why they exist: re-exported batches, retries, or a grain misunderstanding. Count before dropping and keep the most complete copy.

topics.title: Near-duplicates
topics.description: Rows that differ only by whitespace, case, punctuation or a trailing zero are duplicates in meaning. Normalising a comparison key, rounding numbers and hashing the result reveals them without changing the stored values.

topics.title: Fuzzy string matching
topics.description: Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler and token-set ratios from rapidfuzz score how similar two strings are, so "Jon Smith Ltd" and "John Smith Limited" can be matched with a threshold. Phonetic keys catch spelling variants of names.

topics.title: Record linkage and blocking
topics.description: Matching records across sources compares candidate pairs on several fields; blocking on a cheap key such as postcode keeps the pair count manageable. The recordlinkage and splink libraries implement this with probabilistic scoring.

topics.title: Univariate outlier detection
topics.description: z-scores flag values many standard deviations out but are distorted by the outliers themselves; the IQR rule and the median absolute deviation are robust. Plot the distribution first: some "outliers" are the real signal.

topics.title: Multivariate outlier detection
topics.description: A 1.9 m tall person weighing 45 kg is normal on each axis and impossible together. Mahalanobis distance, Isolation Forest and Local Outlier Factor score rows by their joint unusualness.

topics.title: Treating outliers
topics.description: Options are remove, cap (winsorise), transform (log), flag and keep, or fix if the value is a known error. The choice depends on whether the value is impossible, implausible or merely rare, and on the downstream use.

topics.title: Domain rules and plausibility checks
topics.description: Statistics cannot know that ages above 120 or negative prices are wrong; domain rules can. Encode them as explicit range and relationship checks that run on every load and report violation counts by source.

topics.title: Parsing dates and times
topics.description: Mixed formats, day-month ambiguity, two-digit years, time zones and Excel serial dates all arrive in one column. Parse with explicit formats per pattern, coerce failures to NaT, and inspect what failed instead of trusting inference.

topics.title: Parsing numbers and currencies
topics.description: Thousands separators, decimal commas, currency symbols, parentheses for negatives, percent signs and unit suffixes all block numeric conversion. Strip and normalise with regex, convert with to_numeric, and keep the currency in its own column.

topics.title: Booleans, flags and enumerations
topics.description: Yes/No, Y/N, 1/0, true/false, TRUE and blanks may all mean the same flag. Map to a nullable boolean explicitly, decide what blank means, and turn known code lists into categoricals with validation of unknown codes.

topics.title: Identifiers that look like numbers
topics.description: Postcodes, phone numbers, account ids and product codes lose leading zeros and become floats or scientific notation when read as numbers. Read them as strings, validate with a pattern and pad back what was lost.

topics.title: Encodings and file format quirks
topics.description: Latin-1 bytes decoded as UTF-8, mojibake, BOMs, embedded newlines in quoted fields and Windows line endings corrupt data before you see it. Detect encodings with charset-normalizer and fix at load time, never with string replace later.

subtopics.title: Fixing at load rather than after

topics.title: Whitespace, case and punctuation normalisation
topics.description: Trailing spaces, tabs, non-breaking spaces, inconsistent case and stray punctuation split one category into ten. A normalisation function applied consistently on load, with the raw value preserved, fixes most of it.

topics.title: Unicode normalisation
topics.description: The same accented letter can be one code point or a base letter plus a combining mark, so equal-looking strings compare unequal. unicodedata.normalize with NFC or NFKC unifies them, and stripping accents may be needed for matching.

topics.title: Inconsistent categories and canonical values
topics.description: value_counts reveals "NY", "New York", "new york" and "N.Y." as separate labels. Build a mapping table to canonical values, apply it with map or replace, report unmapped values, and version the mapping alongside the code.

topics.title: Placeholder and sentinel values
topics.description: Strings like "N/A", "-", "unknown", "null", "?", 0, -1, 9999 and 1900-01-01 are missing values in disguise. Find them with value_counts per column and convert them to real nulls so they stop distorting statistics.

topics.title: Free-text fields
topics.description: Comments, addresses and product descriptions need different handling: extract structured parts with regex, normalise addresses with a parser, redact personal data, and decide whether the field is analysable at all.

topics.title: Mixed units and conversions
topics.description: A weight column mixing kg and lb, temperatures in C and F, or distances in miles and km produces silent nonsense. Detect from ranges, suffixes or a unit column, convert everything to one unit, and record the unit in the column name.

topics.title: Scale and magnitude errors
topics.description: Values stored in thousands, cents versus dollars, percentages as 0.5 versus 50, and off-by-1000 file batches show up as bimodal distributions. Comparing to known totals and plotting by source date exposes them.

topics.title: Cross-field consistency
topics.description: Rules that involve several columns: end after start, total equals sum of parts, quantity times price equals amount, child age below parent age. Each is a vectorised boolean check with a violation count and sample.

topics.title: Reference data and referential integrity
topics.description: Codes must exist in the lookup table, foreign keys must resolve, and country or currency codes must be valid ISO values. Anti-joins and isin checks find orphans; reference tables need their own versioning.

subtopics.title: ISO codes for countries and currencies

topics.title: Schema validation with pandera
topics.description: A pandera DataFrameSchema declares column dtypes, nullability, uniqueness and value checks, and validate raises with every failing row listed. Putting it at the boundary of each pipeline step turns assumptions into enforced contracts.

topics.title: Great Expectations overview
topics.description: Great Expectations manages suites of expectations, runs them against batches of data and produces data docs, which suits recurring pipelines and teams. It is heavier than pandera and pays off when many datasets need monitored checks.

subtopics.title: When to choose it over pandera

topics.title: Assertions and tests in cleaning code
topics.description: Cheap checks inside functions: row counts before and after each step, no new nulls introduced, keys still unique, totals reconciled. pytest tests on small fixture files keep cleaning functions from regressing when the source changes.

topics.title: Building a cleaning pipeline
topics.description: One function per step taking and returning a DataFrame, composed with pipe, with configuration such as mappings and thresholds passed in rather than hard-coded, so the same pipeline runs on every new export.

subtopics.title: Separating raw, interim and clean layers

topics.title: Idempotence and reproducibility
topics.description: Running the pipeline twice must give identical output: fixed seeds for any sampling, deterministic ordering, pinned library versions, and outputs written atomically so a crash never leaves half a file.

topics.title: Documenting cleaning decisions
topics.description: Every dropped row, imputed value and remapped category is a judgement that changes results. A cleaning log with counts per rule, a data dictionary for the clean table and a changelog of rules let others trust and reproduce the work.

subtopics.title: Data dictionary for the clean table

topics.title: Project: cleaning NYC taxi trip records
topics.description: Take a raw month of yellow taxi trips: remove trips with zero distance and non-zero fare, impossible timestamps and out-of-city coordinates, fix payment type codes with the lookup, cap durations, validate with a pandera schema and log every rule count.

topics.title: Project: retail product catalogue deduplication
topics.description: Merge product catalogues from two retail systems: normalise names and units, resolve near-duplicates with rapidfuzz, reconcile prices in different currencies, build a canonical product table with a mapping back to source ids and measure match precision on a hand-labelled sample.

subtopics.title: Measure precision on a labelled sample

topics.title: Project: Titanic with injected mess
topics.description: Start from a deliberately corrupted Titanic file with mixed date formats, placeholder ages, inconsistent embarkation codes, duplicate passengers and fares in two currencies; restore a clean table and prove it matches the reference with tests.

topics.title: Project: air quality sensor pipeline
topics.description: Build a rerunnable pipeline for hourly air quality feeds from several stations: unify timestamps and zones, treat negative and stuck-sensor readings, impute short gaps by interpolation and flag long ones, validate with a schema and publish a cleaning report.

topics.title: Data cleaning interview questions
topics.description: What interviewers probe: how you would profile an unfamiliar dataset, MCAR versus MAR versus MNAR, when to drop versus impute, handling duplicates across systems, outlier policy, and how you make cleaning reproducible and reviewable.

subtopics.title: Walk-through of profiling a new dataset

topics.title: Cleaning exercises on messy samples
topics.description: Timed tasks on small messy frames: parse mixed dates, convert currency strings, unify category spellings, find near-duplicates, write a pandera schema and explain each decision in one line, as done in take-home tests.
