title: Data Modeling
description: Designing schemas that hold up: conceptual to physical models, entity-relationship diagrams, normalisation and denormalisation, keys and constraints, dimensional modelling with facts, dimensions and grain, slowly changing dimensions, bridge and factless tables, events and time, application versus analytical models, schema evolution and documentation.

categories.title: Modelling Levels and Process
categories.description: From business conversation to CREATE TABLE.

topics.title: Conceptual, logical and physical models
topics.description: The conceptual model names business things and relationships, the logical model adds attributes, keys and cardinalities independent of any database, and the physical model maps it to tables, types, indexes and partitions of one engine.

subtopics.title: Logical model with keys and attributes

topics.title: Gathering requirements and business questions
topics.description: Models are shaped by the questions they must answer: interviewing stakeholders, collecting the reports and metrics they need, listing source systems, and writing the questions down so every table can be traced to one.

topics.title: Choosing the grain
topics.description: Grain states exactly what one row represents (one order line, one daily balance per account). Declaring it first prevents mixed-grain tables that double-count and makes every later measure and dimension decision mechanical.

topics.title: Notation and modelling tools
topics.description: Crow's foot, Chen and IE notations for ER diagrams, UML class diagrams for application models, and text-first tools (dbdiagram, DBML, Mermaid erDiagram) that keep diagrams in version control next to the DDL.

subtopics.title: Mermaid and DBML diagrams as code

categories.title: Entity-Relationship Modelling
categories.description: Entities, relationships and the shapes that recur in every domain.

topics.title: Entities, attributes and identifiers
topics.description: Deciding what deserves to be an entity versus an attribute, choosing a stable identifier, separating identifying from descriptive attributes, and spotting hidden entities inside repeated or multi-valued columns.

topics.title: Relationships and cardinality
topics.description: One-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many with minimum and maximum cardinality (optional or mandatory), where the foreign key lives in each case, and how optionality becomes nullability.

subtopics.title: One-to-one and where the key lives

topics.title: Resolving many-to-many relationships
topics.description: An associative (junction) entity with a composite key or its own surrogate resolves many-to-many, and often turns out to be a real entity with dates and attributes, such as an enrolment or a subscription.

topics.title: Supertypes and subtypes
topics.description: Modelling inheritance (Party as Person or Organisation): single table with a type column, one table per subtype with a shared parent, or one table per concrete type, and the query and constraint trade-offs of each.

topics.title: Weak entities and identifying relationships
topics.description: Entities that only exist within a parent (order lines, invoice items) take part of their key from the parent; identifying relationships model this and cascade deletes naturally.

categories.title: Normalisation, Keys and Constraints
categories.description: The rules that keep data consistent, and when to bend them.

topics.title: Functional dependencies and normal forms
topics.description: Working normalisation as a design tool: identify functional dependencies, split tables to reach 3NF or BCNF, and recognise the update, insert and delete anomalies each form removes (the basic definitions live in track-sql).

topics.title: Denormalisation trade-offs
topics.description: Deliberately duplicating data for read speed: pre-joined columns, counters and summary tables, with the write-side cost of keeping copies consistent and the triggers, jobs or application logic that do so.

topics.title: Natural, surrogate and composite keys
topics.description: Natural keys carry meaning but change and leak; surrogate integers or UUIDs are stable and compact; composite keys express identity but bloat child tables. Most designs use a surrogate primary key plus a unique natural key.

topics.title: Constraints as model enforcement
topics.description: Foreign keys, unique, check and exclusion constraints encode business rules in the database so bad data is rejected at write time, which is cheaper than finding it in a report months later.

topics.title: Nullability, defaults and domains
topics.description: Each nullable column is a design decision: what NULL means, whether a default or a sentinel is better, and whether an enum, lookup table or domain type should restrict values.

categories.title: Dimensional Modelling
categories.description: The star schema and its vocabulary.

topics.title: Facts, dimensions and grain
topics.description: Fact tables hold measurements at a declared grain with foreign keys to dimensions; dimensions hold the descriptive context used to filter and group. Getting grain and measure additivity right is most of the work.

topics.title: Star versus snowflake schemas
topics.description: A star denormalises each dimension into one table for simple, fast queries; a snowflake normalises dimension hierarchies into several tables to save space and centralise maintenance, at the cost of more joins.

topics.title: Fact table types
topics.description: Transaction facts record events at the moment they happen, periodic snapshots record state at regular intervals, and accumulating snapshots track a process through milestones with one row updated over time.

topics.title: Conformed dimensions and the bus matrix
topics.description: Shared dimensions with identical keys and attributes across fact tables allow drill-across queries; the bus matrix documents which processes use which dimensions and drives the build order.

topics.title: Degenerate, junk and role-playing dimensions
topics.description: Order numbers stay in the fact as degenerate dimensions, low-cardinality flags are combined into a junk dimension, and one date dimension plays several roles (order date, ship date) through multiple foreign keys.

topics.title: Measures, ratios and counts
topics.description: Storing components (numerator and denominator) rather than ratios, counting with a quantity column, handling currencies and units, and avoiding measures that cannot be aggregated across the dimensions users expect.

categories.title: Advanced Dimensional Patterns
categories.description: History, many-valued relationships and hierarchies.

topics.title: Slowly changing dimensions in the model
topics.description: Choosing per attribute whether history is overwritten (Type 1), versioned (Type 2) or kept as a previous value (Type 3), and the surrogate key, effective dates and current flag a Type 2 dimension needs.

topics.title: Bridge tables and many-valued dimensions
topics.description: When a fact relates to many dimension rows (a patient with several diagnoses), a bridge table with an optional weighting factor connects them without exploding fact rows or double-counting totals.

topics.title: Factless fact tables
topics.description: Tables with only dimension keys record that an event happened (student attended class) or that a condition held (product on promotion), enabling coverage and "what did not happen" questions.

topics.title: Hierarchies: fixed, ragged and parent-child
topics.description: Fixed-depth hierarchies flatten into columns, ragged ones need padding or a bridge, and parent-child tables model arbitrary depth but need recursion or a closure table to query efficiently.

topics.title: Date and time dimensions
topics.description: A date dimension with one row per day carries fiscal periods, holidays and weekday flags so queries never compute them; time of day is a separate dimension or a fact attribute, and timestamps stay on the fact.

categories.title: Modelling Events and Time
categories.description: Immutable histories and the two kinds of time.

topics.title: Event modelling
topics.description: Storing what happened as immutable, timestamped event rows with a type and a payload, deriving current state from them, and the wide-event and activity-schema styles that keep analytics queries simple.

topics.title: Valid time and transaction time
topics.description: Valid time is when a fact was true in the world; transaction time is when the database learned it. Bitemporal tables keep both so a report can be reproduced exactly as it looked on a past date.

topics.title: Modelling state changes
topics.description: Status history tables with effective ranges, current-state columns maintained alongside them, and the choice between range columns, PostgreSQL range types and event logs for reconstructing state at any moment.

subtopics.title: Range types versus start and end

topics.title: Aggregation and rollup tables
topics.description: Designing summary tables at coarser grains, keeping them consistent with atomic facts, and modelling the time buckets and dimensions they preserve so they answer the questions that justified them.

categories.title: Application versus Analytical Models
categories.description: The same business, two very different schemas.

topics.title: Schema design for applications
topics.description: OLTP schemas optimise for correctness and fast writes: normalised tables, tight constraints, indexes matched to access paths, and avoiding wide tables that lock and bloat under frequent updates.

topics.title: Analytical schemas and wide tables
topics.description: Analytics favour star schemas or One Big Table: pre-joined wide tables with many columns that columnar engines scan cheaply, at the cost of duplication and refresh logic.

topics.title: Semi-structured columns in relational models
topics.description: Using JSONB columns for sparse or fast-changing attributes next to fixed columns for everything queried and constrained, and the point where JSON should be promoted to real columns or tables.

topics.title: Modelling for document and key-value stores
topics.description: Embedding versus referencing in document databases, designing around the queries rather than the entities, and the duplication and consistency trade-offs relational modellers must consciously accept.

categories.title: Evolution and Documentation
categories.description: Models change; making that safe and understandable.

topics.title: Schema evolution and migrations
topics.description: Additive changes first, expand-and-contract for renames and type changes, backfills in batches, and never dropping a column while a consumer still reads it (migration tooling itself is covered in track-sql).

topics.title: Versioning models and data contracts
topics.description: Publishing a schema as a contract with owners, semantics and compatibility rules, versioning it, and validating producers against it so downstream models break in CI rather than in production.

topics.title: Documenting models
topics.description: A data dictionary with column meanings and units, ERDs kept as code, naming conventions, and tool-generated docs (dbt docs, schema comments) so the model explains itself to the next engineer.

topics.title: Reviewing and validating a model
topics.description: Walking the model against the business questions, writing sample queries for each, checking grain, keys, nullability and hierarchies, and hunting anti-patterns such as EAV tables, missing keys and fan traps.

subtopics.title: Anti-patterns: EAV, fan and chasm traps

categories.title: Projects and Interview Preparation
categories.description: Model real domains end to end, then explain your choices.

topics.title: Project: application schema for a marketplace
topics.description: Model buyers, sellers, listings, orders, payments and reviews for a marketplace: ERD in Mermaid, normalised DDL with constraints, indexes for the main screens, and a migration that adds a feature without downtime.

topics.title: Project: dimensional model for the marketplace
topics.description: Turn the application schema into a star schema: bus matrix, grain per fact, SCD Type 2 seller and listing dimensions, a date dimension, a bridge for listing categories, and SQL that answers ten business questions.

topics.title: Project: event and bitemporal model
topics.description: Design an event log for subscription changes, derive a current-state table and a bitemporal history that can answer "what did we know on date X", with exclusion constraints preventing overlaps.

topics.title: Project: model review and documentation pack
topics.description: Take an existing messy schema, reverse-engineer its ERD, list anti-patterns, propose a refactored model with a migration plan, and deliver a data dictionary and diagrams as code.

topics.title: Data modeling interview questions
topics.description: Star versus snowflake, what grain means, how SCD Type 2 works, natural versus surrogate keys, when to denormalise, what a bridge table is, and how to model many-to-many and hierarchies.

topics.title: Whiteboard modelling exercises
topics.description: Timed prompts: model a ride-sharing trip, a hotel booking system, a music streaming service and a hospital admission, each in conceptual then dimensional form with grain, keys and history decisions stated.

title: Data Pipelines
description: Running data workflows as reliable systems: DAG design, scheduling and dependencies, backfills, idempotent partitioned tasks, Airflow, Dagster and Prefect compared, configuration and secrets, observability and lineage, alerting and SLAs, cost control, testing, CI/CD and reliability patterns.

categories.title: Pipeline Architecture
categories.description: How tasks, data and dependencies fit together.

topics.title: Pipelines as DAGs
topics.description: A pipeline is a directed acyclic graph of tasks where edges are data dependencies; the DAG decides what can run in parallel, what a failure blocks and what a backfill must recompute.

topics.title: Task granularity and boundaries
topics.description: Tasks that are too small drown in scheduling overhead; too large and a failure repeats hours of work. Splitting at durable outputs, retry scope and ownership boundaries gives the right size.

subtopics.title: Retry scope as a splitting rule

topics.title: Batch, micro-batch and streaming pipelines
topics.description: Batch runs on a schedule over intervals, micro-batch runs every few minutes over small windows, streaming processes each event; latency needs, cost and complexity decide which, and many systems combine them.

topics.title: Passing data between tasks
topics.description: Tasks should hand off through durable storage (tables, object paths) and pass only small metadata such as paths and counts through the orchestrator, because orchestrator metadata stores are not built for data.

categories.title: Scheduling and Dependencies
categories.description: When things run, what they wait for, and how the past gets recomputed.

topics.title: Schedules, intervals and logical dates
topics.description: A scheduled run has a logical date or data interval distinct from the moment it executes; cron expressions, interval schedules and time zones define it, and every task should process that interval, not "now".

topics.title: Dependencies and sensors
topics.description: Upstream task success, external dataset arrival and cross-pipeline dependencies are expressed as edges or sensors; sensors poll or defer until a condition holds, and poorly bounded ones waste workers.

topics.title: Event-driven and asset-based triggering
topics.description: Triggering runs when data arrives or an upstream asset materialises, rather than on a clock, cuts latency and avoids empty runs; asset-based orchestrators model this natively with dataset or asset dependencies.

topics.title: Catch-up and backfills
topics.description: Backfills run a pipeline over past intervals to load history or repair bad logic; they need idempotent tasks, bounded concurrency, source rate limits respected and a way to exclude already-correct partitions.

subtopics.title: Concurrency and rate limits during backfills

topics.title: Reprocessing and partial reruns
topics.description: Clearing a task and its downstream tasks for one interval, rerunning only failed tasks, and marking tasks as success when the output already exists, all without repeating unaffected work.

categories.title: Idempotency and Partitions
categories.description: The properties that make reruns and backfills safe.

topics.title: Idempotent tasks
topics.description: A task that can run any number of times for the same interval and leave the same result: deterministic inputs, overwrite or merge outputs, state changed after commit, and no dependence on prior runs having happened.

topics.title: Partition-based processing
topics.description: Mapping each run to exactly one partition (a day, an hour, a region) of input and output makes work units independent, parallelisable and replaceable, and lets the orchestrator show which partitions exist and which are missing.

topics.title: Watermarks and incremental state
topics.description: Some tasks must track progress rather than partitions, storing a watermark or cursor in a metadata table; the state must be updated atomically with the output and be resettable for reprocessing.

topics.title: Late data across partition boundaries
topics.description: Events for a closed partition keep arriving, so pipelines reprocess a trailing set of partitions each run, choose the lookback from measured lateness, and expose which partitions were restated.

categories.title: Orchestration Tools
categories.description: Three widely used orchestrators and how to choose.

topics.title: Airflow essentials
topics.description: DAG files in Python, operators and the TaskFlow API, the scheduler and executors (Local, Celery, Kubernetes), connections and variables, and the conventions that keep an Airflow deployment maintainable.

topics.title: Dagster essentials
topics.description: Software-defined assets with lineage built in, partitions and backfills as first-class objects, resources for external systems, and the asset graph UI that shows freshness and materialisation history.

topics.title: Prefect essentials
topics.description: Flows and tasks as decorated Python functions, deployments and work pools for scheduling and infrastructure, and a lighter model that suits teams who want orchestration close to ordinary Python.

topics.title: Choosing an orchestrator
topics.description: Task-first versus asset-first models, hosting and operational burden, ecosystem of integrations, developer experience and local testing, and how existing team skills weigh against each tool's strengths.

categories.title: Configuration and Secrets
categories.description: The same pipeline, many environments, no leaked credentials.

topics.title: Configuration and environments
topics.description: Pipeline settings in versioned YAML or TOML per environment, validated at load time, with the pipeline code identical across dev, staging and production and only the configuration differing.

topics.title: Secrets management
topics.description: Credentials from a secrets backend (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, cloud KMS) injected at runtime, rotated without redeploying, never logged and never written into DAG files or repositories.

topics.title: Parameters and templating
topics.description: Run-time parameters (interval, partition, flags) reach tasks through templated fields or typed configuration, letting the same DAG serve schedules, backfills and manual runs.

topics.title: Pinning versions and dependencies
topics.description: Pipeline images and environments pinned to exact library versions, orchestrator and provider versions upgraded deliberately, and a rollback path when an upgrade changes behaviour.

categories.title: Observability and Lineage
categories.description: Knowing what ran, what it touched and whether it is on time.

topics.title: Logging and run metadata
topics.description: Task logs with run and task ids, centralised in a log store, plus a metadata record per run (status, duration, rows, versions) that answers most operational questions without reading logs.

topics.title: Pipeline metrics and dashboards
topics.description: Duration, success rate, rows processed, freshness and queue times per pipeline, trended over time so degradation is visible before it becomes an outage.

topics.title: Data lineage
topics.description: Tracking which datasets each run read and wrote, at table or column level, with OpenLineage-style events, so impact analysis and root-cause investigation follow the graph instead of guesswork.

topics.title: Alerting and on-call
topics.description: Alerts on failures, SLA misses and anomalies routed to owners with context and runbooks, deduplicated and tiered by severity so people respond to real problems and not noise.

topics.title: SLAs and freshness checks
topics.description: Defining when each dataset must be ready and how fresh it must be, measuring against those targets, and checking freshness at the data level so an SLA is judged on the output, not on task status.

categories.title: Cost and Reliability
categories.description: Staying within budget and surviving failure.

topics.title: Cost control
topics.description: Right-sizing workers and clusters, spot instances for retryable tasks, scheduling heavy jobs off-peak, limiting warehouse compute per pipeline and attributing cost to owners so waste has a name.

topics.title: Retries, timeouts and circuit breakers
topics.description: Retry policies per task with backoff, execution timeouts to kill hung tasks, and circuit-breaker behaviour that stops hammering a failing dependency across many tasks.

topics.title: Partial failure and compensation
topics.description: Deciding whether downstream tasks run when an upstream partially succeeded, trigger rules such as all_done or one_failed, and compensating actions that clean up half-written outputs.

topics.title: Concurrency limits and pools
topics.description: Capping concurrent tasks per pipeline, per resource pool and per source system so backfills and busy periods do not overload databases, APIs or the orchestrator itself.

topics.title: Disaster recovery and replay
topics.description: Backing up the orchestrator metadata database, keeping raw data so any layer can be rebuilt, documenting replay procedures and testing them, because the ability to recompute is the real backup.

categories.title: Testing and CI/CD
categories.description: Shipping pipeline changes with confidence.

topics.title: Unit testing pipeline code
topics.description: Testing task logic as plain functions with fixtures, mocking external systems, and keeping orchestrator-specific wiring thin so most code is testable without a scheduler running.

topics.title: DAG integrity tests
topics.description: Tests that import every DAG file, assert no cycles, unique ids, owners and retries set, and reasonable parse time, catching broken deployments before the scheduler does.

topics.title: Integration tests with sample data
topics.description: Running a pipeline end to end against small sample inputs in an isolated environment, asserting outputs and data quality checks, on every pull request or before promotion.

topics.title: CI/CD for pipelines

topics.title: Data pipeline interview questions

topics.title: Pipeline operations exercises
topics.description: Scenario drills: a backfill is overloading the source, a task hangs nightly, a partition was restated and dashboards changed, costs doubled last month; diagnose and propose fixes in ten minutes each.

title: Data Quality and Governance
description: Making data trustworthy and accountable: quality dimensions and profiling, validation with Great Expectations, Soda and pandera, data contracts, tests in pipelines, anomaly detection, lineage and catalogues, ownership, master data, privacy and GDPR basics, retention, governance frameworks and data incident management.

categories.title: Foundations of Data Quality
categories.description: What quality means, how to measure it, and where problems come from.

topics.title: Dimensions of data quality
topics.description: Accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness and validity are separate failure modes with separate checks; naming which dimension a problem belongs to is the first step to fixing it.

topics.title: Where bad data comes from
topics.description: Source system bugs, free-text entry, schema changes, integration mismatches, late or duplicated loads, and silent transformation errors; mapping each cause to the control that catches it earliest.

topics.title: Data profiling

topics.title: Quality metrics and scorecards
topics.description: Turning checks into measurable rates (percent valid, percent complete, freshness lag) per dataset, tracking them over time, and presenting a scorecard that owners and consumers both read.

categories.title: Validation Frameworks
categories.description: Turning rules into code that runs every time data moves.

topics.title: Great Expectations: expectations and suites
topics.description: Expectations such as expect_column_values_to_not_be_null and expect_column_values_to_be_between grouped into suites; validating a batch of data and reading the validation result.

topics.title: Great Expectations: data sources, checkpoints and Data Docs
topics.description: Connecting to Pandas, Spark or SQL data sources, checkpoints that bundle a suite with a batch and actions, and Data Docs that render results as browsable HTML.

topics.title: Soda and SodaCL
topics.description: Declaring checks in YAML (row_count > 0, missing_count(email) = 0, freshness(updated_at) < 1d) and running soda scan against a warehouse; its fit for SQL-first teams.

topics.title: pandera for DataFrame schemas
topics.description: Defining a DataFrameSchema or DataFrameModel with column types, checks and nullability, validating pandas or Polars frames in code, and using it as a typed contract in Python pipelines.

topics.title: Choosing and combining frameworks
topics.description: Warehouse-native checks (dbt tests, Soda) for SQL layers, pandera for Python code, Great Expectations for cross-source suites; avoiding two tools checking the same thing.

categories.title: Data Contracts and Pipeline Testing
categories.description: Agreeing what data should look like and enforcing it automatically.

topics.title: Data contracts
topics.description: A contract states schema, semantics, SLAs and ownership of a dataset agreed between producer and consumer; versioned in the repo, enforced at the boundary, and changed through a review process rather than a surprise.

topics.title: Schema enforcement and evolution
topics.description: Registering schemas (JSON Schema, Avro, Protobuf, dbt contracts), compatibility rules, and handling additive versus breaking changes with versions and deprecation windows.

topics.title: Tests inside pipelines
topics.description: Placing checks at ingestion, after transformation and before publishing; fail-fast versus warn-and-continue, quarantining bad rows, and blocking downstream tasks on failures.

topics.title: Unit and regression tests for transformations
topics.description: Testing transformation logic with small fixed inputs and expected outputs, golden datasets that catch regressions, and running these in CI so logic changes cannot silently alter results.

topics.title: Reconciliation between systems
topics.description: Comparing counts, sums and hashes between source and target after each load to catch lost or duplicated rows; tolerances for timing differences and automated reconciliation reports.

categories.title: Anomaly Detection and Monitoring
categories.description: Catching problems no one wrote a rule for.

topics.title: Metric-based anomaly detection
topics.description: Tracking row counts, null rates, distinct counts and distributions per run and flagging deviations from history with z-scores, seasonal baselines or interquartile ranges instead of static thresholds.

topics.title: Distribution and drift checks
topics.description: Comparing value distributions between runs or segments with population stability index and KS tests to detect drift in categories, ranges or proportions.

topics.title: Freshness and volume monitoring
topics.description: Expected arrival times and volumes per dataset, detecting late or missing loads, and alerting on a partition that never arrived, which rule-based validation cannot see.

topics.title: Alert design and noise reduction
topics.description: Routing alerts to owners, severity tiers, grouping related failures, and tuning thresholds so alerts stay actionable; the cost of alert fatigue on a data team.

categories.title: Lineage, Catalogues and Metadata
categories.description: Knowing where data came from, who uses it, and what it means.

topics.title: Data lineage
topics.description: Table and column level lineage from ingestion to dashboard, captured from SQL parsing, orchestrator integrations or OpenLineage events; using it for impact analysis and root cause of quality issues.

topics.title: Metadata catalogues

topics.title: Business glossary and definitions
topics.description: Agreed definitions for terms like active customer or net revenue linked to the columns that implement them, so the same word means the same thing in every report.

topics.title: Tagging, classification and sensitivity labels
topics.description: Tagging columns as PII, financial or confidential, automated classifiers that detect emails and card numbers, and using tags to drive masking and access policies.

categories.title: Ownership and Master Data

topics.title: Ownership and stewardship
topics.description: Owners are accountable for a dataset's quality and access; stewards maintain definitions and resolve issues day to day; publishing ownership in the catalogue and in on-call rotations.

topics.title: Master data management
topics.description: A single trusted record for customers, products and suppliers built by matching, merging and surviving attributes from multiple systems, and the golden record concept.

topics.title: Reference data and code lists

topics.title: Entity resolution and deduplication
topics.description: Deterministic and probabilistic matching of records that refer to the same entity, blocking to keep comparisons tractable, and tools such as Splink for scalable matching.

categories.title: Privacy, Retention and Compliance

topics.title: PII classification and handling

topics.title: Anonymisation, pseudonymisation and masking
topics.description: Hashing with a secret salt, tokenisation, generalisation and k-anonymity, dynamic masking in warehouses, and why hashing alone is not anonymisation.

topics.title: Retention and lifecycle policies
topics.description: Retention periods per dataset driven by legal and business needs, automated deletion or archiving, and proving deletion happened, including in derived tables and backups.

topics.title: Audit logging and access reviews
topics.description: Logging who accessed which data, periodic access reviews that remove stale grants, and audit trails for changes to sensitive tables as evidence for compliance.

categories.title: Governance and Incident Management
categories.description: Running quality as an operational discipline.

topics.title: Governance frameworks
topics.description: DAMA-DMBOK knowledge areas, data mesh federated governance, and lightweight policy-as-code approaches; choosing enough structure for the organisation without a bureaucracy nobody follows.

topics.title: Data quality SLAs

topics.title: Postmortems and preventive controls
topics.description: Blameless postmortems that trace the timeline and root cause, then convert findings into new checks, contracts or process changes; tracking action items to closure.

topics.description: Write a YAML contract for an events dataset with schema, SLAs and owner, generate a JSON Schema and pandera model from it, enforce it at ingestion, and add a CI check that rejects breaking changes to the contract.

topics.title: Project: anomaly monitor for warehouse tables
topics.description: A job that records row counts, null rates and distinct counts per table daily, computes seasonal baselines, flags anomalies with z-scores, and posts alerts to Slack with the affected owner from a catalogue file.

topics.description: Scan a warehouse for PII columns with pattern classifiers, tag them in a catalogue, implement a right-to-erasure job that deletes or pseudonymises a subject across all tagged tables, and log evidence.

topics.title: Data quality and governance interview questions
topics.description: Explaining the quality dimensions, where to place checks, how contracts work, lineage tools, handling PII and GDPR requests, and how you ran a data incident.

topics.title: Designing a quality programme for a case study
topics.description: Given a company with a warehouse, several teams and no ownership, propose owners, contracts, checks by layer, monitoring, a catalogue and an incident process, with a phased rollout.

Aggregate by hour, zone and payment

title: Data Visualization

code.label: Python with the usual libraries (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, torch)

categories.title: Choosing the Chart
categories.description: Start from the question, not the library.

topics.title: Matching the chart to the question
topics.description: Every chart answers one of a few questions: how is a value distributed, how do groups compare, how do two variables relate, how does something change over time, what makes up a whole. Naming the question first picks the chart family and avoids decorative charts.

topics.title: The grammar of a chart
topics.description: A chart is data mapped to marks (points, lines, bars, areas) through encodings (position, length, colour, size, shape) on scales inside a coordinate system. Thinking in this grammar makes any library, from matplotlib to plotly, feel the same.

subtopics.title: Encodings map columns to visual channels

topics.title: Encoding effectiveness ranking
topics.description: Cleveland and McGill showed people judge position on a common scale most accurately, then length, then angle and area, with colour hue last for quantities. Put the most important comparison on the most accurate channel.

subtopics.title: Angle and area are read poorly

topics.title: Small multiples versus one busy chart
topics.description: When more than four or five series share axes, lines tangle and colours run out. Small multiples (facets) repeat one simple chart per group on shared scales so the eye compares shapes instead of decoding a legend.

categories.title: Matplotlib Fundamentals
categories.description: The library every other Python plotting tool sits on.

topics.title: Line, scatter and bar primitives

subtopics.title: ax.scatter with s and c arrays

topics.title: Ticks, scales and axis formatting

topics.title: Legends, titles and labels

topics.title: Subplots and layout

subtopics.title: Iterating over a flattened axes array

topics.title: Styles, rcParams and figure sizing

categories.title: Seaborn Statistical Plots

subtopics.title: melt to long format for seaborn

topics.title: histplot, kdeplot and ecdfplot

categories.title: Plotly Interactive Charts

topics.description: Plotting events at coordinates with scatter_mapbox or GeoPandas, sizing bubbles by a measure with area not radius, clustering dense points, and basemap tiles.

subtopics.title: Basemap tiles with contextily or mapbox

topics.title: Projections and normalisation
topics.description: Coordinate reference systems, why Mercator distorts area, choosing an equal-area projection for thematic maps, and normalising counts by population or area before colouring.

categories.title: Colour, Annotation and Storytelling
categories.description: Where an accurate chart becomes a clear one.

topics.title: Sequential, diverging and categorical palettes
topics.description: Sequential maps (viridis) for ordered magnitudes, diverging maps centred on a meaningful midpoint, categorical palettes with few distinguishable hues, and why rainbow and jet distort perception.

topics.title: Colour blindness and contrast
topics.description: About 8% of men cannot separate red and green; colour-blind-safe palettes, redundant encodings (shape, label, pattern), sufficient contrast for text, and simulators to check a chart.

subtopics.title: Redundant encoding with shape or label

topics.title: Direct labelling and annotation
topics.description: Labels placed on the data with ax.annotate and text, arrows to the point that matters, value labels on bars, and avoiding label collisions with adjustText or manual offsets.

topics.title: Highlighting and de-emphasising
topics.description: One accent colour on the series that matters with the rest in light grey, thicker lines for the focus, and removing gridlines and borders that compete with data.

topics.title: Titles that state the takeaway
topics.description: A title that says what the chart shows (Churn doubled after the price change) rather than what it is (Churn by month), subtitles for method and source notes for trust.

topics.title: Building a narrative sequence
topics.description: Ordering charts from context to detail to recommendation, keeping scales and colours consistent across a sequence, and building up one chart progressively for presentations.

topics.title: Misleading charts to avoid
topics.description: Truncated bar axes, dual y axes that invent correlation, cherry-picked windows, 3D effects, area-scaled icons and cumulative charts that hide decline; how to spot and fix each.

topics.title: Dashboards with Streamlit and Dash
topics.description: Turning charts into an app: Streamlit widgets and caching for quick internal tools, Dash callbacks for production interactivity, and layout principles that dashboard-design covers in depth.

topics.title: Exporting for print and web
topics.description: Vector (SVG, PDF) for print and scaling, PNG at 2x for screens, transparent backgrounds, embedding fonts, and bbox_inches="tight" to keep labels inside the file.

topics.title: Reproducible figure scripts
topics.description: Figures generated by scripts from raw data, not hand-tweaked in notebooks: a chart function per figure, fixed random seeds, versioned data inputs and a Makefile or script that rebuilds every figure.

subtopics.title: Rebuilding all figures from a script

topics.title: Project: exploratory report on a public dataset
topics.description: Take a public dataset (for example city bike trips), profile it, and produce a ten-chart report in matplotlib and seaborn covering distributions, comparisons and trends, each chart with a takeaway title and consistent styling, built by a script.

subtopics.title: Build the report from a script

topics.title: Project: interactive sales explorer in plotly
topics.description: A plotly and Streamlit app over sales data with a time series of revenue, a sortable bar of products, a treemap of categories and a map of regions, linked by filters, with hover templates and an export button.

topics.title: Project: chart makeover
topics.description: Collect five misleading or cluttered published charts, diagnose each problem (truncated axis, rainbow map, pie with ten slices), and redraw each one honestly with before-and-after images and a written rationale.

topics.title: Project: geospatial analysis of a city
topics.description: Map a city dataset (incidents, listings or stations): a choropleth of rates per district with GeoPandas, a density map of points, and an equal-area projection, with a written note on normalisation choices.

topics.title: Data visualization interview questions
topics.description: Explaining chart choice for a given question, why pies and dual axes fail, colour accessibility, how to show uncertainty, and critiquing a chart on the spot with a fix.

topics.title: Take-home visualization tasks
topics.description: Typical take-home briefs: build a short analysis with charts from a CSV, explain each choice in a paragraph, and deliver a clean notebook or script that reviewers can run.

subtopics.title: Reading the brief for the question

title: Data Warehousing
description: How analytical databases are designed, loaded and run: OLTP versus OLAP, Kimball, Inmon and Data Vault, columnar engines, Snowflake, BigQuery and Redshift concepts, Delta and Iceberg lakehouses, loading patterns, slowly changing dimensions, partitioning, cost, governance and semantic layers.

categories.title: Foundations and Architectures
categories.description: Why a warehouse is not just a big database, and the schools of thought on how to build one.

topics.title: OLTP versus OLAP workloads
topics.description: Transactional systems do many small reads and writes by key; analytical systems scan millions of rows for a few columns. Row stores, indexes and normalisation serve the first, columnar scans and denormalised schemas serve the second.

subtopics.title: Access patterns of OLTP and OLAP
Why operational databases are poor for analytics

topics.title: Warehouse layers: staging, core and marts
topics.description: Raw data lands untouched in staging, is integrated and historised in a core layer, and is served through marts shaped for consumers. The medallion naming (bronze, silver, gold) describes the same progression in lakehouses.

topics.title: The Kimball dimensional approach
topics.description: Kimball builds the warehouse bottom-up from business processes modelled as facts and dimensions, tied together by conformed dimensions listed in a bus matrix so marts can be joined across processes.

topics.title: The Inmon corporate information factory
topics.description: Inmon builds a normalised enterprise data warehouse first as the single integrated source, then derives departmental marts from it, trading faster initial delivery for consistency across the organisation.

topics.title: Data Vault overview
topics.description: Data Vault separates business keys (hubs), relationships (links) and descriptive history (satellites) so new sources can be added without restructuring, at the cost of more joins that a presentation layer must hide.

categories.title: Storage and Query Engines
categories.description: What happens under the hood when a warehouse runs a query.

topics.title: Columnar storage and compression
topics.description: Storing each column contiguously lets a scan read only the columns requested and compress similar values with run-length, dictionary and delta encodings, which is why analytical queries run tens of times faster than on row stores.

topics.title: Distributed query execution
topics.description: MPP warehouses split data across nodes, run vectorised operators in parallel and shuffle rows over the network for joins and aggregations; understanding where shuffles happen explains most slow queries.

subtopics.title: Shuffles for joins and group by

topics.title: Snowflake concepts
topics.description: Virtual warehouses provide isolated compute over shared micro-partitioned storage; automatic clustering, time travel, zero-copy cloning and the result cache shape how work is organised and billed.

topics.title: BigQuery concepts
topics.description: A serverless engine that bills by bytes scanned or reserved slots, so partitioning, clustering and column selection directly change cost; nested and repeated fields model one-to-many data without joins.

subtopics.title: Slots and on-demand versus capacity pricing
Bytes scanned as the cost driver

topics.title: Redshift concepts
topics.description: A provisioned or serverless MPP cluster where distribution style and sort keys decide how much data moves and is skipped; RA3 nodes separate storage, Spectrum queries S3, and VACUUM and ANALYZE remain part of operations.

categories.title: Lakehouse and Table Formats
categories.description: Warehouse guarantees on top of files in object storage.

topics.title: Lakehouse architecture
topics.description: Open file formats in object storage plus a transactional table layer give warehouse features (ACID, schema enforcement, time travel) with lake economics and multiple engines reading the same tables.

topics.title: Delta Lake
topics.description: A JSON transaction log next to Parquet files records every commit, giving ACID writes, time travel, MERGE, schema enforcement and OPTIMIZE with Z-ordering for data skipping on lakes read by Spark and other engines.

topics.title: Apache Iceberg
topics.description: Iceberg tracks snapshots, manifests and per-file statistics in a metadata tree, supports hidden partitioning and safe partition evolution, and is read natively by Spark, Trino, Flink, Snowflake and BigQuery.

topics.title: Catalogs and metastores
topics.description: A catalog maps table names to current metadata and arbitrates commits: Hive Metastore, AWS Glue, Unity Catalog and Iceberg REST catalogs such as Apache Polaris let several engines agree on what a table is.

subtopics.title: Role of a catalog in commits

categories.title: Loading Patterns
categories.description: Getting data into the warehouse correctly, repeatedly and at volume.

topics.title: Bulk loading from stages
topics.description: Warehouses load fastest from files in object storage: Snowflake COPY INTO from stages, BigQuery load jobs from GCS, Redshift COPY from S3 with manifests, all parallel across files and far faster than row inserts.

topics.title: Incremental loads and watermarks
topics.description: Loading only rows changed since the last run using an updated_at high-water mark or a change sequence, with an overlap window and dedup to tolerate late updates and clock skew.

topics.title: MERGE in warehouses
topics.description: MERGE INTO target USING source matches on keys and inserts, updates or deletes per branch in one statement; warehouses implement it by rewriting affected partitions or files, so limiting the matched range keeps it cheap.

topics.title: Streaming and continuous ingestion
topics.description: Snowpipe, BigQuery Storage Write API and Kafka connectors land events within seconds, trading micro-batch efficiency for freshness, and require dedup keys because delivery is usually at-least-once.

topics.title: Idempotent and auditable loads
topics.description: Each load records what it did (files, row counts, run id) in an audit table, writes to staging, and either swaps, overwrites a partition or merges, so any run can be repeated or reconciled without corrupting the target.

categories.title: Slowly Changing Dimensions
categories.description: Keeping history when descriptive attributes change.

topics.title: SCD types 0, 1, 2 and 3
topics.description: Type 0 never changes, Type 1 overwrites, Type 2 adds a new row per version with validity dates, Type 3 keeps a previous-value column. The choice decides whether reports show history as it was or as it is now.

topics.title: Implementing SCD Type 2 in SQL
topics.description: A MERGE or two-step statement that closes the current row (sets end date and current flag) and inserts a new version when a hash of tracked attributes changes, with care for same-day changes and initial loads.

subtopics.title: Closing and inserting in one transaction

topics.title: Surrogate keys and late-arriving dimensions
topics.description: Facts reference the dimension version by surrogate key, not natural key; when a fact arrives before its dimension row, an inferred placeholder row is inserted and later updated, keeping referential integrity.

subtopics.title: Key lookup at fact load time

topics.title: Snapshots and history tables
topics.description: Periodic full snapshots of a source table, or tool-managed snapshots such as dbt snapshots, give history when the source has no change tracking, at the cost of storage proportional to snapshot frequency.

categories.title: Performance and Cost
categories.description: Making queries fast and bills predictable.

topics.title: Partitioning and clustering
topics.description: Partitioning splits a table by a column such as date so queries skip whole partitions; clustering orders data within storage units so range filters skip blocks. Both only help when queries filter on the chosen columns.

topics.title: Writing queries that prune
topics.description: Pruning needs filters the engine can evaluate against metadata: literal or parameter comparisons on partition columns, no functions wrapping them, and joins that carry the partition predicate to the large table.

subtopics.title: Checking bytes scanned or partitions read

topics.title: Materialised views and result caching
topics.description: Warehouse materialised views maintain precomputed aggregates automatically and can rewrite queries to use them; result caches return identical queries free, which changes how dashboards should be written.

topics.title: Cost models and controlling spend
topics.description: Per-second compute (Snowflake), per-byte or slot reservations (BigQuery) and provisioned nodes (Redshift) reward different habits; auto-suspend, query limits, resource monitors and cost attribution tags keep bills predictable.

topics.title: Workload management and concurrency
topics.description: Separating ETL, BI and ad hoc workloads onto their own compute (warehouses, slot reservations, WLM queues) prevents a heavy load from stalling dashboards and makes each team's usage visible and limitable.

categories.title: Security and Governance
categories.description: Controlling who sees what, and proving it.

topics.title: Access control and masking
topics.description: Role hierarchies grant privileges on schemas and tables; row access policies filter by user attributes, and dynamic data masking returns redacted values to unprivileged roles without duplicating tables.

topics.title: PII, classification and retention
topics.description: Tagging columns as PII or sensitive, tokenising or hashing identifiers, keeping raw PII out of marts, and enforcing retention and deletion so the warehouse can satisfy GDPR-style requests.

topics.title: Lineage, catalogs and audit
topics.description: Query history and information_schema views show who ran what; lineage tools trace a column from source to dashboard, and a data catalog documents owners and definitions so consumers trust and find data.

topics.title: Data sharing and marketplaces
topics.description: Snowflake secure shares, BigQuery Analytics Hub and Iceberg tables in shared storage let organisations expose live tables to partners without copying, with the provider controlling scope and the consumer paying for compute.

categories.title: Semantic Layers and Serving
categories.description: From tables to metrics people agree on.

topics.title: Semantic layers and metric definitions
topics.description: A semantic layer (dbt Semantic Layer, LookML, Cube) defines metrics, dimensions and joins once so every tool computes revenue the same way, replacing per-dashboard SQL with governed definitions.

subtopics.title: Metrics, dimensions and joins as definitions

topics.title: Aggregate tables and OLAP cubes
topics.description: Pre-aggregating facts to common grains (daily, by region) cuts scan cost for dashboards; classic cubes and modern engines like Druid or ClickHouse serve sub-second slices when the warehouse is too slow or expensive for interactive use.

topics.title: BI connectivity and query patterns
topics.description: BI tools run either live queries or scheduled extracts; live mode needs well-partitioned marts and caching, extracts need refresh schedules, and both benefit from wide, flat views designed for the tool.

categories.title: Projects and Interview Preparation
categories.description: Build a warehouse end to end, then defend its design in an interview.

topics.title: Project: retail star schema warehouse
topics.description: Design a bus matrix for orders, shipments and returns, build conformed customer, product and date dimensions with SCD Type 2, load facts from staged CSV files, and verify totals against the source.

topics.title: Project: incremental lakehouse table
topics.description: Create an Iceberg or Delta table over object storage, load daily partitions with MERGE from a changing source, evolve the schema by adding a column, time-travel to a previous snapshot, and compact small files.

topics.title: Project: cost and performance audit
topics.description: Take a sample warehouse with slow, expensive queries: profile query history, add partitioning and clustering, rewrite non-pruning filters, create an aggregate table, and report the before-and-after cost and runtime.

topics.title: Project: governed metrics layer
topics.description: Define revenue, active customers and return rate in a semantic layer over the star schema, apply row-level and masking policies for two roles, and demonstrate that two BI tools return identical numbers.

topics.title: Data warehousing interview questions
topics.description: Recurring questions: Kimball versus Inmon, star versus snowflake, how SCD Type 2 works, why columnar is faster, what a micro-partition is, how to cut BigQuery cost, and what a lakehouse adds over a lake.

topics.title: Warehouse design exercises
topics.description: Timed design prompts: model a subscription business, choose partition and clustering keys for a 10 TB event table, design a load for late-arriving facts, and estimate the cost of a dashboard on BigQuery.

subtopics.title: Choosing keys for a large table
