topics.description: Input and output classifiers, safety checkers on image pipelines, prompt-level refusals and the trade-off between over-blocking and harm; building a layered approach rather than trusting one filter.

subtopics.title: False positive and false negative costs

topics.title: Watermarking and provenance
topics.description: Marking generated content statistically (token-level watermarks, SynthID) or with signed metadata (C2PA content credentials), how detection works, and what can and cannot survive editing.

topics.title: Licensing, copyright and training data
topics.description: Model licences (open weights, non-commercial, Llama-style terms), dataset licences and opt-outs, memorisation and regurgitation risks, and what ownership of generated output means in practice.

topics.title: Bias, hallucination and misuse
topics.description: Demographic and stylistic bias in generations, confident fabrications in text, deepfakes and disinformation, and the mitigations available: prompt design, grounding, red-teaming and usage policies.

categories.title: Building Generative Applications
categories.description: Turning a model call into something people use.

topics.title: Architecture of a generative app
topics.description: A request path of API, queue and GPU worker, why generation is asynchronous, idempotent job ids, storing outputs in object storage and the difference between hosted APIs and self-hosted models.

topics.title: Streaming generation to the user
topics.description: Token streaming with server-sent events or WebSockets, progressive image previews from intermediate diffusion steps, and handling cancellation and partial failures gracefully.

topics.title: Cost, caching and rate limits
topics.description: Token and GPU-second economics, caching identical requests and prompt prefixes, batching diffusion jobs, tiered model routing, and enforcing per-user limits before the bill arrives.

topics.title: Observability and feedback loops
topics.description: Logging prompts, parameters and outputs with ids, capturing thumbs-up and edits as signals, dashboards for latency and refusals, and using the logs to build eval sets and fine-tuning data.

topics.title: Project: train a VAE and a GAN on Fashion-MNIST
topics.description: Implement a convolutional VAE and a DCGAN in PyTorch on the same dataset, visualise latent interpolations and sample grids over training, compute FID for both, and write up why the samples differ.

topics.title: Project: style LoRA for Stable Diffusion
topics.description: Collect 20 to 50 images of a consistent style, train a LoRA on the U-Net with diffusers, compare guidance scales and ranks, generate a gallery with fixed seeds, and document the licence and consent for the images.

topics.title: Project: streaming writing assistant
topics.description: Build a web app that streams LLM output with exposed temperature, top-p and length controls, a stop button, a system-prompt editor and logging of every generation with feedback buttons.

topics.title: Project: narrated summaries pipeline
topics.description: Summarise articles with an LLM, synthesise speech with an open TTS model, stitch audio with intros, evaluate summaries with an LLM judge and a small human study, and publish an RSS-style feed of results.

subtopics.title: Evaluate with a judge and humans

topics.title: Generative AI interview questions
topics.description: Why VAEs blur and GANs collapse, what a diffusion model predicts, how classifier-free guidance works, LoRA versus full fine-tuning, FID limits, temperature versus top-p, and how you would watermark output.

topics.title: Whiteboard derivations
topics.description: Derive the ELBO from Jensen's inequality, write the GAN minimax objective and its optimal discriminator, derive the closed-form q(x_t | x_0), and sketch a sampling loop with temperature and top-p in NumPy.

title: Go Backend Development
description: Production HTTP services in Go: net/http and the 1.22 ServeMux, chi and Gin, handlers and middleware, JSON and validation, database/sql, sqlx, pgx and GORM, migrations, authentication, configuration, slog, graceful shutdown, concurrency patterns, httptest and table tests, observability, Docker and deployment.

categories.title: net/http Foundations
categories.description: The standard library server is enough for most services; everything else builds on it.

topics.title: The net/http server model
topics.description: http.Server accepts connections and runs each request in its own goroutine, so handlers must be safe for concurrent use; ListenAndServe versus a configured Server with read, write and idle timeouts that stop slow clients pinning resources.

topics.title: Handlers, HandlerFunc and ServeMux
topics.description: The http.Handler interface with one method, HandlerFunc as the adapter that turns a function into a Handler, and ServeMux as the router that matches paths and dispatches; understanding these three explains every Go web framework.

topics.title: Go 1.22 ServeMux patterns
topics.description: The enhanced mux matches methods and path wildcards ("GET /users/{id}"), exposes r.PathValue, and has precedence rules for overlapping patterns, which removes the need for a third-party router in many services.

topics.title: Request context and values
topics.description: Every request carries a context.Context that is cancelled when the client disconnects; middleware stores per-request data (user, request id) with typed keys, and handlers pass ctx to every downstream call.

subtopics.title: Propagating ctx to database and HTTP calls

topics.title: Writing responses
topics.description: Header order rules (set headers before WriteHeader, WriteHeader before Write), status codes, streaming with http.Flusher, serving files, and why writing after an error has been sent corrupts responses.

topics.title: chi: routers, groups and URL params
topics.description: chi is a lightweight router compatible with net/http Handler: Route groups, Mount for sub-routers, chi.URLParam, and its middleware package; it stays idiomatic because everything remains a Handler.

topics.title: Gin: engine, groups and binding
topics.description: Gin uses its own gin.Context instead of the standard signature, bundles JSON binding and validation, route groups and a recovery middleware; faster to write, less composable with plain Handlers.

topics.title: Middleware as handler wrappers
topics.description: A middleware is func(http.Handler) http.Handler; it runs code before and after calling next, can short-circuit, and chains compose outermost-first, which determines who sees what.

topics.title: Common middleware: logging, recovery, CORS and request ids
topics.description: The middleware every service needs: panic recovery that returns 500 instead of killing the goroutine, request logging with duration, CORS preflight handling, request ids for tracing, and timeouts.

topics.title: Encoding and decoding JSON
topics.description: encoding/json with struct tags for names and omitempty, pointer fields to distinguish absent from zero, custom MarshalJSON for types like money and time, and the cost of reflection-based encoding.

topics.title: Decoding request bodies safely
topics.description: http.MaxBytesReader to cap body size, DisallowUnknownFields to reject typos, checking for trailing data, and mapping decode errors to precise 400 messages instead of leaking internals.

topics.title: Validation with go-playground/validator
topics.description: Struct tags like validate:"required,email,min=3", registering custom rules, translating errors into field-level messages, and keeping validation in the transport layer while domain invariants stay in the domain.

topics.title: Error handling in handlers
topics.description: Handlers that return error to a small wrapper, sentinel and typed errors mapped to status codes with errors.Is and errors.As, wrapping with %w for context, and never exposing internal messages to clients.

topics.title: Problem details and consistent error bodies
topics.description: One error response shape for the whole service (RFC 9457 problem details, covered in track-rest-api), a helper that writes it, and a validation variant listing field errors.

subtopics.title: Error codes clients can switch on

topics.title: Configuration from environment and flags
topics.description: Reading config from environment variables with defaults and validation at startup (envconfig or hand-written), flags for local overrides, and a Config struct passed explicitly rather than global state.

topics.title: Structured logging with log/slog
topics.description: The standard slog package with JSON and text handlers, levels, attributes and groups, and configuring a handler once in main so every package logs consistently.

topics.title: Request-scoped loggers and correlation ids
topics.description: Attaching a logger carrying request id, method and path to the context in middleware, retrieving it in handlers and repositories, and correlating with traces.

subtopics.title: Retrieving the logger in deep layers

topics.title: Project layout and packages
topics.description: cmd/ for binaries, internal/ for private packages, packages organised by domain rather than by layer, avoiding the util package, and wiring dependencies in main without a framework.

categories.title: Database Access
categories.description: Standard library first, then the libraries that reduce boilerplate. SQL itself lives in track-sql.

topics.title: database/sql and connection pools
topics.description: sql.DB is a pool, not a connection: opening lazily, PingContext to verify, SetMaxOpenConns and SetConnMaxLifetime, and the driver registration pattern.

subtopics.title: Max open, idle and lifetime settings

topics.title: Queries, scanning and NULL handling
topics.description: QueryRowContext and QueryContext with placeholders, scanning into variables, closing rows, sql.NullString and pointers for nullable columns, and ErrNoRows.

topics.title: sqlx and sqlc
topics.description: sqlx adds struct scanning and named queries to database/sql; sqlc generates type-safe Go from SQL files at build time, giving compile-time checks without an ORM.

topics.title: pgx for PostgreSQL
topics.description: The native PostgreSQL driver and toolkit: pgxpool, binary protocol, COPY for bulk loads, LISTEN/NOTIFY, and the pgx interface versus using it through database/sql.

subtopics.title: pgx types for arrays and JSONB

topics.title: GORM
topics.description: The mainstream ORM: model structs with conventions, AutoMigrate, associations and preloading, hooks, and the cost of hidden queries; when it speeds you up and when raw SQL is clearer.

topics.title: Transactions and the repository pattern
topics.description: BeginTx with isolation options, defer rollback with commit on success, passing the transaction through a context or an interface, and repository interfaces sized to what the service needs.

topics.title: Migrations with golang-migrate and goose
topics.description: Versioned SQL migration files with up and down, applying them from CI or a migrate subcommand rather than at startup, embedding with embed.FS, and handling failed migrations.

topics.title: Password hashing and sessions
topics.description: bcrypt or argon2id via golang.org/x/crypto, constant-time comparison, server-side sessions stored in Redis or the database with secure cookie flags, and session fixation and expiry.

topics.title: JWT with golang-jwt
topics.description: Signing and verifying tokens with HS256 or RS256, registered claims, validating expiry and issuer, key rotation with a kid header, and keeping access tokens short-lived.

topics.title: Authorization middleware and roles
topics.description: Middleware that loads the principal into context, route-level role checks, resource-level checks in the service layer, and returning 401 versus 403 correctly.

topics.title: Security headers, CSRF and rate limiting
topics.description: Setting HSTS and content-type headers, CSRF tokens for cookie-authenticated forms, per-client rate limiting with golang.org/x/time/rate or a token bucket in Redis, and TLS termination choices.

categories.title: Concurrency in Services
categories.description: Language-level goroutines and channels are in track-go; this is how they show up inside a server.

topics.title: Goroutines inside request handlers
topics.description: Fanning out to several backends in parallel inside a handler, collecting results with channels or errgroup, and the rule that spawned goroutines must not outlive the request unless deliberately detached.

topics.title: Context cancellation and timeouts
topics.description: Deriving deadlines per operation, honouring ctx in database and HTTP calls, cleaning up when the client disconnects, and reporting 504 or 499-style outcomes.

subtopics.title: Cancellation in DB and HTTP clients

topics.title: Worker pools and errgroup
topics.description: Bounded concurrency with a fixed number of workers reading from a channel, errgroup.WithContext to cancel siblings on first error and SetLimit for bounds, and semaphores for shared resources.

topics.title: Background jobs and graceful shutdown
topics.description: Catching SIGTERM with signal.NotifyContext, Server.Shutdown to drain in-flight requests, stopping background workers and closing pools in order, and readiness flipping before shutdown.

topics.title: Shared state, sync and the race detector
topics.description: Protecting in-memory caches and counters with sync.Mutex and RWMutex, sync.Once for lazy init, atomic counters, and running tests with -race to catch data races before production does.

topics.title: httptest recorders and servers
topics.description: httptest.NewRecorder to call a handler directly and inspect status, headers and body, and httptest.NewServer for a real listener when testing clients or full middleware chains.

topics.title: Table-driven handler tests
topics.description: A slice of cases with name, request builder and expected status/body, run with t.Run subtests and t.Parallel, covering happy path, validation errors and auth failures in one readable test.

topics.title: Testing database code
topics.description: Running a real PostgreSQL in tests with testcontainers-go or a docker-compose service, migrations in TestMain, per-test transactions or truncation, and why mocking SQL is rarely worth it.

topics.title: Mocks, interfaces and testify
topics.description: Hand-written fakes implementing small interfaces, generated mocks with mockery or gomock, testify assert and require, and keeping mocks at service boundaries rather than everywhere.

categories.title: Observability and Deployment
categories.description: Docker and cloud platforms in depth live in track-docker and track-observability.

topics.title: Metrics with the Prometheus client
topics.description: Exposing /metrics with promhttp, counters and histograms for requests by route and status, the RED method, and cardinality discipline for labels.

topics.title: Tracing with OpenTelemetry
topics.description: otelhttp to instrument servers and clients, spans around database calls, context propagation across services, and exporting to an OTLP collector.

topics.title: Health checks and pprof
topics.description: Separate liveness and readiness endpoints that check dependencies, and net/http/pprof for CPU, heap and goroutine profiles on a private port when production misbehaves.

subtopics.title: Analysing profiles with go tool pprof

topics.title: Building binaries and Docker images
topics.description: Static binaries with CGO_ENABLED=0, ldflags for version stamping, multi-stage Dockerfiles from a distroless or scratch base, and image size and startup time.

topics.title: Running in production
topics.description: GOMAXPROCS and memory limits in containers, environment-driven config, structured logs to stdout, running behind a reverse proxy or load balancer, and zero-downtime rollouts.

topics.title: Project: URL shortener with Redis and PostgreSQL
topics.description: Build a shortener with the 1.22 mux: create and resolve links, Redis cache in front of Postgres, click counting via a background worker, rate limiting, table-driven tests and a Docker image.

topics.title: Project: bookings API with chi and sqlc
topics.description: A room booking service: chi routes, sqlc-generated queries, transactions that prevent double booking, JWT auth, validator-based input checks, problem details errors and testcontainers integration tests.

topics.title: Project: file processing service with worker pools
topics.description: Uploads land in object storage, a worker pool processes them (resize, virus scan, metadata), progress is exposed over Server-Sent Events, and graceful shutdown finishes in-flight jobs.

topics.title: Project: observable Gin microservice
topics.description: A product catalogue in Gin with GORM, OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics, slog JSON logs with request ids, health probes, and a Kubernetes-ready distroless image.

topics.title: Go backend interview questions
topics.description: What interviewers ask: how net/http handles concurrency, context propagation, sql.DB pooling, middleware order, error wrapping, graceful shutdown and choosing GORM versus sqlc.

topics.title: Go service design questions
topics.description: Designing a rate limiter, structuring packages for a growing service, choosing sync versus async processing, handling partial failures in fan-out, and reviewing a handler with goroutine leaks.

title: Go
description: Go from the toolchain and modules to production services: slices and maps, interfaces, errors as values, goroutines, channels, context, sync and atomic, net/http, database/sql, testing and pprof, containerised cloud-native deployment, projects and interview practice.

categories.title: Environment and Tooling
categories.description: The toolchain, modules and formatting conventions that every Go project relies on.

topics.title: Installing Go and the toolchain
topics.description: Installing the go command, what GOROOT, GOPATH and the module cache are for today, checking go version and go env, and how the toolchain directive lets a module pin a newer Go automatically.

subtopics.title: GOROOT, GOPATH and the module cache

topics.title: go run, go build and go install
topics.description: The three ways to execute a program: compile-and-run for iteration, build for a binary in the current directory, and install for a tool placed on the PATH, plus the ./... package pattern.

topics.title: Modules: go.mod, go.sum and go get
topics.description: go mod init names a module by its import path, go get adds dependencies at a semantic version, go.sum records hashes so builds are verifiable, and go mod tidy keeps both files honest.

subtopics.title: go mod init and the module path

topics.title: gofmt, go vet and linters
topics.description: Formatting is not negotiable in Go: gofmt produces one canonical layout, go vet catches suspicious code such as bad Printf verbs and copied locks, and staticcheck or golangci-lint add deeper checks via gopls in the editor.

topics.title: Packages, main and imports
topics.description: Every file starts with a package clause, an executable needs package main with func main, imports are paths not names, unused imports and variables are compile errors, and capitalised identifiers are exported.

subtopics.title: Unused imports and variables fail to compile

topics.title: Variables, constants and iota
topics.description: var declarations versus := short declarations, why every variable has a usable zero value, typed and untyped constants, and iota for enumerated constants with bit flags.

topics.title: Basic types and conversions
topics.description: int and sized integers, float32 and float64, byte and rune aliases, bool and string, why Go has no implicit numeric conversion, and how untyped constants avoid most casts.

topics.title: Operators and expressions
topics.description: Arithmetic, comparison and logical operators, bitwise operators including &^ (AND NOT), why ++ is a statement rather than an expression, integer division and modulo, and the absence of a ternary operator.

topics.title: Conditions, switch and loops
topics.description: if with an init statement, switch without automatic fallthrough and with no-condition form, the single for keyword covering while and infinite loops, range over slices, maps, strings, integers and functions, and labeled break and continue.

topics.title: Functions, multiple returns and variadics
topics.description: Functions return several values, conventionally (result, error), named results document intent and enable bare returns, and variadic parameters collect trailing arguments as a slice expanded with ....

topics.title: Closures and function values
topics.description: Function literals capture variables by reference, per-iteration loop variables since Go 1.22 remove the classic capture bug, and closures give you generators, memoisation and callbacks without classes.

topics.title: defer and evaluation order
topics.description: defer schedules a call to run when the surrounding function returns, in LIFO order, with arguments evaluated at the defer statement; it is how Go closes files, unlocks mutexes and adjusts named results.

topics.title: Arrays and slices
topics.description: Arrays are fixed-size values copied on assignment; slices are views onto an array with length and capacity, created with literals or make, extended with append and iterated with range.

topics.title: Slice internals, append and aliasing
topics.description: A slice header holds a pointer, length and capacity, so sub-slices share memory; append reallocates only when capacity runs out, which is why two slices can silently overwrite each other, and copy, full slice expressions and the slices package help.

subtopics.title: Aliasing bugs from shared backing arrays

topics.title: Maps and the maps package
topics.description: Hash maps created with make or literals, the comma-ok lookup, delete and clear, deliberately randomised iteration order, why maps are not safe for concurrent writes, and helpers in the maps package.

topics.title: Structs, pointers and copies
topics.description: Structs group named fields and are copied by value; pointers with & and * share one value, there is no pointer arithmetic, Go auto-dereferences p.field, and choosing value or pointer decides whether callers see mutations.

topics.title: Strings, bytes and runes
topics.description: Strings are immutable UTF-8 byte sequences: len counts bytes, indexing yields bytes, range yields runes with byte offsets, and conversions to []byte and []rune are how you edit or count characters.

topics.title: strings, strconv and fmt
topics.description: The strings package for searching, splitting and building text efficiently with strings.Builder, strconv for converting to and from numbers, and fmt verbs such as %v, %+v, %#v, %T and %q for output.

topics.title: Regular expressions with regexp
topics.description: RE2 syntax with linear-time guarantees but no backreferences, compiling once with MustCompile at package level, Find and FindAll variants with submatches, and ReplaceAllString with $1 expansions.

topics.title: Sorting and searching with slices and sort
topics.description: slices.Sort and slices.SortFunc with cmp.Compare for ordered and custom sorts, stable variants, slices.BinarySearch on sorted data, and the older sort.Slice and sort.Interface when you meet them in code.

topics.title: Errors as values
topics.description: error is a one-method interface, functions return it as the last value, callers check if err != nil immediately, and errors.New and fmt.Errorf create messages; this explicit style replaces exceptions.

subtopics.title: Handle once, do not log and return

topics.title: Wrapping, errors.Is and errors.As
topics.description: fmt.Errorf with %w wraps a cause while adding context, errors.Is walks the chain to compare against sentinels, errors.As extracts a typed error, and errors.Join combines several failures.

topics.title: Designing error types
topics.description: Exported sentinel errors for expected conditions, struct error types carrying fields such as status codes, adding context at each layer without repeating it, and keeping messages lowercase and unpunctuated.

topics.title: panic, recover and when not to use them
topics.description: panic unwinds the stack running deferred calls, recover inside a deferred function stops it, runtime errors such as nil map writes and index out of range panic, and panics are for programmer bugs rather than expected failures.

topics.title: Designing packages and exported APIs
topics.description: Short lowercase package names that read well at call sites, internal/ directories the compiler enforces, doc comments starting with the identifier, NewT constructors with useful zero values and functional options, and why import cycles are illegal.

subtopics.title: NewT constructors and useful zero values

topics.title: Module versions, replace and workspaces
topics.description: Semantic version tags, the /v2 suffix rule for breaking changes, replace directives for local forks, go.work for multi-module development, vendoring, and how the module proxy and GOPRIVATE interact.

topics.title: Files with os and bufio
topics.description: os.ReadFile and os.WriteFile for whole files, os.Open with deferred Close for streams, bufio.Scanner for line-by-line reading with its token size limit, bufio.Writer with Flush, and file permissions.

topics.title: io.Reader and io.Writer
topics.description: Two tiny interfaces that compose the whole I/O ecosystem: files, sockets, gzip, HTTP bodies and buffers all implement them, so io.Copy, io.MultiWriter, io.TeeReader and io.LimitReader work everywhere.

topics.title: JSON with encoding/json
topics.description: Marshal and Unmarshal driven by struct tags, omitempty and the - tag, json.Decoder for streams and DisallowUnknownFields, custom MarshalJSON, and why unexported fields are silently skipped.

topics.title: Command-line tools with flag, os/exec and signals
topics.description: Parsing options with the flag package, subcommands with flag.NewFlagSet, exit codes and stderr, running child processes with os/exec and capturing output, and cancelling on Ctrl-C with signal.NotifyContext.

topics.title: Methods and receivers
topics.description: Methods attach to any named type, value receivers copy and pointer receivers mutate, the method set rules decide which interfaces a type satisfies, and Go auto-addresses variables so v.Method() works with pointer receivers.

topics.title: Interfaces and implicit satisfaction
topics.description: A type satisfies an interface just by having the methods, so interfaces are defined by consumers and kept small; accept interfaces and return structs, and beware the nil-pointer-inside-interface trap.

subtopics.title: Interface values and the typed nil trap

topics.title: Type assertions and type switches
topics.description: x.(T) recovers the concrete type with a comma-ok form to avoid panics, switch v := x.(type) branches on several types, and any (interface{}) is the empty interface every value satisfies.

topics.title: Composition and embedding
topics.description: Go has no inheritance: embedding a struct or interface promotes its fields and methods, outer methods shadow inner ones, and embedding is how you extend types such as sync.Mutex or an http.Handler.

topics.title: Generics with type parameters
topics.description: Type parameters on functions and types, constraints built from interfaces with type sets, comparable and cmp.Ordered, type inference at call sites, and choosing generics over interfaces only when it removes real duplication.

subtopics.title: Type parameters on functions and types

topics.title: Stack, heap and escape analysis
topics.description: The compiler decides per variable whether it lives on the goroutine stack or escapes to the heap; go build -gcflags=-m shows why, and returning pointers, storing in interfaces or capturing in closures are common causes.

topics.title: The garbage collector and GOGC
topics.description: Go uses a concurrent tri-colour mark-and-sweep collector with tiny pauses; GOGC tunes how much the heap grows before a cycle, GOMEMLIMIT caps total memory, and allocation rate rather than heap size usually drives cost.

subtopics.title: Allocation rate as the real cost

topics.title: Reducing allocations and PGO
topics.description: Preallocating slices with capacity, reusing buffers with sync.Pool, avoiding boxing into interfaces in hot loops, string and byte conversions, and profile-guided optimisation with a default.pgo file.

topics.title: Secure coding in Go
topics.description: Parameterised queries against SQL injection, html/template contextual escaping against XSS, limiting request bodies, validating paths against traversal, crypto/rand and bcrypt for tokens and passwords, and govulncheck for vulnerable dependencies.

categories.title: Concurrency
categories.description: Goroutines, channels, synchronisation and cancellation, the reasons most people pick Go.

topics.title: Goroutines and the scheduler
topics.description: go f() starts a lightweight goroutine multiplexed onto OS threads by the M:N scheduler; GOMAXPROCS bounds parallelism, main returning kills everything, and sync.WaitGroup waits for a batch to finish.

topics.title: Channels
topics.description: Unbuffered channels synchronise sender and receiver, buffered channels decouple them, close signals no more values, range drains until closed, nil channels block forever, and direction types document ownership.

topics.title: select, timers and tickers
topics.description: select waits on several channel operations choosing randomly among ready ones, default makes it non-blocking, time.After and time.NewTimer add timeouts, and time.Ticker drives periodic work that must be stopped.

topics.title: sync: Mutex, RWMutex, Once and WaitGroup
topics.description: Protecting shared state with Mutex and RWMutex, the rule that locks must not be copied, sync.Once for one-time initialisation, sync.Map for specific read-heavy cases, and choosing channels versus mutexes.

topics.title: The atomic package and the memory model
topics.description: Lock-free counters and flags with atomic.Int64 and atomic.Bool, compare-and-swap, atomic.Pointer, and the happens-before rules of the Go memory model that define what a data race is.

topics.title: Context for cancellation and deadlines
topics.description: context.Context travels as the first parameter to carry cancellation, deadlines and request-scoped values; WithCancel, WithTimeout and WithDeadline derive children, and every long operation must watch ctx.Done().

topics.title: Concurrency patterns
topics.description: Worker pools bounded by a channel, pipelines of stages connected by channels, fan-out and fan-in, semaphores from buffered channels, and errgroup for running goroutines that share cancellation and the first error.

topics.title: Race detector, deadlocks and goroutine leaks
topics.description: go test -race instruments memory accesses to catch data races at runtime, the runtime reports all goroutines asleep as a deadlock, and leaked goroutines blocked on channels nobody reads are found with pprof or goleak.

topics.title: Tests with the testing package
topics.description: Tests live in _test.go files beside the code, functions named TestXxx take *testing.T, t.Errorf continues while t.Fatalf stops, t.Helper improves failure locations, and go test ./... runs everything with caching.

topics.title: Table-driven tests and subtests
topics.description: A slice of cases with names and expected values, t.Run for each so failures are named and filterable, t.Parallel for independent cases, and golden files for large expected outputs.

topics.title: Fakes, interfaces and httptest
topics.description: Because interfaces are implicit, hand-written fakes are usually simpler than mocking frameworks; httptest.NewServer and NewRecorder test HTTP code without sockets, and testify or go-cmp help with assertions and diffs.

topics.title: Benchmarks, examples and fuzzing
topics.description: BenchmarkXxx with b.Loop or b.N and -benchmem to measure allocations, Example functions whose Output comment is verified by go test, and FuzzXxx with a seed corpus for randomised input testing.

topics.title: Profiling and debugging with pprof, trace and Delve
topics.description: CPU, heap, block and mutex profiles from go test -cpuprofile or net/http/pprof in a live service, reading them with go tool pprof and flame graphs, the execution tracer for scheduler and GC behaviour, and Delve for breakpoints and goroutine inspection.

subtopics.title: go tool pprof and flame graphs

categories.title: HTTP Services and Cloud-Native Applications
categories.description: Building the backend and cloud services Go is best known for; HTTP and REST fundamentals live in track-rest-api.

topics.title: net/http servers and routing
topics.description: The Handler interface and HandlerFunc, ServeMux with method and wildcard patterns since Go 1.22, path values, http.Server with read and write timeouts, and why the defaults without timeouts are unsafe in production.

subtopics.title: ServeMux patterns with methods and wildcards

topics.title: Middleware and handler composition
topics.description: Wrapping handlers in functions that return handlers for logging, recovery, auth and request IDs, ordering the chain, passing data through context, and where chi or gorilla add value over the standard mux.

topics.title: JSON APIs and request validation
topics.description: Decoding bodies with size limits and unknown-field checks, validating fields explicitly, consistent error response shapes and status codes, content negotiation basics and setting Content-Type correctly.

topics.title: HTTP clients with net/http
topics.description: A shared http.Client with a Timeout, always closing response bodies, connection pooling in Transport, requests with context, checking status codes, and retries with exponential backoff and jitter.

topics.title: Databases with database/sql and pgx
topics.description: sql.DB as a connection pool, QueryRow, Scan and Exec with placeholders, transactions with rollback on error, pool sizing, pgx for PostgreSQL features, sqlc for generated code and golang-migrate for schema changes.

topics.title: gRPC and Protocol Buffers
topics.description: Defining services in .proto files, generating Go code with protoc and protoc-gen-go-grpc, unary and streaming RPCs, interceptors for logging and auth, deadlines through context, and when gRPC beats REST.

topics.title: Structured logging and observability
topics.description: log/slog with JSON handlers, levels and attributes, logging with context, Prometheus metrics via promhttp, OpenTelemetry traces across services, and health and readiness endpoints.

topics.title: Configuration, graceful shutdown and deployment
topics.description: Twelve-factor configuration from environment variables, server.Shutdown with a context on SIGTERM so in-flight requests finish, static binaries with CGO_ENABLED=0 and cross-compilation, ldflags for versions, and distroless containers with Kubernetes probes.

topics.title: Project: CLI todo tool with JSON storage
topics.description: Build a todo CLI with flag subcommands (add, list, done, rm), atomic JSON persistence in the user config directory, table-driven tests using t.TempDir, and a cross-compiled release with a version injected by ldflags.

subtopics.title: Design subcommands and the data model

topics.title: Project: concurrent web crawler
topics.description: Crawl a site with a bounded worker pool, a visited set behind a mutex, per-request context timeouts, cancellation on Ctrl-C, and export a link graph; verify it with the race detector and httptest servers.

topics.title: Project: REST API with PostgreSQL and Docker
topics.description: A net/http service with a ServeMux, middleware for logging and recovery, database/sql or pgx with migrations, integration tests against a test database, graceful shutdown, and a multi-stage distroless Dockerfile.

subtopics.title: Integration tests with a real database

topics.title: Project: gRPC microservice with observability
topics.description: Define a proto service, implement server and client with interceptors for logging and auth, add Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry traces, health checks, and deploy two instances behind a load balancer locally.

subtopics.title: Add metrics, traces and health checks

topics.title: Project: log processing pipeline
topics.description: Stream a large log file with bufio.Scanner through a pipeline of goroutine stages (parse, filter, aggregate), fan out CPU-bound parsing, emit JSON summaries, and profile with pprof to remove allocations.

subtopics.title: Fan out parsing with a worker pool

topics.title: Go interview questions
topics.description: The questions that come up in Go interviews: slices versus arrays, nil interfaces, value versus pointer receivers, goroutine leaks, channel semantics, select, context, GC behaviour and how Go compares to Java or Rust.

topics.title: Coding interviews in Go
topics.description: Solving problems quickly in Go: bufio for fast input, slices and maps as the workhorses, container/heap, sort with custom comparators, strings.Builder for output, and avoiding common allocation and off-by-one traps.

subtopics.title: Common Go traps under time pressure

title: GraphQL
description: GraphQL servers and clients in TypeScript: the schema definition language, queries, mutations and subscriptions, resolvers and context, the N+1 problem and DataLoader, schema design and Relay pagination, auth, error handling, federation, persisted queries and caching, Apollo and urql clients, testing and security limits.

categories.title: Foundations
categories.description: What GraphQL changes about API design and how a server is stood up.

topics.title: GraphQL compared with REST
topics.description: A typed schema, client-specified field selection in one request and a single endpoint replace resource URLs and fixed payloads; what that buys (no over- or under-fetching) and what it costs (caching, complexity control, tooling).

subtopics.title: When GraphQL is the wrong tool

topics.title: Setting up a server with Apollo Server or Yoga
topics.description: Installing graphql and @apollo/server or graphql-yoga, defining typeDefs and resolvers, mounting on Express or a standalone listener, and enabling the explorer in development.

subtopics.title: Installing graphql and a server library
Yoga and the envelop plugin system

topics.title: Operations, documents and introspection
topics.description: A request carries a document, an operation name and variables; the server validates it against the schema before executing; introspection lets tools discover the schema and should be restricted in production.

topics.title: Tooling: GraphiQL, Code Generator and ESLint
topics.description: GraphiQL and Apollo Sandbox for exploring, GraphQL Code Generator for typed resolvers and operations, the ESLint plugin for schema and operation rules, and VS Code extensions that validate documents against the schema.

topics.title: Scalars, object types and fields
topics.description: The five built-in scalars (Int, Float, String, Boolean, ID), object types with typed fields, the root Query type as the entry point, and describing fields with docstrings.

topics.title: Non-null and list modifiers
topics.description: Bang and brackets compose: [String!]! versus [String]!, how null propagates up to the nearest nullable parent when a non-null field fails, and why that shapes nullability decisions.

topics.title: Enums, input types and arguments
topics.description: Enums for fixed sets, input object types for structured arguments (separate from output types), default argument values, and argument validation at the schema layer.

topics.title: Interfaces and unions
topics.description: Interfaces share fields across types, unions group unrelated types; clients select with inline fragments and __typename, and the server needs resolveType or isTypeOf to identify the concrete type.

topics.title: Custom scalars
topics.description: Defining DateTime, JSON or Money scalars with serialize, parseValue and parseLiteral, using graphql-scalars for common ones, and what validation a scalar should and should not do.

topics.title: Directives and descriptions
topics.description: Built-in @include, @skip and @deprecated, schema directives that annotate types and fields for auth or transformation, and descriptions that become documentation in every tool.

topics.title: Queries, selection sets and aliases
topics.description: Reading data by walking the graph from root fields through nested selection sets, aliases to request the same field twice with different arguments, and how the response mirrors the query shape.

topics.title: Variables and fragments
topics.description: Typed variables instead of string interpolation, default values, named fragments for reusable selections colocated with components, and fragment spreads across operations.

topics.title: Mutations and their design
topics.description: Mutations run root fields serially, take a single input argument by convention, return a payload with the changed object, and are named as verbs (createOrder, not orderCreate) on a consistent pattern.

topics.title: Subscriptions
topics.description: Long-lived operations that push events over WebSockets (graphql-ws) or SSE, the PubSub abstraction on the server, filtering per subscriber, and why Redis PubSub is needed across instances.

topics.title: Operation naming and documents
topics.description: Naming every operation for logs, tracing and persisted queries, one operation per document, and organising .graphql files per feature with fragments alongside the components that use them.

topics.title: Resolver functions and default resolvers
topics.description: A resolver receives (parent, args, context, info) and returns a value or promise; fields without resolvers fall back to reading the property from parent, so most object fields need none.

topics.title: The context object
topics.description: A per-request object built once and passed to every resolver, holding the authenticated user, data sources, loaders and a request id; it must be created per request so caches never leak across users.

subtopics.title: Data sources and loaders in context

topics.title: Execution model and resolver chains
topics.description: Execution walks the selection set breadth-first per level, resolving sibling fields concurrently and child fields after their parent resolves; understanding this explains where database calls happen and how many.

topics.title: The N+1 problem
topics.description: A list of 50 posts each resolving author fires 50 author queries, because resolvers are independent; recognising the pattern in query logs and understanding why naive joins do not fix it for a graph.

topics.title: DataLoader batching and caching
topics.description: DataLoader collects keys requested in one tick, calls a batch function once, and caches per request; writing batch functions that return results in key order and handling missing keys.

topics.title: Resolver-level authorization
topics.description: Checking permissions inside resolvers or via wrappers, returning null versus throwing for forbidden fields, and centralising rules in a service layer so REST and GraphQL share them.

subtopics.title: Null versus error for forbidden data

topics.title: Schema-first versus code-first
topics.description: Writing SDL and mapping resolvers, or generating the schema from code with Pothos, Nexus or TypeGraphQL; how each keeps types in sync and which suits a team.

topics.title: Designing for clients and nullability
topics.description: Model the graph around client use cases rather than tables, make fields nullable unless guaranteed, and avoid generic types that force clients to guess.

topics.title: Relay connections and pagination
topics.description: The Connection spec: edges with cursors and nodes, pageInfo with hasNextPage and endCursor, first/after and last/before arguments, and implementing opaque cursors over keyset queries.

topics.title: Mutation payloads and errors as data
topics.description: Returning a payload type with the result and a userErrors list (or a union of Success and error types) so expected failures are typed and selectable, while unexpected failures use the errors array.

topics.title: Schema evolution and deprecation
topics.description: Additive changes are safe; removing or changing types breaks clients; @deprecated with usage tracking, schema registries and breaking-change checks in CI keep a versionless API healthy.

categories.title: Authentication, Authorization and Errors
categories.description: Token formats and OAuth flows live in track-rest-api; this is the GraphQL integration.

topics.title: Authentication in context
topics.description: Verifying a bearer token or session in the context factory, attaching the user, letting unauthenticated requests through for public fields, and rejecting at the resolver rather than the transport.

topics.title: Authorization patterns
topics.description: Schema directives like @auth(requires: ADMIN), graphql-shield rule trees, and plain checks in resolvers; how to combine them and keep object-level checks close to data access.

topics.title: Error handling and partial data
topics.description: GraphQLError with extensions.code, partial responses with both data and errors, masking internal errors, and formatting errors consistently with a formatError hook.

topics.title: Input validation
topics.description: Schema types catch shape errors, but ranges, formats and cross-field rules need validation in resolvers or with zod or class-validator, returning typed userErrors.

topics.title: Apollo Federation
topics.description: Subgraphs own parts of the graph and extend entities with @key; the router composes a supergraph and plans queries across services; entity resolution via _entities and reference resolvers.

topics.title: Schema stitching versus federation
topics.description: Stitching merges schemas in a gateway with delegation; federation pushes ownership into subgraphs with a spec; trade-offs in coupling, tooling and team autonomy.

topics.title: Persisted queries and APQ
topics.description: Sending a hash instead of the document to cut bandwidth and enable GET caching, automatic persisted queries negotiated at runtime, and safelisted persisted queries that block arbitrary operations.

topics.title: Response caching and cache hints
topics.description: Per-field @cacheControl hints combined into a response max-age, full-response caches in the server or CDN, and entity-level caching in clients; what is safe to cache per user versus publicly.

topics.title: Security: depth, complexity and batching limits
topics.description: Rejecting deeply nested or expensive queries with depth limits and cost analysis, limiting batched operations and aliases, disabling introspection in production, and timeouts per operation.

topics.title: Apollo Client queries and the normalised cache
topics.description: useQuery with loading and error states, the InMemoryCache normalising objects by __typename and id, fetch policies, and type policies for custom keys and pagination merging.

subtopics.title: Cache normalisation by typename and id

topics.title: Apollo Client mutations and cache updates
topics.description: useMutation, automatic cache updates for returned objects with ids, manual update functions and cache.modify for lists, optimistic responses, and refetchQueries as the blunt tool.

topics.title: urql and exchanges
topics.description: A smaller client built around an exchange pipeline (cache, fetch, auth, retry), document caching by default with Graphcache as the normalised option, and when it beats Apollo.

topics.title: Typed operations with Code Generator
topics.description: Generating TypeScript types and hooks from operations, the client preset with TypedDocumentNode, fragment masking, and running codegen in watch mode and CI.

topics.title: Unit testing resolvers
topics.description: Calling resolver functions directly with fake parent, args and context, testing DataLoader batch functions, and asserting on thrown GraphQLErrors.

topics.title: Integration testing with executeOperation
topics.description: Running operations against the real schema with server.executeOperation or a Yoga fetch, seeding a test database, and checking both data and errors in responses.

topics.title: Schema checks and operation safety
topics.description: Comparing the proposed schema against production usage to flag breaking changes, validating client operations against the schema in CI, and gating deploys on both.

topics.title: Observability and tracing
topics.description: Logging operation names and durations, per-resolver traces with Apollo usage reporting or OpenTelemetry, field-level metrics, and alerting on error rates per operation.

topics.title: Project: bookshelf API with DataLoader
topics.description: A GraphQL API for books, authors and reviews on Postgres: SDL schema, resolvers with DataLoader, Relay connections, mutation payloads with userErrors, JWT context auth and integration tests.

topics.title: Project: live dashboard with subscriptions
topics.description: Metrics pushed to a React dashboard: subscriptions over graphql-ws with Redis PubSub, filtered per tenant, Apollo Client cache updates from subscription data and reconnect handling.

topics.title: Project: federated commerce graph
topics.description: Products, inventory and reviews as three subgraphs with @key entities composed by the Apollo Router; add a field from inventory onto Product, run composition checks in CI and trace a query plan.

topics.title: Project: hardened public GraphQL API
topics.description: Take the bookshelf API public: persisted query safelist, depth and cost limits, introspection off, response cache hints, rate limits per client, and k6 load tests.

topics.title: GraphQL interview questions
topics.description: What interviewers ask: GraphQL versus REST, N+1 and DataLoader, nullability, mutation design, subscriptions transport, caching challenges, federation, and security limits.

topics.title: GraphQL schema design exercises
topics.description: Design a schema for a social feed, a marketplace or a booking system in 30 minutes: entities, connections, mutations with payloads, auth boundaries and evolution strategy.

title: gRPC
description: gRPC services in Go with Protocol Buffers: messages, enums and schema evolution, service definitions and code generation with buf, unary and streaming RPCs, deadlines and cancellation, status codes and rich errors, interceptors, TLS and token auth, load balancing, gRPC-Web and grpc-gateway, observability, testing and performance.

categories.title: Foundations
categories.description: What gRPC is, why it sits on HTTP/2, and a first service running end to end.

topics.title: What gRPC is and when to use it
topics.description: A contract-first RPC framework using Protocol Buffers over HTTP/2 with generated clients in many languages; strong for service-to-service calls, streaming and polyglot systems, weaker for browsers and public APIs where JSON over REST wins.

topics.title: HTTP/2 as the transport
topics.description: How gRPC maps calls onto HTTP/2 streams: one TCP connection multiplexes many RPCs, headers carry metadata, length-prefixed messages form the body, and trailers carry the status; this is why plain HTTP/1.1 proxies break gRPC.

topics.title: Installing protoc, buf and the Go plugins
topics.description: Setting up protoc or buf, protoc-gen-go and protoc-gen-go-grpc, go module layout for generated code, and the go_package option that decides import paths.

topics.title: A first service end to end
topics.description: Writing greeter.proto, generating code, implementing the server interface, registering it on a grpc.Server, dialing from a client with grpc.NewClient, and calling it with grpcurl.

categories.title: Protocol Buffers
categories.description: The schema language and wire format behind every gRPC message.

topics.title: Messages, fields and scalar types
topics.description: message blocks with typed fields, the scalar types (int32, int64, uint, sint, fixed, float, double, bool, string, bytes), proto3 defaults, and how each maps to Go types.

subtopics.title: Scalar types and their Go mapping

topics.title: Field numbers and the wire format
topics.description: Each field is encoded as a tag (number and wire type) followed by the value, numbers 1 to 15 cost one byte, unknown fields are preserved, and why numbers must never be reused.

topics.title: Enums and defaults
topics.description: enum definitions with a required zero value, the UNSPECIFIED convention, allow_alias, and how unknown enum values arrive from newer senders.

subtopics.title: Unknown enum values from newer peers

topics.title: Nested, repeated and map fields
topics.description: Nested messages, repeated fields as lists with packed encoding, map fields and their key restrictions, and how Go represents each (slices, maps, pointers to nested structs).

topics.title: oneof and optional
topics.description: oneof for mutually exclusive fields with presence, proto3 optional for scalar presence tracking, and how Go generates interfaces for oneof and pointers for optional.

topics.title: Well-known types
topics.description: Timestamp, Duration, Empty, Any, Struct, wrappers and FieldMask from google/protobuf, and how to convert them in Go with timestamppb and durationpb.

subtopics.title: Struct and Value for JSON-like data

topics.title: Schema evolution and compatibility rules
topics.description: Safe changes (adding fields, renaming, adding enum values, converting between compatible types), unsafe ones (changing numbers or types, removing required semantics), reserved numbers and names, and buf breaking checks.

topics.title: Defining services and RPCs
topics.description: service blocks with rpc methods that take and return exactly one message each, the stream keyword for streaming, and request/response message naming conventions.

subtopics.title: One request and one response message

topics.title: Generated Go code: clients and servers
topics.description: What protoc-gen-go-grpc emits: a client interface with methods per RPC, a server interface, the Unimplemented struct, registration functions and stream types; reading it avoids surprises.

topics.title: buf: lint, breaking and generate
topics.description: buf.yaml modules, buf lint with the standard style rules, buf breaking against the main branch, buf.gen.yaml templates for plugins, and the Buf Schema Registry for sharing protos.

topics.title: Packages, imports and options
topics.description: proto packages as namespaces, importing other files and well-known types, versioned package names like shop.v1, and file and field options that tune generation.

topics.title: Unary RPCs
topics.description: The request-response call: server method signature with ctx and request, client call with ctx and options, and passing per-call options such as timeouts and metadata.

topics.title: Server streaming
topics.description: One request, many responses: the server calls stream.Send in a loop and returns to end the stream; the client calls Recv until io.EOF; use cases like tailing logs and paging large results.

topics.title: Client streaming
topics.description: Many requests, one response: the client Sends then calls CloseAndRecv; the server Recvs until io.EOF and returns via SendAndClose; useful for uploads and batched metrics.

topics.title: Bidirectional streaming and flow control
topics.description: Independent send and receive streams, goroutines for concurrent reading and writing, the rule that Send and Recv are each safe from one goroutine at a time, and ending cleanly with CloseSend.

subtopics.title: Concurrency rules for Send and Recv

topics.title: Deadlines and cancellation
topics.description: Clients set a deadline on the context that propagates across hops; servers check ctx.Err() and stop work; DEADLINE_EXCEEDED and CANCELED statuses, and why every RPC should have a deadline.

topics.title: Status codes
topics.description: The 17 canonical codes (OK, INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND, ALREADY_EXISTS, PERMISSION_DENIED, UNAUTHENTICATED, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, FAILED_PRECONDITION, UNAVAILABLE, INTERNAL and more), creating them with status.Error, and mapping domain errors consistently.

topics.title: Rich error details
topics.description: Attaching typed details (BadRequest field violations, RetryInfo, ErrorInfo) to a status with WithDetails, reading them on the client, and keeping messages free of secrets.

topics.title: Metadata: headers and trailers
topics.description: Key-value metadata sent as HTTP/2 headers (before the response) and trailers (after), setting it from clients with metadata.AppendToOutgoingContext, reading it in servers, and binary keys with the -bin suffix.

topics.title: Retries and hedging
topics.description: Client-side retry policy via service config for safe, retryable codes, exponential backoff, hedging for latency, and the server-side pushback and idempotency conditions that make retries safe.

topics.title: Unary and stream interceptors
topics.description: Middleware for gRPC: unary interceptors wrap a handler call, stream interceptors wrap the stream and can wrap ServerStream to observe messages; used for logging, auth, metrics and recovery.

topics.title: Chaining interceptors
topics.description: grpc.ChainUnaryInterceptor and ChainStreamInterceptor, execution order, and placing recovery first, then logging, auth, and metrics so failures are always observed.

topics.title: TLS and mutual TLS
topics.description: credentials.NewTLS for server certificates, client verification of the server, mutual TLS where clients present certificates, certificate rotation, and why insecure credentials are for local only.

topics.title: Token authentication with per-RPC credentials
topics.description: Sending bearer tokens in metadata via credentials.PerRPCCredentials, requiring transport security for them, validating tokens in a server interceptor, and returning UNAUTHENTICATED.

topics.title: Authorization in interceptors
topics.description: Extracting the principal from a validated token or client certificate, per-method permission tables keyed by full method name, resource checks inside handlers, and PERMISSION_DENIED semantics.

topics.title: Channels, connection states and keepalive
topics.description: A ClientConn manages connections and reconnects, connectivity states from IDLE to READY to TRANSIENT_FAILURE, keepalive pings to detect dead peers, and server enforcement policies.

topics.title: Name resolution and client-side load balancing
topics.description: Resolvers (dns, passthrough, xds) turn a target into addresses, pick_first versus round_robin balancers, why one long-lived connection defeats L4 balancing, and service config delivery.

topics.title: Proxy load balancing and Kubernetes
topics.description: L7 proxies (Envoy, Linkerd, nginx with grpc_pass) that balance per request, headless Services for client-side balancing in Kubernetes, and readiness so new pods receive traffic safely. Kubernetes itself lives in track-kubernetes.

topics.title: gRPC-Web
topics.description: A browser-compatible protocol variant with trailers in the body, requiring Envoy or the Go grpc-web wrapper, supporting unary and server streaming only, and generated TypeScript clients.

subtopics.title: Envoy grpc_web filter or Go wrapper

topics.title: grpc-gateway and REST transcoding
topics.description: Annotating RPCs with google.api.http options so grpc-gateway generates a JSON reverse proxy, mapping paths and bodies, producing OpenAPI, and error translation from status codes to HTTP.

topics.title: Logging and metrics
topics.description: Logging interceptors that record method, code and duration, Prometheus metrics via go-grpc-prometheus or OpenTelemetry, and the RED metrics per method. Observability tooling lives in track-observability.

topics.title: Tracing with OpenTelemetry
topics.description: otelgrpc stats handlers on client and server, trace context propagated in metadata, spans per RPC and per stream message, and exporting via OTLP.

topics.title: Health checking and reflection
topics.description: The standard grpc.health.v1 service for per-service status, wiring it to Kubernetes probes via grpc_health_probe or native gRPC probes, and server reflection for grpcurl and debugging.

topics.title: Testing with bufconn
topics.description: Running a real gRPC server on an in-memory bufconn listener, dialing it from tests, table-driven RPC tests, and asserting status codes with status.Code.

topics.title: Testing streaming and mocks
topics.description: Driving streaming RPCs in tests with goroutines and channels, generated mocks for client interfaces with mockgen, and fakes for downstream services.

topics.title: Performance tuning
topics.description: Message size limits, compression with gzip, connection reuse and pooling, keepalive settings, streaming instead of large unary calls, and benchmarking with ghz.

topics.title: Project: inventory service with buf and bufconn tests
topics.description: Build an inventory service: versioned protos linted with buf, unary CRUD RPCs with rich validation errors, deadlines, a logging interceptor, health checks, reflection and bufconn tests in CI with buf breaking.

topics.title: Project: log streaming with server and client streams
topics.description: A log service where agents upload batches via client streaming and dashboards tail logs via server streaming with filters, handling backpressure, cancellation and reconnect.

topics.title: Project: chat with bidirectional streaming and auth
topics.description: A chat backend with bidi streams, mTLS between services, bearer tokens for users, per-room fan-out with goroutines, and a gRPC-Web or Connect front end.

subtopics.title: Browser access via gRPC-Web or Connect

topics.title: Project: orders API exposed via grpc-gateway
topics.description: An orders service with google.api.http annotations, a generated JSON gateway, OpenAPI output, consistent status-to-HTTP mapping, OpenTelemetry tracing across gateway and service, and load tests with ghz.

topics.title: gRPC interview questions
topics.description: What interviewers ask: gRPC versus REST, why HTTP/2, protobuf compatibility rules, streaming types, deadlines, status codes, load balancing pitfalls and browser support.

topics.title: gRPC API design exercises
topics.description: Design the protos and RPCs for a payments service or a notification system: message evolution, streaming choices, error details, deadlines, auth and gateway exposure.

title: HTML
description: HTML as a language rather than a formality: document structure, semantic elements, text, links, responsive images and media, tables, forms with built-in validation, metadata and SEO, embedding SVG and canvas, the DOM, templates and web components, validation habits, and projects.

categories.title: Documents and Structure
categories.description: What a browser needs from a file before anything renders, and the rules the parser follows.

topics.title: Setting up an HTML project and the browser tools
topics.description: A folder, an editor with Emmet, a live-reload server and the Elements panel of DevTools: enough to see every change instantly and inspect what the browser actually built from your markup.

subtopics.title: Serving files with a local server
View source versus the live DOM

topics.title: The anatomy of an HTML document
topics.description: The doctype that switches on standards mode, the html root with a lang attribute, head for metadata and body for content, and what the browser silently inserts when you leave parts out.

topics.title: Elements, attributes and nesting rules
topics.description: Tags, content and void elements, boolean and enumerated attributes, quoting rules, and the content model that decides which elements may legally live inside which.

subtopics.title: Start tags, end tags and void elements

topics.title: Character encoding, entities and whitespace
topics.description: Declaring UTF-8 first in the head, when to use named and numeric entities such as & and —, and how the parser collapses runs of whitespace so that layout does not depend on your indentation.

topics.title: Headings and paragraphs
topics.description: h1 to h6 as an outline for readers and assistive tech, p for blocks of prose, br and hr for the rare cases they fit, and why headings should never be chosen for their default font size.

subtopics.title: h1 to h6 as structure not style

topics.title: Inline text semantics
topics.description: strong and em for importance and stress versus b and i for typographic offset, mark, small, abbr with a title, time with a machine-readable datetime, and span as the meaningless fallback.

subtopics.title: strong and em versus b and i

topics.title: Lists: ul, ol and dl
topics.description: Unordered and ordered lists with start, reversed and type, nested lists placed inside li, and description lists for term and definition pairs such as glossaries and metadata.

subtopics.title: ul and ol with start and reversed

topics.title: Quotations, code and preformatted text
topics.description: blockquote and q with cite, pre for whitespace-preserving blocks, code, kbd, samp and var for technical prose, and how to escape angle brackets inside code samples.

topics.title: Anchors, hrefs and URL forms
topics.description: The a element with absolute, root-relative and document-relative URLs, fragment links to ids, mailto and tel schemes, and how the base element changes resolution.

topics.title: Link targets, rel and download
topics.description: target="_blank" with rel="noopener" (now implied), rel values such as nofollow, external and alternate, the download attribute, and writing link text that makes sense out of context.

topics.title: Navigation landmarks and skip links
topics.description: Wrapping primary navigation in nav, marking the current page with aria-current, and adding a skip link so keyboard users jump past repeated menus straight to main content.

subtopics.title: The nav element and when to use it

topics.title: The img element and alt text
topics.description: src, width and height to reserve space, alt that describes function rather than appearance, empty alt for decorative images, and formats such as JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF and SVG.

topics.title: Responsive images with srcset and sizes
topics.description: Letting the browser choose among candidates: width descriptors with sizes for fluid images, density descriptors for fixed-size ones, and why sizes must reflect the CSS layout.

subtopics.title: How the browser picks a candidate

topics.title: Art direction with picture
topics.description: The picture element with source media and type attributes for cropping differently per breakpoint or serving AVIF with a JPEG fallback, always ending in an img that carries the alt.

topics.title: Video and audio elements
topics.description: video and audio with controls, multiple source formats, poster images, preload and autoplay rules (muted only), and track elements for captions and subtitles.

topics.title: Figures, captions and lazy loading
topics.description: figure and figcaption for self-contained illustrations, loading="lazy" and decoding="async" on images below the fold, and fetchpriority for the hero image that matters most.

subtopics.title: loading="lazy" and when not to use it

topics.title: Table structure: thead, tbody and tfoot
topics.description: table, tr, th and td, grouping rows into head, body and foot so headers repeat when printing and styles target the right region, and why tables are for data not layout.

topics.title: Headers, scope and captions
topics.description: caption for the table title, scope="col" and scope="row" so screen readers announce the right header with each cell, and headers/id pairing for complex tables.

subtopics.title: headers and id for complex tables

topics.title: Spanning cells and column groups
topics.description: colspan and rowspan for merged cells, colgroup and col for column-wide styling, and keeping row counts consistent so the table stays a rectangle.

categories.title: Forms and Inputs
categories.description: Collecting input with markup that validates, autofills and reads correctly before any JavaScript is involved.

topics.title: The form element and submission
topics.description: action and method, how GET encodes fields into the query string and POST into the body, enctype for files, the name attribute that decides what gets sent, and implicit submission with Enter.

subtopics.title: The name attribute and submitted data

topics.title: Input types
topics.description: text, email, url, tel, number, range, date, time, color, search, password, checkbox, radio, hidden and file: each changes the keyboard, the widget and the validation the browser applies for free.

topics.title: Labels, fieldsets and legends
topics.description: Explicit for/id and implicit wrapping labels that enlarge the click target and give controls an accessible name, fieldset and legend for grouping related controls such as radio sets.

topics.title: Validation attributes and the constraint API
topics.description: required, minlength, maxlength, min, max, step and pattern give native validation with browser messages; novalidate turns it off, and the :valid and :invalid states plus setCustomValidity extend it.

topics.title: select, datalist, textarea and buttons
topics.description: select with option and optgroup, multiple selection, datalist for suggestions on a free-text input, textarea rows and wrap, and the three button types with type="button" as the safe default.

topics.title: File uploads and autofill
topics.description: input type="file" with accept and multiple, capture for cameras, and autocomplete tokens such as given-name, email and one-time-code that make browsers and password managers fill fields correctly.

topics.title: Landmark elements: header, main, footer, nav and aside
topics.description: The five landmarks that let assistive technology jump around a page, exactly one main per page, and header and footer that mean something different inside an article than at the top level.

subtopics.title: Landmarks as navigation for screen readers

topics.title: article versus section versus div
topics.description: article for self-contained pieces that make sense syndicated, section for thematic groups that deserve a heading, and div when you only need a styling or scripting hook.

topics.title: Heading hierarchy and the document outline
topics.description: Why the promised outline algorithm was never implemented, so the visible heading levels are the outline, and how to check a page with a headings map before shipping.

topics.title: Global attributes: id, class, data-*, hidden, title and tabindex
topics.description: Attributes any element accepts: unique ids, classes for styling hooks, data-* for custom values read via dataset, hidden, title tooltips, tabindex rules and contenteditable.

topics.title: Meta tags and the viewport
topics.description: The viewport meta that makes mobile layouts work, theme-color, robots directives, http-equiv refresh and why most keywords-style meta tags are ignored.

subtopics.title: Meta tags that no longer matter

topics.title: Title, description and canonical URLs
topics.description: The title element as the tab label and search result headline, meta description as the snippet, and rel="canonical" to tell search engines which of several duplicate URLs is the original.

topics.title: Open Graph, Twitter cards and favicons
topics.description: og:title, og:image and friends that control link previews in chat and social apps, Twitter card tags, and the modern favicon set: an SVG icon, a PNG fallback and the apple-touch-icon.

topics.title: Structured data with JSON-LD
topics.description: Embedding schema.org types such as Article, Product and FAQPage in a script type="application/ld+json" block so search engines can show rich results, and validating with the Rich Results test.

topics.title: Linking stylesheets and scripts
topics.description: link rel="stylesheet" and its render-blocking cost, script placement with defer, async and type="module", the difference between them, and resource hints like preconnect and preload.

topics.title: iframes and sandboxing
topics.description: Embedding another document with iframe, the sandbox and allow attributes that restrict scripts, forms and permissions, loading="lazy", and why cross-origin frames cannot touch each other.

topics.title: Inline SVG
topics.description: Writing vector graphics directly in the page: viewBox and coordinate systems, basic shapes and paths, styling with CSS, reusing symbols with use, and when an img src is better than inline.

subtopics.title: Styling SVG with CSS and currentColor
symbol and use for icon sets

topics.title: Canvas basics
topics.description: The canvas element as a bitmap drawn with JavaScript: getContext("2d"), paths, fills and strokes, text, images, and why canvas content is invisible to assistive technology unless you provide fallback.

topics.title: details, summary and dialog
topics.description: Native disclosure widgets with details and summary, the name attribute for exclusive accordions, and the dialog element with showModal, backdrop styling and form method="dialog".

categories.title: The DOM, Templates and Web Components

topics.title: How the parser builds the DOM
topics.description: Tokenising and tree construction, error recovery that fixes unclosed tags, the difference between the source and the tree DevTools shows, and how scripts pause parsing.

subtopics.title: Error recovery and implied end tags

topics.title: Querying and changing the DOM
topics.description: Nodes versus elements, querySelector and querySelectorAll, reading and setting attributes, textContent versus innerHTML and its injection risk, and creating or removing elements.

topics.title: Events from HTML's point of view
topics.description: Inline on* attributes versus addEventListener, bubbling and capture, the load and DOMContentLoaded events, and default actions such as link navigation and form submission that preventDefault stops.

topics.title: The template and slot elements
topics.description: template holds inert markup that is parsed but not rendered, cloned with content.cloneNode for repeated UI, and slot marks where light DOM children land inside a shadow tree.

topics.title: Custom elements
topics.description: Defining a class that extends HTMLElement, registering it with customElements.define, the connectedCallback and attributeChangedCallback lifecycle, and the required hyphen in the tag name.

topics.title: Shadow DOM and encapsulation
topics.description: attachShadow creates a scoped subtree whose styles do not leak in or out, open versus closed modes, ::part and CSS custom properties as the styling API, and declarative shadow DOM.

topics.title: Validating markup
topics.description: Running pages through the W3C Nu HTML Checker, reading its errors versus warnings, wiring html-validate or similar into CI, and the bugs invalid nesting causes across browsers.

topics.title: Accessibility baked into markup
topics.description: The accessibility you get for free from correct HTML: native controls, labels, alt, headings and landmarks, and the ARIA rule that you should use a native element before reaching for a role.

topics.title: HTML that loads fast
topics.description: Ordering the head for early discovery, keeping critical CSS small, deferring scripts, setting image dimensions, lazy loading below the fold and avoiding deep DOM trees that slow style and layout.

topics.title: Common mistakes and legacy HTML
topics.description: Deprecated elements and attributes such as center, font and bgcolor, tables for layout, divs for everything, inline styles, missing alt and label, and how to modernise an old page.

topics.title: Project: semantic personal portfolio
topics.description: Build a multi-page portfolio with correct landmarks, heading hierarchy, a nav with aria-current, responsive images via picture and srcset, Open Graph metadata and a validated, JavaScript-free contact form.

topics.title: Project: accessible registration form
topics.description: A registration form with labels, fieldsets for grouped choices, the right input types and autocomplete tokens, native constraint validation with pattern and required, and a confirmation dialog element.

topics.title: Project: data table report page
topics.description: A report page with a captioned data table using thead, tbody, tfoot, scoped headers, colgroup styling and merged cells, plus a figure with an inline SVG chart and a print-friendly structure.

subtopics.title: Check it with a screen reader

topics.title: Project: web component card library
topics.description: A small set of custom elements: a product card with named slots, a disclosure widget built on details, and a modal built on dialog, styled through ::part and custom properties, with declarative shadow DOM for SSR.

topics.title: HTML interview questions
topics.description: The questions that keep coming up: semantic elements and why they matter, block versus inline, defer versus async, srcset versus picture, data attributes, forms without JavaScript and the DOM versus source.

topics.title: Whiteboard markup exercises
topics.description: Practice writing markup by hand under time pressure: a card list, a pricing table, a login form and a navigation bar, choosing the right elements and defending each choice.
