title: iOS Development with SwiftUI
description: Shipping iPhone and iPad apps in Swift: Xcode, SwiftUI views and layout, the Observation framework and environment, NavigationStack, SwiftData and Core Data, URLSession with async/await, actors, notifications, accessibility, animations, UIKit interop, XCTest, Instruments, Keychain and the App Store release workflow.

categories.title: Xcode and Project Setup
categories.description: The tools and the app skeleton before the first view.

topics.title: Swift features SwiftUI code relies on
topics.description: A fast recap of the Swift that fills every SwiftUI file: structs and value semantics, property wrappers, trailing closures and result builders, optionals and if let, protocols with associated types (some View), and async/await. The Swift track covers each in depth.

topics.title: Xcode projects, targets and schemes
topics.description: Creating an app project, the difference between a project, target and scheme, build settings and Info.plist, simulators and running on a device, and adding dependencies with Swift Package Manager.

topics.title: App entry point and scenes
topics.description: The @main App struct, WindowGroup and other Scene types, how SwiftUI creates the root view, the @UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor bridge for delegate callbacks, and where app-wide services get created.

topics.title: Previews and the Canvas
topics.description: The #Preview macro, previewing multiple states, devices, colour schemes and Dynamic Type sizes, injecting sample data and mock environment values, and using previews as the fastest UI dev loop.

subtopics.title: Device, colour scheme and Dynamic Type variants

categories.title: SwiftUI Views and Modifiers
categories.description: Views are cheap value descriptions; the framework diffs them and updates the screen.

topics.title: Views as structs and the body property
topics.description: A View is a struct whose body describes what to show; SwiftUI recreates these values freely and diffs them, so a view must be cheap and deterministic. Why views are not objects and why heavy work belongs elsewhere.

topics.title: Modifiers and modifier order
topics.description: Each modifier wraps the view in a new view, so padding then background differs from background then padding. Building custom ViewModifiers, conditional modifiers, and reading the type of a modified view to understand the wrapping.

topics.title: Text, images, SF Symbols and buttons
topics.description: Text with fonts, styles and Markdown, Image from assets and SF Symbols with rendering modes, Label, Button with roles and styles, and Link and ShareLink for system actions.

topics.title: Custom views and ViewBuilder
topics.description: Extracting reusable views with properties and @ViewBuilder closures for slots, generic views over content, preference keys for child-to-parent data, and the style protocols that let a component take many looks.

topics.title: View identity and lifecycle
topics.description: Structural identity from the view tree position versus explicit identity with id, why changing identity resets state and triggers onAppear, transitions on identity change, and onAppear, onDisappear and task as the lifecycle hooks.

categories.title: Layout
categories.description: Parents propose sizes, children choose, parents position.

topics.title: Stacks, spacing and alignment
topics.description: HStack, VStack and ZStack with spacing and alignment, Spacer and Divider, alignment guides for lining up baselines and custom edges, and lazy stacks for long content.

topics.title: The layout process and frames
topics.description: Parent proposes a size, child returns its size, parent places it. frame with fixed and min/max values, fixedSize, layoutPriority, and why a Text shrinks while an Image does not.

subtopics.title: frame with min, ideal and max
Reading layout with the view debugger

topics.title: Grids: LazyVGrid, LazyHGrid and Grid
topics.description: Column definitions with GridItem fixed, flexible and adaptive sizing, section headers in lazy grids, and the eager Grid with GridRow for aligned tables of a few cells.

topics.title: GeometryReader and safe areas
topics.description: Reading available size and coordinates with GeometryReader, why it takes all offered space, the safe area and ignoresSafeArea, safeAreaInset for pinned bars, and the newer onGeometryChange and containerRelativeFrame options.

topics.title: ScrollView and adaptive layouts
topics.description: ScrollView with scroll targets and position, size classes for iPhone versus iPad, ViewThatFits for content that adapts, Dynamic Type-aware layouts, and landscape and multitasking handling.

categories.title: State Management and Data Flow
categories.description: Source of truth, ownership, and how changes reach the screen.

topics.title: @State and @Binding
topics.description: @State gives a view private storage that outlives struct recreation, @Binding shares read-write access with a child, $ produces a binding, and the rule that state should be owned as low in the tree as possible.

topics.title: @Observable models and @Bindable
topics.description: The Observation framework: mark a class @Observable, store it with @State in the owner, pass it plainly to children, and use @Bindable for bindings. Views track only the properties they read, so updates are precise.

topics.title: ObservableObject, @StateObject and @ObservedObject
topics.description: The pre-iOS 17 model layer still found in most codebases: @Published properties, @StateObject for ownership versus @ObservedObject for injection, and the bugs that happen when the wrong one is used.

topics.title: The environment
topics.description: Values that flow down the tree: built-in keys such as colorScheme and dismiss, injecting @Observable models with .environment, custom EnvironmentKey values, and when environment beats passing parameters.

topics.title: App lifecycle and scene phase
topics.description: Reacting to the app moving between active, inactive and background with @Environment(\.scenePhase), saving state on background, restoring on launch, background time limits, and state restoration with SceneStorage.

topics.title: NavigationStack and navigationDestination
topics.description: Stack navigation driven by a path array: NavigationLink with values, navigationDestination(for:) to map a type to a screen, programmatic push and pop by editing the path, and toolbar and title configuration.

topics.title: TabView and NavigationSplitView
topics.description: Top-level app structure: TabView with a selection binding and per-tab navigation stacks, NavigationSplitView for iPad and Mac sidebars with two or three columns, and preserving each tab's stack on switch.

topics.title: List, ForEach and editing
topics.description: List with sections, ForEach over Identifiable data, swipe actions, delete and move with an EditButton, selection, list styles, refreshable for pull-to-refresh, and why identity matters for animations.

topics.title: Sheets, alerts, dialogs and search
topics.description: Presenting with sheet(isPresented:) and sheet(item:), fullScreenCover, alerts and confirmationDialog with roles, presentation detents for half sheets, and searchable with suggestions and scopes.

topics.title: SwiftData models, container and @Query
topics.description: Declaring persistent classes with @Model, creating a ModelContainer in the App, @Query to fetch live results into a view with sorting and filtering, and inserting and deleting through the ModelContext.

topics.title: SwiftData relationships, predicates and migrations
topics.description: One-to-many relationships with delete rules, #Predicate for type-safe filters, FetchDescriptor for fetches outside views, versioned schemas with lightweight and custom migrations, and CloudKit sync considerations.

topics.title: Core Data overview
topics.description: The older framework SwiftData is built on: NSPersistentContainer, managed object model and NSManagedObject subclasses, @FetchRequest in SwiftUI, background contexts, and when a project still needs Core Data instead of SwiftData.

topics.title: UserDefaults, @AppStorage and files
topics.description: Small preferences with UserDefaults and @AppStorage bindings, Codable JSON files in the documents directory, FileManager paths, caches versus documents, and what belongs in each store.

topics.title: URLSession with async/await
topics.description: Building URLRequests, data(for:) with async/await, checking HTTPURLResponse status codes, configuring sessions with timeouts and caching, uploading and downloading, and where the network layer sits in the architecture.

topics.title: Codable in practice
topics.description: Decoding nested JSON into structs, CodingKeys for renamed fields, key and date decoding strategies, optional and defaulted fields, custom init(from:) for awkward payloads, and encoding for request bodies.

topics.title: Structured concurrency in apps
topics.description: Task and the .task modifier tied to view lifetime, async let and TaskGroup for parallel requests, cooperative cancellation with Task.checkCancellation, and avoiding detached tasks that outlive their screen.

topics.title: Actors, MainActor and Sendable
topics.description: Protecting shared mutable state with actors, why UI models are @MainActor, Sendable checks under strict concurrency, and the compiler errors that appear when data crosses isolation boundaries.

topics.title: Error handling, caching and AsyncImage
topics.description: Typed error enums for the network layer, mapping to user-facing messages with retry, URLCache and ETag-based caching, offline fallback from the persistence layer, and AsyncImage with placeholder and phase handling.

topics.title: Local and push notifications
topics.description: Requesting authorisation with UNUserNotificationCenter, scheduling local notifications with calendar and time-interval triggers, categories and actions, registering for APNs remote notifications, and handling taps through the delegate.

topics.title: Accessibility
topics.description: VoiceOver labels, values and hints, accessibility traits, grouping elements, Dynamic Type with scaled fonts, reduce motion and increased contrast settings, and testing with the Accessibility Inspector and VoiceOver.

topics.title: Integrating UIKit
topics.description: UIViewRepresentable and UIViewControllerRepresentable with coordinators for delegates, UIHostingController to embed SwiftUI in UIKit apps, and choosing UIKit for text views, cameras, maps and other gaps.

topics.title: Keychain and security
topics.description: Storing tokens with Keychain Services and its access control flags, biometric unlock with LocalAuthentication, App Transport Security, keeping secrets out of the bundle, and protecting data with file protection classes.

topics.title: Location, camera and photos
topics.description: CoreLocation with authorisation levels and async updates, PhotosPicker for selecting images without permission, capturing with the camera through UIImagePickerController or AVFoundation, and the Info.plist usage strings each requires.

topics.title: Implicit and explicit animations
topics.description: withAnimation for state-driven changes, the animation modifier bound to a value, spring and timing curves, and why animations only run when identity is stable and the change is animatable.

topics.title: Transitions and matchedGeometryEffect
topics.description: Insertion and removal transitions with .transition, asymmetric and combined transitions, matchedGeometryEffect for hero-style moves between states, and the zoom navigation transition in recent iOS.

topics.title: Phase and keyframe animators and gestures
topics.description: PhaseAnimator for multi-step sequences, KeyframeAnimator for timed tracks, DragGesture with @GestureState, gesture composition and priorities, and combining gestures with animation for interactive sheets and cards.

topics.title: Unit tests with XCTest and Swift Testing
topics.description: A test target, XCTestCase with setUp and assertions, the newer Swift Testing @Test and #expect macros, parameterised tests, and structuring models so logic can be tested without views.

topics.title: Testing async code and mocking
topics.description: async test functions, injecting fake API clients through protocols, URLProtocol stubs for URLSession, testing @MainActor models, and expectations for callback-based code.

topics.title: UI tests with XCUITest
topics.description: Launching the app with arguments, finding elements by accessibility identifiers, tapping and typing, waiting for existence, screenshots, and keeping UI tests few and stable.

topics.title: Instruments
topics.description: Profiling a release build with Time Profiler for CPU, Allocations and Leaks for memory, the SwiftUI instrument for view body counts, Network and Hangs for stalls, and reading the call tree.

topics.title: SwiftUI performance
topics.description: Common causes of slow SwiftUI: expensive body computations, over-broad observation, AnyView erasure, non-lazy stacks, and identity churn. Diagnosing with Self._printChanges and fixing with smaller views and precise dependencies.

topics.title: Signing, certificates and capabilities
topics.description: Apple Developer Program, bundle identifiers, development and distribution certificates, provisioning profiles, automatic signing, entitlements and capabilities such as push and app groups, and fixing common signing errors.

topics.title: Archiving, App Store Connect and TestFlight
topics.description: Archiving a release build, uploading with Xcode or Transporter, version and build numbers, App Store Connect records, TestFlight internal and external testing, and collecting tester feedback and crashes.

topics.title: App Review, privacy and the listing
topics.description: App Review guidelines that cause rejections, privacy nutrition labels and the privacy manifest, required-reason APIs, screenshots and metadata, age rating, and responding to a rejection.

topics.title: CI/CD and crash monitoring
topics.description: Xcode Cloud workflows or fastlane match and gym on a CI runner, automated tests on each push, uploading to TestFlight from CI, and crash and hang monitoring with MetricKit and Xcode Organizer.

categories.title: Projects and Interview Preparation
categories.description: Apps that exercise the whole track, then the questions hiring teams ask.

topics.title: Project: notes app with iCloud sync
topics.description: A notes app with SwiftData models synced through CloudKit, a NavigationSplitView list and editor, search, rich text formatting, conflict-tolerant models, and unit tests for the model logic.

topics.title: Project: weather app
topics.description: Current and hourly weather for the device location using CoreLocation and a weather API with async/await, cached last result, animated SF Symbol conditions, widgets via WidgetKit, and graceful permission denial.

topics.title: Project: e-commerce catalogue with cart
topics.description: A product grid with LazyVGrid and paging, search and filters, a detail view with matchedGeometryEffect, a cart persisted with SwiftData, checkout validation, and Keychain-stored auth tokens.

topics.title: Project: habit tracker with notifications
topics.description: Daily habits with streaks, per-habit local notification reminders with actions to mark done, a monthly heatmap, SwiftData persistence, and tests for streak logic.

topics.title: iOS interview questions
topics.description: The questions that keep coming up: value versus reference semantics in views, @State versus @Observable versus environment, view identity, the layout algorithm, structured concurrency and actors, SwiftData versus Core Data, and memory management.

topics.title: Live coding a SwiftUI screen
topics.description: Building a list-detail screen from an API in an interview: model first, an @Observable loader with loading and error states, NavigationStack, a List with async loading, and explaining what you would test.

title: Apache Kafka
description: Kafka as a durable, partitioned event log: topics and offsets, producers and consumer groups, delivery guarantees, Schema Registry, Connect, Streams and ksqlDB, retention and replication, security, operations, and the patterns (CDC, event sourcing) teams build on it.

code.label: Python (confluent-kafka) with shell and YAML where needed

categories.title: Foundations and Setup
categories.description: What Kafka is, how a cluster is put together, and a local setup to experiment against.

topics.title: Kafka as a distributed commit log
topics.description: Kafka stores events in an append-only, partitioned log that many consumers read independently at their own pace; why that model decouples producers from consumers and replaces point-to-point queues and nightly file drops.

subtopics.title: Where Kafka fits in a data platform

topics.title: Brokers, clusters and KRaft
topics.description: A cluster is a set of brokers that host partitions; how the controller assigns leadership, and how KRaft replaced ZooKeeper for cluster metadata so a cluster runs without a separate coordination service.

topics.title: Running Kafka locally with Docker Compose
topics.description: A single-broker KRaft cluster in Docker Compose with Schema Registry and a UI, the listener settings that trip everyone up (advertised.listeners), and how to reset the cluster between experiments.

subtopics.title: Compose file for a KRaft broker
Adding Schema Registry and a UI

topics.title: CLI tools and first messages
topics.description: kafka-topics, kafka-console-producer and kafka-console-consumer for creating topics, sending and reading records, describing partitions, and inspecting consumer groups before writing any application code.

subtopics.title: Inspecting consumer groups from the CLI

categories.title: Topics, Partitions and Offsets
categories.description: The storage model that every guarantee in Kafka rests on.

topics.title: Topics and partitions
topics.description: A topic is split into partitions, each an ordered, immutable sequence; partitions are the unit of parallelism, placement and ordering, so the count chosen at creation shapes throughput and consumer scaling.

topics.title: Offsets and consumer position
topics.description: Each record has a monotonically increasing offset within its partition; consumers track their position by committing offsets, which is what makes replay, resume and lag measurement possible.

subtopics.title: Seeking to an offset or timestamp

topics.title: Keys, partitioning and ordering
topics.description: Records with the same key hash to the same partition, which gives per-key ordering (all events for one customer in sequence); null keys round-robin or stick to batches, and hot keys skew partition load.

topics.title: Choosing partition counts and replication factor
topics.description: Sizing a topic: target throughput per partition, expected consumer parallelism, the cost of too many partitions on brokers, and why replication factor 3 with min.insync.replicas 2 is the usual production baseline.

categories.title: Producers
categories.description: Writing records with confluent-kafka and choosing the durability and throughput trade-offs deliberately.

topics.title: The producer API in confluent-kafka
topics.description: Configuring a Producer, produce() as an asynchronous buffered call, delivery callbacks that report success or error per record, and why poll() and flush() must be called for callbacks to fire and buffers to drain.

topics.title: acks, retries and durability
topics.description: acks=0, 1 and all trade latency for safety: all waits for every in-sync replica, and with retries and delivery.timeout.ms the producer survives transient broker failures without losing acknowledged writes.

topics.title: Idempotent producers
topics.description: enable.idempotence assigns a producer id and sequence numbers so broker-side deduplication removes duplicates from retries, giving exactly-once per partition per producer session with ordering preserved.

topics.title: Batching, compression and linger
topics.description: batch.size and linger.ms collect records into larger requests; compression.type (lz4, zstd, snappy, gzip) shrinks them on the wire and disk; the combination is where most producer throughput comes from.

topics.title: Headers, timestamps and custom partitioners
topics.description: Record headers carry metadata such as trace ids and schema hints without touching the payload; CreateTime versus LogAppendTime timestamps; and when a custom partitioning function beats the default hash.

categories.title: Consumers and Delivery Semantics
categories.description: Reading reliably: groups, rebalances, commits and the guarantees you can actually get.

topics.title: The consumer poll loop
topics.description: A Consumer subscribes and loops on poll(); how max.poll.interval.ms and session.timeout.ms detect a dead or stuck consumer, and why heavy processing inside the loop causes surprise rebalances.

topics.title: Consumer groups and rebalancing
topics.description: Members of a group.id split a topic's partitions among themselves; how the group coordinator assigns partitions, why eager rebalances stop the world, and how cooperative sticky assignment reduces the pause.

topics.title: Offset commits: auto and manual
topics.description: enable.auto.commit commits on a timer regardless of processing state; manual commit after processing (sync or async) is what makes at-least-once real, and commit granularity controls how much is reprocessed after a crash.

subtopics.title: Committing per batch versus per record

topics.title: At-most-once and at-least-once delivery
topics.description: Commit-before-process yields at-most-once (may drop), process-before-commit yields at-least-once (may duplicate); why consumers should be idempotent and how a dedupe key or upsert makes duplicates harmless.

topics.title: Exactly-once with transactions
topics.description: A transactional producer writes output records and the consumer's offsets atomically; read_committed consumers skip aborted data, giving exactly-once for Kafka-to-Kafka pipelines but not for arbitrary external sinks.

categories.title: Serialization and Schema Registry
categories.description: Bytes on the wire need a contract; Schema Registry makes that contract enforceable.

topics.title: Serialization choices
topics.description: JSON is readable but untyped and bulky; Avro and Protobuf are compact and schema-driven; how the serializer and deserializer must agree, and the wire format Confluent uses (magic byte plus schema id).

topics.title: Schema Registry
topics.description: A service that stores versioned schemas per subject and rejects incompatible changes at register time; how the serializer fetches and caches schemas by id so consumers always know how to decode a record.

topics.title: Avro with confluent-kafka
topics.description: Defining an Avro schema, using AvroSerializer and AvroDeserializer with to_dict and from_dict hooks, and how defaults and unions let a schema evolve without breaking old readers.

subtopics.title: Logical types for dates and decimals

topics.title: Protobuf and JSON Schema
topics.description: Protobuf field numbers make evolution safe by design and generated classes give typed access; JSON Schema validates loosely typed payloads; when each is preferred and how Schema Registry handles them.

subtopics.title: Picking a format for a team

topics.title: Schema evolution and compatibility
topics.description: BACKWARD, FORWARD and FULL compatibility modes define which changes are allowed (add with default, remove optional); why backward is the default and how upgrade order of producers and consumers depends on the mode.

subtopics.title: Upgrade order of producers and consumers

categories.title: Kafka Connect, Streams and ksqlDB
categories.description: The ecosystem that moves data in and out and processes it without custom services.

topics.title: Kafka Connect architecture
topics.description: Connect runs connectors as tasks across a cluster of workers, storing config, offsets and status in internal topics; distributed mode versus standalone, and the REST API that manages connectors.

topics.title: Source and sink connectors
topics.description: JDBC and Debezium sources pull database changes into topics; S3, JDBC and Elasticsearch sinks write topics out; configuring converters, error tolerance and dead-letter topics for a resilient connector.

topics.title: Single message transforms
topics.description: SMTs modify records inside a connector pipeline (rename fields, mask values, route by topic, set keys) without a separate stream job; chaining transforms and knowing when logic has outgrown them.

topics.title: Kafka Streams overview
topics.description: A Java library for stateful stream processing inside a normal application: KStream and KTable, stateful operators backed by RocksDB and changelog topics, and how tasks scale with partitions.

topics.title: ksqlDB overview
topics.description: SQL over topics: streams and tables, persistent queries that write derived topics, push and pull queries, and where ksqlDB is enough versus when a code-based processor is needed.

categories.title: Storage, Retention and Replication
categories.description: How records live on disk and how the cluster keeps them safe.

topics.title: Log segments and retention
topics.description: Partitions are stored as rolled segment files with offset and time indexes; retention.ms and retention.bytes delete whole segments, so the active segment is never purged and data outlives the configured time slightly.

topics.title: Log compaction
topics.description: cleanup.policy=compact keeps only the latest record per key, with tombstones for deletes, turning a topic into a changelog you can rebuild state from; how the cleaner works and its delay settings.

topics.title: Replication, ISR and leader election
topics.description: Each partition has a leader and followers that fetch from it; the in-sync replica set tracks who is caught up, and a follower in the ISR is promoted when the leader fails so writes are not lost.

topics.title: min.insync.replicas and unclean elections
topics.description: With acks=all, min.insync.replicas sets how many replicas must confirm a write or the producer gets an error; unclean.leader.election.enable trades data loss for availability when no in-sync replica is left.

categories.title: Security
categories.description: Encrypting traffic, proving identity and limiting what each client may do.

topics.title: TLS encryption and listeners
topics.description: Configuring SSL listeners with keystores and truststores, enabling client authentication with certificates, and the listener-per-protocol layout that keeps plaintext off the network.

topics.title: SASL authentication
topics.description: SASL/PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-512 and OAUTHBEARER authenticate clients with credentials rather than certificates; how SCRAM credentials are stored in cluster metadata and how confluent-kafka is configured for each mechanism.

topics.title: ACLs and authorization
topics.description: The built-in authorizer grants principals operations (Read, Write, Create) on resources (topics, groups, cluster) with literal or prefixed patterns; least privilege for producers, consumers and Connect workers.

categories.title: Operations and Monitoring
categories.description: Keeping a cluster and its clients healthy in production.

topics.title: Broker and client metrics
topics.description: The JMX metrics that matter: under-replicated partitions, request latency, network and request handler idle ratios, producer record-error-rate and consumer fetch latency; exporting them with a JMX exporter to Prometheus.

topics.title: Consumer lag monitoring
topics.description: Lag per partition is the primary health signal for a consumer: measuring it with kafka-consumer-groups, Burrow or exporters, alerting on trend rather than instantaneous values, and tracing lag to slow processing or rebalances.

subtopics.title: Lag per partition and per group

topics.title: Partition reassignment and cluster changes
topics.description: Adding brokers does not move data by itself: kafka-reassign-partitions generates and executes moves with throttles, and rolling restarts rely on preferred leader election to keep leadership balanced.

topics.title: Troubleshooting common failures
topics.description: A diagnostic playbook: producers timing out, consumers rebalancing in loops, offsets reset unexpectedly, disks filling from misconfigured retention, and reading broker logs to find the actual cause.

categories.title: Design Patterns and Performance
categories.description: The architectures Kafka enables and the settings that make them fast.

topics.title: Event sourcing and event-driven services
topics.description: Storing state changes as immutable events that services consume to build their own views; how compacted topics act as the source of truth and how the outbox pattern publishes events atomically with a database write.

subtopics.title: Events as the source of truth

topics.title: Change data capture with Debezium
topics.description: Debezium reads a database's write-ahead log and emits row-level change events per table with before and after images; snapshotting, the envelope format, and handling schema changes and deletes downstream.

topics.title: Retries, dead-letter topics and poison messages
topics.description: A record that keeps failing must not block a partition: retry topics with backoff, a dead-letter topic with error headers for inspection, and a replay tool that resubmits fixed records.

topics.title: Producer and consumer performance tuning
topics.description: Working through the levers in order: batching and compression on producers, fetch.min.bytes and max.poll.records on consumers, partition count, and measuring with kafka-producer-perf-test before and after.

topics.title: Multi-cluster replication and disaster recovery
topics.description: MirrorMaker 2 and Cluster Linking replicate topics across regions with offset translation; active-passive versus active-active layouts and what a failover actually requires from consumers.

topics.title: Project: order events pipeline with Schema Registry
topics.description: Build a producer that emits Avro order events keyed by order id, a consumer group that enriches and upserts them into Postgres with manual commits, and a compatibility test that rejects a breaking schema change.

subtopics.title: Design the topic and Avro schema

topics.title: Project: CDC from Postgres to a data lake
topics.description: Run Debezium via Kafka Connect against a Postgres database, land change events in S3 (or MinIO) as Parquet with an S3 sink connector partitioned by date, and verify deletes and updates are represented.

subtopics.title: Configure the S3 sink and partitioning

topics.title: Project: exactly-once enrichment service
topics.description: A consume-transform-produce service that reads clickstream events, joins them to a compacted user-profile topic held in memory, and writes enriched events with a transactional producer, with a test that kills the service mid-batch.

subtopics.title: Load a compacted topic into state

topics.title: Project: secured cluster with monitoring
topics.description: A three-broker KRaft cluster in Docker Compose with SASL_SSL listeners, ACLs for a producer and consumer principal, the JMX exporter feeding Prometheus, and a Grafana dashboard with an alert on consumer lag.

topics.title: Kafka interview questions
topics.description: The recurring questions: why partitions matter, how consumer groups scale, what acks=all really guarantees, exactly-once boundaries, compaction versus retention, and how you would size and secure a cluster.

topics.title: Kafka system design scenarios
topics.description: Whiteboard exercises: a clickstream ingestion path, a CDC feed into a warehouse, a notification fan-out, and an audit log, each with topic layout, keys, retention and failure handling argued out loud.

subtopics.title: Topic and key design for a scenario

title: Kotlin
description: Kotlin from the JDK and Gradle setup to idiomatic, coroutine-driven code: null safety, data and sealed classes, extension functions, the collections API, Java interoperability, coroutines and flows, testing with JUnit and MockK, Android and Ktor applications, projects and interview practice.

categories.title: Environment and Tooling
categories.description: A JDK, a build tool and an IDE that understands Kotlin, before the first real file.

topics.title: Installing Kotlin, a JDK and IntelliJ IDEA
topics.description: Kotlin compiles to JVM bytecode, so you need a JDK (17 or 21 LTS) plus the Kotlin compiler bundled with IntelliJ IDEA or Android Studio; how the Kotlin plugin, SDK selection and language versions fit together.

subtopics.title: Choosing a JDK and LTS versions
IntelliJ IDEA and the Kotlin plugin

topics.title: Gradle with the Kotlin DSL and ktlint
topics.description: build.gradle.kts declares the Kotlin plugin, JVM toolchain and dependencies in Kotlin itself; the Gradle wrapper pins the build tool version, and ktlint or detekt enforce the official code style in CI.

topics.title: Scripts, the REPL and Kotlin Playground
topics.description: Running one-off code without a project: kotlinc for compiling single files, .main.kts scripts with dependency annotations, Kotlin Notebook inside IntelliJ, and the browser Playground for sharing snippets.

topics.title: main, packages and top-level declarations
topics.description: A Kotlin file can hold top-level functions, properties and classes without a wrapping class; main needs no arguments, packages need not match directories, semicolons are optional, and imports can alias names.

topics.title: Variables, basic types and inference
topics.description: val for read-only references and var for mutable ones, type inference from initialisers, Int, Long, Double, Boolean, Char and String as objects, no implicit widening between numeric types, and unsigned integers.

topics.title: Operators and expressions
topics.description: Arithmetic and comparison operators, == for structural equality versus === for identity, ranges with .., ..< and downTo, the in operator, and bitwise operations as named infix functions like shl and and.

subtopics.title: Bitwise infix functions shl, and, xor

topics.title: if and when as expressions
topics.description: if returns a value so there is no ternary, when replaces switch and matches values, ranges, types and arbitrary conditions, and when over a sealed or enum type must be exhaustive.

subtopics.title: when with values, ranges and types

topics.title: Loops, ranges and labels
topics.description: for iterates anything with an iterator, including ranges with step and indices via withIndex, while and do-while, break and continue with labels for nested loops, and repeat for counted iteration.

categories.title: Null Safety and Functions
categories.description: The two features that most change how Kotlin code is written.

topics.title: Nullable types and safe calls
topics.description: String and String? are different types checked by the compiler; the safe call ?., the Elvis operator ?: for defaults or early returns, let for scoped null handling, and why !! is a code smell.

subtopics.title: The !! operator and when to avoid it

topics.title: Smart casts and type checks
topics.description: After an is check or null check the compiler treats a val as the narrower type automatically; as? casts safely to null, and smart casts fail on mutable vars or open properties because they could change underneath.

topics.title: lateinit, lazy and nullability strategies
topics.description: lateinit for non-null properties initialised later such as in DI or tests, by lazy for deferred computation, when to choose nullable fields versus defaults, and isInitialized checks.

topics.title: Functions, default and named arguments
topics.description: Single-expression functions, default parameter values that replace overloads, named arguments for readability, vararg with the spread operator, plus infix, operator overloading and tailrec functions.

topics.title: Extension functions and properties
topics.description: Adding members to existing types without inheritance: extensions are resolved statically on the declared type, cannot access private members, can be declared on nullable receivers, and are how much of the standard library works.

topics.title: Lambdas and function types
topics.description: Function types like (Int) -> String, lambda syntax with it for a single parameter, trailing lambdas outside parentheses, function references with ::, anonymous functions, and closures capturing mutable variables.

topics.title: Inline, reified and scope functions
topics.description: inline copies a function and its lambdas into the call site to avoid allocation and allow non-local returns, reified type parameters survive erasure, and let, run, with, apply and also each differ by receiver and return value.

topics.title: Lists, sets, maps and arrays
topics.description: Read-only List, Set and Map interfaces versus their Mutable counterparts, listOf and mutableListOf builders, buildList, the difference between Array and IntArray, and why read-only is not immutable.

topics.title: Transforming collections
topics.description: map, filter, flatMap, mapNotNull, associate and associateBy, zip and unzip, partition, take and drop, and the habit of chaining pure transformations instead of writing loops.

topics.title: Sorting, grouping and aggregating
topics.description: sortedBy and sortedWith with compareBy for multi-key ordering, groupBy and groupingBy for counts, fold and reduce, sumOf, maxByOrNull, and the OrNull family that avoids exceptions on empty input.

topics.title: Sequences and lazy evaluation
topics.description: asSequence turns eager chains into lazy element-by-element processing, which avoids intermediate lists on large data; generateSequence and sequence builders with yield create infinite or on-demand streams.

topics.title: Destructuring, Pair and Triple
topics.description: Destructuring declarations pull componentN values out of data classes, pairs and map entries; to creates a Pair, and destructuring in lambdas and for loops keeps code short without exposing tuples in APIs.

topics.title: String templates and raw strings
topics.description: Strings are immutable; $name and ${expr} interpolate, triple-quoted raw strings keep newlines and backslashes with trimIndent or trimMargin, and escapes work only in regular strings.

topics.title: String functions, StringBuilder and Regex
topics.description: split, substringBefore, padStart, toIntOrNull and the other string extensions, buildString for efficient concatenation, and the Regex class with find, findAll, matchEntire and named groups.

topics.title: Exceptions and try as an expression
topics.description: Kotlin has no checked exceptions, try/catch/finally is an expression that yields a value, the exception hierarchy comes from the JVM, and the @Throws annotation exists only for Java callers.

topics.title: Result, runCatching and failure modelling
topics.description: Result<T> with runCatching, getOrElse and fold captures success or failure as a value, sealed classes model domain errors explicitly, and when each style beats throwing.

topics.title: Preconditions, custom exceptions and Nothing
topics.description: require for argument checks, check for state, error for impossible branches, defining exception classes with extra fields, and the Nothing type that lets a throwing function fit any expression.

topics.title: Packages, visibility modifiers and modules
topics.description: public by default, private to a file or class, protected in subclasses, and internal for module-wide visibility that Java cannot express; how Gradle modules map to internal and how to structure a multi-module project.

topics.title: File I/O and command-line programs
topics.description: Reading and writing with File.readText, readLines, useLines for streaming, bufferedWriter, kotlin.io.path for Path helpers, readln for stdin, args in main, and exitProcess for exit codes.

topics.title: kotlinx.serialization and JSON
topics.description: The compiler plugin generates serialisers for @Serializable classes, Json.encodeToString and decodeFromString round-trip data, and configuration handles default values, unknown keys, sealed hierarchies and custom serialisers.

topics.title: Classes, constructors and properties
topics.description: Primary constructors declare properties inline, init blocks run in order, secondary constructors delegate, and properties have generated getters and setters with custom accessors and the field backing identifier.

topics.title: Inheritance, interfaces and abstract classes
topics.description: Classes are final unless marked open, override is mandatory, abstract classes hold state, interfaces hold default method bodies but no state, and super<Interface> resolves diamond conflicts.

topics.title: Data classes
topics.description: data class generates equals, hashCode, toString, copy and componentN from the primary constructor, making value objects one line; the rules on constructor properties and why copy is shallow.

topics.title: Sealed classes and interfaces
topics.description: A sealed hierarchy lists every subtype at compile time, so when over it is exhaustive without else; the standard way to model states, results and events, with data objects for singleton cases.

topics.title: Enum classes, objects and companion objects
topics.description: Enum classes with properties, methods and entries, object declarations for singletons, companion objects as the place for factory functions and constants, and object expressions for anonymous implementations.

topics.title: Delegation and property delegates
topics.description: Class delegation with by forwards an interface to another object without boilerplate, and property delegates such as lazy, observable, vetoable and map-backed properties plus custom getValue and setValue operators.

subtopics.title: Custom delegates with getValue and setValue

topics.title: Generics and variance
topics.description: Generic classes and functions, upper bounds with where, declaration-site variance with out and in, star projections, and why List<out E> lets a List<String> be a List<Any> while MutableList does not.

categories.title: Java Interoperability
categories.description: Kotlin lives on the JVM beside Java; both directions have rules worth knowing.

topics.title: Calling Java from Kotlin
topics.description: Java getters and setters appear as Kotlin properties, single-method interfaces accept lambdas through SAM conversion, Java collections map to Kotlin mutable types, and static members are called through the class name.

topics.title: Calling Kotlin from Java
topics.description: Top-level functions become static methods on a FileNameKt class renamed with @JvmName, @JvmStatic exposes companion members statically, @JvmOverloads generates overloads for default arguments, and @JvmField skips accessors.

subtopics.title: Kotlin types as seen from Java

topics.title: Platform types and nullability annotations
topics.description: Values from unannotated Java have platform types (String!) whose nullability Kotlin cannot check, so NPEs can surface at Kotlin call sites; @Nullable and @NotNull annotations fix that, and mixed builds need consistent JVM targets.

subtopics.title: Where NPEs surface in mixed code
kapt versus KSP for annotation processors

topics.title: JVM memory, boxing and value classes
topics.description: Kotlin objects live on the JVM heap under the garbage collector, nullable Int? and generics box primitives, @JvmInline value classes wrap a single value with no allocation in most positions, and references not ownership decide lifetime.

subtopics.title: Heap objects and the JVM garbage collector

topics.title: Resource management with use and Closeable
topics.description: Files, sockets and streams implement Closeable or AutoCloseable; use { } closes them even on exceptions like Java try-with-resources, and try/finally handles resources without that interface.

topics.title: Profiling and benchmarking Kotlin
topics.description: Measure before optimising: JVM profilers such as IntelliJ Profiler and async-profiler, kotlinx-benchmark and JMH for micro-benchmarks that beat JIT warm-up, and common wins like sequences, primitive arrays and avoiding lambda allocation.

topics.title: Secure Kotlin code
topics.description: Parameterised queries with JDBC or Exposed, validating and bounding input with require, avoiding deserialisation of untrusted classes, hashing passwords with bcrypt or argon2, and dependency scanning with OWASP or Gradle tooling.

categories.title: Coroutines and Flows
categories.description: Asynchronous code that reads sequentially: the kotlinx.coroutines library.

topics.title: Suspending functions and coroutine builders
topics.description: suspend functions can pause without blocking a thread, launch starts fire-and-forget work, async returns a Deferred you await, runBlocking bridges to blocking code, and delay replaces Thread.sleep.

topics.title: Structured concurrency and cancellation
topics.description: Coroutines form a parent-child tree through CoroutineScope and Job, so a parent waits for and cancels its children; cancellation is cooperative and checked at suspension points, with coroutineScope and supervisorScope for grouping.

topics.title: Dispatchers and withContext
topics.description: Dispatchers.Default for CPU work, IO for blocking calls, Main on Android, withContext to switch threads inside a coroutine, and why blocking a Default thread starves everything else.

topics.title: Exception handling in coroutines
topics.description: Exceptions in launch propagate to the parent and cancel siblings, async exceptions surface at await, SupervisorJob isolates failures, CoroutineExceptionHandler catches uncaught ones, and try/catch must not swallow CancellationException.

topics.title: Channels and shared mutable state
topics.description: Channels pass values between coroutines with suspension instead of locks, produce builds a producer coroutine, Mutex protects shared state suspendingly, and confining state to one coroutine avoids races.

topics.title: Flow: cold streams and operators
topics.description: A Flow emits values lazily each time it is collected, operators like map, filter, take and transform stay lazy, flowOn changes the upstream dispatcher, and catch and onCompletion handle errors and cleanup.

topics.title: StateFlow, SharedFlow and hot streams
topics.description: StateFlow holds the latest value for UI state, SharedFlow broadcasts events with replay and buffering, stateIn and shareIn convert cold flows, and combine and flatMapLatest merge sources.

topics.title: JUnit 5, kotlin.test and Kotest
topics.description: Writing tests with JUnit 5 annotations or the kotlin.test wrappers, backtick test names, parameterised tests, assertion styles, and Kotest as an alternative with its spec styles and property testing.

topics.title: MockK and fakes
topics.description: MockK mocks Kotlin classes, final by default, with every { } stubs and verify { } checks, coEvery for suspend functions, relaxed mocks, and when a hand-written fake behind an interface is clearer.

topics.title: Testing coroutines and flows
topics.description: runTest skips delays with virtual time, StandardTestDispatcher and advanceUntilIdle control scheduling, Turbine makes Flow assertions readable, and Main dispatcher replacement for Android tests.

topics.title: Debugging in IntelliJ IDEA
topics.description: Breakpoints with conditions and logging, evaluating expressions, stepping into inline and suspend functions, the Coroutines debugger tab, and decompiling to Java bytecode to see what the compiler generated.

topics.title: Gradle dependencies, version catalogs and packaging
topics.description: implementation versus api scopes, version catalogs in libs.versions.toml, the Kotlin BOM, building runnable jars with the application plugin or shadow, and publishing libraries with maven-publish.

categories.title: Kotlin for Android and Ktor
categories.description: The two places Kotlin is used most; deeper coverage lives in track-android and the backend tracks.

topics.title: Android: activities, ViewModel and lifecycle-aware coroutines
topics.description: How an Activity or Fragment lifecycle interacts with Kotlin code, ViewModel surviving configuration changes, viewModelScope and lifecycleScope for coroutines, and repeatOnLifecycle for collecting flows safely.

topics.title: Jetpack Compose fundamentals
topics.description: Declarative UI in Kotlin: @Composable functions, state with remember and mutableStateOf, recomposition, state hoisting, and collecting a StateFlow with collectAsStateWithLifecycle.

topics.title: Ktor server: routing, plugins and content negotiation
topics.description: embeddedServer with Netty or CIO, the routing DSL with route groups and parameters, plugins installed per application such as ContentNegotiation with kotlinx.serialization, CallLogging and StatusPages.

topics.title: Ktor: persistence with Exposed and authentication
topics.description: Exposed DSL and DAO for typed SQL, HikariCP pooling and transactions on Dispatchers.IO, the Authentication plugin with JWT or sessions, and configuration through application.conf or environment variables.

topics.title: Ktor client and Kotlin Multiplatform
topics.description: HttpClient with engines per platform, JSON via ContentNegotiation, timeouts and retries, and how Kotlin Multiplatform shares that code between Android, iOS, desktop and web with expect/actual declarations.

topics.title: Project: command-line expense tracker
topics.description: Build a CLI that records expenses in a JSON file with kotlinx.serialization, models categories with a sealed class, aggregates monthly totals with groupingBy, and ships with kotlin.test coverage and a runnable distribution.

subtopics.title: Test and package with the application plugin

topics.title: Project: Ktor REST API with Exposed and JWT
topics.description: A Ktor service exposing CRUD routes for a resource, Exposed tables with migrations, JWT-protected endpoints, StatusPages error mapping, integration tests with testApplication, and a Dockerfile.

topics.title: Project: Android notes app with Compose and Room
topics.description: A notes app with Jetpack Compose screens, a ViewModel exposing StateFlow, Room for local storage observed as a Flow, coroutine-backed repository, and unit tests with runTest and Turbine.

topics.title: Project: concurrent web scraper with coroutines
topics.description: Fetch many pages with the Ktor client and a bounded number of concurrent coroutines, parse with jsoup, stream results through a Flow into a CSV, handle timeouts and cancellation on Ctrl-C.

topics.title: Kotlin interview questions
topics.description: What interviewers ask: val versus var, nullable types and !!, data versus regular classes, sealed classes, extension resolution, inline and reified, coroutines versus threads, structured concurrency, and Java interop pitfalls.

topics.title: Coding interviews in Kotlin
topics.description: Solving problems fast in Kotlin: readLine and split parsing, IntArray and ArrayDeque, PriorityQueue from Java, sortedWith comparators, StringBuilder output, and avoiding boxing and hidden allocations in tight loops.
