description: Building layouts that work from a 320px phone to an ultrawide monitor: the viewport, mobile-first thinking, fluid sizing, media and container queries, fluid type, responsive images, flexible grids, navigation and table patterns, touch input, device testing and print, finished with real projects.

categories.title: Viewport and Mobile-First Foundations
categories.description: Why a page renders the way it does on a phone, and the mindset that makes every later decision easier.

topics.title: The viewport and the viewport meta tag
topics.description: Layout viewport versus visual viewport, why mobile browsers pretend to be 980px wide without the meta tag, and what width=device-width and initial-scale actually change.

topics.title: Mobile-first versus desktop-first
topics.description: Writing base styles for the smallest screen and adding complexity with min-width queries, versus starting wide and overriding downward, and why mobile-first produces less CSS and better priorities.

subtopics.title: Base styles for the narrowest screen

topics.title: Device pixels, CSS pixels and device pixel ratio
topics.description: Why a 1080px-wide phone reports 360 CSS pixels, how devicePixelRatio drives image and font crispness, and what it means for choosing image sizes and hairline borders.

subtopics.title: CSS pixels as a reference unit

topics.title: Choosing breakpoints from content
topics.description: Letting the content decide where layouts break instead of copying device sizes, resizing until something looks wrong, using em-based breakpoints and keeping the set small.

topics.title: Percentages, max-width and fluid containers
topics.description: Boxes that stretch and stop: percentage widths, max-width to cap line length, the centred container pattern with width: min(100% - 2rem, 70rem) and why fixed pixel widths break first.

topics.title: Intrinsic sizing and content-based layout
topics.description: min-content, max-content and fit-content, flex and grid auto sizing that lets content define width, and Jen Simmons's intrinsic web design idea of layouts that adapt to content as well as viewport.

subtopics.title: Auto tracks that size to content

topics.title: Fluid media and aspect-ratio
topics.description: max-width: 100% and height: auto so images and videos never overflow, aspect-ratio to reserve space for embeds and cards, and object-fit for cropping into fixed boxes.

topics.title: Preventing overflow and horizontal scroll
topics.description: The usual culprits behind a page that scrolls sideways on phones: fixed widths, long words, 100vw with scrollbars, negative margins and images, and how to find and fix each.

topics.title: Media query syntax and range notation
topics.description: Media types and features, and, or and not logic, the modern range syntax (width >= 48em) and how a query applies to the whole viewport including scrollbars.

topics.title: Orientation, resolution and display features
topics.description: orientation for landscape phones, resolution and min-resolution for high-density assets, display-mode for installed apps, and why orientation alone is a poor proxy for device type.

topics.title: User preference queries
topics.description: prefers-color-scheme, prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-contrast and forced-colors, responding to system settings so the interface respects what the user already chose.

topics.title: Organising media queries in a codebase
topics.description: Queries next to the component versus grouped at the end, custom media with PostCSS, breakpoint tokens, and why nesting queries inside components keeps behaviour readable.

topics.title: Containment and container-type
topics.description: Declaring container-type: inline-size on a wrapper so children can query its width, why size containment is required and what it prevents, and naming containers.

topics.title: Component-level responsive design
topics.description: Writing a card, nav or table that rearranges based on the space it is given, so it works in a sidebar, a main column and a modal without extra classes.

topics.title: Container units and style queries
topics.description: cqi, cqw and cqb for sizing relative to the container, fluid type inside components, and style queries that react to custom property values on the container.

topics.title: Type scales and rem-based sizing
topics.description: Modular scales with a ratio, sizing in rem so the user's font preference is respected, and stepping the scale per breakpoint before going fully fluid.

topics.title: Fluid type with clamp
topics.description: Interpolating font size between a minimum and maximum across a viewport range using clamp with a vw term plus rem, generating the formula, and the zoom accessibility trap of pure vw.

subtopics.title: Adding rem to keep zoom working

topics.title: Measure, line-height and reading comfort
topics.description: Keeping lines to roughly 45 to 75 characters with max-width in ch, adjusting line-height as text grows, and text-wrap: balance and pretty for headings.

topics.title: Fluid spacing scales
topics.description: Applying the same clamp technique to margins, padding and gaps so spacing grows with the screen, and using custom properties for a spacing scale shared across components.

topics.title: srcset and sizes matched to layout
topics.description: Choosing width descriptors that cover real rendered sizes, writing a sizes attribute that mirrors the CSS layout at each breakpoint, and verifying the browser choice in the Network panel.

topics.title: Art direction with picture and media
topics.description: Serving a tight crop on phones and a wide crop on desktop with picture and media attributes, keeping the focal point visible, and combining with format fallbacks.

subtopics.title: When art direction is worth it

topics.title: Background images and image-set
topics.description: Responsive backgrounds with background-size, media queries and image-set for density and format, and why content images should be img and not CSS backgrounds.

topics.title: Image CDNs and modern formats
topics.description: Generating sizes and formats on the fly with an image CDN or build step, AVIF and WebP with fallbacks, and lazy loading and decoding hints for images below the fold.

topics.title: Auto-fit grids without media queries
topics.description: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 18rem), 1fr)) as the workhorse responsive grid, why the inner min() prevents overflow on narrow screens, and controlling the maximum column count.

subtopics.title: Gap and alignment in fluid grids

topics.title: Flex-based wrapping layouts
topics.description: flex-wrap with flex-basis and flex-grow for rows that reflow, the switcher pattern that flips from row to column at a container width using a single calc, and gap for consistent spacing.

topics.title: Sidebar, holy grail and page-level layouts
topics.description: Composing a page with grid-template-areas that change per breakpoint, the sidebar pattern that collapses when the main column gets too narrow, and full-bleed sections inside a centred layout.

topics.title: Layout primitives and composition
topics.description: Reusable layout components such as stack, center, cover and grid from Every Layout, so pages are composed from a handful of tested primitives rather than bespoke CSS per page.

topics.title: Navigation patterns
topics.description: Horizontal nav that collapses into a hamburger, priority-plus that hides overflow items in a menu, bottom tab bars on phones, and how to keep each accessible with proper buttons and focus.

topics.title: Off-canvas drawers and overlays
topics.description: Sliding panels for navigation and filters, using dialog or inert for focus trapping, transform-based animation, and locking body scroll without breaking iOS.

topics.title: Cards, modals and forms at every width
topics.description: Cards that switch between vertical and horizontal, modals that become full-screen sheets on phones, and form layouts that stack labels and inputs when space runs out.

topics.title: Sticky headers, safe areas and the address bar
topics.description: Sticky headers that shrink on scroll, env(safe-area-inset-*) for notches and home indicators, dynamic viewport units and the address bar problem on mobile browsers.

topics.title: Touch targets and spacing
topics.description: Minimum target sizes of about 44 by 44 CSS pixels, spacing between targets, enlarging hit areas with padding or pseudo-elements, and the WCAG target size criterion.

topics.title: hover, pointer and any-pointer queries
topics.description: Detecting coarse versus fine pointers and whether hover is available, designing states that do not depend on hover, and handling devices that have both touch and mouse.

topics.title: Scrolling, gestures and scroll snap
topics.description: Horizontal carousels with scroll-snap, overscroll-behavior to stop scroll chaining, touch-action to control browser gestures, and momentum scrolling in overflow containers.

topics.title: Scrolling table containers
topics.description: Wrapping a wide table in an overflow-x: auto container with a visible scroll affordance, sticky first columns and headers, and keeping the container keyboard-focusable.

topics.title: Stacked and card-style tables
topics.description: Turning each row into a card on narrow screens with display changes and data-label pseudo-content, the accessibility costs of changing display on table elements and the role="table" fix.

topics.title: Responsive charts and data visuals
topics.description: SVG charts that scale with viewBox, simplifying visuals on small screens, switching from charts to lists when there is no room, and responsive containers for charting libraries.

topics.title: Device emulation and real device testing
topics.description: DevTools device mode and its limits, remote debugging on real phones over USB, cloud device farms, and the bugs only real devices show: font rendering, address bars, touch latency.

topics.title: Cross-browser and progressive enhancement
topics.description: Checking support on Can I Use and Baseline, layering enhancements with @supports, and testing in Safari, Firefox and Chromium because layout differences still exist.

topics.title: Print stylesheets
topics.description: A print media query that hides navigation, expands link URLs, avoids page breaks inside cards and tables, resets colours for ink, and how to preview print in DevTools.

topics.title: Responsive delivery and performance on mobile
topics.description: Slow networks and weak CPUs make mobile the performance floor: reducing CSS for small screens, conditional loading with media on link elements, and testing with throttling.

topics.title: Project: mobile-first news site
topics.description: Build an article listing and reading page that stacks on phones and grows into a multi-column layout, with fluid type, art-directed hero images, priority-plus navigation and a print stylesheet.

topics.title: Project: container-query component library
topics.description: A set of cards, product tiles, stat panels and a nav bar that adapt to their container, demonstrated in a sidebar, a main column and a modal on a single page.

topics.title: Project: responsive data dashboard
topics.description: A dashboard with scrolling and stacked tables, SVG charts that scale, a collapsible sidebar, touch-friendly filters in a drawer and correct behaviour on a phone in landscape.

topics.title: Project: e-commerce product page
topics.description: A product page with an image gallery using scroll snap, a sticky buy box on desktop that becomes a bottom bar on mobile, size selectors with large targets and a responsive review section.

subtopics.title: Sticky buy box to bottom bar

topics.title: Responsive design interview questions
topics.description: The questions that keep coming up: mobile-first reasoning, srcset versus picture, container versus media queries, fluid type maths, dvh versus vh and how to prevent layout shift.

topics.title: Live responsive layout exercises
topics.description: Timed exercises: make a fixed-width page fluid, add a breakpoint to a broken card grid, fix a horizontal scroll bug and convert a desktop nav to a phone menu while explaining each step.

title: REST API Engineering
description: Designing, securing, documenting and operating HTTP APIs in any language: HTTP semantics, caching and conditional requests, resource modelling and URL design, versioning, pagination, RFC 9457 errors, idempotency keys, rate limiting, API keys, OAuth 2.0 and JWT, OpenAPI, contract and load testing, OWASP API Top 10, webhooks and governance.

categories.title: HTTP Semantics
categories.description: The protocol rules that make an API predictable to every client, proxy and cache in between.

topics.title: HTTP methods, safety and idempotency
topics.description: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS as defined in RFC 9110, which are safe (no side effects) and which are idempotent (repeatable), and why proxies and retry logic rely on those promises being kept.

topics.title: Status codes that matter
topics.description: The 2xx, 3xx, 4xx and 5xx classes and the specific codes a well-behaved API uses: 200, 201 with Location, 202, 204, 304, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 412, 422, 429, 500 and 503; picking the precise code is part of the contract.

topics.title: Headers and content negotiation
topics.description: Content-Type declares what is sent, Accept declares what is wanted, and the server chooses a representation or returns 406 or 415; plus Content-Language, Vary, and custom headers that should stay rare.

subtopics.title: Vary and its effect on caches

topics.title: HTTP caching with Cache-Control and ETag
topics.description: Freshness (max-age, s-maxage, no-cache versus no-store, private versus public) and validation (ETag, Last-Modified) so browsers, CDNs and gateways can serve or revalidate without hitting the origin.

topics.title: Conditional requests and optimistic concurrency
topics.description: If-None-Match for cheap 304 responses and If-Match for updates that fail with 412 when someone else changed the resource first, giving lost-update protection without server-side locks.

topics.title: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 for API developers
topics.description: Head-of-line blocking in HTTP/1.1, multiplexing and header compression in HTTP/2, QUIC in HTTP/3, and what changes for API design (fewer reasons to batch, connection reuse) versus what stays the same. Networking depth lives in track-networking.

topics.title: Resources, collections and identifiers
topics.description: Modelling nouns rather than verbs, collection versus item resources, choosing identifiers (sequential ids, UUIDs, slugs, ULIDs) and why exposing sequential ids leaks information and invites enumeration.

topics.title: URL naming conventions
topics.description: Plural nouns, lowercase with hyphens, no trailing slashes or file extensions, query strings for filtering not identification, and consistency enforced by a style guide.

subtopics.title: No verbs or extensions in paths

topics.title: Relationships and sub-resources
topics.description: When to nest (/customers/{id}/orders) versus link (/orders?customer=id), depth limits, embedding related data versus separate calls, and representing many-to-many links as resources.

topics.title: Actions that are not CRUD
topics.description: Modelling "cancel an order" or "send an invoice" as state transitions (PATCH status), sub-resources (POST /orders/{id}/cancellations) or controller endpoints, and picking the option that keeps semantics honest.

subtopics.title: Controller endpoints as a last resort

topics.title: Hypermedia and the Richardson maturity model
topics.description: Levels from tunnelling everything through POST to full hypermedia with links that tell clients what they can do next; where HAL, JSON:API and plain links fit, and how much HATEOAS is worth in practice.

topics.title: Request and response body design
topics.description: Consistent JSON conventions: camelCase or snake_case chosen once, envelopes only where needed, ISO 8601 timestamps with time zones, money as strings or minor units, nulls versus absent fields, and enums as strings.

topics.title: Pagination: offset and cursor
topics.description: Offset pagination is simple but slow and unstable on large or changing data; cursor (keyset) pagination encodes the last seen key, stays consistent under inserts and is index-friendly; both need clear metadata and links.

topics.title: Filtering, sorting and field selection
topics.description: Query parameter grammars for equality, ranges and lists, multi-field sort with direction, sparse fieldsets to shrink payloads, and validating every parameter against an allow-list.

topics.title: Error responses with RFC 9457 problem details
topics.description: One error shape for the whole API: application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail and instance, extension members such as errors[] for validation, and stable machine-readable codes.

topics.title: Validation, 400 and 422
topics.description: Syntactic failures (malformed JSON, wrong types) as 400, semantic failures (valid shape, invalid business rule) as 422, per-field error lists, and validating at the boundary before any side effect.

topics.title: Partial updates: PUT, PATCH and JSON Merge Patch
topics.description: PUT replaces the whole representation, PATCH applies a change; JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386) uses null to delete and cannot express array edits, JSON Patch (RFC 6902) lists operations and supports tests.

topics.title: Idempotency keys
topics.description: Letting clients retry POSTs safely: a unique Idempotency-Key header, storing the first response keyed by it, replaying it on retries, detecting key reuse with different payloads, and expiring keys.

topics.title: Rate limiting and quotas
topics.description: Token bucket versus sliding window, limits per key, user or IP, communicating limits with RateLimit headers and 429 plus Retry-After, and quotas that cap monthly usage separately from burst protection.

topics.title: Timeouts, retries and backoff
topics.description: Client and server timeouts that add up along a call chain, exponential backoff with jitter, retrying only idempotent or key-protected requests, and circuit breakers to stop hammering a failing dependency.

subtopics.title: Which requests are safe to retry

topics.title: Bulk operations and long-running jobs
topics.description: Batch endpoints with per-item results (207-style or an array of outcomes), async jobs that return 202 with a status resource to poll, and callbacks or webhooks when polling is wasteful.

topics.title: Versioning strategies
topics.description: URL versions (/v1), header versions (Accept or a custom header), date-based versions like Stripe, and no versioning with strict compatibility; their trade-offs for caching, routing and client simplicity.

subtopics.title: Versioning per resource versus whole API

topics.title: Backwards-compatible change rules
topics.description: What clients tolerate (new optional fields, new endpoints, new enum values only if documented) and what breaks them (renaming, removing, changing types, tightening validation), and tolerant reader expectations.

topics.title: Deprecation and sunset
topics.description: Announcing removal with Deprecation and Sunset headers, migration guides, usage analytics to find remaining callers, brownouts to flush stragglers, and finally returning 410 Gone.

categories.title: Authentication and Authorization
categories.description: The mechanisms APIs use to identify callers and decide what they may do. Identity systems in depth live in track-iam.

topics.title: API keys
topics.description: Simple bearer secrets for machine clients: generation and storage as hashes, transmission in a header rather than the query string, scoping and rotation, and why they identify an application rather than a user.

topics.title: OAuth 2.0 flows
topics.description: Authorization code with PKCE for user-facing apps, client credentials for service-to-service, refresh tokens, scopes, and why implicit and password grants are deprecated.

topics.title: JWT access tokens and validation
topics.description: Structure and signing, validating signature, expiry, issuer and audience, JWKS for key discovery and rotation, short lifetimes plus refresh, and opaque tokens with introspection as the alternative.

topics.title: Scopes, roles and resource permissions
topics.description: Scopes limit what a token may do, roles describe who a user is, and object-level checks decide whether this caller may touch this record; missing the last step is the top API vulnerability.

topics.title: CORS and browser clients
topics.description: Why browsers block cross-origin reads, preflight OPTIONS requests, Access-Control-Allow-Origin with credentials, and what CORS does not protect against.

topics.title: OpenAPI document structure
topics.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document: info, servers, paths with operations, parameters, requestBody, responses and security; writing one by hand well enough to review generated ones.

topics.title: Schemas, components and reuse
topics.description: Defining reusable schemas, parameters, responses and examples under components, $ref, composition with allOf and oneOf plus discriminators, and readOnly/writeOnly for asymmetric fields.

topics.title: Design-first, code-first and linting
topics.description: Writing the spec before code and generating stubs versus generating the spec from annotations, keeping either in sync in CI, and enforcing style rules with Spectral.

topics.title: Client generation and documentation portals
topics.description: Generating SDKs with openapi-generator or vendor tools, publishing docs with Redoc, Swagger UI or Stoplight, curl examples for every operation, and changelogs developers can subscribe to.

subtopics.title: Docs as part of the definition of done

topics.title: The API test pyramid
topics.description: Unit tests for handlers and validators, integration tests against a real database, end-to-end tests through the deployed API, and what each level is best at catching.

topics.title: Contract testing with Pact
topics.description: Consumers record the requests and responses they rely on, providers verify them in CI, and a broker tracks which versions are compatible so deployments cannot break a client.

topics.title: Schema validation against OpenAPI
topics.description: Validating real responses against the spec in tests and in a middleware, fuzzing with Schemathesis, and treating a mismatch as a failing build.

topics.title: Load testing with k6
topics.description: Scripting user journeys, ramping virtual users, thresholds on p95 latency and error rate, running against a staging environment, and reading results to find the first bottleneck.

categories.title: Performance and Security
categories.description: Generic web security in depth lives in track-web-security; this is the API-specific view.

topics.title: Caching layers: CDN, gateway and application
topics.description: Where a response can be cached (browser, CDN, API gateway, application cache), which headers each honours, cache keys and Vary, and invalidation strategies from TTLs to purge APIs.

topics.title: Payload size and compression
topics.description: gzip and brotli negotiated via Accept-Encoding, sparse fieldsets and pagination to shrink bodies, avoiding over-fetching, and when the compression CPU cost is not worth it.

topics.title: Connection reuse and latency budgets
topics.description: Keep-alive and connection pooling on clients, DNS and TLS handshake costs, tail latency, and setting latency budgets per endpoint that drive design decisions.

topics.title: OWASP API Top 10: authorization and authentication
topics.description: Broken object-level authorization (BOLA), broken authentication, broken property-level authorization and broken function-level authorization: how each is exploited and the checks that prevent them.

topics.title: OWASP API Top 10: resource consumption, SSRF and misconfiguration
topics.description: Unrestricted resource consumption, unrestricted access to sensitive business flows, server-side request forgery through user-supplied URLs, security misconfiguration, improper inventory management and unsafe consumption of third-party APIs.

topics.title: Input handling, injection and secrets
topics.description: Parameterised queries, encoding output for the format, strict content-type checks, size limits, avoiding secrets in URLs and logs, and security headers relevant to APIs.

topics.title: Webhook design
topics.description: Event naming and payload shape, thin payloads with a fetch-back URL versus fat payloads, event ids for deduplication, ordering caveats, and subscription management endpoints.

topics.title: Webhook security and delivery
topics.description: HMAC signatures with timestamps to stop replay, retries with backoff and dead-lettering, receiver timeouts and fast acknowledgement, and secret rotation.

topics.title: API gateways
topics.description: What a gateway centralises (auth, rate limits, routing, TLS, logging), products like Kong, Apigee, AWS API Gateway and Envoy, and the risks of putting business logic in it.

topics.title: API governance and style guides
topics.description: A written style guide, automated linting, design reviews before implementation, an API catalogue, ownership and lifecycle stages, and metrics for adoption and quality.

topics.title: API observability and SLOs
topics.description: Structured request logs with correlation ids, RED metrics per endpoint, distributed traces, SLOs on availability and latency, and dashboards per consumer. Deeper coverage lives in track-observability.

topics.title: Project: design and document an e-commerce API
topics.description: Model products, carts, orders and payments; write the OpenAPI 3.1 document design-first with problem details, cursor pagination, idempotent checkout and versioning; lint it with Spectral and publish docs with Redoc.

topics.title: Project: implement and test the API
topics.description: Implement the e-commerce spec in any framework: validation, RFC 9457 errors, ETags with If-Match, rate limiting, JWT auth with object-level checks, response validation against the spec, and k6 thresholds in CI.

topics.title: Project: webhook delivery platform
topics.description: A service that lets tenants subscribe to events, signs and delivers webhooks with retries and dead-letter queues, exposes delivery logs and a replay endpoint, and rotates secrets without downtime.

topics.title: Project: public API with OAuth 2.0 and a developer portal
topics.description: Add third-party access to an existing API: client registration, authorization code with PKCE, scopes, per-client rate limits, SDK generation and a portal with a changelog and deprecation policy.

topics.title: REST API interview questions
topics.description: The classics: PUT versus PATCH, idempotency, status code choices, pagination trade-offs, versioning, caching headers, JWT versus sessions, and how you would secure an endpoint.

topics.title: API design interview exercises
topics.description: Whiteboard exercises: design the API for a ride-hailing app, a file-sharing service or a notification system, covering resources, auth, pagination, errors, rate limits and evolution in 30 minutes.

title: Ruby
description: Ruby the way Rubyists write it: everything is an object, blocks, procs and lambdas, Enumerable, modules and mixins, metaprogramming, gems and Bundler, RSpec and Minitest, concurrency with threads, Ractors and Fibers, a Rails overview, buildable projects and interview practice.

categories.title: Environment and Tooling
categories.description: A version-managed Ruby, an interactive console and a project skeleton with Bundler.

topics.title: Installing Ruby with a version manager
topics.description: Why projects pin a Ruby version, installing with rbenv, asdf or mise, the .ruby-version file, and checking ruby -v and gem env before anything else.

topics.title: irb, ruby and the standard tools
topics.description: Running scripts with ruby file.rb, experimenting in irb with autocompletion, ruby -e one-liners, ri for documentation, and the shebang line for executable scripts.

topics.title: Gems, Bundler and the Gemfile
topics.description: RubyGems as the package registry, gem install versus a Gemfile, Bundler resolving and locking versions in Gemfile.lock, groups, and bundle exec to run inside the bundle.

topics.title: RuboCop and editor setup
topics.description: RuboCop enforces the community style guide and finds bugs, .rubocop.yml configuration, auto-correct, and editor integration through the Ruby LSP.

topics.title: Everything is an object
topics.description: Numbers, nil, true and classes are all objects that receive messages; method calls with and without parentheses, the receiver and self, and why 1 + 2 is 1.+(2).

topics.title: Variables, constants and naming
topics.description: Local, instance (@), class (@@) and global ($) variables, constants that warn on reassignment, snake_case and CamelCase conventions, and predicate and bang method names.

topics.title: Numbers, symbols and truthiness
topics.description: Integer with arbitrary precision, Float, Rational and BigDecimal for exactness, symbols as immutable identifiers, and the rule that only nil and false are falsy.

subtopics.title: Only nil and false are falsy

topics.title: Operators, ranges and safe navigation
topics.description: Arithmetic and comparison, the spaceship <=>, ||= for memoisation, ranges with .. and ..., the safe navigation operator &., and how everything is an expression with a value.

topics.title: Conditions, case and loops
topics.description: if, unless and modifier forms, case/when with === matching on classes, ranges and regexes, case/in pattern matching, while and until, and why each beats for.

topics.title: Defining methods and arguments
topics.description: def with implicit return of the last expression, default, keyword and splat arguments, the double splat for options, and method visibility with private and protected.

topics.title: Blocks, yield and block_given?
topics.description: Passing a block with do...end or braces, yield to call it, block_given? to make blocks optional, and how blocks make iteration and resource handling idiomatic.

topics.title: Procs and lambdas
topics.description: Proc.new and lambda as callable objects, the differences in argument strictness and return behaviour, the -> stabby syntax, call and the .() shorthand, and Symbol#to_proc.

topics.title: Closures and scope
topics.description: Blocks and lambdas capture the surrounding variables by reference, scope gates at def, class and module, binding objects, and the counter-generator pattern.

topics.title: Method objects and functional composition
topics.description: Turning methods into objects with method(:name), composing callables with >> and <<, then and tap for pipelines, and passing methods where blocks are expected.

topics.title: Arrays
topics.description: Creating, indexing with negative offsets and ranges, push, pop, shift and unshift, flatten, compact, zip and the mutating versus non-mutating method pairs.

topics.title: Hashes
topics.description: Symbol keys and the shorthand syntax, fetch with defaults versus [] returning nil, default values and default procs, iteration order, and transform_values and dig.

topics.title: Enumerable in depth
topics.description: Including Enumerable by defining each, then map, select, reject, reduce, each_with_object, group_by, partition, sort_by, min_by, sum, tally and each_slice.

topics.title: Lazy enumerators and Enumerator
topics.description: External enumerators with next, Enumerator.new for custom sequences, lazy chains that process infinite ranges, and each_with_index and with_index chaining.

topics.title: Sets, Structs and Data
topics.description: Set for uniqueness and set algebra, Struct for quick value-like classes with accessors, Data.define for immutable value objects, and Comparable for ordering.

topics.title: Strings and interpolation
topics.description: Single versus double quotes, interpolation with #{}, heredocs with <<~ for indentation stripping, frozen string literals, and mutation with << versus +=.

topics.title: String methods and formatting
topics.description: split, strip, gsub, sub, start_with?, center and ljust, format and % for padded output, and encoding methods for bytes and UTF-8.

topics.title: Regular expressions
topics.description: Regexp literals and =~, match and MatchData, named captures binding local variables, gsub with hashes and blocks, scan, and the special variables $~ and $1.

topics.title: Files, directories and IO
topics.description: File.read, File.write, File.foreach for streaming, File.open with blocks, Dir.glob, Pathname, FileUtils, STDIN and ARGF for scripts.

topics.title: JSON, YAML and CSV
topics.description: JSON.parse with symbolize_names and JSON.generate, YAML.safe_load for configuration, the CSV library with headers and converters, and ERB for templating text.

topics.title: raise, rescue, ensure and retry
topics.description: Raising with a class and message, rescue clauses ordered by specificity, ensure for cleanup, retry for transient failures, and method-level rescue without begin.

topics.title: Custom exception hierarchies
topics.description: Subclassing StandardError, a base error per gem or app, adding data to exceptions, the cause chain, and raise versus fail conventions.

topics.title: catch, throw and control flow alternatives
topics.description: catch and throw for non-error unwinding, why exceptions are slow for control flow, returning nil or result objects, and the safe navigation idiom.

topics.title: Debugging with debug and pry
topics.description: The debug gem with binding.break, stepping and inspecting, pry for a richer console, pp and inspect, warnings with -w, and reading backtraces.

topics.title: Classes, initialize and attr accessors
topics.description: Defining classes with initialize, attr_reader, attr_writer and attr_accessor generating methods, to_s and inspect, and class methods with self.

topics.title: Inheritance and super
topics.description: Single inheritance with <, super with and without arguments, overriding, the ancestors chain and Object and BasicObject at the top.

topics.title: Modules as namespaces and mixins
topics.description: Modules grouping constants and methods, include for instance methods, extend for singleton methods, prepend for wrapping, module_function, and where each lands in ancestors.

topics.title: Method lookup and the singleton class
topics.description: How Ruby resolves a message through the singleton class, prepended modules, the class, included modules and superclasses, then method_missing, plus define_method on the fly.

topics.title: Metaprogramming techniques
topics.description: send and public_send, instance_variable_get, class_eval and instance_eval, Module.new and Class.new, hooks like inherited and method_added, and the risks of too much magic.

topics.title: Refinements, freeze and object identity
topics.description: Scoped monkey patching with refine and using, freezing objects and constants, dup versus clone, object_id and equal?, and why Comparable and Enumerable are the idiomatic reuse.

topics.title: Duck typing and designing small objects
topics.description: Relying on respond_to? rather than class checks, small objects with one responsibility, value objects, composition with delegation via Forwardable and SimpleDelegator.

topics.title: Object allocation and garbage collection
topics.description: Every literal and string allocates, the generational GC and compaction, ObjectSpace for counting, GC.stat, and reducing allocations with symbols, frozen literals and in-place methods.

topics.title: Threads, the GVL and Mutex
topics.description: Thread.new and join, the Global VM Lock allowing one thread to run Ruby code at a time, I/O releasing the lock, Mutex and Queue for coordination, and thread-safety pitfalls.

topics.title: Fibers and the Fiber scheduler
topics.description: Fibers as cooperative coroutines with resume and yield, how Enumerator uses them, and the Fiber scheduler interface behind async gems for non-blocking I/O.

topics.title: Ractors and processes
topics.description: Ractors for true parallelism with isolated object spaces and message passing, shareable objects, and fork with Process.wait for the traditional multi-process model.

topics.title: Minitest
topics.description: The standard library test framework: test classes and assertions, spec-style describe blocks, setup and teardown, and running with rake test or ruby -Itest.

topics.title: RSpec fundamentals
topics.description: describe, context and it, expect with matchers, let and let! for lazy fixtures, before hooks, subject, and organising spec files to mirror lib.

topics.title: Doubles, stubs and shared examples
topics.description: instance_double for verified doubles, allow and expect for stubs and message expectations, shared examples for duck-typed contracts, and avoiding over-mocking.

topics.title: Rake tasks and project layout
topics.description: lib and bin directories, require_relative versus $LOAD_PATH, Rakefile tasks with dependencies, and a default task that runs tests and RuboCop.

topics.title: Building and publishing a gem
topics.description: The gemspec with files, dependencies and executables, semantic versioning, gem build and gem push, and testing the gem against several Ruby versions in CI.

topics.title: Performance and profiling
topics.description: benchmark-ips for comparisons, stackprof and memory_profiler, YJIT, avoiding allocation in hot loops, and the cost of method_missing and string building.

topics.title: Security in Ruby code
topics.description: Never eval or send user input, safe YAML and Marshal handling, avoiding shell injection with system arrays, bundler-audit for vulnerable gems, and secure random tokens.

categories.description: How Ruby powers the web through Rails; the full framework has its own track (Ruby on Rails).

topics.description: rails new, the MVC folders, convention over configuration, generators, the development server, and how naming links models, tables, controllers and views.

topics.title: Routing, controllers and views
topics.description: resources routes, RESTful controller actions, strong parameters, ERB views and partials, and the flow from request to rendered HTML.

topics.title: Active Record essentials
topics.description: Models backed by tables, migrations, validations, associations like has_many and belongs_to, query methods, and includes against N+1.

topics.description: Active Job with Sidekiq or Solid Queue, Action Mailer, and the Rails test stack with fixtures and system tests; each is covered fully in the Rails track.

topics.title: Project: log analyser CLI

topics.description: Model rooms, items and commands with small objects and modules, parse player input, persist game state as YAML, and let scenarios be defined in a Ruby DSL using instance_eval.

title: Rust

topics.title: Installing Rust with rustup

topics.title: Cargo: new, build, run and test
topics.description: Cargo is the build tool, package manager and test runner in one: creating a project, the src/main.rs and src/lib.rs conventions, debug versus release builds, cargo run and cargo test, and the target directory.

topics.title: rustfmt, clippy and rust-analyzer

topics.title: Anatomy of a Rust program
topics.description: fn main, println! as a macro rather than a function, semicolons turning expressions into statements, blocks that return their last expression, and the compiler messages that explain what went wrong.

subtopics.title: fn main and the entry point

topics.title: Scalar types, operators and overflow
topics.description: Integers of fixed width (i32, u8, usize), floats, bool and char as a Unicode scalar, arithmetic that panics on overflow in debug and wraps in release, explicit as casts, and the wrapping and checked method families.

subtopics.title: Overflow behaviour in debug and release

topics.title: Tuples, arrays and compound types
topics.description: Tuples for fixed heterogeneous groups with destructuring, arrays with a compile-time length and bounds checks, the unit type (), and how these differ from Vec and slices that come later.

topics.title: Conditions and loops as expressions
topics.description: if without parentheses that must be a bool, if as an expression, loop with break carrying a value, while, for over ranges and iterators, and labelled breaks for nested loops.

topics.title: Functions and return values
topics.description: Typed parameters and return types, returning the final expression or with return, the unit return, functions as values, and why parameter types are never inferred.

subtopics.title: Implicit return of the last expression

topics.title: Ownership and moves
topics.description: Every value has exactly one owner; assigning or passing a non-Copy value moves it and the old binding is unusable. Copy types, clone as an explicit deep copy, and drop at scope end.

topics.title: References and borrowing
topics.description: Borrowing with & and &mut instead of moving: any number of shared references or exactly one mutable reference at a time, no references to dropped data, and how this rules out data races and iterator invalidation.

topics.title: Slices
topics.description: Views into contiguous data: &[T] and &str carry a pointer and length, range syntax to slice, why functions should take slices rather than Vec or String, and the difference between a slice and an array reference.

topics.title: Lifetimes and annotations
topics.description: Every reference has a lifetime the compiler checks; annotations like <'a> relate input and output references in signatures, elision rules cover most cases, and 'static marks data that lives for the whole program.

topics.title: Borrow checker errors and fixes
topics.description: Reading E0382, E0499, E0502 and E0597, the usual fixes (clone, restructure, shorten borrows, return owned data, use indices), non-lexical lifetimes, and knowing when the compiler is right about a real bug.

subtopics.title: Does not live long enough errors

topics.title: Structs and impl blocks
topics.description: Named-field, tuple and unit structs, impl blocks with methods taking self, &self or &mut self, associated functions like new, update syntax, and deriving Debug to print them.

topics.title: Enums and Option
topics.description: Enums whose variants carry data are Rust's sum types; Option<T> replaces null with Some and None, forcing every absence to be handled, and enums with impl blocks model state machines cleanly.

topics.title: match and exhaustiveness
topics.description: match compares a value against patterns in order and the compiler rejects missing cases; binding parts of variants, the wildcard _, match as an expression, and why exhaustiveness catches bugs when an enum grows.

topics.title: if let, let else and while let
topics.description: Concise handling of one pattern: if let for a single case, let else to diverge when a pattern fails, while let for draining iterators and stacks, and when a full match is clearer.

subtopics.title: Choosing between if let and match

topics.title: Pattern syntax in depth
topics.description: Destructuring structs, tuples and nested enums, ranges and multiple patterns with |, match guards, @ bindings, ref and ref mut, and ignoring parts with .. and _.

topics.title: Defining and implementing traits
topics.description: Traits declare shared behaviour; impl Trait for Type provides it, default methods reduce boilerplate, the orphan rule decides where impls may live, and traits replace inheritance as the way to share behaviour.

topics.title: Generic functions and types
topics.description: Type parameters on functions, structs and enums, monomorphisation that generates a specialised copy per type, turbofish syntax for explicit arguments, and const generics for array lengths.

topics.title: Trait bounds and where clauses
topics.description: Constraining generics with T: Trait, combining bounds with +, where clauses for readability, impl Trait in argument and return position, and how bounds let generic code call methods.

subtopics.title: impl Trait in arguments and returns

topics.title: Trait objects and dynamic dispatch
topics.description: dyn Trait behind a reference or Box for heterogeneous collections, vtables and the cost of dynamic dispatch, object safety rules, and choosing between generics and trait objects.

topics.title: Derivable and conversion traits
topics.description: The standard traits every type should consider: Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Ord and Default via derive, Display by hand, From and Into for conversions, and operator traits like Add.

topics.title: Closures and the Fn traits
topics.description: Closures capture their environment by reference, mutable reference or move; the Fn, FnMut and FnOnce traits describe how they can be called, move closures for threads, and returning closures with impl Fn.

topics.title: Vec and slices in practice
topics.description: The growable array: push, pop, insert and remove costs, capacity and with_capacity, sorting and deduplication, slicing and windows, and the borrow rules that shape how you mutate while reading.

topics.title: HashMap, HashSet and BTreeMap
topics.description: Hash-based maps and sets with the entry API for insert-or-update, ownership of keys, the default SipHash and faster alternatives, and BTreeMap when you need ordered keys or range queries.

topics.title: String, &str and UTF-8
topics.description: String owns UTF-8 bytes and &str borrows them; indexing by integer is forbidden, chars versus bytes versus grapheme clusters, push_str and format!, and converting between the two types.

topics.title: Formatting, Display and parsing
topics.description: format! and the {} versus {:?} placeholders, width and precision, implementing Display for your types, parse::<T>() through FromStr, and splitting and trimming text.

topics.title: Iterators and adapters
topics.description: iter, iter_mut and into_iter, lazy adapters such as map, filter, enumerate, zip and take, consumers like collect, sum and fold, and why iterator chains compile to the same code as hand-written loops.

topics.title: Implementing Iterator
topics.description: Writing your own iterator by implementing next, getting every adapter for free, IntoIterator so for loops work on your types, DoubleEndedIterator and ExactSizeIterator, and peekable iterators for parsers.

topics.title: Result and the ? operator
topics.description: Recoverable errors are values: Result<T, E>, matching or unwrapping, the ? operator that returns early and converts errors with From, and main returning Result.

topics.title: Option combinators
topics.description: Working with maybe-values without match: map, and_then, unwrap_or and unwrap_or_else, ok_or to convert into Result, filter, take and as_ref, and when combinator chains stop being readable.

topics.title: Custom error types and the Error trait
topics.description: An enum of failure cases per module, implementing Display and std::error::Error, wrapping sources for chains, From impls so ? converts automatically, and Box<dyn Error> for quick programs.

topics.title: thiserror, anyhow and panic policy
topics.description: thiserror derives Error boilerplate for libraries, anyhow adds context and ergonomic errors for applications, unwrap and expect as deliberate choices, and when a panic is the correct response.

topics.title: Modules, visibility and use paths
topics.description: mod declares modules in files or directories, pub controls visibility, use brings paths into scope, crate:: and super:: paths, pub(crate) for internal APIs, and re-exports that shape a public surface.

topics.title: Crates, workspaces and Cargo.toml
topics.description: Library and binary crates, the package manifest, multiple binaries, workspaces that share one Cargo.lock and target directory across related crates, and profiles for debug and release settings.

topics.title: Dependencies, features and semver
topics.description: Adding crates with cargo add, version requirements and how Cargo.lock pins them, optional dependencies and feature flags, semver compatibility rules, and cargo tree to inspect the graph.

topics.title: Publishing, docs and build scripts
topics.description: Doc comments with /// and //! that cargo doc renders, publishing to crates.io with metadata and a license, build.rs for code generation and native libraries, and cfg attributes for platform-specific code.

topics.title: Reading and writing files
topics.description: std::fs for whole-file reads and writes, BufReader and BufWriter for line-by-line and buffered I/O, the Read and Write traits, paths with PathBuf, and propagating io::Error with ?.

topics.title: Command-line apps with clap
topics.description: Parsing arguments with clap derive, subcommands and flags with help generated automatically, reading stdin and environment variables, exit codes, and writing errors to stderr.

topics.title: Serialisation with serde

topics.title: Stack, heap and Box

topics.title: Rc, Arc and reference counting
topics.description: Shared ownership when one owner is impossible: Rc for single-threaded graphs, Arc for cross-thread sharing with atomic counts, Weak to break cycles, and the cost compared with borrowing.

topics.title: Drop, RAII and resource cleanup
topics.description: The Drop trait runs when a value goes out of scope, in reverse declaration order; files, locks and sockets clean up without finally blocks, and std::mem::drop releases early.

topics.title: Interior mutability
topics.description: Mutating through a shared reference under controlled rules: Cell for Copy values, RefCell with runtime borrow checking and panics on violation, the Rc<RefCell<T>> pattern, and OnceCell for lazy initialisation.

topics.title: Deref and smart pointer ergonomics
topics.description: The Deref trait lets Box, Rc and custom wrappers behave like references, deref coercion turns &String into &str at call sites, and Cow avoids allocation when data may or may not need owning.

topics.title: Threads and scoped threads

topics.title: Send, Sync and thread safety

subtopics.title: Why Rc and RefCell are not thread safe

topics.title: Channels

subtopics.title: Invariants the compiler no longer checks

title: Security Foundations
description: The vocabulary and mental models every security role builds on: CIA triad and core principles, threat actors, the kill chain and MITRE ATT&CK, risk and frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001), control types, defence in depth and zero trust, identity, network, endpoint, application and data basics, SOC operations, social engineering, certifications and a safe home lab.

code.label: the language or tool that fits (bash, python, yaml)

categories.title: Principles and Vocabulary
categories.description: The words and models the whole field is built on, used precisely from day one.

topics.title: The CIA triad
topics.description: Confidentiality, integrity and availability as the three properties every control protects, with concrete failures for each (a leaked database, a tampered invoice, a ransomed file server) and why a fix for one can weaken another.

topics.title: AAA, non-repudiation and accountability
topics.description: Authentication proves who you are, authorization decides what you may do and accounting records what you did; non-repudiation (signatures, tamper-evident logs) stops a party denying an action later.

topics.title: Vulnerabilities, threats and risk
topics.description: A vulnerability is a weakness, a threat is something that could exploit it, and risk is the likelihood times the impact of that happening; keeping the three apart is what makes prioritisation possible.

topics.title: Threat actors and their motivations
topics.description: Who attacks and why: financially motivated crime groups, state-sponsored espionage, hacktivists, insiders and opportunistic script kiddies, and how motivation and capability shape which defences matter for a given organisation.

topics.title: Core security design principles
topics.description: Least privilege, fail-safe defaults, separation of duties, economy of mechanism, complete mediation and open design (no security through obscurity): the Saltzer and Schroeder rules that still explain most good and bad decisions.

categories.title: How Attacks Unfold
categories.description: Models for describing an intrusion step by step, so defences can be placed where they break the chain.

topics.title: The cyber kill chain
topics.description: Lockheed Martin's seven stages from reconnaissance through weaponisation, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control, to actions on objectives, and the idea that breaking any one link stops the attack.

topics.title: MITRE ATT&CK overview
topics.description: A public matrix of adversary tactics (the why) and techniques (the how) observed in real intrusions, used to name behaviours, map detections and measure coverage; how to read a technique page and navigate the Enterprise matrix.

topics.title: Common attack vectors
topics.description: The ways intrusions actually begin according to breach reports: phishing and credential theft, exploitation of exposed services, stolen or reused passwords, malicious attachments, supply-chain compromise and misconfiguration.

topics.title: CVE, CVSS and vulnerability disclosure
topics.description: How vulnerabilities get a CVE identifier, how CVSS scores severity from base metrics, why a 9.8 is not always your top priority (exploitability, exposure, KEV), and how coordinated disclosure and bug bounties work.

categories.title: Risk Management and Frameworks
categories.description: Turning threats into decisions a business can make, and the frameworks that structure a programme.

topics.title: Risk assessment
topics.description: Identifying assets, threats and vulnerabilities, then estimating likelihood and impact qualitatively (heat maps) or quantitatively (annualised loss expectancy) to produce a ranked risk register.

topics.title: Risk treatment options
topics.description: The four responses to a risk (mitigate with controls, transfer via insurance or contracts, avoid by not doing the thing, accept with sign-off) and residual risk that remains after treatment.

topics.title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
topics.description: The six CSF 2.0 functions (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover), how categories and subcategories describe outcomes rather than tools, and how profiles and tiers measure maturity.

topics.title: ISO 27001 and the ISMS
topics.description: What an Information Security Management System is, the plan-do-check-act cycle, the Annex A control set, the statement of applicability and what an audit and certification actually involve.

topics.title: Regulation and compliance
topics.description: Why laws and standards such as GDPR, PCI DSS, HIPAA and SOC 2 exist, what each demands at a high level, and the difference between being compliant and being secure.

categories.title: Controls and Architecture
categories.description: The types of control and the architectural ideas that decide where they go.

topics.title: Preventive, detective and corrective controls
topics.description: Classifying controls by when they act: preventive stops the event (MFA, firewall), detective spots it (alerts, log review), corrective restores (backups, patches), with deterrent and compensating controls filling gaps.

topics.title: Administrative, technical and physical controls
topics.description: The second axis of classification: policies and training, software and hardware mechanisms, and locks, badges and cameras; how a single risk is usually treated with all three.

topics.title: Defence in depth
topics.description: Layering independent controls so that one failure does not become a breach: perimeter, network, host, application, data and people layers, and why layers must fail differently to be worth having.

topics.title: Zero trust
topics.description: Replacing the trusted internal network with per-request verification of identity, device and context, least-privilege access to individual resources, and continuous monitoring; NIST 800-207 components and a realistic migration path.

topics.title: Network segmentation and security zones
topics.description: Dividing a network into zones (internet, DMZ, internal, restricted) with controlled crossings, VLANs and firewall rules, so an attacker who lands in one place cannot roam freely.

categories.title: Identity, Network and Endpoint Basics
categories.description: The three places most controls live, at the level needed before the dedicated tracks.

topics.title: Identity and access basics
topics.description: Accounts, credentials and the authentication factors (something you know, have, are), why MFA blocks most credential attacks, and how role-based access assigns permissions without per-user chaos.

topics.title: Passwords and credential hygiene
topics.description: What makes a password strong against offline cracking versus online guessing, why length beats complexity rules, how password managers and breach checks help, and what NIST 800-63B now recommends.

topics.title: Network security basics
topics.description: Firewalls and their rule order, NAT, VPNs for remote access, IDS versus IPS, and what a proxy sees; enough of the network stack to reason about where traffic can be inspected or blocked.

topics.title: Wireless security
topics.description: How Wi-Fi authentication and encryption evolved from WEP to WPA3, why open networks expose traffic, enterprise 802.1X versus pre-shared keys, and rogue access point risks.

topics.title: Endpoint security
topics.description: Protecting laptops and servers: patching, signature and behavioural antivirus, EDR telemetry and response, disk encryption, application allow-listing and hardening baselines, and why endpoints are where most incidents are detected.

topics.title: Email security
topics.description: How SPF, DKIM and DMARC let receivers reject forged sender domains, what secure email gateways filter, and why email remains the most common delivery path for phishing and malware.

categories.title: Applications, Data and Privacy
categories.description: Where the valuable data lives and the basic ways applications and storage fail.

topics.title: Application security basics
topics.description: The OWASP Top 10 as a map of how web applications fail (injection, broken access control, misconfiguration, vulnerable components), and the idea that security is built in with validation, least privilege and testing, not bolted on.

topics.title: Cryptography in practice
topics.description: Where encryption, hashing and signatures show up in everyday systems (TLS, disk encryption, password storage, code signing), what each guarantees, and why key management is the hard part.

subtopics.title: Encryption in transit and at rest

topics.title: Data classification and protection
topics.description: Labelling data by sensitivity (public, internal, confidential, restricted) so handling rules follow the label, and the protections that rely on it: encryption, DLP, retention limits and the 3-2-1 backup rule.

topics.title: Privacy principles
topics.description: Privacy as a distinct discipline: data minimisation, purpose limitation, consent and lawful basis, data subject rights, privacy by design, and the difference between PII, sensitive data and anonymised data.

categories.title: Operations and People
categories.description: How security is run day to day, and the human layer attackers target first.

topics.title: Security operations overview
topics.description: What a SOC does: collecting logs into a SIEM, writing detections, triaging alerts by tier, threat hunting and the metrics (MTTD, MTTR, false-positive rate) that show whether it is working.

topics.title: Incident response lifecycle
topics.description: The NIST phases (preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned), what a playbook contains, and why containment decisions are made before the full picture is known.

topics.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery
topics.description: Keeping the business running through outages: business impact analysis, RTO and RPO targets, backup and failover strategies, and testing the plan before it is needed.

topics.title: Social engineering
topics.description: Manipulating people rather than systems: phishing, vishing, pretexting, baiting and tailgating, the psychological levers (urgency, authority, reciprocity) they pull, and how to recognise and report an attempt.

topics.title: Security awareness programmes
topics.description: Designing training that changes behaviour: role-specific content, simulated phishing done without shaming, clear reporting paths, measuring click and report rates, and making the secure path the easy one.

categories.title: Careers, Certifications and Home Lab
categories.description: Where the field goes from here and how to practise safely and legally.

topics.title: Security roles and career paths
topics.description: What SOC analysts, security engineers, penetration testers, GRC specialists, cloud security engineers and application security engineers actually do day to day, and which skills transfer between them.

subtopics.title: Entry routes from IT and dev

topics.title: CompTIA Security+ domains
topics.description: The five SY0-701 domains (general concepts, threats and mitigations, architecture, operations, programme management), what each expects, and how to use the objectives as a self-study checklist.

topics.title: CISSP domains overview
topics.description: The eight CISSP domains from security and risk management to software development security, why it is a management-level certification with an experience requirement, and how its breadth maps to this track.

topics.title: Building a safe home lab
topics.description: A practice environment that cannot harm anyone: VirtualBox or Proxmox with an isolated host-only network, Kali plus deliberately vulnerable targets (Metasploitable, DVWA, Juice Shop), snapshots for reset, and TryHackMe or Hack The Box for guided rooms.

topics.title: Legal and ethical boundaries
topics.description: Computer misuse laws, why written authorisation and scope define legal testing, responsible disclosure etiquette, and how to practise offensive techniques without ever touching systems you do not own.

categories.title: Projects and Interview Preparation
categories.description: Defensive lab work that turns the vocabulary into evidence of skill.

topics.title: Project: isolated home lab with vulnerable targets
topics.description: Build a hypervisor lab with a host-only network, a Kali VM, Metasploitable and OWASP Juice Shop, snapshots for every machine, and a written network diagram and reset procedure; verify no target can reach the internet.

topics.title: Project: risk register for a small business
topics.description: Model a fictional 20-person company, inventory its assets, list realistic threats, score likelihood and impact, choose a treatment for each risk and map controls to NIST CSF functions in a spreadsheet plus a two-page summary.

topics.title: Project: phishing analysis and awareness kit
topics.description: Collect sample phishing emails from public corpora, analyse headers for SPF/DKIM/DMARC results, extract indicators safely, and produce a one-page staff guide plus a reporting procedure.

topics.title: Project: ATT&CK-mapped incident walkthrough
topics.description: Take a public breach report, reconstruct the attack as kill-chain stages, map each action to ATT&CK techniques in Navigator, and propose one preventive and one detective control per stage.

subtopics.title: Choose and read a breach report

topics.title: Security fundamentals interview questions
topics.description: The questions asked for entry-level security roles: explain the CIA triad with examples, difference between a vulnerability and a threat, how you would prioritise patches, what zero trust means, and how you stay current.

topics.title: Scenario and behavioural questions
topics.description: Walking through scenarios interviewers love: a user reports a suspicious email, a server shows unexpected outbound traffic, a developer wants to disable MFA; how to structure an answer with triage, containment and communication.

title: Spring Boot
description: Spring Boot 3 from the IoC container to production: dependency injection, starters and auto-configuration, profiles, REST controllers, validation and ProblemDetail errors, JPA and transactions, security, slice tests and Testcontainers, caching, messaging, Actuator and tracing, Docker, Spring Cloud, and four deployable projects.

categories.title: Spring Fundamentals and Dependency Injection
categories.description: What the container actually does before any Boot magic is layered on top.

topics.title: Inversion of control and the ApplicationContext
topics.description: Why objects should receive their collaborators instead of constructing them, how the ApplicationContext builds a graph of beans from metadata, and what it means that Spring owns object lifecycles.

topics.title: Beans, stereotypes and component scanning
topics.description: @Component, @Service, @Repository and @Controller mark classes for discovery; how @ComponentScan picks a base package and why the main class location decides what Boot sees.

topics.title: Constructor, setter and field injection
topics.description: How Spring resolves dependencies by type and then by name, why constructor injection makes beans immutable and testable, and how @Qualifier, @Primary and Optional handle ambiguity.

topics.title: Bean scopes and lifecycle callbacks
topics.description: Singleton by default, prototype, request and session scopes, what a scoped proxy does when a singleton depends on a request bean, and @PostConstruct, @PreDestroy and InitializingBean hooks.

topics.title: @Configuration and @Bean methods
topics.description: Declaring beans for classes you do not own, how CGLIB proxies make @Bean calls inside a @Configuration return the same singleton, and proxyBeanMethods=false for lite mode.

topics.title: Conditional beans and ordering
topics.description: @Conditional, @ConditionalOnProperty, @ConditionalOnMissingBean and @Profile decide whether a bean exists; @Order and @DependsOn shape ordering; this is the mechanism Boot auto-configuration is built on.

topics.title: AOP and proxies behind @Transactional
topics.description: How Spring wraps beans in JDK or CGLIB proxies to add behaviour, why a self-invocation bypasses @Transactional, @Cacheable and @Async, and how to write an @Aspect for cross-cutting logging.

categories.title: Project Structure and Starters
categories.description: What a generated Boot project contains and why it starts with zero XML.

topics.title: Creating a project with Spring Initializr
topics.description: Generating a Boot 3 project with Java 17+, choosing Maven or Gradle, picking starters, and what the wrapper scripts, parent POM and generated main class give you.

topics.title: Starters and dependency management
topics.description: spring-boot-starter-web pulls in MVC, Jackson and Tomcat with matching versions; how the BOM pins versions, how to exclude a transitive dependency, and how to swap Tomcat for Jetty or Undertow.

topics.title: Auto-configuration and @SpringBootApplication
topics.description: How AutoConfiguration.imports lists candidates, how conditions on classpath and beans decide what activates, and how to read the auto-configuration report to see why something did or did not happen.

topics.title: Package layout and layering
topics.description: Organising controllers, services, repositories and domain by feature or by layer, keeping the web layer free of entities, and why package-private classes and ArchUnit tests keep boundaries honest.

subtopics.title: Package by feature versus by layer

topics.title: Running, packaging and the fat jar
topics.description: mvn spring-boot:run versus java -jar, how the repackaged jar nests dependencies and boots with a custom launcher, layered jars for Docker, and the difference between jar and war packaging.

topics.title: Logging with Logback and SLF4J

topics.title: UserDetailsService and DaoAuthenticationProvider
topics.description: Loading a user by username from your database, returning UserDetails with password hash and authorities, and how DaoAuthenticationProvider compares the submitted password with the encoder.

topics.title: Password hashing and PasswordEncoder
topics.description: BCrypt, Argon2 and SCrypt as slow salted hashes, the DelegatingPasswordEncoder id prefix that lets you migrate algorithms, and upgrading hashes on successful login.

subtopics.title: Why slow hashes resist brute force

topics.title: Form login
topics.description: UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter, the generated login page and a custom one, success and failure handlers, saved requests and redirects, and logout with session invalidation.

topics.title: HTTP Basic and API keys
topics.description: BasicAuthenticationFilter decoding the Authorization header, why Basic is only acceptable over TLS, and implementing API-key authentication with a custom filter and provider.

topics.title: Custom authentication providers and events
topics.description: Writing an AuthenticationProvider for LDAP-like or one-time-code schemes, publishing AuthenticationSuccessEvent and failure events, and lockout counters built from them.

topics.title: Remember-me and persistent logins
topics.description: Hash-based versus persistent-token remember-me, the cookie and its risks, and why a remembered login is treated as weaker than a fresh one for sensitive actions.

categories.title: Authorization
categories.description: Deciding what an authenticated caller may do.

topics.title: Roles, authorities and GrantedAuthority
topics.description: Authorities as plain strings, the ROLE_ prefix convention behind hasRole, storing authorities per user or via groups, and why fine-grained permissions age better than roles alone.

topics.title: URL authorization with authorizeHttpRequests
topics.description: requestMatchers for paths and methods, permitAll, authenticated, hasRole and access with a custom AuthorizationManager, and how matchers interact with servlet path handling and MVC patterns.

topics.title: Method security with @PreAuthorize
topics.description: @EnableMethodSecurity, expressions that see method arguments and the return value, @PostAuthorize, @PreFilter and @PostFilter, and where the proxy boundary hides checks.

topics.title: Custom permission evaluators and domain checks
topics.description: hasPermission with a PermissionEvaluator that consults ownership, calling a bean from SpEL with @beanName.check(...), and keeping authorization logic testable.

topics.title: Role hierarchies
topics.description: Declaring that ADMIN implies USER with a RoleHierarchy bean so rules stay short, and how the hierarchy is applied in both URL and method security.

topics.title: Access denied and entry points
topics.description: AuthenticationEntryPoint for unauthenticated callers, AccessDeniedHandler for denied ones, and returning JSON error bodies instead of redirects for APIs.

categories.title: CSRF, CORS and Sessions
categories.description: Browser-specific threats and the state behind a login.

topics.title: CSRF protection
topics.description: Why a browser sends cookies with cross-site requests, how the synchronizer token pattern stops it, the deferred token loading in Security 6 and when a stateless API can disable it.

topics.title: CSRF tokens for single-page apps
topics.description: CookieCsrfTokenRepository with a readable XSRF-TOKEN cookie, the X-XSRF-TOKEN header convention, and the XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler that defends against BREACH.

topics.title: CORS with Spring Security
topics.description: Preflight requests hitting the filter chain before controllers, a CorsConfigurationSource bean the CorsFilter uses, allowed origins versus patterns, and credentials rules.

topics.title: Session management and fixation
topics.description: SessionCreationPolicy options, session fixation protection by changing the id on login, concurrent session limits, and invalidating sessions on logout.

topics.title: Distributed sessions with Spring Session
topics.description: Storing sessions in Redis or JDBC so any instance can serve a logged-in user, cookie configuration, and the trade-off against stateless tokens.

topics.title: Security headers
topics.description: The headers Spring adds by default: Cache-Control, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS, X-Frame-Options; configuring a Content-Security-Policy and when to relax frame options.

categories.title: JWT and Resource Servers
categories.description: Token-based security for APIs.

topics.title: JWT structure and signature verification
topics.description: Header, claims and signature, HS256 versus RS256 and ES256, the exp, iss and aud claims that must be checked, and why the alg header must never be trusted.

subtopics.title: alg none and key confusion attacks

topics.title: Configuring a JWT resource server
topics.description: oauth2ResourceServer().jwt() with an issuer-uri or jwk-set-uri, how NimbusJwtDecoder fetches and caches keys, and validating audience with a custom OAuth2TokenValidator.

topics.title: Mapping claims to authorities
topics.description: JwtAuthenticationConverter and JwtGrantedAuthoritiesConverter, reading scope versus roles claims, the SCOPE_ prefix, and building a custom principal object from claims.

topics.title: Issuing tokens yourself
topics.description: Signing JWTs with Nimbus or JwtEncoder for a first-party API, short-lived access tokens with refresh tokens, key rotation with kid, and why an authorization server is the better long-term answer.

topics.title: Opaque tokens and introspection
topics.description: When tokens are references rather than self-contained, calling the introspection endpoint per request, caching results, and comparing latency and revocation trade-offs against JWTs.

categories.title: OAuth2 Client and Login
categories.description: Delegating login and calling third-party APIs on behalf of users.

topics.title: OAuth2 roles and the authorization code flow
topics.description: Resource owner, client, authorization server and resource server; the redirect-based authorization code flow with PKCE, and why implicit and password grants are gone.

topics.title: OpenID Connect login with oauth2Login
topics.description: ID tokens on top of OAuth2, the built-in provider registrations, scopes and the userinfo endpoint, and the OidcUser principal you receive after login.

topics.title: Mapping external identities to local users
topics.description: An OAuth2UserService or OidcUserService that finds or creates a local account, assigns authorities from your database, and links several providers to one user.

topics.title: Calling APIs as an OAuth2 client
topics.description: oauth2Client with OAuth2AuthorizedClientManager to obtain and refresh access tokens, client credentials for service-to-service calls, and attaching tokens to RestClient or WebClient.

topics.title: Spring Authorization Server
topics.description: Running your own issuer: registered clients, token settings, the consent page, JWK source, and when a hosted identity provider is the wiser choice.

categories.title: Testing Security
categories.description: Proving the rules do what you think.

topics.title: @WithMockUser and @WithUserDetails
topics.description: Populating the SecurityContext for a test method with a fake user or one loaded through your UserDetailsService, and testing method security without HTTP.

topics.title: MockMvc security post-processors
topics.description: user(), jwt(), oauth2Login() and csrf() from SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors to shape each request, and asserting redirects, 401s and 403s precisely.

topics.title: Integration tests against a real issuer
topics.description: Running Keycloak or a mock OIDC server in Testcontainers, obtaining real tokens in tests, and verifying JWKS discovery and audience validation end to end.

topics.title: Security regression tests
topics.description: A test per rule that asserts anonymous, wrong-role and right-role outcomes, parameterised over endpoints, so a rule reordering fails the build rather than a pentest.

categories.title: Common Misconfigurations
categories.description: The mistakes that show up in audits, and how to spot them in review.

topics.title: Rule ordering and overly broad permitAll
topics.description: anyRequest before specific rules, permitAll on /api/** for a health check, and pattern mismatches such as /admin versus /admin/ that open more than intended.

topics.title: Disabling CSRF or CORS carelessly
topics.description: csrf().disable() copied into a session-based app, allowedOriginPatterns("*") with credentials, and the difference between a secure API and one that merely works in the demo.

topics.title: Weak secrets and token handling
topics.description: Short HS256 keys, secrets in application.yml, long-lived tokens in localStorage, missing audience checks, and logging Authorization headers.

topics.title: Trusting the wrong source of truth
topics.description: Authorization decided from client-supplied ids or roles, mass assignment of a role field, and object-level checks skipped because the URL was protected.

topics.title: Proxies, HTTPS and forwarded headers
topics.description: requiresSecure loops behind a TLS-terminating proxy, trusting X-Forwarded-For from anyone, and secure cookie flags that never get set because the app thinks it is on HTTP.

topics.title: Security auditing and dependency hygiene
topics.description: Reading the debug filter listing, a checklist for reviews, keeping Spring Security patched, and scanning dependencies for known CVEs in CI.
